name: Jasper Mountain Trail Fest 2026
description:
USA Track & Field-Sanctioned Event

2026 Jasper Mountain Trail Fest Video

Introduction

Welcome to one of the most unique and rewarding trail running experiences in the Pacific Northwest. Jasper Mountain Trail Fest features some of the best-maintained and most thoughtfully designed single-track trails in Eastern Washington, set within the protected Jasper Mountain Reserve, an environmental 501(c)3 non-profit organization dedicated to conservation and public enjoyment.

Whether you are a seasoned trail runner looking for a rugged, higher-elevation challenge, a marathoner ready to push your limits off-road, or a team eager to take on a truly one-of-a-kind relay adventure, this event delivers. With distances ranging from a family-friendly 7K to a demanding full marathon and an all-day relay, there is something here for every level of runner. Come test yourself on beautiful, wild terrain while supporting conservation and experiencing a trail system that truly stands apart.

For 2026, we are offering four unique race options:

1) Our classic (sixth annual!) 4-person relay race, 52.4 miles total distance
2) Solo Half marathon, 13.1 miles with 2,570 feet of elevation gain
3) Solo Full marathon, 26.2 miles with 5,140 feet of elevation gain
4) Solo 7k Family Run (4.4 miles) with minimal elevation gain

 

Price increases are on  April 15, 2026, May 17, 2026, and June 13, 2026. Sign up by May 31, 2026 to guarantee you receive a race t-shirt and medal! (we have a few extras for late registrants on a first come-first serve basis). Contact info@jaspermountainreserve.org with any questions.

 

All races take place on the following single track trails (click on each for details):

Red Loop (3.3 miles)
Green Loop (4.4 miles)
Black Loop (5.4 miles)

 

Reserve Information and Accommodations

The start and finish line is at Jasper Mountain Reserve, Dayton, WA 99328. Type "Jasper Mountain Reserve" into Google or Apple Maps and follow online directions.

Come and camp with us on our beautiful campground direct on the race course. On-site camping guarantees a stress-free morning. name: July 4th Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
Run Free. Run Proud.
Celebrate America’s independence with the July 4th Freedom Run — where every stride honors liberty, courage, and the spirit of freedom.
Whether you walk, jog, or race your heart out, come together to move for what unites us all.

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: K9 Candy Cane 5K Fun Run
description:
The K9 Candy Cane 5K Fun Run and Walk is held at the Renton Community Center Campus. Runners and walkers travel along the paved beautiful Cedar River Trail before looping back to the Community Center Campus. Competitive runners, fun runners, walkers and families (with or without) dogs are all invited to this annual event. Accurate and professional chip timing is provided by Negative Split. If registered before 9:00AM on Wednesday, November 25, participants will receive a hooded sweatshirt. Don't forget about our Annual Pet Food Drive for furry friends in need, help us FILL THE TRUCK! 

Registration Windows:

  • Early Bird Registration - August 19 to November 1.
    • Guarantees you a hooded sweatshirt. 
    • Ages 4 to 17 fee:        $20
    • Ages 18 and up fee:   $30
  • Standard Price Registration - November 2, ending at 9:00AM, November 25.
    • Guarantees you a hooded sweatshirt.  
    • Ages 4 to 17 fee:       $30
    • Ages 18 and up fee:  $40
  • Last Chance Registration -  Begins 9:01AM November 25, through 1:00PM on Saturday December 5.
    • Not eligible to receive a hooded sweatshirt, Fun Run Only.
    • Ages 4 to 17 fee:       $30
    • Ages 18 and up fee:  $40

Race Bib Number Pick Up:
If you have pre-registered, you may pick up your race bib and sweatshirt (if applicable) at The Renton Community Center, 1715 Maple Valley Hwy. Renton, 98057, Saturday, December 6, 9:30AM – 5:00PM. If you are picking up for family members or friends, you will need their race day registration confirmation. You will also have the opportunity to pickup your race bib and sweatshirt onsite the morning of the race. 

Race Guidelines for Humans and Dogs:

  • Strollers are welcome on the course for both humans and dogs.
  • Participants NOT wanting to be timed should NOT pass through the finish line, please exit the course to the left or right prior to entering the timing chute.
  • Your race bib is your timing chip. Please wear it outside of your clothing facing forward for accurate timing.
  • Timing will conclude 45 minutes after the start of the race.
  • Walkers stay to the right of the race course.
  • Extra sweatshirts are NOT purchased and will NOT be available day of race.
  • No more than two dogs per person.
  • All dogs are required to be current on vaccinations.
  • No dogs under six months of age.
  • Dogs must be on leash no more than 6 feet in length.
  • Owners are responsible for the well-being and safety of their dog(s) at all times
  • No female dogs in heat. 
  • No aggressive dogs or aggressive owners. Any signs of aggression towards other dogs or participants will result in being asked to leave the event.
  • Owners are responsible for always picking up after their dog(s). 

Pet Food Drive:
Please bring a can/bag of pet food to be donated to local animals in need. Help us FILL THE TRUCK! 

Click here: Course Map

Course Closure:
Recreational walkers/runners are non-competitive and will not be timed if finishing after 45 minutes. If you are participating in this event but are not being timed please be considerate and not cross the finish line where timing is taking place. Keep to the right or left of the timing chute.

Awards and Results:
Awards will be given to the top three runners overall in the following categories: Male 55+, Female 55+, Male 18-54, Female 18-54, Non-Binary Adult 18+, Youth 1-17. 

Hooded Sweatshirts:
After 9:00AM November 26, hooded Sweatshirts are no longer available. Extra sweatshirts are not purchased and will NOT be available at the end of the race. The sweatshirt size you selected is what's purchased. Sweatshirts are unisex sizing.

name: Kaiser Permanente Seafair Torchlight Run
description:
The Kaiser Permanente Seafair Torchlight Run is back again, returning on Saturday, July 25, 2026. This fan favorite will once again fill the streets of Seattle as thousands of participants lace up their sneakers and race ahead of the iconic Alaska Airlines Seafair Torchlight Parade. The race will kick off at 6:00 PM, setting the stage for an unforgettable evening of family fun and entertainment while inviting participants of all ages and abilities to take part in one of Seattle’s most vibrant summer traditions. 

Kicking off at 6:00pm, the 5K event will once again fill the streets along the downtown Seattle waterfront. This year’s theme, Light Up The Night, encourages the thousands of runners and walkers to add sparkle and glow to their race attire as they soak up golden hour views and the electric atmosphere just ahead of the Alaska Airlines Seafair Torchlight Parade. 

Set against the stunning backdrop of the newly revitalized Seattle Waterfront, the all-new race route offers runners a unique chance to experience downtown like never before. Open to runners of all experience levels, the Torchlight Run is perfect for seasoned athletes, casual joggers, first-timers, and families looking to enjoy the summer spirit of Seafair.

Once you cross the finish line, the celebration doesn't stop. Stick around for the Alaska Airlines Seafair Torchlight Parade, beginning at 7:30 PM, and enjoy live entertainment, music, and vibrant Seattle energy as the city comes together in celebration.

name: Kent Cornucopia Days 5K
description:
Participants 60 and over just $15! 

The 2026 race will still start and stop at Three Friends Fishing Hole and head north along the Green River Trail.  We're going north around Briscoe Park and briefly into Tukwila and head back home.  The course is certified and chip timed by Bell Lap Productions.  Parking is located Columbia Distributing. Please do not park in neighboring businesses.

Awards will go to the top 5 places in each age group and overall winners.  Awards ceremony to take place approximately 20 minutes after the first person has crossed the finish line.

Race Day Registration - 7:30 a.m.

Start of Race - 9:00 a.m.

Participants age 60 and over just $15!  (Add $15 for a shirt)

Race without shirt is $20 

Race with shirt is $35   (Must order by June 12)  No shirt orders on day of race

Race day fee is $25 (No shirts available)

Early packet pick up on Thursday, July 9, 4-7 p.m. at RoadRunner Sports, Kent Station  (You may pick up for friends)

name: Lake Meridian Triathlon
description:
Welcome to the big stage.

The Lake Meridian Triathlon is the crown jewel of the Pacific Northwest and the undisputed flagship of the RTB season. This is where the energy is highest, the crowds are loudest, and the competition is at its peak. Whether you’re taking on the endurance test of the Olympic, the high-speed Sprint, or the explosive Super Sprint, this is the race where you show the world what you’re made of.

Round up your crew for our Sprint & Olympic Relays, or fly solo to claim your glory.

The Perks of the Podium
Every athlete who crosses the line earns a finisher medal, but we’ve got something extra for the front-runners. We’re awarding custom pint glasses to:

Sprint & Olympic: Top 5 in each age group.
Super Sprint: Top 3 in each age group.

Don’t miss out on the swag: Register on or before August 1st to guarantee your official race T-shirt. After you crush your finish, stick around for the post-race meal, the celebration, and the awards ceremony. Lake Meridian Park is the ultimate spectator-friendly venue, so bring the family—there’s plenty of room for the kids to play while they cheer you toward the finish.

 
Complete the Journey: Earn The Trident
One race is a challenge. Three races is a legacy.

To honor the athletes who grind with us all summer long, we’ve created The Trident. This isn’t just another medal—it’s a custom-crafted, heavy-duty trophy designed to recognize pure grit and consistency.

To claim the steel and the glory, you must complete the journey through all three iconic 2026 RTB stages:

  1. Black Diamond Triathlon (The Opener)
  2. Lake Meridian Triathlon (The Big Stage)
  3. Bonney Lake Triathlon (The Grand Finale)

When you cross that final finish line at Bonney Lake, the Trifecta Trident will be placed in your hands—the ultimate symbol of a season well-fought.

 
The Grand Finale: Bonney Lake
While Lake Meridian is our biggest party, Bonney Lake is the perfect ending. We’ve revitalized this classic course with the RTB standard of excellence to give your season the finish it deserves.

A Pristine Course: Dive into the clear waters of Lake Tapps, hammer through the rolling farmlands of Pierce County, and finish your run under the watchful gaze of Mount Rainier.
The RTB Vibe: Expect a seamless experience from packet pickup to the final celebration. We’re turning up the volume to make sure your 2026 season ends with a roar.

One Season. Three Races. One Legendary Trophy. The bar has been raised. Complete the journey at Lake Meridian to keep the dream alive, then lock in your spot at the finale to claim your Trident.

name: Lampson Cable Bridge Run
description:
This year marks the 48th annual running of the Lampson Cable Bridge Run! Finisher Medals will be given out to the first 2200 participants who finish the run. To receive your medal please ensure that your race bib is visible as you cross the finish line. So tell your friends and come out and enjoy this fun and exciting holiday tradition! Runners, no matter the distance they choose (5K or 10K) will start their race crossing over the Columbia River from Kennewick to Pasco, WA on the scenic Cable Bridge. The 1-Mile runners will end shortly after crossing the bridge and be shuttled to the 5K/10K finish area. The 5K & 10K finish line is located at the Lampson warehouse. At the finish line you will receive your medal and refreshments before proceeding to catch the shuttle bus back to the fairground's parking lot. 

There is a discounted, non-timed 1-Mile Fun Run category for those that want to experience the fun and excitement of this yearly event, and still receive the finisher medal. Also there is a Kids 4 & Under category that is free of charge. Participants in this category will receive their own special bib but will not be timed nor receive a finisher medal, instead they will receive a child's finisher ribbon.

For all timed race categories, timing chips are used and awards are given to the top participants in each age category. So if you are a competitive runner or someone who just wants to have fun walking with your friends, the Lampson Cable Bridge Run has what you are looking for.

name: Langlauf 10K XC Ski Race
description:
Langlauf is a 10K Cross Country Ski Race that takes place at the Mount Spokane Nordic Ski Center which is the premier Cross Country Ski Area in the Inland Northwest.  The race takes place on the traditional 10K course and has wave starts to accommodate skiers of all abilities and speeds.  Even maybe more epic than the race itself, are the pre and post race amenities that are enjoyed by all racers.  This is the biggest and oldest Cross Country Race in the Pacific Northwest...you don't want to miss it!

Once again, this year we are offering an adaptive skier category. If you are visually impaired or a sit skier you will be able to participate in our Wave start, but at Junction 1 will continue on Linder Road to a turnaround at the Inland gate then back to Brian's and our traditional finish line. Adaptive skiers must register but their guide skier can accompany them for no cost. Guides will need to sign a waiver the morning of the race and do not need to pay to register unless they want to be timed. Guides will be considered a volunteer and be entered in the prize drawing.

name: Last Chance Marathon and Half Marathon
description:
OK, here is your Last Chance to run a 1/2 marathon or full marathon this year! The 1/2 marathon course is an out and back and the full marathon course is the same out and back course two times, starting at Fairhaven Park Pavillion, running the Interurban trail out to Clayton Beach for the full 13.1 miles or 26.2. Course is subject to change if trail conditions mandate.

 

This trail has spectacular views and very few hills, just enough hills to make it interesting, and break up the flat sections. FYI: We have been known to have SNOW this time of the year so plan accordingly. The majority of this trail is covered with a canopy of trees which deflects some of the rain or snow, but this also means it doesn’t heat as fast as an open course would. It can get cold. The majority of the trail is an old railroad bed, very easy to run on gravel surface, with the exception of Arroyos Park. Arroyos Park is a double track trail with a few bridges and a few fun hills. It is a very well maintained set of trails.

 

The bathrooms at Fairhaven Park will be unlocked as well as the warm heated Pavillion.

 

You should plan on being self-sufficient and carrying your own water and aid. The 1st aid station on the course is ~ 3.5 miles into the race off Chuckanut Crest Drive. In the 1/2 marathon you will run by this aid station twice, and 4 times in the full marathon.  There will be an aid station at the turn around which you will access once in the 1/2 marathon and twice in the full marathon. We will also have an aid station at the start/finish so full 1/2 marathoners will have 3 chances to refill their water bottles, about every 3 to 3.5 miles, & marathoners will have 7 chances to refill their water bottles.  We will have water, an electrolyte drink and other snacks at the aid stations.  Usually I put some type of candy like candy corn, gummy bears, bananas, pretzels, typical ultra style foods. You won’t go hungry!
Keep an eye on the website for any changes to the event. Finishers will receive a Last Chance coin/medal similar to the quality of the Woolley Runs coin.  We will provide food at the end like all the NW Ultra Events.  While all your friends are recovering from their hang over and resting up before the evening’s festivities, you’ll be burning calories and ready to PARTY hardy knowing you’ve already burned off that extra beer or two, or three.

name: Last Splash of Summer
description:
Last Splash of Summer is a family event! We have events for adults and kids. 
 
HIGHLIGHTS:
  • 500-yard races for adults and kids, registration fee $35.00
  • Want to wear fins? You can in the 500-yard or 1-mile events designated FIN
  • Lake temperatures are expected to be in the mid 60's
  • This year's giveaway is a large swim buoy 
PLACE: Lake Meridian 14800 SE 272nd St Kent, WA 98042

REGISTRATION: 

Early Bird Registration Friday, May 1st - Friday, May 15th $65.00
Regular Registration Saturday, May 16gh - Thursday, September 17th $75.00
Day of Race Registration, Saturday, September 19th $85.00
500 Yard Swim Friday, May 1st - September 17th $35.00

EVENTS:
  • 500 Yards Wetsuit / No-Wetsuit
  • 500 Yards Wetsuit FIN / No-Wetsuit FIN
  • 1 Mile Wetsuit / No-Wetsuit
  • 1 Mile Wetsuit FIN / No-Wetsuit FIN
  • 2 Mile Wetsuit / No-Wetsuit

PARENTAL GUARDIAN: Those 18 and under must be supervised by a parent or guardian and approval of parent or guardian supplied with entry. 

RULES: Last Splash of Summer is not a USMS sanctioned event. We will follow the open water rules of USMS. The use of neoprene wetsuits and other nonporous attire is allowed in the wetsuit events. Fins are allowed in the 500-yard FIN and 1 mile FIN events. Fins must be no longer than 12" and no mono fins allowed. Pull buoys, snorkels, mp3 players are examples of items that are not allowed. 

10 and unders MUST swim the 500 yards

10 - 12 year olds that want to swim the mile need to submit the name of their coach and swim club as well as submit records (proof) they have swum a 500 in a USA swim meet in a time of 7:30 or faster including the name of the meet and date. Photo of results would be great. Please send information to Wendy Neely at wendy@bluewave-aquatics.com. 

AGE GROUPS:  12 & under, 13-14, 15 & Over, 18-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80-84, 85-89, etc.)
Ages determined by date of birth as of December 31st.
 
TIMELINE:
  • 7:30 AM     Registration Check-In 
  • 8:30 AM     Mandatory Safety Meeting
  • 9:00 AM     Event Start: 2 Mile
  • 9:10 AM     Event Start: 1 Mile
  • 9:20 AM     Event Start: 1 Mile FIN
  • Event Start: 500 Yards - usually when the course is cleared
 
RACE INSURANCE: Race / Event insurance is available for purchase during registration from REGShield. If you are interested, please read the information provided to understand what is covered and what is not covered. Any claims should be directed to REGShield. Blue Wave Aquatics is not affiliated with REGShield. 

MERCHANDISE: Fleece Pullover Hoodies are available for purchase during registration. X-SM, SM, MD, LG, X-LG $50.00, 2-XL, 3-XL $55.00 PLEASE NOTE: We will be closing the sweatshirt order on Sunday, August 30th. 

REFUNDS: Open water registrations are non-refundable and non-transferable.

name: Liberty Christian XC Fundraiser Run
description:
Join the excitement at our COLOR RUN! Gather your family or friends for a vibrant and unforgettable experience. Whether you prefer to walk, jog, dance, or run the Patriot's 5k or Liberty Loop, this event promises a BLAST of color and fun.

No running experience needed - just come ready to enjoy yourself and support the cross country team! Every participant helps contribute to the team's season. 

Finish the course in a spectacular cloud of color and create an incredible, joy-filled day you'll never forget!

 

Date:

RACE - Saturday, August 29th, 2026

 

Start Times:

8:00am - Bib pick and in-person registration 

8:30am - Patriot's 5k starts

8:35am  - Liberty Loop starts

 

Start Location: 

The race will start and finish at Liberty Christian School

(at the corner of Acacia Ave & Sacramento Blvd.)

 

Prices:

Patriot's 5k  -  $20  [registration on the day of the race will be $25]

Liberty Loop - $10  [registration on the day of the race will be $15]

 

After the race there will be an electrolyte drink, ice water and cold treats! Get your cameras ready to capture this hilarious & colorful run!   Sunglasses recommended; wear a white shirt for the colors to show up better

 

Awards:

Each finisher will receive a medal. Overall top finishers 1st, 2nd, 3rd Male & Female for the 5k will receive a special award. This race will not be officially chipped timed.

name: LIBERTY LAKE LOOP
description:
The Liberty Lake Loop is back - just at a new location.  Join us at Orchard Park in Liberty Lake for:

  • 5K Timed Running Race for ages 13+ (start and end at Orchard Park and along Centennial Trail and East Indiana Avenue)
  • Half Mile Kids Race - Ages 6-9 (1 lap around the park)
  • One Mile Kids Race - Ages 10-12 (2 laps around the park)

Medals for Top 3 finishers for Men & Women and Boys & Girls in each of the races.  

Registration price includes $16 for t-shirt (through June 25th). 5K race is $25 without shirt; kids races are $20 without shirt.  Select 'No Shirt' during registration, and the registration price will be reduced accordingly.

Sponsored by and all proceeds benefit Valley Flash Running Club.

name: Lookin For A Cure Seattle
description:
"We're "Lookin' For a Cure" in scenic Warren G Magnesun Park! Join A Cure In Sight on Saturday July 25th, 2026 from 8AM-11AM, to walk or run with us. We will be taking steps to find a cure for a rare eye cancer, Ocular Melanoma. Ocular Melanoma is estimated by the American Cancer Society to have roughly 3000 new cases each year nationwide. Bring your friends and family to the race day--all ages welcome to walk or run with us.

Register, become a fund raiser, make a team, grab your friends and family and raise money to support local research with Dr. Stacey and Fred Hutch Cancer Center.  Prizes will be awarded for largest team, largest fundraiser as well as top finishers.

Race Swag

  • Guarantee t-shirt if registered by June 29th.
  • Finisher Medal
  • Food & Drink
  • Aid Station
  • Commemorative Race Bib
  • Free downloadable photos
  • Official finishers time with age group placements

Race day schedule

  • Registration 8AM
  • Race start 9AM
  • Announcements Awards 10AM

Parking

Free parking past the boat launch area, just steps from the start line. If you have an issue on race day, please call 919-885-5264 for directions.

name: Maple Valley Bear Run & Walk 5K
description:
REGISTRATION NOW OPEN!!


$35 for adults; kids 12 and under are FREE, thanks to our sponsors, when you register online by May 31st (a small handling fee will apply for all registrations).  Participants 8 years old and younger must register with and be accompanied by an adult or participant 13 years or older.  

 

SCHEDULE FOR RACE DAY, 6/27/2026

7:30am - 8:30am   Packet pick up and day-of registration*
9:00am                  5K race starts
10:00am                Awards
*Day-of registration (until 8:30am) using your personal mobile device, then come pick up your bib from us! No on-site payments will be accepted.

 

RACE COURSE

5K Run/Walk Race Course map
 

PARKING

Parking will be available at Lake Wilderness Park. We highly encourage carpooling with others. Arrive early so you have enough time before race start!
Please see attached map for specifics. Parking and Race Day Map

 

PRE-RACE PACKET PICK UP

Pre-race packet pick up will be offered at Road Runner Sports in Kent, June 25, 2026 from 4-7pm.  Come and get your race bib and t-shirt* before the race.  Grab all of your race day needs when you come in to grab your race bib!  
*T-shirts only guaranteed for those who register by May 31st.
 

CHIP TIMING

Chip timing will be provided by Tortoise and Hare Timing. Disposable chips will be placed on back of bib numbers. 

 

AWARDS 

Awards for male and female categories.  Age Group Awards will be given based on Chip Time.  Must be present to receive Award

1st place in each age division wins the coveted Bear Run Bear! 
2nd-3rd place in each age division receive Bear Run Bells
Special awards for top 3 overall men and women will be based on gun time.

 

RACE RESULTS

Official race results will be posted on our website and online at Tortoise & Hare Timing.  Results will be based on chip time (crossing start line to crossing finish line).

 

STROLLERS, DOGS & WATER

We encourage the use of jogging strollers along the trails of this family-friendly 5K!  Out of consideration for other participants, dogs will not be allowed on the course (with the exception of service dogs). We do offer water at the end of the race.

 

GIVING BACK TO THE COMMUNITY 

Proceeds from the Bear Run will benefit Tahoma High School distance running programs administered by the Tahoma Cross Country Running Club.  The funds fill a wide range of needs for our large team of athletes including support for athletes and families who need help with team participation and summer camp fees, multiple scholarships awarded each year, and travel expenses beyond that available from the school district budget.  These kids work hard and run hard all year while maintaining exceptional grade point averages.  They deserve our support!

 

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION

Send email to Katie Leh at mvbearrunwalk@gmail.com

name: March for the Fallen 2026
description:
Registration Opens Memorial Day Weekend, 2026! 

Choose from a timed 5, 10 or 15.6k ruck, run or walk. 

Ruckers, runners, walkers, kids and leashed dogs are welcome! 

  • Event tees
  • Ruck patches
  • BBQ
  • Historic Military Vehicles
  • Lawn games
  • Special pricing for kids 12 & under

Please note, this event takes place in Riverside State Park and a Discover Pass is REQUIRED in the Park and will be enforced. 

​March for the Fallen is part of the WA State Fallen Heroes Project, a 501c3 with EIN 46-2481053, dedicated to honoring and remembering fallen military members, supporting their families, and engaging our communities in doing both. Thank you for your support!

name: MCCM Monster Mash 5k & Creature Crawl 1k
description:
🎃 4th Annual Monster Mash 5K & Creature Crawl 1K 👾


Save the Date: October 24, 2026
Join the Mid-Columbia Children's Museum for Monster Mash 5K & Creature Crawl 1K, a family-friendly Halloween event that brings together costumes, movement, and hands-on fun in support of the future Mid-Columbia Children's Museum.
Whether you're running the 5K, walking with friends, or cheering on your little monster in the Creature Crawl, there's something for everyone.
Event Details
📅 Saturday, October 24, 2026
📍 Howard Amon Park | Richland, WA
What to Expect
🎃 Costume-friendly 5K run/walk
👾 Creature Crawl 1K for kids and families
🔬 STEM-inspired activities
🍂 Family-friendly fall fun
❤️ Support for the future Mid-Columbia Children's Museum
Registration Coming Soon
Registration will open later this summer. For now, save the date, spread the word, and start thinking about your costume!
We look forward to celebrating another year of community, creativity, curiosity, and fun with you.
Sponsorship Opportunities
Interested in reaching local families while supporting hands-on learning in our community? Sponsorship opportunities for the 2026 Monster Mash 5K & Creature Crawl 1K are now available.
To learn more about sponsorship levels and benefits, please contact fundraising@mccmuseum.org.

🔬 STEM-inspired activities
🍂 Family-friendly fall fun
❤️ Support for the future Mid-Columbia Children's Museum
Registration Coming Soon
Registration will open later this summer. For now, save the date, spread the word, and start thinking about your costume!
We look forward to celebrating another year of community, creativity, curiosity, and fun with you.
Sponsorship Opportunities
Interested in reaching local families while supporting hands-on learning in our community? Sponsorship opportunities for the 2026 Monster Mash 5K & Creature Crawl 1K are now available.
To learn more about sponsorship levels and benefits, please contact fundraising@mccmuseum.org.

name: Medical Lake- Trailblazer Triathlon/Duathlon/5K
description:
The Medical Lake Trailblazer Tri/Du/5k is one of the many things to do in Medical Lake on Founders Day weekend. This is an athlete-friendly race with a point-to-point open water swim, bike, and run on paved roads & trails.

Trailblazer Triathlon
A 350m swim, 12.2mi bike ride, and 2.92 mi run starting and ending at Waterfront Park. 

Trailblazer Duathlon
A 1mi run, 12.2mi bike ride, and 2.92 mi run starting and ending at Waterfront Park. 

Trailblazer 5k
A traditional 2.92 mi run around Medical Lake Trail starting and ending at Waterfront Park.

name: Metaline Falls Bigfoot 5K Race & LittleFoot Kids Run
description:
Bigfoot 5k Race - Saturday, June 20, 2026 at 8:00am

Join us at our 6th Annual Bigfoot 5k Race in beautiful Metaline Falls, WA on Saturday, June 20th at 8:00am! The course will take you from downtown Metaline Falls, up and down Lehigh Hill with gorgeous mountain views, past the historic Cutter Theatre, along the beautiful Pend Oreille river, and finish at the town's Busta Park.

After the event, join in at the fun festivities of the Metaline Falls Bigfoot Festival! There will be vendors, food, and entertainment!

A virtual race option is also available and swag will be mailed to you after the race!

Registration fee includes:

name: Miles for Meso 5K Run/Walk
description:
The Miles for Meso WA Memorial 5K Run/Walk will return for its eleventh year to the scenic Federal Way, Washington, on July 4. This event is held in memory of Dick Dyhrman, a geologist with Weyerhaeuser Company; Bud Hatley, Federal Way School District Athletic Director; Bob Stewart, Federal Way High School teacher and coach; and other Washington residents who have lost their lives to mesothelioma.

The mission of this event is to raise awareness for mesothelioma, a fatal cancer caused by asbestos exposure. This year, organizers aim to raise $20,000 through registration fees and donations, with all proceeds benefiting the Mesothelioma Applied Research Foundation. The 5K course will take participants along the BPA Trail and through Celebration Park, offering stunning views of Mount Rainier.

Important Race Day Information:

  • Road closures begin at 8:30 AM.
  • The Run/Walk will be open for 1.5 hours. Participants are welcome to continue after this time; however, please note that roads will reopen.
  • There will be NO access out of the parking lot until 10:30 AM. If you need to leave earlier, you will need to park at Celebration Park or at City Hall and use 334th street to exit towards 6th ave.  Access from the event lot will be restricted.
  • The Awards Ceremony and Silent Auction will commence at 10:45 AM.

To guarantee a shirt and size, please register by June 15th.

For more details, including a course map and additional race information, please visit-

https://itallhappenshere.org/event/miles-for-meso-5k/

description:
Join Clark Roberts and get pledges for your Kindness Miles throughout the month of August, run, bike, walk or roll (or swim, golf, have a lemonade stand, roller skate, etc.) to raise awareness and Kindness, One Mile & One Smile at a Time all while promoting Community, Kindness, Compassion, and Fun!!

We thank you for partnering with us as we transform the lives of children for generations to come!

name: Millwood Daze 5k
description:
Discount Pricing for Youth!

We want our Active for Youth participants - $8 for <13 years

Middle and High School XC runners - this is a fast 5k 2 days before practice begins for your school team - $10 <17 years

Community celebration 5k favorite!   From it's tree-lined start in historic Millwood, its a flat, fast loop course great for runners and walkers.  Join us for the Millwood Daze celebration after the run with a pancake breakfast, street fair with community booths, and a classic car show.  The Pancake Breakfast is FREE with your 5k registration!

Tee shirts available for purchase all registrants, during the registration process.  Register and Order by 8/12 to have tee shirt by race day.  After that, tee shirt price may increase and pick up or delivery will be arranged.

name: Mimosa 5K
description:
Join us for a fun summer run/walk through beautiful Downtown Puyallup!
Participants will run or walk along sidewalks and through one of Puyallup’s vibrant neighborhoods, taking in the charm and local flavor along the way.
The event will start and finish at the Lazy Ballerina Wine Bar,
📍 319 S Meridian, Puyallup, WA 98371

After you cross the finish line, stick around and enjoy amazing mimosas and Sunday brunch at the Lazy Ballerina. Looking for a more family-friendly post-race option? Head just up the street to our fantastic partners at Firemind Brewing and CaskCades, where everyone can continue the fun.

Whether you’re running, walking, or strolling, this is the perfect way to kick off a summer Sunday! ☀️👟🍾

Registration includes custom medal, custom race bib and race day snacks.

name: MLK Jr. Freedom Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
Join in our annual Martin Luther King Jr. Day Run! Today, we gather to honor the legacy of Dr. King and his enduring commitment to justice, equality, and peace. As we lace up our shoes and hit the pavement, let’s reflect on his powerful message of love and resilience.
This event is not just about fitness; it’s a celebration of community, a call to action for social change, and a reminder of the work still to be done. Together, we can honor Dr. King’s dream and inspire one another to continue striving for a better world. Let’s run with purpose and passion! 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: Move Puyallup 5K
description:
Join us on Saturday, August 15th for the FREE “Move Puyallup” 5K in partnership with the City of Puyallup Parks & Recreation! Gather your friends, family, co-workers, and neighbors and enjoy a fun and active morning along the scenic Puyallup Riverwalk Trail starting near Fred Meyer.

This chip timed, family-friendly event welcomes runners and walkers of all ages and abilities. Whether you are chasing a personal best, enjoying a morning walk with friends, or introducing your family to a healthy and active lifestyle, the “Move Puyallup” 5K is the perfect community event. The paved Riverwalk Trail offers a beautiful and welcoming course for everyone to enjoy.

This FREE event is open to the entire community, so lace up your shoes and come enjoy fresh air, movement, community spirit, and a great morning on the trail. Let’s Move Puyallup together!

Please NO dogs!  We love our furry friends but for their safety and the safety of your fellow runners and walkers, please leave your pets at home.  In addition, our insurance does not cover dogs.  

Absolutely NO scooters, roller blades, and/or any wheeled items.  Strollers are welcome.

Check In:  8:00 AM

Event Begins:  9:00 AM

name: Mt. Spokane Trail Run
description: Experience the rugged beauty of Mt. Spokane State Park with three distance options featuring lush singletrack, challenging climbs, and sweeping summit views. All courses start and finish at Selkirk Lodge, delivering a true mountain trail adventure in a stunning alpine setting.

name: Mud Mountain Trail Fest
description:
Join us on Saturday, July 11th at the breathtaking Mud Mountain Dam in Enumclaw, Washington for an unforgettable trail running experience in the heart of the Pacific Northwest.

Choose between the 4 Miler or the 10K and take on a moderately challenging course that winds through the scenic Mud Mountain trail system. You’ll navigate forested paths surrounded by towering evergreens, crisp mountain air, and stunning natural views at every turn.

This race is the perfect blend of adventure and challenge—designed for those ready to test their endurance, embrace the terrain, and experience the raw beauty of true trail running.

Come ready to push yourself, connect with nature, and enjoy every step of the journey.

The Night Nation Run is the World’s first Running Music Festival the ultimate blend of a Music Festival and a Fun Run. Experience a music filled course with Live DJs, Bubble Zones, Light Shows, Neon, and Black Lights! Cross the finish line into an Epic Main Stage After Party featuring Top Headliner DJs!

To date, over 2 MILLION people across the World have become a member of the Night Nation™!

The Night Nation Run is proud to support Stand Up To Cancer (SU2C) as their official charity. Stand Up To Cancer (SU2C) is a groundbreaking initiative created to accelerate innovative cancer research that will get new therapies to patients quickly and save lives now.

Celebrate Life. Celebrate friends and family. Celebrate Music. Run with the Night Nation™!

REGISTRATION INCLUDES:

  • Night Nation T-shirt (Premium & VIP Registration)
  • Race Bib
  • Glow Necklace
  • Free Giveaways
  • Pre and Post Race Concerts
  • Admission into the Night Nation after party
  • The best night of your life!

name: Ninja 5K, 10K & 13.1M at Everett, WA (31)
description:
Please note that our race location has changed.

We will now be at McCollum Park Athletic Field instead of Langus Riverfront Park.

 

Race Information
The race starts at 8:30 AM.
Packet pickup starts 30 minutes before the race and ends 10 minutes before the race starts.
All runners must register on RunSignup. 
No on-site registration.

Additional Information
Park at the North Creek Trail.

5K & 10K Course (0.78M)
https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6634249787 
The course is an out-and-back (1.56M)
The 5K does the out-and-back two times.
The 10K does the out-and-back four times.

Half Marathon Course (1.09M)
https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6634249965

Half Marathon does the course six times. 

Course Time Limit
3 hours and 30 minutes.

description:

name: North Bend Trail Fest 30k - 10k
description:
Get ready for the ultimate test of strength and endurance at the North Bend Trail Fest. This thrilling event features two incredible mountain running races that will leave you breathless.

First up, we have the Vert Running Series Championship - North Bend Skyline 30k. Prepare to push your limits as you conquer a challenging 6600 feet of vert and three magnificent peaks. The top man and woman will even earn a coveted spot in the prestigious Broken Arrow 23k race.

If you're looking for a slightly shorter yet equally exhilarating challenge, look no further than the Mt Si 10k. With breathtaking views of Snoqualmie Valley from the Little Si summit, this race promises to test your endurance while rewarding you with stunning vistas.

But it doesn't end there! The North Bend Trail Fest is more than just a race. It's a full-blown mountain adventure festival! Immerse yourself in an atmosphere of excitement, camaraderie, and celebration as you mingle with fellow athletes, explore vendor booths, groove to live music, and indulge in delicious local food.

name: OAT Run
description:
* 50K * Half Marathon * 12K *

The Olympic Adventure Trail Run (OAT Run) is a point-to-point trail 12K and half marathon as well as an out-and-back 50K that traverses Kelly Ridge between the Olympic National Park and the Strait of Juan de Fuca in Washington State, all on single-track trail.  Limit 130 runners per distance.

The OAT Run Experience

OAT Run is for trail runners who enjoy lush green forests filled with moss and ferns, towering evergreens, and spring trailside flowers. Runners will get a stunning view of the Elwha River Valley as they run by the “Living Room”. And if this wasn’t epic enough, get ready to eat, drink, and relax post-race with an amazing view of the Olympic Mountains. The after-party at Extreme Sports Park is a fun atmosphere, and racers will get hot burritos from Little Devil's Lunchbox and cold drinks, a toasty campfire, and door prizes (woot!). There will be a beer garden at the after-party as well, with proceeds to support 4PA, a local non-profit organization. 

What’s included?

In addition to an epic outdoor experience in the far northwest corner, all runners receive a professional well-organized event, a well-marked course, hydration and snacks at water stations along the course, a great piece of custom race swag, shuttle to start (and return shuttle back to parking area / party), chip timing, race photos, and after-party at Extreme Sports Park including a hot meal and a chance to win great door prizes from our local retailers. 

Bring cash or card as there will be a beer garden at the finish line, hosted by and benefitting local non-profit organization 4PA. 

This race sells out every year, so don't delay registering!

Giving Back

This race is a friendly, community-based event, and a portion of race proceeds is donated to the Peninsula Trails Coalition (Olympic Discovery Trail) and the Peninsula Chapter of the Back Country Horsemen of Washington, in appreciation for their countless hours of trail construction and maintenance on the North Olympic Peninsula.

Where to stay
Olympic Lodge in Port Angeles is offering a special 25% off discount for OAT Runners.
Booking link here. 
Or phone direct at 360-452-2993 and use booking code OAT to receive the same discounted pricing.

REFUND POLICY:
  • 50% refund available until March 15, NO REFUNDS AFTER THIS DATE. No deferrals to another race or next year's race.
  • You will have the choice during the registration process to buy cancellation insurance (unavailable for Canadian racers 
     - rules of the insurance company and not us or RunSignUp). With the insurance, you will get a full refund in certain circumstances including accident, illness and family emergency, even after the March 15th date. Here are details and FAQ about the RegShield insurance.
  • Transfers are allowed until 3 days before the race  Transfer instructions.
  • No deferrals
  • If we are forced to cancel for any reason, runners will get a free transfer to the next year, or an 80% refund

name: OCRA Rivkin Family SummeRun
description:
The Ovarian Cancer Research Alliance Rivkin Family SummeRun was started by Dr. Saul Rivkin, founder of the Rivkin Center for Ovarian Cancer Research, and his five daughters after the loss of his wife and the girls' mother, Marsha Rivkin. The Rivkin organization is now part of OCRA, and we’re proud to continue this beloved event, which has become one of the largest private funders of ovarian cancer research in the country.

Because of the hard work of SummeRun Team Captains and participants and many other generous donors, SummeRun has raised more than $10M for ovarian cancer research.

Funds raised through the SummeRun will benefit OCRA’s research programs, including the Rivkin Pilot Grants. OCRA is proud to continue the Rivkin Center’s extraordinary legacy of hope, determination, and relentless pursuit of a cure.

name: OktoberFeast
description:
Run, Walk, and Rally to End Senior Hunger with Mid-Columbia Meals on Wheels!

Join us Saturday, October 3 at 10 AM for our Oktoberfeast-themed 5K Fun Run & Walk along the beautiful Columbia River. Whether you’re racing for a personal best, strolling with friends, bringing the kids (and dogs!), or just showing up for the fun—this event is all about coming together for a cause that stays right here at home!

📍 Start & Finish: 2600 North Columbia Center Boulevard
(Parking near New Vintage Church)

 
Everyone Is Welcome
Runners, walkers, strollers, wheelchair users, kids, teams, and dogs are all encouraged to join.
And yes… costumes are highly encouraged too! 🎉

 
Make Your Miles Matter
New this year: every participant is a fundraiser—but it’s totally flexible.

When you register, you’ll automatically get your own fundraising page where friends, family, and coworkers can support your 5K.

Fundraise as much or as little as you’d like
No minimum required—your registration is enough to participate
Want to go all in? Form a team or even create a page for your dog 

Can't come in person? Or not interested in racing? Consider selecting our virtual 5K option to still help support our cause to outrun Senior hunger!

Every dollar raised stays right here in our community for Mid-Columbia Meals on Wheels, helping ensure local seniors have access to nutritious meals and meaningful connection.

 
Join the Fun (and Friendly Competition!)

  • Top Fundraiser Award
  • Largest Team Prize
  • Costume Contest (people and pups!)
  • Timed race option with prizes

Free Community After-Party

The finish line is just the beginning!

Stick around for a free OktoberFeast-style celebration open to everyone—even if you didn’t participate in the race.

  • Food & refreshments
  • Live music
  • Beer garden
  • Family activities
  • Kid Zone
  • Dog Zone
  • And more!

📍 Located at the Mid-Columbia Meals on Wheels campus (right by end the end of the race)
      Festivities continue until 2 PM

 
Registration Details
     Online registration open until the night before
     Day-of registration available on-site
     Register by September 9 to guarantee your event t-shirt (Later registrations will receive shirts after the event)
     Virtual Racing option available 
 
Questions? donate@gencare.org

name: Oly Turkey Day 4 Miler
description:
OLY TURKEY DAY 4 MILER

Start your Thanksgiving morning with a fun and festive tradition at the Oly Turkey Day 4 Miler Run/Walk! Gather your family and friends and enjoy a great 4-mile course that’s perfect for runners and walkers of all levels. It’s a wonderful way to get moving before the holiday feast while celebrating community, health, and gratitude.

All participants will receive a chip-timed race bib, finisher medal, and after-race snacks. Registrants will also receive a custom Junk Brand headband with their registration. The headband guarantee date is Friday, October 3rd. Finisher medals are not guaranteed after October 6th.

Race shirts are available for purchase. The cutoff date to purchase a race shirt is Wednesday, October 22nd.

In the spirit of giving back during the holiday season, we ask participants to bring NEW adult and school-aged kids socks to donate to those in need in our community. Donations will be distributed through the Skoolie Foundation. Thank you in advance for your generosity and support.

Come celebrate Thanksgiving with movement, community, and gratitude at the Oly Turkey Day 4 Miler Run/Walk. We look forward to seeing you at the start line! 🦃🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️

Packet Pick Wednesday November 25th Location TBD

If you wish to pick up your event swag on Thanksgiving morning there will be a $20 service fee.

Absolutely NO dogs, scooters or bicycles.  Our insurance does not cover dogs and we want to protect our furry friends and your fellow runners/walkers.  Thank you for your cooperation!

name: Olympia Lakefair Races - Half Marathon, 8K & 3K
description:
2026 marks the 50th Anniversary of the Olympia Lakefair Races, which include the Jerry Miller Half Marathon, an 8K and a 3K including free entry for Kids 14 and under; taking runners on routes that circle around the town of Olympia and beyond into Tumwater and Thurston County.

Both the 3K and 8K start and finish on 5th Avenue in front of Heritage Park.  They both circle Capitol Lake, with the 8K continuing into Tumwater Historical Park before returning. Both are flat and fast courses. 

The Jerry Miller Half Marathon heads briefly through downtown Olympia, then along the Woodland Trial and Chehalis Western Trail biking paths.  The course continues on rural streets and a short trail and tour of Squaxin Park before heading back along East Bay Drive and running through downtown Olympia to the finish line in front of Heritage Park.  Runners will enjoy tree-lined trails and scenic landscapes while enjoying flat and narrow paved trails throughout.

Once runners have completed the course, there is an awards ceremony with several raffle awards as well as age group award up to 90+ for all three races.  Participants, family and friends can then enjoy festival activities that are held all around Heritage Park including food and beer tents, carnival rides, booths, a parade and more.  

The Valley Athletic Club is proud to be the 2026 Presenting Sponsor.  The Olympia Lakefair Races are brought to you by the Lake Run Organization and the Rotary Club of Olympia, and benefit local public High School Cross Country and Track programs and Rotary Club of Olympia Scholarship and Grant recipients.

See you July 18, 2026!

name: Olympia Mile and Festival
description:
The Olympia Mile and Festival

This is a fun 1 mile bike, run, walk down Capitol Blvd and finishing at Sylvester Park for the festival where people will have the opportunity to meet local groups, clubs and teams involved in different sporting activities. There is an option for a "competitive mile race" for runners who want to run fast and receive a time. 

 

The goal of the event is to highlight all of the wonderful clubs, groups, teams that Olympia has to offer that encourage physical activity and foster social connection. A portion of Capitol Blvd will be closed to traffic during the event. 
 
The event is free for all, but you must register to participate in the bike/run/walk. 
There will be food trucks, giveaways, great community and fun. 

 

Be sure to check back often for updates to the event. 

Tentative Schedule of Events

Bikes roll at 9:00 am
Runners start at 9:15 am
Walkers at 9:20 am
The road will be closed until 10:30 am. 
Festival in Sylvester Park from 9 am to 12 pm. 

 

If you are a club or a team interested in having a tent at Sylvester Park, email us at clubolyroadrunners@gmail.com.

name: One Step Closer
description:
What do you get when you take Orca Running and mix it with Evergreen Trail!? Welcome to One Step Closer. An exciting summer endurance event created by Orca Running AND Evergreen Trail Runs. Part whale, part trail-and loopy. Held in the one and only Lincoln Park, this race is going to be THE summer endurance event you won’t want to miss.

Course: Loops at Lincoln Park. Amazingly diverse for its size, this race experience has a bit of everything. Runners will take on a 2 mile course loop, and complete the loop as many times as they can during their selected time period: 18 hours, 12 hours, 6 hours, or 3 hours. All runners will finish together at 10:00pm with a finish line party! 

Check out all the details on our website!

NEW for 2026:

Battle of the run clubs: During registration, you will have the opportunity to be part of a “team.” Teams can consist of 2-5 members and The top 3 teams with the most loops at the end of the event will earn a special finishers plaque and ultimate run club (or friend group) bragging rights.

Kid's Loopy Race: Choose from 30 minutes or 1 hour. Kid’s will complete as many loops around the baseball field as they can within their selected time. Kids can take as many breaks as they choose, and the course will run through the snack station for treats as they go (just like the adults). All of the kids will finish together in a special One Step Closer kid’s race celebration. Each Kid’s Race runner will be awarded a One Step Closer medal upon completion.

name: OUTLAST SEATTLE
description:
What Is OUTLAST?

OUTLAST is a 6-hour trail endurance challenge where runners complete a 5K every hour, on the hour. Each lap must be finished within the hour to stay in the event. If you finish early, you rest until the next round. Miss a lap, and you’re out.

Complete all six rounds, and you OUTLAST.

This isn't just about speed — it's about pacing, discipline, and mental grit. Whether you're trying to survive all six or win your division, the challenge is the same: show up each hour, push your limits, and stay in it.

Each course is trail-based, with natural terrain, elevation, and unpredictable conditions. You’ll have time between rounds to recover, refuel, and refocus — but not much.

 

What You Earn:

​4 laps = “Grit Earned” patch
5 laps = “Survivor” patch
6 laps = Premium “OUTLAST” medal

​​All participants receive a premium OUTLAST Tee.

Top male and female with the fastest combined 5K times at each event win the 1st Place OUTLAST award. 

Finishers are ranked on the national leaderboard—and the fastest runner across all OUTLAST 6-hour events will be crowned National Champion and take home $1,000.

The 1st Place Male and Female 6-hour champions from each city will earn a spot in the Outlast Championship, where they’ll compete against the best of the best at the end of the Tour, and the 1st place male and female winners take home $1000 each. (This is separate from the national leaderboard prize money.)

By the end of the tour, the top 100 best times nationally will be invited to also compete in the Outlast Championship.

 

Frequently Asked Questions:

Do I have to run all 6 laps?
Nope. Run as many as you can. If you complete 4 or 5, you'll still earn a patch. Only those who finish all 6 get the OUTLAST medal and leaderboard ranking.

What happens if I don’t finish a lap in time?
You're out. The next lap starts at the top of the next hour, and only those who completed the last lap on time can continue.

How is the race timed?
Each 5K is timed individually. If you complete all 6, your combined time counts toward the local win and national leaderboard.

Are these trail races or road?
Every OUTLAST race is on trail terrain — dirt, rocks, roots, and elevation. Sometimes some pavement and gravel.

Can I walk?
Yes, as long as you finish the 5K within the hour. But some courses are rugged, and time can sneak up on you.

Are there aid stations?
Yes. There will be water, basic hydration, and snacks at the basecamp/loop start. This is a cupless event — bring your own bottle or hydration system.

What should I bring?
Trail shoes, hydration system, layers (weather dependent), fuel between laps, and grit.

Can I setup a tent?
Absolutely, bring your own aid station/tent setup.

Is OUTLAST for beginners?
Yes — if you're mentally tough. You don’t need to be fast, just consistent and ready to suffer a little.

How do I win?
If you finish all 6 laps and have the fastest combined time, you win your division (male/female). Winners are also added to the national leaderboard for a shot at the $1,000 national prize & title.

name: Pacific Runderland 5k & Kids Run
description:
Run, walk or skip for Washington’s national parks! The Pacific Runderland 5K & Kids 1k Run is a charity event hosted in partnership with Washington’s National Park Fund (WNPF), the official philanthropic partner of the three national parks in Washington state.

5k registration includes finisher's medal, t-shirt, collective bib and free race photo downloads. Kids 1k registration includes finisher's ribbon and collective bib. Unfortunately, due to declining participation in the Virtual event and rising costs of shipping, there willl not be a Virtual option in 2026. Thank you for understanding.

5k course is USATF Certified (WA22015RMB).

Organized solely by volunteers, Pacific Runderland donates all race proceeds to WNPF. We have donated over $40,000 to help support our state’s most beautiful parks since 2019. The event is also in honor and memory of the race organizer’s late father, a runner and national park fanatic, who passed away from early-onset Alzheimer’s in 2012. Join us in Auburn, Washington at Roegner Park for the 5K run/walk and kids 1K run.

name: Palouse to Cascades Marathon+ Relay
description:
Experience One of Washington's Most Unique Trail Relay Races

Gather your team and embark on an unforgettable adventure through the heart of Central Washington. The Palouse to Cascades Marathon+ Relay takes runners along the historic Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail, offering a one-of-a-kind relay race experience through scenic landscapes, charming small towns, railroad trestles, tunnels, and breathtaking backcountry terrain.

Whether you're competing with a team of friends, family members, or coworkers—or challenging yourself as a solo runner—this event combines endurance, teamwork, and outdoor adventure in one incredible day.

Why You'll Love This Race

  • Run along the historic Milwaukee Road railroad corridor
  • Experience stunning views of Kittitas County and Central Washington
  • Cross iconic trestles and travel through scenic trail sections
  • Choose from relay team or solo challenge options
  • Perfect for runners seeking a unique trail running experience
  • Enjoy the camaraderie and excitement of a relay race format

As highlighted in the Financial Times article "The Rise of the Relay Marathon," relay races combine some of today's fastest-growing fitness trends: trail running, endurance challenges, team competition, and outdoor adventure. This is your opportunity to experience it firsthand in one of Washington State's most beautiful running destinations.

 
Relay & Solo Race Options

Four-Person Relay Teams
Form a team of four runners and divide the course into manageable relay segments. Male, female, and co-ed teams are welcome.

Two-Person Relay Teams

Take on a greater challenge by splitting the course between two runners. Male, female, and co-ed divisions are available.

Solo Challenge

Ready to test your limits? Register as a solo participant and complete the entire course yourself.

name: PAPER MAKER OCR
description:
Join us for the 5th Annual Paper Maker OCR!


This hometown obstacle course race brings together athletes, families, and friends from across the PNW for a morning of challenge, laughter, and teamwork — all surrounded by the scenic forest trails and natural terrain of Lacamas Lake Regional Park.

Whether you’re a returning racer or trying OCR for the first time, expect natural-style obstacles, new features to celebrate our fifth year, and a shared spirit of grit, community, and adventure.

 
Course Details

Distance: 4+ miles
Obstacles: 10+ challenges designed to test full-body strength, endurance, agility, and determination.
Terrain: Packed dirt trails, rocky paths, shaded forest corridors, and natural elevation shifts through Lacamas Lake Regional Park. Runners will encounter tree-rooted trails, rolling hills, and a few water crossings.
Obstacle Style: Expect crawls, carries, balance tests, tree hurdles, and log jumps — built right into the natural terrain. Bypass options are available for those needing to modify or skip safely. Please bring your own hydration for the trail. What you pack in, pack out. There are No Water Stations on the Course. 
 
New This Year — The Paper Makers Kiddo Race!
To celebrate our 5th anniversary, we’re excited to introduce the Paper Makers Kiddo Race — a short, fun, and safe obstacle course designed just for our youngest athletes! A signature wall to sign after your accomplishment! New obstacles, and always an updated course. 

Food Partner: Shorty’s Bar-B-Q
We are excited to welcome Shorty’s Bar-B-Q as the official food partner for the 5th Annual Paper Maker OCR!

After conquering the trails, obstacles, creek crossings, and waterfall climbs, racers, volunteers, and spectators can enjoy delicious slow-smoked barbecue just steps away from the festival area. Located within walking distance of the event festivities, Shorty’s Bar-B-Q will be serving up their crowd-favorite smoked meats and classic BBQ flavors throughout race day.

Whether you're celebrating a podium finish, cheering on family and friends, or simply refueling after an epic morning on the course, make sure to stop by and support this fantastic local business.

Come race hard, then reward yourself with some amazing barbecue!

Thank you to Shorty’s Bar-B-Q for helping make the 5th Annual Paper Maker OCR an unforgettable experience.

Details:

Ages: 4 – 10 years old
Start Time: ~ 9:00 AM (heats every 5 minutes)
Course: A short loop featuring mini obstacles like low crawls, small hurdles, and balance challenges — perfect for introducing kids to the OCR spirit.
Parent Supervision: Required — parents can run alongside or cheer from the sidelines.
Finish Reward: Each kiddo will earn their very own Paper Maker Kiddo Race Shirt to celebrate their accomplishment!
The perfect way for little racers to get muddy, have fun, and feel like true Paper Makers!

 Race Day Schedule
Check-In Opens: 8:00 AM
Kids Race: ~ 9:00 AM (heats every 5 min)
Main OCR Heats Begin: 9:30 AM for all adult and team participants

Competitive Wave
Open Community Wave -

Trail run it if you don't want to do the obstacles ( open racers only, although we really want you to do the obstacles )

All heats will launch from the start line located on the backside of the festival and registration area, with clear signage and volunteers directing racers.

Competitive Division & Prizes Are you ready to race for the podium? The Competitive Wave is where grit meets precision — and this year, we’re upping the stakes!

Top Two Male Racers — Cash Prizes Awarded
Top Two Female Racers — Cash Prizes Awarded


Rules & Standards:

Competitive racers must complete all obstacles to standard and finish the entire 4+-mile course to qualify for prizes.
Failure to complete any obstacle or mandatory standard will result in disqualification from prize eligibility.
Final results and awards will be verified at the finish line.
Awards time will be announced at the event.
Bring your best — earn your bragging rights, your cash prize, and your place among the strongest in the community!

Timing Brought To You By Zornick Timing 

 
Registration, Parking & Logistics

Registration Area: Near the main bathrooms by the playground at Lacamas Lake Regional Park.
Parking Options:

Main Lot: 3344 NE Everett Street — located beside the playground and restrooms, closest to the registration zone.
Overflow Lot: Gravel lot north of the lake, accessed by crossing the bridge between Round Lake and Lacamas Lake and turning onto 35th Ave. This lot provides ample parking and easy walk-in access to the festival area.
Additional Street Parking: Limited parallel parking is available along Everett Street near the park entrance — please park respectfully and obey signage.


Facilities: Restrooms (Only at registration area), Water Bottles at Finish Line, Snacks and  Fun Festival Area With Local Vendors & Small Business.
 

Why You’ll Love This Race

Celebrate five amazing years of teamwork, challenge, and community.
Experience a 4+ mile forest-trail course featuring 10+ natural and built obstacles.
Family-friendly atmosphere — from kids to grandparents, everyone belongs here.
Exclusive 5-Year Paper Maker OCR Tanks for adult racers. Deadline for Guaranteed tanks 6/1/2026 
Paper Maker Kiddo Shirts for our youngest participants.
Enjoy the post-race festival with music, Food, local vendors, and the 5-Year Finisher Wall — sign your name and celebrate your accomplishment!
 
Community & Spirit

The Paper Maker OCR is more than a race — it’s a family tradition and a celebration of perseverance, faith, and unity.
Every year, we’re reminded that strength doesn’t just show up on the course — it’s built in the moments of encouragement, teamwork, and joy shared along the way.

Whether you’re sprinting, walking, or crawling through the mud — you’re part of something bigger.

Run your race. Conquer your obstacles. Leave your mark.

With gratitude and grit,
Your Paper Maker Creators & Family
Ryan Polin, Bennie Crocker & Nikki Crocker

name: Paul Ruston Memorial Run
description:
Come join us for the annual Paul Ruston Memorial Run at Thomas Jefferson High School!

Lace up your sneakers and honor the memory of beloved community member Paul Ruston. All proceeds will be donated to the Ruston Family Foundation, a non-profit organization focused on making the sport of cross country understandable and memorable for young athletes & families. Bring together friends, family, and neighbors for a morning of fun and fitness. Whether you're a seasoned runner or a leisurely walker, we would love you to join us in honoring Coach Ruston's legacy at the Paul Ruston Memorial Run.

View the course map and check out our website to learn more about the foundation and what we've been up to!

Race will be chip-timed by GC Racing and bibs will be available for pick up on race day during check-in (7:00AM-8:30AM).

Awards will be at 9:45AM. Prize money to overall top-3 male and female racers!

Don't miss out on this special event! Please email rustonfamilyfoundation@gmail.com for questions, concerns, or details on special student and group priced tickets!!

name: PB&J Fuel Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
Smooth vibes. Sweet energy. Bold moves. 🥜🍓


PB&J Fuel Run is all about a combo that just works. Mix your pace, spread the fun, and stick with it all the way to the finish. No stress, no expectations, just miles that feel good and a finish that feels even better. Run it your way, enjoy every step, and fuel your finish with good energy and great company. Let’s make this run unforgettable. 🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️✨

 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)

name: PeaceHealth Appletree Marathon
description:
Join us for the 9th Annual PEACEHEALTH APPLETREE Boston-Qualifying Marathon, NEW First Responder’s Relay Marathon, Half Marathon & Sunset 5K. This “Run Through History” will take you on a flat, fast and scenic course through Fort Vancouver, Officer’s Row, the Army Barracks, Pearson Airport – the oldest operating airport in the USA, the Historical Old Apple Tree, along the majestic Columbia River and many other historical vantage points. There’s so much to see that the miles will fly by!

This event will quickly be regarded as one of the prettiest and most unique courses in the Northwest and perhaps the USA! When do you get to experience a history lesson during your race?!

The quaint community of Vancouver WA will welcome you and your family with open arms and provide you with a racing experience that you just can’t get anywhere else. The volunteer support is off the charts and the energy along the course will make it an enjoyable experience that you will want to return to year after year.

NEW: We designed a flat and fast new 1 loop Boston Qualifying course that is spectator-friendly and highlights the beauty of this community.  The new route offers an exciting racing experience with many energetic water stations and plenty of entertainment to keep you engaged. The Half Marathon will offer the same experience with the joy of knowing you get to start the party a little earlier than your Marathon counterparts!

This is the third year of our First Responder’s Marathon Relay created to honor all our first responders – Peace Officers, Health Care Professionals, Fire Safety and those in our military branches.  We offer relays for those teams as small as two members up to nine members (with additional alternates), customized relay shirts and the opportunity to compete within their profession as well as against other divisions to obtain the coveted 202 PeaceHealth Appletree First Responder Baton inspired by the logo created by PAL’s, the beneficiary of the race.

The Sunset 5K will offer a shorter distance for our friends, family, and others in the community who would like the opportunity to enjoy the racing experience. It will also allow for a Pre-race shake-down for our Marathon and Half Marathon athletes and the opportunity for them to earn the coveted BEAST medal for an athlete who races both Saturday and Sunday.

Since Vancouver WA is right across the river from Portland OR, you are within a 20-minute drive to the PDX International Airport and minutes away from the big city.

WHY APPLETREE? Vancouver WA is known for its history including the Old Apple Tree Park, home of the Oldest Apple Tree in the Northwest and maybe even the entire Pacific West Coast. The APPLETREE Marathon, Half Marathon & 5K will celebrate all this history, capture the beauty of the Northwest and create a theme of all things ‘APPLE’.

name: PeaceHealth Appletree Marathon
description:

This event will quickly be regarded as one of the prettiest and most unique courses in the Northwest and perhaps the USA! When do you get to experience a history lesson during your race?!
