For the fifth straight year we're going free-range with our wild Turkey Trot at Newberry Hill Heritage Park. All events are run in the woods -- away from streets, sidewalks, and cars.  The park offers a scenic 2.7 mile loop fire road which offers a great course for our 1-Mile, 5K and 10K events.   

"Protect My Race " option in sign-up process.  During the sign-up process you will be asked if you want to buy "insurance" on your sign-up.  YOU DO NOT NEED THIS!  The Silverdale Rotary Club will happily return any registration fee, for any reason, upon request.  You do not need insurance to secure this.

NOTE:  There will not be day-of-race registration available. 

Changes in 2026:  

  • We will NOT have race-day registration in 2026.  We will, however, have last-minutes sign-ups in the week of the event.  Please check back for details!
  • Medals will be presented to the top male and female finisher in each of th 1-Mile, 5K, and 10K events.  Ribbons will be awarded for 1st - 5th place by event and age category for the 1-Mile, 5K, and 10K.  As in the past a commemorative ribbon will be presented to all Kids-Dash participans.
  • In 2026 we are increasing the numbers of port-a-potties to alleviate the lines we had in 2024.
  • Since 2022, this has been a chip-timed event.  
  • Since 2023, we have initiated a "Family Registration" (discount!) package.  Please see below for instructions. 

 

All proceeds from this event will benefit non-profit organizations and causes to fight hunger in our community.

- Parking is available on the property of Klahowya Secondary School.  Please enter off of Newberry Hill and follow signs to the parking area.   Staging, registration, and kids' dashes will occur on an access road to the Heritage Park.  From the parking lot this access road will be clearly marked.

- Race packets will be distributed at multiple events during the week preceding the race.  Packets will also be available on race day.

name: Skagit Flats Marathon, Half & 5k
description:
Welcome to the 49th Annual Skagit Flats Marathon, Half Marathon and 5K race.

Run the Valley with Skagit Runners

Our marathon course is the flattest Boston qualifier in all of Washington state!

Registration is limited to 800, so be sure to register soon for one of the best small-town marathons in the state!

Date: Sunday, September 13, 2026
Race Start Time: 8:15 am Full and Half, 8:30 am for 5k. 
Distances: Marathon (26.2 miles), Half Marathon (13.1 miles), and 5k (3.1 miles)
Chip Timing: We will be using chip timing by Northwest Endurance Events for all three races.  

Discounts: 5k only-automatic age-based STUDENT discount for ages 18 or younger 

*Active Duty Military, Veterans, & First Responders-use code: FREEDOM for discount at check out

Personal Gear: We will not have a gear check.  We are not aware of any past problems with items left in vehicles. The parking lot is a relatively safe area and the risk can be further reduced if valuables are not left in plain sight.  We will not be responsible for any lost or stolen items so please plan accordingly.

Weather: The temperature on race day is usually mild. The average low is 46° F, the average high is 64° F, with an average mean temperature of 52° F. 

Race Results: Live results can be obtained at Chronokeep.com. 

Post Race: All runners will receive a finishers medal. Water will be available at the finish line along with lots of food for ALL finishers. The high school locker rooms will be open for showers and changing.

Changing Races: Race switches from the full marathon to the half marathon and vice versa must be completed before the end of Saturday packet pickup at the latest. There will be no refund for transferring down to a shorter race and a fee for the price difference will be charged for transferring up. If you are unable to make it to Saturday packet pickup, email us before Friday so that we can make a new bib number and assign a new chip. 

Pricing:

                                                Marathon     Half Marathon          5K
Early Bird - before 5/19/26          $65               $45                       $30
5/19/26  to 7/13/26                      $80               $55                       $35
7/14/26  to  9/10/26                     $95               $65                       $40
9/11/26  to  9/14/26                     $110              $75                       $45

T-Shirt and Packet Pickup:
You can pick up race packets from 12 pm to 5pm on Saturday, September 12th, at the Skagit Running Company (724 S 1st St, Mount Vernon, WA 98273). This is the best day to pick up your packet to avoid long lines during packet pick-up on race morning.

Day of Race Packet Pickup:
Race packets can be picked up on the morning of the race at Burlington-Edison High School from 6:45 am until 8:00 am. It is preferable to pick up your packet the day prior to the race in order to avoid long lines the morning of the race.

Hotel, Dining, and Exploration Discounts for Skagit Flats participants available courtesy of the Skagit Valley Tourism Bureau.

 

Race Contact Info
If you have any questions about this race, please contact the race director at skagitrunnersrd@gmail.com
 
Course

Flat and fast rural course through the Skagit Valley.  The marathon is a Boston qualifier with a certification course number of USATF # WA21009RMB. The half marathon is also certified with a course number of USATF # WA19017RMB .  The race start is on Victoria Street on the south side of Burlington Edison High School.

The Skagit Flats marathon course is designed to favor roads with less traffic and lower speed limits. The marathon and half marathon are run on rural roads through the Skagit Valley farmlands (see course map for exact route) and finish on the Burlington-Edison High School track. The course will be clearly marked, with monitors at all intersections. Due to course restrictions, participants must finish within 6 hours. The course closes at 2:15 pm.

The 5K start and finish is at the same location as the full and half marathon.

Course Narrative:
Start on Victoria Street just west of the gym and make a left on Norris street. Continue under I-5, go straight at the stop sign, and after about 1 mile take a right on Pulver. Go straight through the next stop sign at Josh Wilson and then make a left on Maiben. Right on Avon-Allen, then a left on Benson.  After about a mile and a half the full marathon turns off to the right (North) on Thomas road.  The half continues about three quarters of a mile to a turnaround point and returns via the same route.  The full marathoners will follow Thomas road north to a turnaround point at Sunset Road, return south on Thomas, turn right (west) on Field road, right (north) on Church road to a turnaround point at Farm to Market road and return to Thomas road.  Runners will turn right (south) on Thomas, turn right (west) on Benson and continue straight across Allen west onto T-Loop Rd to a turn-around point.  After you turn around you will follow the course back on T-Loop, Benson all the way to Avon-Allen and continue to backtrack the route you came out. When you get back to the starting line, you will make a left and run between the gym and track and onto the track.

Course Closure:
The course will be open for 6 hours. All participants must finish the race in 6 hours. Runners and walkers who have not finished by 2:15 pm will be responsible for their own safety.  Participants receiving support from bicyclists, unregistered runners or unofficial vehicles will be disqualified.

Aid Stations:
There will be full-service aid stations located along the course. There will also be water stations near miles 12 and 18 at the last two full marathon turnaround points. The full-service aid stations will be staffed by local cross-country teams. Water, FLUID Performance sports drink, and Honey Stinger Gels will be available at these aid stations.

The approximate positions of the aid stations for the full marathon course are as follows: 1.25 miles, 3.75 miles, 5.75 miles, 7.75 miles, 9.75 miles, 11.75 miles (water only), 14 miles, 16 miles, 18 miles (water only), 20.25 mile, 22.5 miles, 24.75 miles.

Porta Potties:
We will have porta potties along the course, located adjacent to the aid stations.

Medical:
Volunteers will be riding the course with cell phones. Cell phones will also be located at the aid stations.
 

Rules and Regulations
1. You must be able to complete the course in 6 hours.
2. You must be in good health and physically prepared to undertake the challenges of a marathon or half marathon.
3. Event bib numbers are required for participation. Participants must fasten their bibs to the front of their shirts.
4. All participants must be registered in order to participate.
5. No strollers, skateboards, dogs or inline skates will be allowed on the course. Please do not force us to disqualify and remove you from the course for violating these rules.
6. Headphones or I-pods are discouraged during the race. Participants must be able to hear oncoming vehicles, other runners and course officials. If you cannot hear directions from course officials because you are wearing headphones you will be disqualified.
7. Participants must run no more than 2 abreast and stay to the left side of the road into traffic. Remember cars, trucks, and farm tractors are bigger than you and have the right of way along the roadway!
8. Participants must give vehicle traffic the right of way.  This event is on a course open to vehicle traffic and no special privileges are afforded to us (except for the police escort at the start).  Washington state pedestrian laws apply!

Walkers and slower participants: The Skagit Flats Marathon/Half/5K welcomes walkers! However, individuals with a 16+ minute pace are recommended to consider using a fanny pack that accommodates a water bottle. If you plan on participating at a 16+ minute pace per mile or slower, be aware that the course closes 6 hours from the start.

FAQ
Question: Are baby joggers or strollers allowed in the race? 
Answer: Because the races are run on the shoulder and edge of county roads and are not closed to traffic, baby joggers and strollers are not allowed.  


Question: What about headphones?
Answer: All participants will need to listen for traffic as well as instructions from course officials.  If you must wear headphones, keep the volume low enough to be aware of traffic and course instructions. A participant may be disqualified if they are unable to hear instructions from course officials due to the use of headphones.


Question: Will the race be chip timed?
Answer: Yes, with both starting and finishing mats.


Question: Can I help with the race even if I am not a club member?
Answer: Yes! Please contact the race director if you want to volunteer. 


Question: I don’t see an elevation map on your website. Can I get an elevation map?
Answer: The course is flat and at sea level. The only slight hill on the course has been eliminated with the new routes. There is an elevation profile available at the USATF web site.


Question: Can I switch races after I have registered?
Answer: Yes, we would be happy to help you switch races! If you are switching from the half marathon to the full marathon, you will need to pay the difference in cost. No refunds will be issued if you switch from the full marathon to the half marathon. Please contact the race director to help you make these changes.


Question: Do you cover expenses for elite runners?
Answer: No. This is a small local race put on by volunteers for the purpose of fundraising and sharing our love of running. We do not have funds available for free entries or expenses.


Question: Can I have my own personal supplies delivered to the aid stations before the race?
Answer: No. The school cross country programs each set up their own aid stations, which will be well stocked with water and sports drinks. A few aid stations should also have gels, candy and small food items available. 


Question: Will the roads where the course runs be closed to vehicular traffic?
Answer: No. The county will not allow these roads to be closed, so runners will be sharing the roads with cars (and possibly bikes). Please be aware of traffic and be especially careful at all intersections.


Question: My chip time is faster than some runners who are listed ahead of me in the results? Why is that?
Answer: Per USATF rule 245 (3), the order of finish is based on gun time, not chip time. This means that the results will be listed in the order that runners cross the finish line as it would be if chip timing was not used.

Social Media
Get the latest news by checking out Skagit Runners-Run the Valley (Facebook) or @skagitrunners_runthevalley on Instagram or at skagitrunners.com

Race Support
This project partially funded by Skagit County and City of Burlington Lodging Tax funds.

Start on Victoria Street just west of the gym and make a left on Norris street. Continue under I-5, go straight at the stop sign, and after about 1 mile take a right on Pulver. Go straight through the next stop sign at Josh Wilson and then make a left on Maiben. Right on Avon-Allen, then a left on Benson.  After about a mile and a half the full marathon turns off to the right (North) on Thomas road.  The half continues about three quarters of a mile to a turnaround point and returns via the same route.  The full marathoners will follow Thomas road north to a turnaround point at Sunset Road, return south on Thomas, turn right (west) on Field road, right (north) on Church road to a turnaround point at Farm to Market road and return to Thomas road.  Runners will turn right (south) on Thomas, turn right (west) on Benson and continue straight across Allen west onto T-Loop Rd to a turn-around point.  After you turn around you will follow the course back on T-Loop, Benson all the way to Avon-Allen and continue to backtrack the route you came out. When you get back to the starting line, you will make a left and run between the gym and track and onto the track.

Course Closure:
The course will be open for 6 hours. All participants must finish the race in 6 hours. Runners and walkers who have not finished by 2:15 pm will be responsible for their own safety.  Participants receiving support from bicyclists, unregistered runners or unofficial vehicles will be disqualified.

Aid Stations:
There will be full-service aid stations located along the course. There will also be water stations near miles 12 and 18 at the last two full marathon turnaround points. The full-service aid stations will be staffed by local cross-country teams. Water, FLUID Performance sports drink, and Honey Stinger Gels will be available at these aid stations.

The approximate positions of the aid stations for the full marathon course are as follows: 1.25 miles, 3.75 miles, 5.75 miles, 7.75 miles, 9.75 miles, 11.75 miles (water only), 14 miles, 16 miles, 18 miles (water only), 20.25 mile, 22.5 miles, 24.75 miles.

Porta Potties:
We will have porta potties along the course, located adjacent to the aid stations.

Medical:
Volunteers will be riding the course with cell phones. Cell phones will also be located at the aid stations.
 

Rules and Regulations
1. You must be able to complete the course in 6 hours.
2. You must be in good health and physically prepared to undertake the challenges of a marathon or half marathon.
3. Event bib numbers are required for participation. Participants must fasten their bibs to the front of their shirts.
4. All participants must be registered in order to participate.
5. No strollers, skateboards, dogs or inline skates will be allowed on the course. Please do not force us to disqualify and remove you from the course for violating these rules.
6. Headphones or I-pods are discouraged during the race. Participants must be able to hear oncoming vehicles, other runners and course officials. If you cannot hear directions from course officials because you are wearing headphones you will be disqualified.
7. Participants must run no more than 2 abreast and stay to the left side of the road into traffic. Remember cars, trucks, and farm tractors are bigger than you and have the right of way along the roadway!
8. Participants must give vehicle traffic the right of way.  This event is on a course open to vehicle traffic and no special privileges are afforded to us (except for the police escort at the start).  Washington state pedestrian laws apply!

Walkers and slower participants: The Skagit Flats Marathon/Half/5K welcomes walkers! However, individuals with a 16+ minute pace are recommended to consider using a fanny pack that accommodates a water bottle. If you plan on participating at a 16+ minute pace per mile or slower, be aware that the course closes 6 hours from the start.

FAQ
Question: Are baby joggers or strollers allowed in the race? 
Answer: Because the races are run on the shoulder and edge of county roads and are not closed to traffic, baby joggers and strollers are not allowed.  


Question: What about headphones?
Answer: All participants will need to listen for traffic as well as instructions from course officials.  If you must wear headphones, keep the volume low enough to be aware of traffic and course instructions. A participant may be disqualified if they are unable to hear instructions from course officials due to the use of headphones.


Question: Will the race be chip timed?
Answer: Yes, with both starting and finishing mats.


Question: Can I help with the race even if I am not a club member?
Answer: Yes! Please contact the race director if you want to volunteer. 


Question: I don’t see an elevation map on your website. Can I get an elevation map?
Answer: The course is flat and at sea level. The only slight hill on the course has been eliminated with the new routes. There is an elevation profile available at the USATF web site.


Question: Can I switch races after I have registered?
Answer: Yes, we would be happy to help you switch races! If you are switching from the half marathon to the full marathon, you will need to pay the difference in cost. No refunds will be issued if you switch from the full marathon to the half marathon. Please contact the race director to help you make these changes.


Question: Do you cover expenses for elite runners?
Answer: No. This is a small local race put on by volunteers for the purpose of fundraising and sharing our love of running. We do not have funds available for free entries or expenses.


Question: Can I have my own personal supplies delivered to the aid stations before the race?
Answer: No. The school cross country programs each set up their own aid stations, which will be well stocked with water and sports drinks. A few aid stations should also have gels, candy and small food items available. 


Question: Will the roads where the course runs be closed to vehicular traffic?
Answer: No. The county will not allow these roads to be closed, so runners will be sharing the roads with cars (and possibly bikes). Please be aware of traffic and be especially careful at all intersections.


Question: My chip time is faster than some runners who are listed ahead of me in the results? Why is that?
Answer: Per USATF rule 245 (3), the order of finish is based on gun time, not chip time. This means that the results will be listed in the order that runners cross the finish line as it would be if chip timing was not used.

Social Media
Get the latest news by checking out Skagit Runners-Run the Valley (Facebook) or @skagitrunners_runthevalley on Instagram or at skagitrunners.com

Race Support
This project partially funded by Skagit County and City of Burlington Lodging Tax funds.

https://www.visitskagitvalley.com/

name: Sleigh that 5k
description:
🎄 Sleigh That 5K 🎄
Dashing Through the Snow... in Running Shoes!
Get ready to sleigh your way into the holiday season! Join us at Green Lake Park for the Sleigh That 5K—a festive, in-person fun run that’s all about movement, merriment, and just the right amount of jingle.

Whether you’re a seasoned runner or a casual walker with a passion for peppermint mochas, this event is your chance to kick off the holidays with joy, energy, and plenty of holiday cheer. Ugly sweaters, elf ears, Santa hats—all festive flair is welcome (and encouraged)!

🎅 Expect:

A scenic 5K route with lots of holiday vibes
Festive music and photo ops
Holiday outfits that would make Rudolph proud
Fun for the whole family (reindeer not required)


So grab your crew, bundle up, and get ready to sleigh the day. Let’s make spirits (and sneakers) bright!

name: Sloth Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
🦥🏃‍♂️ The Sloth Run – Slow Is the New Fast! 🏃‍♀️🦥

Tired of high-speed races and intense competition? Us too.
Welcome to the Sloth Run, where the pace is slow, the vibes are chill, and everyone's a winner (eventually).

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: Snoqualmie Tunnel 5k Glow Run
description:
Saturday, July 11th, 2026
Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail - Hyak Parking
Snoqualmie Pass, WA US 98068

All-ages, 5k walk or run through the historic Snoqualmie tunnel. Afraid of the dark? Have no fear, the tunnel will be partially lit with LED lights. Following the race, head to Dru Bru (Sno Pass) for an outdoor, all-ages, block party. We’ll have food, games, beer, cider, wine, and soda! 

OPTIONAL ADD-ONS:

  • Race T-Shirt, $15.50 (available until 6/26)
  • LED Gloves, $14.00
  • Participation Medal, $7.50

You will pick up your race merch onsite the day of the event. Additional glow gear is highly encouraged; the brighter the better! If you're looking for wearable inspiration, check out GlowUniverse.com. We also suggest a personal flashlight or headlamp. 

THE RACE:

Wave 1 - Runners Only. Must be able to complete a 5K in under 45mins

  • Check-In / gear pick-up from 9:00am - 9:50am
  • Race starts at 10:00am

Wave 2 - Joggers/Walkers/Strollers

  • Check-In / gear pick-up from 9:00am -10:30am
  • Race starts at 10:45am

The race is a loop. You will start and end at the Palouse to Cascades State Park - Hyak Trailhead parking lot (formerly the Iron Horse State Park Trail). The course is pretty flat. You will start ~.5 mile outside the tunnel, run/walk approximately one mile in, turn around, and run/walk one mile out, back to the start. LED lights will help illuminate the tunnel and race course, but a personal light is also recommended.

Additional Tunnel details and directions can be found here: Palouse to Cascades Trail - The Tunnel 
Using Google Maps search for "Hyak Parking Lot, Snoqualmie Pass, WA 98068." Traveling East or West on I-90 you will take exit 54. 


PARKING:

There are two parking lots.

  • Lot 1 - Hyak Trailhead lot. All vehicles entering the state park must have a Discover Pass. These are sold onsite (and can be purchased the day of) or online (http://www.discoverpass.wa.gov/). This lot fills up fast.
  • Lot 2 - The Summit East Lower Lot, which is a 5min walk to the event. No Discover Pass is required. 


TUNNEL CONDITIONS: 
Be prepared for extreme darkness and cold temperatures. For this event, LED lights will help illuminate the path, but a personal light is also recommended. The tunnel is chilly; the average temperature (year-round) is ~50 degrees, so we encourage you to wear a long-sleeved shirt or light jacket. The ground is made of compacted gravel.   


BIKES:
To ensure the safety of our runners/ walkers this a bike-free event. Strollers are allowed. Since it's a public park, we are required to keep the tunnel open to the public; therefore, bikes may be present but will not be officially part of the event.


KIDS:
This is a kid-friendly event. Children 4 and under are free (and do not need to register).


DOGS: 
Animals are not allowed due to the number of participants and event conditions.

name: Snoqualmie Valley Half
description:
The Snoqualmie Valley Trail meanders through one of the area’s most beautiful agricultural areas, the Snoqualmie Valley Half showcases this natural gem. This race is flat and fast and the surface is smooth and non-technical and showcases old-growth forest and farmland. You’ll have a spectacular and fast finish in the shadow of the historic big red barn at King County’s Tolt MacDonald Park! The course is USATF certified!

Race Website: https://www.orcarunning.com/snoqualmie-valley-half/

name: SPARRKS First Annual 5K Stride to Recovery
description:
SPARRKS First Annual 5K Stride to Recovery

Join us for the SPARRKS First Annual 5K Stride to Recovery, a powerful community event dedicated to raising awareness for mental health and recovery. This special event will feature a 5K run/walk, creating an opportunity for individuals and families of all ages to come together in support of hope, healing, and wellness.

Our mission is to break the stigma surrounding mental health and recovery while encouraging open conversations, support, and community connection. name: Step By Step's Race
description:
Join us for the 16th Annual Step By Step race! Embrace the distance over 10K, walk/run our 5K family-friendly race, or have your littles do the Kids Dash! 

 

Register before August 16th to be guaranteed a race shirt. 

 

Pricing Schedule:

March 16 - March 30, $35 **2-week special pricing**

March 31 - June 30, $45

July 1 - Sept 18, $55

Race day registration, $65

 

COURSE INFORMATION

The starting and ending location of each race will be at The Grove (our outdoor preschool off of 33rd St. SE). Runners and walkers will head out of the site and through the Van Lierop Park, eventually turning left and onto the Foothills Trail. This is subject to change.

 

RACE TIMELINE

8:00 AM - Kids Dash (must be with parents)

8:15 AM - Group Photo

8:25 AM - Warm-up with Coach Sue

8:30 AM - 10K Start

8:40 AM - 5K Start

9:50 AM - Course closes

 

We encourage you to carpool and arrive early to find parking! 

 

RACE ROUTE

The official 5K and 10K race routes will be uploaded soon!  

 

PACKET PICKUP

It is highly recommended to pick up your bib number and race shirt at the Step By Step offices (next door to Farm 12 Restaurant) on the pickup day listed below.

Location:

3303 8th Ave SE, Unit #A

Puyallup, WA 98372


When:

Thursday, Sept 17 from 9 AM - 7 PM.

 

Please note, packets will not be available for pickup before 9am on Sept. 17th. Please do not call the office with packet pickup questions, if you have questions, please email: sukeighron@stepbystepfamily.org.

 

Packets will be available for pick up on race morning starting at 6:30 AM at the packet picket tent at The Grove. However, we strongly encourage you to pick up your packet on Thursday to avoid long lines and ensure a smooth race day experience. 

 

FUNDRAISE 

We’re working together to raise $55,000 to support the mission of Step By Step. Recruit your friends, family, and colleagues to join your team or invite them to make a donation in your name. Help us raise critical funds needed to help transform the lives of at-risk pregnant women, so they will deliver healthy babies, embrace positive parenting, and establish safe homes and secure futures. 

 

FINISHERS CELEBRATION

After you finish your run, enjoy Happy Donuts donut holes, coffee, tasty treats, a kids zone, and lots more!

 

RAFFLE 

Bring a package of diapers and/or wipes and be entered into our raffle drawing for some great prizes!

 

THANK YOU for partnering with us to build strong families in our community.

All proceeds from this event go to support Step By Step and help local moms and babies in need.

name: Steps ROCK 'n' ROLL STROLL 5K family fun walk/run!
description:
Kick off the Oak Harbor Music Festival weekend with the most rockin’ 5k ever!

Take Steps Together with us on Saturday, September 5th, 2026 at 9:00 am for the third annual Steps ROCK ‘n’ ROLL STROLL to support families caring for infants and toddlers with disabilities or developmental delays.

New this year — BABY STEPS 1/2 Mile Route!
We’re excited to introduce the free Baby Steps 1/2 mile route, perfect for our youngest participants and their families. Strollers, tiny sneakers, and wobbly walkers of all ages are all welcome! Baby Steps participants have the option to purchase an event t-shirt for $10. See the Baby Steps route map here: https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6712831237/

You are invited to bring the whole family to join the fun and dress up as your favorite rock star! We want to see it all: leather, lace, bandanas, giggles, smiles, tutus, crowns, big hair, glitter, and cheers! We encourage strolling, walking, running, skipping, hopping, and especially dancing your way across the finish line.

Our day begins at Windjammer Park in Oak Harbor, WA on Whidbey Island. The 5K course follows the sparkling waterfront out to Catalina Park at the Marina and back to Windjammer Park.

  • Free parking is available at Windjammer Park.

  • Check in at the registration tables to pick up your race bib and t-shirt.

  • All pre-registered 5K participants will receive a free t-shirt. We cannot guarantee t-shirt sizes for registrations after August 21st, 2026.

  • Please arrive at least 30 minutes early to ensure everyone in your group is checked in.

  • After checking in, enjoy kids’ activities, face painting, photo backdrops, and more.

  • This is the perfect time for Rock Star photos! Strollers, tricycles, sea turtles, and fur babies are permitted on the course. Please act responsibly and clean up after your pets.

This is a non-competitive event, with everyone moving at their own pace and all finishers celebrated equally.

At the end of the 5K, enjoy snacks and refreshments. Families are invited to make their way to SE Pioneer Way to continue the fun at the Oak Harbor Music Festival.

 
5K special age based pricing!

Youth - Half price for your 5-11 year old!
Under 5 - Free!
(discount automatically applied when birthdate is entered)

 
Rockstar Diaper Drive!

Help us roll out the love! Please bring new or opened packs of diapers (size 1-5) or wipes to share with our Steps families. Let’s show our little rock stars some big support!

 

Taking Steps Together for 40+ Years

All ROCK ‘n’ ROLL STROLL proceeds benefit Steps, a non-profit organization providing in-home early support services for infants and toddlers, birth to three years of age, with developmental delays in communication, social-emotional, fine or gross motor, adaptive skills, and/or cognitive development. Our early learning and pediatric care team offers therapies, education, and family-centered support that helps children build the skills they need to thrive—at home, in school, and in the broader community. We are continuously taking steps to expand our resources to meet the needs of the children and families we serve on Whidbey Island, Anacortes, and the San Juan Islands.

Visit the Steps website to learn more: www.takingstepstogether.org

name: Strides 2 Survive 5K Virtual Fun Walk/Run
description:
WHO WE ARE -  The Endometrial Cancer Action Network for African-Americans, or ECANA, is a 501(c)3 organization created for African-American women affected by endometrial cancer (commonly known as EC or uterine cancer).  OUR MISSION is to improve the lives of Black people affected by Endometrial Cancer.  We have come together to create support, community, and empowerment for any African American affected by endometrial cancer. Reproductive health care & cancer care for Black people is not as it should be. We are here to bridge the gap through survivor community building, education, and research advocacy.  Our members consist of doctors, patients, survivors, community advocates, and professional leaders across the United States.

OUR EVENT -  STRIDES 2 SURVIVE 5K VIRTUAL FUN WALK/RUN.  Total distance to complete is 5k or 3.1 miles  This is our 3rd Annual Virtual 5K which celebrates Gynecologic Cancer Awareness Month - which is September!

      If you would like to receive a T-shirt & sponsor swag, & Finisher medal, please select "Strides 2 Survive 5K Virtual Fun Walk/Run".

      If you would like to only receive the Finisher Medal, please select "Strides 2 Survive MINI 5K Virtual Fun Walk."

WHEN - EVENT DAY is Saturday September 19, 2026.  Registrants may stretch the event over multiple days in September. Regardless of which day(s) you choose to complete your 5K, we encourage participants to tune in to our social media on 9/19 watch our program highlighting women who are affected by Uterine/endometrial cancer and their caregivers.  You also get the opportunity to see our sponsors who are great partners in this endeavor.  The completion of the 5K is totally on the honor system.

WHO - OUR AUDIENCE includes EVERYONE!  Black women who are endometrial cancer survivors, friends, caregivers, supporters, volunteers, young, old, avid walkers/runners as well as newcomers.  Anyone who supports our cause is welcome. We estimate our attendance will range from 300 – 500 registered attendees.  

WHERE -  ANYWHERE YOU CHOOSE.  The goal is to complete a 5K (3.1 miles).  YOU CHOOSE your location (park, neighborhood, indoor mall, walking trail, home/treadmill, etc) and it's up to you if you would like to break it down into manageable portions. Bring friends along to make it a more memorable day!  

HOW - You may walk/run solo or with a group or team.  If walking/running is not for you, please utilize alternate 5K activities (housework, biking, gardening, etc.)  to achieve the goal of 5K (3.1 miles).  We have provided a generous list of activity ideas for you to choose from. We employ the Honor System in regards to completion.  There is NO pressure to over exert yourself.  Go at your own safe pace!  If you need to break down the distance over several days - please do!  You have the ENTIRE month of September to work towards the goal.

GIFTS/SWAG/Medals - Registrations completed before 8/20 will be guaranteed their items!!  Those who register by this date can expect their items to ship no later than 9/14/2026 (to arrive before race day).  Registrations completed after 8/20 will be mailed out the first week of October.  Items are shipped first come first served until all inventory is depleted.  Inventory on the registration will reflect if items have been depleted.

WHO - OUR AUDIENCE includes EVERYONE!  Black women who are endometrial cancer survivors, friends, caregivers, supporters, volunteers, young, old, avid walkers/runners as well as newcomers.  Anyone who supports our cause is welcome. We estimate our attendance will range from 300 – 500 registered attendees.  

WHERE -  ANYWHERE YOU CHOOSE.  The goal is to complete a 5K (3.1 miles).  YOU CHOOSE your location (park, neighborhood, indoor mall, walking trail, home/treadmill, etc) and it's up to you if you would like to break it down into manageable portions. Bring friends along to make it a more memorable day!  

HOW - You may walk/run solo or with a group or team.  If walking/running is not for you, please utilize alternate 5K activities (housework, biking, gardening, etc.)  to achieve the goal of 5K (3.1 miles).  We have provided a generous list of activity ideas for you to choose from. We employ the Honor System in regards to completion.  There is NO pressure to over exert yourself.  Go at your own safe pace!  If you need to break down the distance over several days - please do!  You have the ENTIRE month of September to work towards the goal.

GIFTS/SWAG/Medals - Registrations completed before 8/20 will be guaranteed their items!!  Those who register by this date can expect their items to ship no later than 9/14/2026 (to arrive before race day).  Registrations completed after 8/20 will be mailed out the first week of October.  Items are shipped first come first served until all inventory is depleted.  Inventory on the registration will reflect if items have been depleted.

name: Sullivan Lake Triathlon 2026
description:
A sprint triathlon located in the beautiful Sullivan Lake Recreational Area of the Colville National Forest near Ione, Washington. You will swim 750m in Sullivan Lake, starting at the Noisy Creek Campground boat launch. Next you will complete a 20km bike on the Sullivan Lake Road, where you will have beautiful views of the lake to inspire your ride. The Bike turn around is at the Mill Pond Campground, returning to the Noisy Creek Day Use Area, your run will take you back out to the Sullivan Lake Road and you will run 2.5km to the Harvey Creek Bridge where you will turn around there and your finish line awaits you back at the Noisy Creek Day Use Area.

You will receive a Finisher's Medal once you cross the finish line! 
To reach the Sullivan Lake Triathlon, head 90 miles north of Spokane, WA, and take Highway 31 north towards Ione. About a mile south of Ione, turn onto Sullivan Lake Road (County Road 9345) and follow it for 8.2 miles to the campground entrance on the south end of Sullivan Lake

All participants will receive a t-shirt, swim cap and racing bib. 

 All those who finish the Sullivan Lake Triathlon will receive a finishers medal. 

Sullivan Lake Triathlon is under a Special Use Permit from the Colville National Forest.

name: Summer Solstice Endurance Run
description:
Celebrate the longest day of the year one loop at a time at the Summer Solstice Endurance Run in beautiful downtown Napavine! Whether you're aiming for a casual 5K walk with friends or pushing yourself toward 50 miles, this unique community event lets you choose your own challenge.

Cost & What’s Included:         

$30 - Online registration Deadline June 15th, 2026 (Midnight) 

$40 - Day of Registration

(2) Running Taco Tickets

(1) Punch Card to keep track of loops

Raffle ticket to win prizes for each loop completed!

Water, coffee and snacks will be provided throughout the day. 

The course features a scenic 5K loop through Napavine, with every loop beginning promptly on the hour, every hour, from 5:00 AM through the evening. Participants can join for a single lap or keep going all day long — the distance is entirely up to you. Runners and walkers of all ages and abilities are welcome.

Throughout the day, enjoy:

Prizes and giveaways
Live entertainment and community fun
Delicious Running Tacos
A festive endurance atmosphere celebrating movement, summer, and community spirit
Best of all, every mile supports a great cause. All proceeds from the event will benefit the Napavine High School Senior Class of 2027.

This event is proudly presented through a collaboration between Tumac Taproom Runners and Run Amok Irish Running Club

Come run, walk, cheer, eat tacos, and celebrate the Summer Solstice with us!

name: SUMMER SPLASH 5K
description:
IMPORTANT UPDATE: The 2026 edition of Summer Splash has been cancelled.  

 

Looking for some summer fun... 

   5k Race & 0.5m Kids Dash

   then cool off in the splash pad!!!!

 

  • Saturday August 8, 2026

  •  8am Badger Mountain Community Park
     350 Keene Road, Richland, WA

 

Schedule of Events:
➔ 7:00 am Start of Registration / Number Pickup 
➔ 7:50 am Pre-race announcement
➔ 8:00 am Start of the Summer Splash 5k
➔ 9:00 am Start of the Kids Splash Dash
➔ 10:00 am Event Ends
The Summer Splash 5k race is 3.1 miles along the Keene Road Trail, starting at the Badger Mountain Park splash pad. The out-and-back course heads east from the park and turns around where the 12-ft wide paved trail crosses Bellerive Road. The course will be marked with chalk and cones and traffic control volunteers will be at each road crossing (Elementary St / Leslie Rd / Venus Cir) to help as crossing guards although you are responsible for safely crossing each roadway (be prepared to stop in case of traffic that is not yielding).

 

5k Registration:
➔ $15 Online (until January 31st)
➔ $25 Online (until May 31st)
➔ $30 Online (until July 31st)
➔ $35 Online (through race day)
➔ 12 & Under are FREE with a paid parent (after registering the parent, please contact us for discount code to use for the child)
 
Kids Splash Dash:
The Kids Splash Dash is a 1⁄2 mile fun run/walk that stays within the Badger Mountain Park and follows the paved loop path around the fields and splash pad. This is FREE and open to anyone 10 years old and younger.
 
All participants will need to sign a waiver and anyone under 18 years old will need the waiver signed by a parent.

 

Awards & Timing:
The 5k race will be timed and results will be posted online after the event. The 1⁄2 mile kids run will not be timed.

Medals will be provided to the top 3 female and male finishers overall and also of each age group in the 5k:
 0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, and 70+

All finishers of the Kids Splash Dash will receive a finisher ribbon.

 

Post Race:
Water and snacks will be available at the finish line.
Please bring chairs and towels so you can hang around after the event. The Badger Mountain Community Park has big grass fields, a playground, and a SPLASH PAD so...
Stay & Play after you Run for some Fun in the Sun!!

Presented by Delta Endurance LLC

name: Sun City Barry James Memorial 5K and Half Marathon
description:
The Sun City Barry James Memorial 5K and Half Marathon are put on every year by the Hard Core Running Club of Central Washington. They take place on the second Sunday of October at Volution Fitness, this year at a new location on University Parkway in Terrace Heights, Washington, just east of Yakima. The 5K and half marathon both start and end at Volution. There will be aid stations at miles 3.5, 7, and 10. The half marathon is a favorite race of many participants with rolling hills alongside orchards.

Race fee is $15 for Hard Core Runner Members, $20 for non-members, and youth under age 12 are free.  Costs go up to $22 on October 1st. Day of race entries will be $25.

name: Sundae Runday
description:
Join us for the 6th annual Sundae Runday, where we combine our love of running with a love for ice cream! Finish your 10K, 5K run, or 2 mile (plus a little bit) walk with a delicious ice cream sundae with all the toppings!

 

 

Race Day Schedule:

8:30AM – Registration and Packet Pickup Opens

9:00AM – Costume Contest

9:15AM – Kids Dash

9:30AM – 10K Start

9:45AM – 5K and 2 Mile start

10:00AM - Ice cream time! 

10:30am - Awards

 

Sundae FUNday Festivities:

- Post-race ice cream treats for all, including your four-legged friends!

- Finisher's item, it will be something fun, and functional! 

- Water and whipped cream at the banana split halfway mark!

- Chance to beat the ice cream

- Free Event Photos

- Kid’s Tent with Games & Crafts

- Kids Dash with finisher items and ice cream

- Costume Contest - put on your Sundae best! 

- Traffic free course through Seward Park and the shores of Lake Washington. 

- Stroller friendly event

- Furry Friends: Dogs are welcome to run with us! Check the box at registration to pre-register your pup and guarantee a doggy treat in the Sundae line!

 

Registration Info:

10K

January 1 - 9: $35
Jan 10 -  May 16: $45
May 17 -  July 16:  $50
July 17 - August 15: $55
Day of Event Registration - $60


5K & 2 Mile Walk

January 1 - 9: $30
Jan 10 -  May 16: $40
May 17 - July 16: $45
July 17 -August 15: $50
Day of Event Registration - $55

 

-  Kids 15 and under - $25 (includes shirt and ice cream)

 

- Kids dash - $10 - (includes ice cream and finisher's ribbon)

 

- Register by July 15 to guarantee your shirt size.

 

Teams of 6 or more get an automatic discount. Once the 6th person signs the first 5 participants get a refund! 

 

Volunteer with us and get a race shirt, and a trip through the sundae toppings bar without all that pesky running!

 

Benefiting Let Me Run - Let Me Run is building a new generation of men by teaching boys to be their best selves through a character development program powered by running.

name: Sunland Estates 5k Run/Walk
description:
The Sunland Estates 5k Run/Walk is an excellent way to kick off the official Sunland Fourth of July activities!  Clear the cobwebs with a stroll or jog or run around the neighborhood. 

You can also sign up for several of the Sunland 4th of July weekend tournaments. 

Race:  Saturday, July 4th at 8:00 am
Packet Pick Up: Friday, July 3rd from 5pm to 6pm in front of the Sunland Office
                           

REGISTER BY MONDAY, JUNE 15th, 2026 TO BE GUARANTEED AN OFFICIAL RACE SHIRT

  • Online registration will be open until July 1st at noon.  A limited number of extra race shirts will be ordered and will be assigned in the order registrations are received for those registering after June15th (size not guaranteed).
  • In-person registrations are only available at Friday Packet Pick Up for $40 per person (cash or check only), and do not guarantee a race shirt. 
  • No race-day registration is offered.
  • Interested in a race shirt without having to race?  Contributions to the Sunland 4th of July Celebration of $25 or greater receive an official dry-fit race shirt (if the donation is received by June 15th).

Pricing:
Adults: $40
Kids 10 and under: $15 (Kids 5 years and younger are Free)

*Registration fees include race shirt and timing bib.

To be a race sponsor, and have your name or logo on the back of the race shirt, visit the Donate page.  Artwork must be received by June 8th to appear on the back of the shirt (black & white pdf preferred).  

Race Shirt Sizes:  Sizes and availability guaranteed for participants registered by June 15th.     
Click here for size chart.

*Note, Sunland Estates HOA is not a 501c charitable organization and your donation is not tax deductible.

name: Sunrise Marathon 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
🌅Run at Sunrise with pretty scenic views!
Start your day — and your journey — with a breathtaking sunrise and fellow runners chasing greatness.

 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: Super Seattle 5K
description:
**** Please Read in Entirety ****

Super Seattle 5K - Produced by Hi5K

Calling all Super Bowl Fans to run (or walk) in the Super Seattle 5K!!! 

This is an Awesome way to get ready for the Super Bowl a day before!!! Yes come and run a 5K in Seattle on Super Bowl Sunday.

Come sporting your  SEAHAWK  colors!!! If you are not a Seahawk, sport your own team's colors!!! Or, wear anything you want - we just want you to come out and have fun AND receive an official 5K chip-timed result.

Event Information

The event will be held at Green Lake Park in Seattle. The course is a 5K on the paved loop around Green Lake with the final stretch coming around the ball fields (see course links below). From a runners perspective - this course is legit, dope, sick, wicked, 'da bomb - 'ya feel me!!!  And it is flat and fast if you are after a PR.
We look forward to you joining us in this exceptionally high quality event. 
If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must register you and sign the waiver that will be presented during the registration process, otherwise if you are 18 you may register yourself.

Race Day (Super Bowl Sunday) Schedule:

7:45AM - 9:10AM:
Bib Pickup at Green Lake softball fields (East side of Green Lake - Look for Hi5K Tents).  You may also drop off any canned food items you'd like to donate at this time. Day-Of-Race registration available at this time as well.
9:30AM:
 5K Race Start 
9:50 AM:
Podium Awards Begin - Top 3 in each age category (Male/Female awarded separately).
Age categories are as follows 1-11, 12-15, 16-18, 19-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60+
9:50AM - 10:40AM:
Post-Race Hydration and Nutrition available

Scholarships:

If you are experiencing any financial hardship, and would still like to participate, please email the race director at:
racedirector@hi5k.com

OR you can send us a message by clicking the  Questions?  button below.

We will get you signed up - no questions asked.

Bib Pickup:

There is no bib pickup prior to race day. Please pick up your bib between 7:45AM and 9:10AM at the starting line tent on race day.

Course Info:

Start/Finish area is at the Greenlake Community Center basketball courts on the East side of Greenlake.  From the start, the race will head west toward the lake and then make an immediate right-hand turn to begin a counter-clockwise loop around the Green Lake on the inner paved path. At approximately mile 2.8 there will be a right hand-turn to exit the inner path and begin a counter-clockwise lap around the play fields (softball / soccer area). The final turn (at "Turn and Burn" corner) will be a left-hand turn with 200 meters remaining to the finish (time to kick! - it's slightly downhill too). 
Timing: This is a chip-timed event. Timing is provided by Bell Lap Productions. 
Weather: Prepare for cold or inclement weather (It's February).
Course Links:
  • https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/2805350536
  • https://ridewithgps.com/routes/31541051
Strava Segments: 
  • https://www.strava.com/segments/22375594 (Full 3.1 Mile Segment)
  • https://www.strava.com/segments/22375610 (200 Meter "Turn and Burn" Finish)
  • https://www.strava.com/segments/16058817 (Mile Somewhere in the Middle)

Donations:

Did you know that the Super Bowl is the 2nd biggest food day of the year!  This race is helps support local food shelters in their efforts to fight hunger in Washington State. If you can, please bring any non-perishable or canned food item to the race and we'll happily drop it to one of the local food shelters we support.

FAQs:

Can I participate with a stroller? 
Absolutely - we are stroller friendly.
Can I run with my dog?
Unfortunately no, USATF (USA Track & Field) will no longer insure or sanction events that allows dogs.

 We can't wait to see you!!! 
 This is going to be so Awesome!!!
 Bring it! Send it!! YEEEET!!!

name: Swing the Gates 5k and 10k
description:
Swing the Gates is back for a 4th year! And this time we are CLOSING the Park on Halloween!

This year will include the popular 10k Team Scavenger Hunt and the classic 5k Fun Run-costumes encouraged.

Come hang out with an amazing community of nature lovers, runners, walkers, and their K-9 companions while exploring the beauty of Deception Pass State Park

5K Fun Run

The 5K fun run will kick off at 9:00 AM, but we recommend coming early to cheer on the 10K team scavenger hunt participants as they complete their first challenge as soon as they cross the start line at 8:00 AM.  

The course will be run primarily on paved surfaces, however does include 400 ft elevation gain with a steep incline at the beginning of the race. Strollers, small children, and dogs are welcome! The race aid station is cup-less again, so be sure to bring your own water bottle or cup.

Course will close at 11:00AM.

10K Team Scavenger Hunt

Challenge yourself and your friends to a unique race experience. Teams will set off along the trails to solve various challenges along the way which will help them uncover the racecourse as they go. Scavenger hunts are more fun with friends, so find three other people to join you at 8:00 AM on race day. Distances and elevation will vary based on your team’s ability to navigate the trails of Deception Pass State Park. 

This is a difficult course run primarily along unpaved trails within the park. If your team is able to navigate the trails efficiently, we expect this year's course to be 6.2 miles and a 1200' elevation.  Each clue station will have cutoff times. The final clue station will close at 11:00 AM to allow park staff to CLOSE the gates to the Park for the season.  If you are still running at this time, we ask that you head to the finish line and check in. This is an unsupported 10K race. Plan to carry your own water and snacks. 

*The first participant will pay the initial fee and then all other teammates are free. Be sure to share your team’s name and password with your teammates so they join the correct team and aren’t paying another fee. If your teammate(s) does/do not register, they will not be allowed on the course for safety reasons.

**For safety reasons, substitutions are not allowed for any races after October 28, 2026 including the 10K team scavenger hunt.

Prices (processing fees not included)

5K Fun Run
$30

10K Team Scavenger Hunt
$120.00

(No matter the day, or number of people on your team, the 10K Scavenger Hunt is the same price. The first participant will pay the initial fee and then all other teammates are free. Be sure to share your team’s name and password with your teammates so they join the correct team and aren’t paying another fee.)

A Discover Pass is required to park in the lot for the race and can be purchased online at www. discoverpass.wa.gov or at the entrance booth on the day of the event.

Prizes

The top three finishers of each race category in 5K Fun Run and the first place team in the 10K Scavenger Hunt will win a special prize!

Volunteering

Volunteers are critical to make this race successful. We need people managing different 10K clues, aiding the check-in process, manning our water station, and much more. If you are interested in volunteering, please email volunteer@deceptionpassfoundation.org to get more information.

name: Tacky Turkey Sweater 5k
description:
Gobble, Jog, and Strut Your Stuff!

Get ready to hit the pavement in style—questionable style, that is! Join us for the most hilariously festive run of the season at Green Lake Park: the Tacky Turkey Sweater 5K.

Dig out your most outrageous, over-the-top, turkey or holiday-themed sweater (the tackier, the better!) and jog, waddle, or strut your way through a 5K course filled with laughter, fall vibes, and questionable fashion choices. 

Bring your friends, your family, and maybe even your weird uncle who actually owns a turkey sweater collection. (Leave your pet turkey at home—trust us on this one.)

Expect:
Festive photo ops
Fabulous prizes for the tackiest sweaters
A fun and inclusive community vibe

So lace up, layer up, and let your turkey flag fly. Let’s make this the most unforgettable (and eye-watering) sweater parade Green Lake Park has ever seen!

name: Tacoma City Marathon / Half / Ghost / 10K / 5K / 1K
description:
Join us for the return of the Ghost of Tacoma on Saturday and the Tacoma City Marathon on Sunday with Marathon Relay, Half Marathon, 5K, 10K and Kids 1K options also available.

Run 3 races in 2 days! Kick off Saturday morning with the 5K or 10K (8:00 am start) and afterwards, run the Ghost of Tacoma Marathon or Half Marathon (9:00 am start). Kids 1K race will be on Saturday at 9:30 am. Then complete the weekend with the Tacoma City Marathon or Half Marathon on Sunday. PLUS receive a $40 Discount on the Ghost of Tacoma if you register for the Sunday Marathon or Sunday Half Marathon. Discount will be automatically applied to your cart when you add both races (must be the same registrant for both races).

Sunday’s Marathon and Half Marathon are point-to-point courses running across the iconic Narrows Bridge and finishing at Tacoma’s beautiful Dune Peninsula Park, the Northwest’s premier waterfront neighborhood. This picturesque entertainment and recreation hub is situated along Commencement Bay with panoramic views of the Puget Sound, the Olympic and Cascade Mountain ranges.

Runners will enjoy a scenic, USATF-Certified and Boston Qualifying course that passes through Point Defiance Park, with over 700 acres of beautiful gardens and old growth forests. After exiting Pt. Defiance, the Marathon and Half Marathon runners will cross over the Wilson Way Bridge with a sweet half mile downhill to the Puget Sound and Dune Peninsula Park where the Half Marathon will finish. The Marathon will continue down the flat and fast waterfront with views of Mt. Rainier and the Puget Sound. The Marathon turnaround is along the Thea Foss Waterway Esplanade and the beautiful Museum of Glass.

name: Tacoma City Turkey Trot
description:
It’s a family affair! The Tacoma City Turkey Trot offers a 5K Run/Walk and a 1K Kids Run in Tacoma’s beautiful Proctor District.

Gobble gobble! The Tacoma City Turkey Trot is a fun 5K Run and Walk on Thanksgiving morning starting at Fleet Feet Tacoma! Whether you are a runner looking for a new PR or you are a walker, there’s no greater way to start your Thanksgiving holiday by coming together with the community and earning that pumpkin pie! We encourage Thanksgiving costumes & accessories!

The Tacoma City Turkey Trot Kids 1K on Thanksgiving morning is a fun way to get the kids (12 and under) to participate! Grown-ups can run with their kids and do not have to register for this distance. We encourage Thanksgiving costumes & accessories!

The Tacoma City Turkey Trot Kids 1K on Thanksgiving morning is a fun way to get the kids (12 and under) to participate! Grown-ups can run with their kids and do not have to register for this distance. We encourage Thanksgiving costumes & accessories!

name: Tacoma Independence Day 5K
description:
Join us for the Annual Independence Day 5K on July 4th for a fun and FAST 5K! This event features a fast point-to-point course that takes runners and walkers from the top of Tacoma and finishes at beautiful Point Ruston.

The 5K is a chip timed race on a fast, flat and downhill course starting at N 37th St & N Vassault St in Tacoma, close to Vassault Park, and finishing at the newly renovated Owen Beach at Pt. Defiance Park. While this is a speedy course for fast runners, it also is a fun course for a power walk before your Independence Day barbecue! Everybody is welcome to participate!

The Owen Beach finish line is also where the Kids 1K will start at 9:15 am. The kid’s run is an out-and-back, so the runners can cross the official finish line as well!

name: Tacoma Narrows Half Marathon / 10K / 5K
description:
Take me out to the ballgame, but first run over the bridge! Feed me a bagel and electrolytes, I just hope that my hamstrings aren’t tight!

The Tacoma Narrows Half Marathon is back, featuring a Half Marathon 10K and 5K course that begins and ends at Cheney Stadium! We’re partnering with the Tacoma Rainiers, it’s going to be a weekend full of running and baseball fun!

The Tacoma Narrows Half Marathon is an out-and-back course that will start outside Cheney Stadium, you’ll then run along the Scott Pierson Trail, cross the pedestrian bridge over highway 16 and run through the quiet Skyline neighborhood* then take you across the majestic Tacoma Narrows Bridge and bring you back inside Cheney Stadium, where you’ll run on the warning track (and where you will see yourself on the jumbotron and be able to say “Look Ma, I made it!”).

*You’ll cross the Skyline Bridge again on the way back and run the neighborhood loop again on the way back to Cheney Stadium.

The Tacoma Narrows 10K & 5K course will also start and finish at Cheney Stadium and include a lap around the warning track.

name: Ten Trails Active Club 5k Turkey Trot
description:
Join the Club!

PLEASE READ ALL OF THIS

We're back at it again for our 4th year! Given that we had over 250 people register for last year's race; you heard that right... 250! We are asking that everyone register as soon as possible so that we can have our ducks in a row come race day!

Registration will be capped at ~250 people and I will NOT accept race day signups like we have in the past. I'm also asking this year that we do not register kids in strollers, on bikes, or anyone/thing not planning to complete the entire 5k course on their own. This is to help ensure that we leave as many spots open for other racers as possible. Kids in strollers are of course still welcome on the course :)

As we've mentioned before, these events are organized and hosted by a very small group of people (less than 5) who pay out-of-pocket and donate their time to ensure these community events continue. During the registration process, you will be asked to donate - please consider a $5 minimum donation to the club to help ensure we can continue to afford and host these events in the future. We will also be selling enamel race/club pins and Pulse Brewed Coffee at the event. Sales of which will go to funding our ongoing club activities. We appreciate your support and understanding!

Onto the race details! We will be continuing to use the same course as last year and will be providing snacks at the end as usual. I will try to have some Pulse Brewed Coffee our there too!! Remember, the race will be hand-timed on an open course, so please be safe out there and comply with the finish line rules to help ensure the event runs smoothly and we're able to quickly compile results at the end :) Remember, we ask everyone to show up 20-30 minutes prior to the start of the race so that everyone gets checked in for a prompt 8:30am race start.

The event is open to folks of all skill levels. There will be prize categories for both walkers and runners, and if you're lucky, you may even get to bring home one of our Thanksgiving Day desserts that will be raffled off after the event!

Lastly, in the spirit of thanksgiving, we will again be collecting food donations for a local food bank during the event. If you are able, all donations are greatly appreciated.

See you out there!

~Coach Dalty
