$40 - Regular Registration w/ Lakad Shirt (August 16-September 1)
$40 - Late Registration, Shirt Not Guaranteed (September 2-6)

 

RACE DAY SCHEDULE

  • 8am Runner Check In
  • 9am Race Begins
  • 10:00am-1pm  Kick back in the park and enjoy some Filipino food, vendors, activities, and live performances.

name: 15th Annual Canby Dahlia Run
description:
Experience the 15th Annual Canby Dahlia Run—where flower fields, farmlands, and countryside charm guide every step. Whether you’re chasing a personal record or enjoying a brisk walk, this is a race like no other.

Organized by the Canby Area Chamber of Commerce, this event drew over 500 participants in 2025—and we’re aiming to sell out again in 2026!


Race Overview


Distances:

+ 5K and 10K run/walk

Course:

+ Start and finish at Swan Island Dahlias
+ Mostly paved roads with a short gravel stretch;  5 & 10K includes a small grass segment leading to the finish

Timing:

+ Chip-timed by Athletic Timing
+ UHF coded bib chips
+ Live results available online and at the finish line
 
Registration:

+ INCLUDES: Official Race T-shirt (deadline is 8/28/26), finisher medal, free parking, and entry to the Swan Island Dahlia Festival
+ ADVANCE REGISTRATION: RunSignUp.com
+ RACE-DAY REGISTRATION: Opens 6:00 AM (if not sold out—updates on Facebook)
   Note: Prices increase closer to race day. Early registration is encouraged.

Race Day Schedule:

   6:00 AM – Race-Day Check-in
   7:00 AM – 5K & 10K RUNNERS Start 
   7:05 AM – 5K & 10K WALKERS Start 
   11:00 AM – Course officially closes

 
Packet Pickup:

Tuesday, September 8, 2026 from 10:00am-6:00pm - Canby Area Chamber Office (191 SE 2nd Ave., Canby, OR 97013)

Wednesday, September 9, 2026 from 10:00am-6:00pm - Canby Area Chamber Office (191 SE 2nd Ave., Canby, OR 97013)

Thursday, September 10, 2026 from 10:00am-6:00pm - Canby Area Chamber Office (191 SE 2nd Ave., Canby, OR 97013)

Friday, September 11, 2025, 2:00-5:30pm - Swan Island Dahlias (995 NW 22nd Ave., Canby, OR 97013)

 

Parking:

Free parking at Swan Island Dahlias (grass field) managed by venue staff
Carpooling recommended due to limited space
 
Course Support:

   Medical & Aid Station: CPR/AED & First Aid available at course start/finish. 
   Water Stations: Located along each course—participants should also hydrate before the race
   Restrooms: Portable toilets at start/finish and mid-course
 
Policies & Restrictions:

   Distance Changes: May switch down in distance (no refunds; difference goes to Chamber as donation). No switching up on race day.
   Refunds & Transfers: Non-refundable, but you may transfer your registration to someone else.
   Pets: No dogs or pets on course; none may be left unattended in vehicles or at venue.
   Strollers: Not allowed.
   Wheelchairs/Handcycles/Barefoot: Welcome if terrain (pavement, gravel, grass) is manageable.
   Headphones/Hearing Devices:

  • General Rule: Headphones are permitted but not encouraged; if used, one ear must remain uncovered for safety.
  • Accessibility Exception: Runners who use assistive hearing devices (e.g., AirPods, bone-conduction headphones, or other adaptive technologies) may use them in both ears, provided the transparency/adaptive sound features are enabled to allow awareness of surroundings.
  • Purpose: These guidelines are in place to maintain runner safety and ensure participants can hear course instructions, traffic, volunteers, and other runners.
  • Responsibility: Runners using headphones are responsible for keeping volumes at safe levels and remaining attentive to their environment.


Weather:

This is a Rain or Shine Event—no refunds for weather delays or cancellations.
 
Finish Line & Awards:

All finishers receive:

   + Medal
   + Fresh-cut Dahlia
   + Free entry to the Swan Island Dahlia Festival
   + Top 3 male and female finishers (5K & 10K, chip times) receive awards per age divisions—must be picked up on race day (no mailing).

  • Categories are: 14 & under | 15–19 | 20–29 | 30–39 | 40–49 | 50–59 | 60–69 | 70+
     

After Party:

   + Water and light snacks at finish line
   + Food available for purchase from on-site vendors
   + Explore Canby’s downtown for additional food, drinks, and events (Canby Area Chamber of Commerce Events)
 
Course Map:

Visit our website or facebook page for both course maps.
 
Questions?
Email the Canby Area Chamber of Commerce for more information.

name: 1st Annual Ostomy 5k, Portland OR
description:
Get ready, Portland! Join us for the 1st Annual Run for Resilience Ostomy 5K on Saturday, October 3rd as we come together to celebrate Ostomy Awareness Day with purpose, pride, and a whole lot of heart. 

This family-friendly event is more than just a run, it’s a celebration of strength, community, and resilience. Enjoy a vibrant morning filled with local vendors, great food, music, and plenty of fun for all ages. Bring your friend and family and meet us at the beautiful Laurelhurst Park for a day you won’t want to miss.

All proceeds support United Ostomy Associations of America, Inc. (UOAA), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to education, advocacy, and empowering the ostomy community nationwide. Donations are tax deductible. Learn more at www.ostomy.org

Race Day Schedule: To Be Announced - Stay Tuned!

name: 2025 17th Annual Stumptown XC Series
description:
The Stumptown Cross series is back for 2025!  Whether you race as an individual or are part of a team, these races are always competitive, and a lot of fun.  If you feel like challenging yourself on some grassy, uneven terrain, then make plans to join us this fall.  These ain't no stinkin' road races!

For 2025 we have a 5-race series lined up:

9/27 Gabriel Park 5K both races
10/11 Lents Park 5K both races 
10/25 Blue Lake 6K both races 
11/08 Fernhill Park 6K/8K
11/22 Pier Park 6k/8K

Women and men race separately at each venue. Women's races begin at 9:00am, with the men's races beginning at 9:40 (for events where women race 5k) and 9:45 when women race a 6k.  Start times and course maps are available on the Stumptown XC Facebook group.
Non-binary athletes are allowed to choose whether they wish to run in the Mens or Womens race, and will be listed in the results as non-binary.

Cost

  • The cost is $80 for the entire series for non TRL members or $55 for TRL members. Series registration includes registration in all five races. 
  • Cost to register for individual races is $30 ($20 for TRL members).  
  • Note that there is a $5 parking fee per vehicle at Blue Lake Regional Park. Carpooling is recommended. No pets are allowed at the park!

name: 2025 17th Annual Stumptown XC Series
description:
The Stumptown Cross series is back for 2025!  Whether you race as an individual or are part of a team, these races are always competitive, and a lot of fun.  If you feel like challenging yourself on some grassy, uneven terrain, then make plans to join us this fall.  These ain't no stinkin' road races!

For 2025 we have a 5-race series lined up:

9/27 Gabriel Park 5K both races
10/11 Lents Park 5K both races 
10/25 Blue Lake 6K both races 
11/08 Fernhill Park 6K/8K
11/22 Pier Park 6k/8K

Women and men race separately at each venue. Women's races begin at 9:00am, with the men's races beginning at 9:40 (for events where women race 5k) and 9:45 when women race a 6k.  Start times and course maps are available on the Stumptown XC Facebook group.
Non-binary athletes are allowed to choose whether they wish to run in the Mens or Womens race, and will be listed in the results as non-binary.

Cost

  • The cost is $80 for the entire series for non TRL members or $55 for TRL members. Series registration includes registration in all five races. 
  • Cost to register for individual races is $30 ($20 for TRL members).  
  • Note that there is a $5 parking fee per vehicle at Blue Lake Regional Park. Carpooling is recommended. No pets are allowed at the park!

name: 2026 Bend Beer Run
description:
What’s Included in Your Registration Fee:

  • A scenic, untimed 5K route through Drake Park and downtown Bend, along the beautiful Deschutes River.
  • Four craft beer stops featuring local breweries along the race course.
  • Entry to The Little Woody Festival, where you can enjoy:
    • A Little Woody Tasting Glass
    • Six drink tokens for beer or cider of your choice
    • Live music, games, and barrel-aged brews.
  • Costume contest prizes for the best-dressed participants—grab your friends and get creative!
  • Event bib for the race.

Event Details:

Check-in:

Begins at 11:00 AM at The Commons Café (875 NW Brooks St., Bend, OR).
Pick up your bib and get ready to run!

Race Start:

The race kicks off promptly at 12:00 PM outside The Commons Café.

Course Information:

This untimed 5K is all about the experience—run, walk, or jog while enjoying beer stops and the lively atmosphere.

Finish Line:

The finish brings you directly into The Little Woody Festival, where your post-race celebration begins!


Important Notes:

This is a 21+ event.
Costumes are highly encouraged for a chance to win fun prizes.
Additional details can be found on the race website. 

Location: Start at The Commons, Finish at Deschutes Historical Museum
 
Join the Bend Beer Run for a brew-tiful blend of fitness, fun, and fantastic craft beer!

name: 2026 Coast Busters Walk for Breast Cancer - Florence, OR
description:
Join us for the CoastBusters Walk for Breast Cancer—a 3-mile FUNdraising walk in Florence, OR on Saturday, October 3, 2026, at Siuslaw Middle School.

CoastBusters was created to bring community, compassion, and tangible support to others facing a diagnosis. This walk is a chance to come together to honor, remember, and stand alongside those navigating breast cancer today.

Early registration runs June 1 through August 31, 2026, and includes a free event T-shirt.

Proceeds from the walk stay local, providing direct support to breast cancer patients in the coastal cities of Lane County. Funds help ease the financial burden of treatment by assisting with things like travel for care, lodging, groceries, and other day-to-day needs so patients can focus on healing.

Whether you walk for yourself, for someone you love, or simply to make a difference, we invite you to be part of this meaningful CoastBusters Walk and the community it brings together.

name: 2026 Happy Girls Sisters
description:
Enjoy some bonding time with women of all ages and levels in the appropriately named town of Sisters, Oregon. Choose between the all-women’s trail half marathon featuring single-track in the Deschutes National Forest (on the Peterson Ridge Trail system) with some pretty stellar views or take part in the 5K and 10K road race that winds through scenic downtown Sisters. All races cross the same finish line, welcoming all to enjoy the beautiful FivePine campus under the towering Ponderosa pines.

**Make sure to register early – the half marathon is limited to 500 runners and sells out every year.

name: 2026 Haulin Aspen
description:
Mountain Trail Running Has Never Been Better

One of Oregon’s favorite trail full marathon and half marathon races returns for the 22nd year on Saturday, August 8th, 2026. 

No pavement here. Featuring a full all-trail marathon, a half marathon, and a 6.5-mile course (dubbed the “Half As”), the Haulin’ Aspen features beautiful trails that wind through the Deschutes National Forest, showcasing some epic views. With varying terrain and elevation, the cool wooded pine setting provides a challenging and exciting experience. Enjoy the beautiful single track, steep trails, fast descents, and amazing views starting at an elevation of nearly 5500'. Make it a destination this summer – Bend and the Cascades welcome you!

NEW THIS YEAR:

The Haulin' Aspen full marathon introduces a three-person relay option, giving teams the chance to experience the full 26.2 mile all-trail course together. The race begins and Wanoga Sno Park, where Runner 1 takes on the first 9.6 miles to Transition 1 at Aid Station 3. Runner 2 then covers the longest leg - approximately 11.7 miles - continuing along the course to Transition 2 at Aid Station 7 (mile 21.3). From there Runner 3 tackles the final 4.9 mile stretch - an uphill push back to the finish at Wanoga. This new format offers a dynamic way to share the challenge while still taking in the scenic, high-elevation terrain of the course.

name: 2026 Hood Hundred
description:
Welcome to Hood Hundred presented by Speedland, a 100 mile mountain trail run on much of Mt. Hood’s most diverse and scenic terrain! Featuring a super crew-accessible lollipop-style course with 17,700’ of ascent and 17,700’ descent, Hood Hundred offers a truly epic and memorable mountain trail endurance run experience.

Staged at Mt. Hood Meadows, a locally owned and operated ski area, Hood Hundred combines equal parts trail running community vibes and professional event production, where we celebrate the sport of trail running, honor the mountain and celebrate each other’s accomplishments under the volcano’s summit at the finish line.

Land Acknowledgement: We honor and recognize that we gather for this event on the traditional lands of the Molalla, Kalapuyan, Chinookan Clackamas, Wasco and Wishram, and Northern Paiute peoples and other Sahaptin speakers who have occupied and stewarded these lands for countless generations.

description:

name: 2026 Runtoberfest - Support McMinnville Schools!
description:
Runtoberfest is a 5K Run/Walk, and Kid's Mile (12 and under) to support the McMinnville Education Foundation that starts and finishes at McMinnville High School’s Wortman Stadium! Help support McMinnville schools at this family-friendly event! Registration for the 5K is $35 online and $48 day of race.  Choose your school affiliation for a chance to win the Golden Shoe Trophy for your Mac 40 school you would like to support.  

Race Day Schedule:
8am: Bib Pickup Starts (please arrive early!)
8:30am: Kids Mile
8:45an: Registration Ends
8:50am: Walkers-only Start
9am: Main Race Start

Bib pickup starts at 8am. Please arrive early to avoid congestion. Day of race registration is only available from 8am to 8:45am. The race organizers would appreciate registering online before the event to minimize day of race registration congestion.

name: 2026 Tillamook YMCA Milk Run
description:
Welcome to the 2026 Milk Run! 

This event features a 2 mile walk/run, 5k walk/run and 10k run in the heart of Tillamook, Oregon. An 8:00am shot-gun allows for plenty of time to participate on the June Dairy Parade and Rodeo

Start and finish at the Tillamook YMCA and enjoy scenic pastures, waterways, and mountain views as you wind your way through the back roads of Tillamook. Turnaround points and water stations will guide you through your leg of the course.

Make it a day of fun on the Oregon coast!

Location: 610 Stillwell Ave, Tillamook, OR 97141
Start time: 8:00 am

Register early – rates increase $10 on June 15th!

Race shirts are not guaranteed with registrations after June 15th.

Questions? Contact info@tillamookymca.org or 503-842-9622 x 104

name: 2026 Wyeast Trailfest
description:
Wy'east Trailfest presented by Speedland is a celebration of mountain trail running featuring Mt. Hood’s illustrious alpine terrain. Wildly beautiful, dynamic and challenging 50 miler, 50K, 28K & 14K mountain courses reach Oregon’s alpine rooftop at 8000’ on Saturday, followed by more cruisy and scenic Half Marathon & 8K (5 miler) trail races on Sunday for those looking for a more approachable trail experience! The Kids Race rounds out the weekend in heartwarming fashion on Sunday as well.

Whether racing, volunteering or spectating, join us up high on Wy'east (the native ancestral name for Mt. Hood) to honor the mountain, celebrate the sport of trail running and this incredible community. We’ll cheer and shout every single runner’s name at the finish as we celebrate with awards, great food, craft beverages, fun finish line games and activities up high at Mt. Hood Meadows.

name: 2027 Happy Girls Bend Run
description:
Calling all Happy Girls!!

The 17th Annual Happy Girls Run series returns to Central Oregon with its first race of the season in Bend, Oregon. Participants of all abilities can choose from the all-women’s Half Marathon, 10K, or 5K races.  

You will be graced with gorgeous scenic views on a mix of trails, groomed paths, and paved surfaces. Cross the finish line and enjoy the post-race party with a fabulous gift bag and a unique Happy Girls medal. Adult beverages and food are provided.

Grab your friends, make a weekend of it, design a team costume, and let's go, girls!

name: 2027 Hot Cocoa Run
description:
Join us on Saturday, Feb 14 for the return of the Hot Cocoa Run!

⭐️ Race entry includes admission to all three days of WinterFest! ⭐️

 

Early registration will close on Thursday, February 12 at midnight. Any latecomers can sign up on-site on Sunday morning starting at 11 am.

RACE STARTS AT NOON

🚨 Check-In Details 🚨
WinterFest entry is included with your registration! All Hot Cocoa Run attendees will receive an emailed WinterFest ticket to your email on file for the run. You will use this ticket to gain entry to WinterFest NOT your registration. Our volunteers at the entry gates can also look up your name if you can not find your WinterFest ticket.

Don't forget to check in! Your QR code will be scanned to get your registration information. Print your QR code or have it available on your phone when you arrive. 

Check-In Options

Packet pickup will be available at
Location: Old Mill District  - SEE COURSE MAP FOR EXACT LOCATION. We will do our best to have signage to direct you to the start area.
Date: Sunday, February 15
Check In Time: 11 am -12 pm

Race starts promptly at noon.

A fun 5K with a full Hot Cocoa bar at the finish with toppings and Crater Lake spirits.

The Hot Cocoa Run will take place during WinterFest 2026 celebrating the magic of winter Feb. 13 - Feb. 15 at the Old Mill in Bend, OR.

This will be an untimed 5K loop on Sunday at noon during the Northwest’s biggest festival. A full hot cocoa bar with all the toppings and Crater Lake spirits, including espresso vodka, await one and all at the finish line. Costumes are encouraged!

name: 2027 Salmon Run
description:
Join us for the 39th annual Salmon Run which returns to Bend, Oregon on April 17, 2027.

Distances include the HALF MARATHON (13.1 miles), 10K, and 5K races. All courses weave along the beautiful Deschutes River on trails and some pavement.

Taking place in the spring, the Salmon Run is one of the first running events of the season and the essential tip-off to the local racing scene in Central Oregon. Traversing beautiful dirt and paved trails amongst junipers and pines, the race course winds through some of the most scenic natural areas in Bend and finishes on the lawn Riverbend Park. Make a weekend of it!

Course Details  

The Salmon Run course takes runners along the beautiful and picturesque Deschutes River.  The half marathon course is 75% paved sidewalks and 25% trail.  The 10K course is 80% paved sidewalks and 20% trail.  The 5K is 65% paved sidewalks and 35% trail.  All courses will be marked with a combination of mile markers and directional arrows.

Finish Line Festivities

Enjoy a post-race party with delicious food and beverages (beer!) and music. We’ve got gift bags and awards for the top three male and female finishers in both open and master’s categories! 1st, 2nd & 3rd place ribbons for top age-group finishers.

Parking for Race Day

There is limited parking at Riverbend Park on race day. We highly recommend carpooling. Parking attendants will direct you as you arrive. Additional parking is available on City streets. 

For full details regarding the Salmon Run, click here.

name: 3D Cross Country Sommer Camp
description:
Join the 3D Running Club for the annual “3D Cross Country Sommer Camp”, named after 3D Running Club founder Coach Jeff Sommer.

 


Camp Dates: June 30th – July 7th

 


This year’s camp will take place in Eugene, Oregon, where we will be staying near the University of Oregon, home of one of the most historic track and field programs in the world.

 


Campers will have the incredible opportunity to attend the Prefontaine Classic, one of the most prestigious track and field meets in the world, featuring many of the best professional runners on the planet.

 


Throughout the week we will train, explore the legendary running trails of Eugene, and experience the culture of “TrackTown USA.” Campers will also take part in team runs, workouts, and activities designed to build fitness, knowledge, and team camaraderie.

We are excited to host our campers and make this an unforgettable running experience in the heart of American distance running.

name: 4th Annual Teal Ribbon Family Fun Walk at the Oregon Zoo to Raise Ovarian Cancer Awareness!
description:
Ovarian Cancer

About 21,010 women in the United States are expected to be diagnosed with ovarian cancer in 2026 — that’s roughly one diagnosis every 25 minutes. In Oregon and Washington, the American Cancer Society estimates 1,610 new diagnoses. These are our grandmothers, mothers, sisters, partners, colleagues, and friends.
Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecologic cancer and the fifth leading cause of cancer-related death among women in the United States. Because symptoms are often subtle and easily dismissed, nearly three-quarters of cases are diagnosed after the cancer has spread beyond the ovaries. While the overall five-year survival rate is about 50 percent, survival drops significantly — to around 30 percent — when the disease is diagnosed at a distant stage.

Call to Action: Teal Ribbon Fun Walk

These statistics make one thing clear: awareness matters. That’s why OCAOSW is hosting the 4th Annual Teal Ribbon Fun Walk on June 27, 2026. There is currently no reliable screening test for ovarian cancer, which makes education about symptoms and risk factors critical. When ovarian cancer is detected at an earlier stage, survival rates improve significantly — and informed communities are better equipped to act.
This 1.5-mile walk at the Oregon Zoo brings together survivors, families, friends, and advocates in visible support of those impacted by ovarian cancer. It’s a chance to show up, stand together, and move the conversation forward.

 Goals

  • Promote education and awareness about ovarian cancer
  • Unite our local ovarian cancer community, including survivors, friends, families, medical professionals, and advocates, for a common goal
  • Raise funds for OCAOSW - donate here

name: A Race for the Rest of Us
description:
*The Race Preferred T-Shirt Deadline is July 12th - we may or may not have your preferred size if you register after this day*

A RACE FOR THE REST OF US

Race Overview

*The Race Preferred T-Shirt Deadline is July 12th - we may or may not have your preferred size if you register after this day*

Senior & Disability Services, a division of Lane Council of Governments, is hosting their 6th annual A Race for the Rest of Us! This is a "race for a good cause" - to raise money for the Senior Meals Program at Senior & Disability Services, which provides food to Lane County seniors who might otherwise go hungry. The distance is a whopping 0.5k - nope, that is not a typo! That is a half kilometer or about one third of a mile, or about 546 yards, or about 1640 feet, or about twice as far as the average good golfer can hit a golf ball off of a tee - you get the idea.

Unable to join the race in person? No problem! You can participate in the 0.5k from wherever you are in the world! 

Every participant gets a T-shirt, a finisher’s medal, and a race sticker to show off your race completion and your support for Senior Meals! Have you seen those oval stickers on the back of someone’s car with the numbers on them? Yep, like that, only much cooler!

  • Distance: in person 0.5k & virtual 0.5k 
  • Race Day: Sunday, August 2nd, 2026, 12pm
  • Swag: T-Shirt, Sticker, Medal!
  • Location: PublicHouse, 418 A Street, Springfield, OR 97477, and also virtually.
  • Terrain: Flat concrete (sidewalk)

Come walk/run/roll with us or do it on your own time. Whatever works best for you. Proceeds from the event will be donated to the Senior & Disability Services Senior Meals Program in Lane County. 

Since this race benefits seniors 60+ in Lane County, seniors that sign up to "race" with us will get a $5 dollar discount! 

Ages 12 and under: $20
Ages 13-59: $30
Ages 60+: $5 discount so only $25 

PACKET PICK UP

Packets can be picked up on Friday, July 31st from 1-5pm at 859 Willamette St., Eugene, OR 5th floor. Packets can also be picked up day of race (August 2nd) starting at 12pm.

SHIRTS & BIBS

Shirts and bibs are printed specifically for each participant. Once a registration is complete (paid for), it cannot be changed. If you chose the in-person option, packet pick-up will be the day of the race or on Friday, July 31st at Lane Council of Governments, 859 Willamette St., Ste 500, Eugene, OR from 1-5pm. If you choose a virtual option, your packet will be available for pick up on August 2nd or shipped directly to you! 

ABOUT THE SENIOR MEALS PROGRAM

The Senior Meals Program is a nutrition wellness program which helps Lane County adults aged 60 and up maintain their independence by providing healthy meals and opportunities to develop and maintain vital social connections. S&DS operates 9 Cafe 60 Meal Sites throughout Lane County and provides nutritious meals, friendly visits, regular safety and wellness checks, and access to a myriad of other community-based services to seniors in their home through the Meals on Wheels program. S&DS serves over 36,000 Cafe 60 meals and delivers over 96,000 Meals on Wheels each year, reaching over 1,400 Lane County seniors. 

To learn more about the Senior Meals Program, please visit https://www.lcog-or.gov/sdslane/page/senior-meals-program

Frequently Asked Questions

  • This is just my speed, can I walk the whole way? Yes! Walk, run, skip, push or pull a wagon, you decide!
  • Is this "race" wheelchair, power chair, and walker friendly? Yes! However you decide to roll to the finish!
  • Is this "race" stroller friendly? Of course!
  • Is this "race" dog friendly? Yes!

name: Boring Marathon, Half-Boring Half Marathon, Constantly Boring 10K, and Somewhat Boring 5K Race Series
description:
The 13th Annual Boring Marathon, Half-Boring Half-Marathon, Constantly Boring 10K, and Somewhat Boring 5K will take place on Sunday, September 13, 2026. All races start and finish at Boring Station Trailhead Park in downtown Boring, Oregon. Parking will be at Boring Middle School, Naas Elementary School, Boring-Damascus Grange, and the surrounding neighborhood. Please make sure to check out the updated parking map, as we have been able to add almost 100 additional parking spots. As always please respect the neighbors by not blocking driveways or fence openings, fire hydrants, or parking where 'no parking' sings are posted. Please use SE Wally Rd and SE School Ave to reach parking after 6:15 am, as runners will be crossing SE Dee St. The four races are all on the Springwater Trail, out and back, with the marathon being 2-loops of the half marathon course. Both the Half Marathon and Marathon Courses are certified courses and the Marathon Course is once again a Boston Qualifier!

The Boring Marathon Course runs the half marathon course twice and you will get a half marathon split time when you turn for lap 2. The course is USATF Certified Certificate # OR24005JH. 

The Half Boring Half Marathon is an out-and-back on the Springwater Trail from Boring Stations Trailhead Park to Towle Ave and back. This course is now a USATF certified Half Marathon course. Certificate # OR24004JH.

The Constantly Boring 10K, which gets really close to the City of Gresham boundary, but never leaves the Boring area, is just a constantly Boring stroll. This race starts at the same spot as the others and is a short 5k out and back course. This race sold out the fastest in 2025, so register early!

The Somewhat Boring 5K, never really leaves the Boring area so truly is just somewhat Boring, starts at the same spot and is a short out and back course. 

For 2026, as like the last few years we will continue to offer a virtual option for those that would like to earn the Boring Shirt and Medal, but cannot travel to our lovely little city.

Race Entry Limits - Marathon is limited to 100 entries, the Half Marathon to 220 entries, the 10K to 140 entries, the 5K 140 entries, and Virtual (Unlimited).

Packet Pick-up Locations and Times - 
Packet Pickup (Friday before the race - September 11) - Boring Brewing Co. Tasting Room (38250 Pioneer Blvd, Sandy, OR 97055) 5:00 pm to 8:00 pm

Packet Pickup (Saturday before the race - September 12) - Boring Station Trailhead Park (28008 Keller Road Boring, OR 97009) 4:00 pm to 7:00 pm

Packet Pickup (Race day - September 13) - Boring Station Trailhead Park (28008 Keller Road Boring, OR 97009) starting at 5:15 am and until each respective race starts.

Time limit - Walkers are welcome, but because we run part of the race along roads, we need to discontinue aid stations and traffic control after 7 hours. However, we will keep the finish line open and staffed until the last runner/walker comes in and nobody will be disqualified by time. Early starts can be arranged - but are not required - for marathoners or half marathoners who expect to take longer than 6 hours. The early start is at 5:30 am.

Boring Sister City of Dull, Scotland - any resident of Dull, Scotland gets free registration (but you pay the travel)

Awards - All entries prior to August 23, 2026 are guaranteed to receive a shirt in their first size choice. Shirts are not guaranteed after August 30th, but we will do our best to order enough shirts to get everyone a shirt. Everyone will get a medal, including our virtual runners! To help guide a shirt choice, we will only be purchasing unisex cut shirts. We use the A4 Cooling Performance Crew for sizing help. 

Refunds & Deferrals - Unfortunately, we cannot offer refunds once you have registered. Deferrals are offered only in rare circumstances.

There will be NO day of race registration.

Changing races - If you signed up for a race and wish to change to a different race, please contact the race director before August 30th at racedirector@boringmarathon.com. There is no refund for the difference in cost when changing races.

The Boring Marathon, Half Marathon, 10K, and 5K are all USATF certified and insured races.

name: Bowerman 5K
description:
Register for the 2026 Bowerman 5k Registration today! 
We are excited to announce the 15th edition of the annual Bowerman 5k! 

This year’s event will be held on Saturday, July 25th, at Nike WHQ. In addition to the main event, we are bringing back the free elementary school 1km race before the running of our annual 5k. 

SCHEDULE
9:30am Kids 1k Race (FREE!)
10:05am  Bowerman 5k

LOCATION/COURSE:
Held at the Nike World Headquarters, participants will run a closed-off interior road within the campus. The smooth tarmac loops around the beautiful Nike WHQ campus, starting and finishing at the Lebron James Courtyard. Race-bib pickup, vendors, and giveaways will take place in the Mia Hamm Courtyard close to the start line.

TEAMS/CLUBS
Calling all Clubs, Corporate teams, and Social Groups!
Whether you're part of a run club, a corporate team, or a social group of friends and family, we encourage you to register as a team! You must have 5 runners to complete a team. The largest team will earn free entries to the 2027 Bowerman 5k! 
Please email dominic.arce@bowermantc.com with any questions

MEMBER ENTRIES
Bowerman Athletes with an active annual membership get Free Entry to the Bowerman 5k! Visit the Bowerman Membership Page to learn more about how you can register to become a Bowerman Athlete and get exclusive access to perks and a free entry to the 5k! Members will receive an email in June to claim their registration.

ELITES
Elite Athletes will have a separate start corral. Please complete the elite entry form. Prize money awarded to the top 3 athletes in Men's and Women's categories.
Contact Race Coordinator dominic.arce@bowermantc.com with inquiries

FUNDRAISING: 
Help us continue to support athletes chasing their dreams within the BTC Community. 
All donations will go directly toward scholarship opportunities to support race opportunities for athletes in the Bowerman Youth Cross Country and Track Program. 
You can have an impact even if you aren’t racing! Encourage family and friends to donate under your registration link. 

ABOUT
Started in 2010, the Bowerman 5k is an annual road race held in the month of July at the Nike Campus in Beaverton, Oregon.  The 5k is a great opportunity to get the whole family involved in a fun and active event.  Our competitors include young kids, stroller walkers, competitive masters and elite runners, and we encourage all ages and abilities to come and join the fun.  If you’re looking for a 5k personal best, the course is a fast one!  Over the years, the race’s popularity has grown and in 2015 it was rated as one of the 7 Must-Do 5k Races in the United States by Competitor Magazine.

name: Bush Park Thursday Nights in August Race Series
description:
Bush Park Thursday Night Races – August 2026


Join us this August for another exciting season of Bush Park Thursday Night Races! Whether you're chasing a personal best or just out for some fun with the local running community, this family-friendly series is a summer favorite.

🏃 Race Info & Registration
This year’s 3K and 5K courses have remained the same from the previous year, and the overall race format remains the same.

Online registration is available via RunSignUp and is highly encouraged. Same-day registration will also be available onsite as in previous years.

💡 Pro tip: Register for multiple races at once to save on processing fees!

Online registration closes each Wednesday night before race day.
Kids' races (500m & 1600m) are in-person registration only, on race night.

📅 Race Nights & Schedule
Join us on Thursdays: August 6th, 13th, 20th, 27th — final week being Ribbon/Awards Night!

**WVRR club members get discounts on all our races, so be sure to join the club. Your membership fees go directly to making these races happen and towards our donation programs and our annual Kelsy Oldham Memorial Scholarship. To learn more, visit our site linked above.**

Evening Schedule:

5:00 PM – Registration Table Opens
6:00 PM – 3000 Meters (Open to All) – $10
6:20 PM – 500 Meters (Ages Under 7) – FREE
6:35 PM – 1600 Meters (Ages 7–12) – FREE
6:50 PM – 5000 Meters (Open to All) – $10

💙 Community Impact
Your participation helps support:

name: CASA Fall Family Run presented by McDonald's of the Gorge
description:
We’re excited to return to the Mark O. Hatfield West Trailhead in Hood River for Columbia Gorge CASA’s 3rd Annual Fall Family Run, proudly presented by McDonald’s of the Gorge. Join us on October 3rd for a fun, family-friendly event set against the stunning backdrop of the Columbia River Gorge—all in support of Columbia Gorge CASA’s advocacy for children who have experienced abuse and neglect.

Rain or shine, we’ll be ready to go—so bring your best weather-ready spirit and join us for a great day outdoors in support of a meaningful cause. Race entries are nonrefundable; however, race insurance is available when registering online and may provide reimbursement depending on coverage. Hydration stations will be along the race route powered by Studio Fit. 

Our fall-themed costume contest returns this year—come dressed in your best autumn-inspired look and show off your seasonal spirit.

Oct. 3rd (Tentative Schedule.) 

8:00 AM - Packet Pick Up 

8:40 AM - Welcome 

8:45 AM - Playhouse Raffle Winner Announcement 

8:50 AM - Costume Contest 

9:00 AM - Race 

2025 RACE RESULTS

name: CASA of Marion County Superhero Run
description:
Join us for CASA of Marion County's Superhero Run!

Not all superheroes wear capes; some run or walk! Join CASA of Marion County at Salem Riverfront Park for our annual Superhero Run. Kid-friendly and costumes strongly encouraged! Through its volunteers, CASA of Marion County advocates for abused and neglected children in foster care. 

All registered 5K and 10K participants receive a Race Day T-shirt thanks to Maps Credit Union and Inova Solutions!

CASA has partnered with Travel Salem - Sports Commission for great perks including discount hotel stays at our Host Hotel partner - The Grand Hotel. For additional information: Click Here  

 

EVENT DAY SCHEDULE OF EVENTS

7:00: Check-In Opens at Riverfront Park Rotary Pavilion

7:30: Festival with booths from our donors, sponsors, community partners, food and fun open until 1:00pm!

8:00: Opening Ceremony – VIP Speakers kickoff event (photo ops)

8:30: Superhero Costume Contest

9:00: 10k runners begin

9:00: 5k runners begin

9:10: One-mile fun run begins

11:00: Course closes

 1:00: Event ends

name: Cherry City Half Marathon, 10K, 5K & Kids Race
description:
Runners and walkers of all ages and skill levels are invited to enjoy a fun, fast and beautiful course in Salem, Oregon. After the race, be sure to stay and enjoy music and awards, cheer on our kids race runners and enjoy award-winning Oregon wines and craft beer!


Sunday September 13, 2026
Riverfront Park - Salem, OR


Event Start Times:

8:00 am - Half Marathon
8:05 am - 10K
8:10 am - 5K
10:30 am - Kids Run (untimed kids 0.4 mile run or walk)


What's Included:

  • Official Race Shirt
  • Special Finisher Medal
  • An awesome finisher party including live music and award winning Oregon beer wine & cider
  • Overall awards for top three male and female finishers
  • Masters (40+) awards for top three masters male and female finishers in each race distance
  • Age group awards for top three male and female finishers per category (See Below)
  • An amazing day amongst friends, new friends and fellow participants!

 

Key Event Details:

Dogs and strollers are not allowed on the course. If you have little ones interested in being a part of race day, please consider taking part in our untimed kids race (they also receive a bib, shirt and medal)!

All Race Courses are set to end at 12:30 PM. Half Marathon participants, please ensure you are able to complete the event in under 4 hours and 30 minutes (roughly 20:35 pace per mile)

Packet Pickup:

Packet Pickup will take place on Friday (9/11/26) and Saturday (9/12/26) and Sunday (9/13/26)

Friday (9/11/26) - Packet Pickup from 4-8 pm at Willamette Valley Vineyards Salem Hills Tasting Room
(8800 Enchanted Way SE Turner, OR 97392)

All race participants age 21+ are invited to enjoy a complimentary seasonal flight during packet pickup. Stay for dinner and enjoy the beautiful views of wine country. Be sure to bring your ID! Thank you to our Premier Sponsor, Willamette Valley Vineyards!

Saturday (9/12/26) - Packet Pickup from 1-5 pm at Gallagher Fitness Resources
(135 Commercial St NE, Salem, OR 97301)

Sunday (9/13/26) - Packet Pickup from 6-7:45 am at Riverfront Park
(200 Water St NE, Salem, OR 97301)

PLEASE CONSIDER TAKING ADVANTAGE OF OUR FRIDAY & SATURDAY PACKET PICKUP OPTIONS


Pre-Race offerings:

Morning packet pickup, coffee, water and bananas for participants. Gear check available at registration booth.


Post-Race:

Enjoy a complimentary 5-ounce pour from our premier sponsor and exclusive wine provider, Willamette Valley Vineyards, or a 12 oz glass of craft beer or cider.

Enjoy music and a variety of food offerings from local food trucks for purchase after the event as well as awards for overall and age group finishers.

Parking:

Please prioritize using Street Parking in Downtown Salem as well as downtown parking garages. Plan for plenty of time to arrive and get situated prior to the event. The Riverfront park Carousel Parking lot will fill very fast the morning of the event. 


Please plan accordingly! Day-of packet pickup ends at 7:50 am. The race will begin on time at 8:00 am.


Awards:

1st, 2nd, and 3rd place awards will be given for the overall winners, master's winners (age 40+) and the following age groups:

19 and Under
20 - 29
30-39
40-49
50-59
60-69
70+


Introducing the Cherry City Team Competition!

Grab your friends and running buddies and be sure to register as part of a team/group during registration! Along with your individual race results, we will tabulate the race results for teams and will have awards for the top male and female teams for all three race distances!

Are you a part of or lead a local/community Run Club?

We would love to get connected with you! Please email us or send us a direct message on social media telling us about your group to see about specials offers and opportunities!

Our mission is to empower the grassroots running and walking community and be a reliable and favorite race on your yearly training calendar!

 

We Need Volunteers!

Our event doesn’t happen without the support of the incredible community of runners, walkers and just all around great people who are willing to support the event. If you’re unable to participate in the Cherry City Half Marathon and still want to be a part of race day please consider volunteering.

name: Christmas 5K/10K/Half Marathon in July - Eugene
description:
Celebrate the holiday spirit in the middle of summer at the Christmas in July 5K/10K/Half Marathon! This means Santa is on Vacay!

Come on out and join us at Kiwanis Park in Eugene.This festive race brings all the cheer of the season—without the cold—giving athletes a fun and energetic way to race during the warm summer months.
Whether you’re tackling the 5K, 10K, or Half Marathon, you’ll enjoy a spirited race atmosphere filled with holiday flair, seasonal fun, and motivation from start to finish. Runners and walkers of all levels are welcome to join in the celebration.
All athletes who cross the finish line will receive a custom finisher medal and a spirited, race-themed shirt to commemorate their accomplishment. Awards will be presented to men and women for all three distances to the top finishers in the usual five-year age groups, starting at 10 & Under.
Break out the holiday cheer, lace up your running shoes, and make summer miles merry at the Christmas in July 5K/10K/Half Marathon.

name: Circle the Bay
description:
This challenging course covers 30 kilometers (18.6 miles), from Ferry Road Park in North Bend through Coos Bay’s waterfront finishing back at Ferry Road Park. Run/walk the whole thing yourself or form a 3-person team and make it a run or walk-cheer-athon.  The first leg is relatively flat, the second is moderately rolling, and the third is for your hill lover!  Note, prices listed are for the entire team.

Aid stations close at noon and the finish line closes at 1:00 PM, so plan to finish the walk in 6 1/2 hours, the run in 5 hours.

Water will be available at the exchanges, approximately every 6 miles.

Not into running or walking that far, but want to be involved? Volunteer!

name: Corvallis Fall Festival Run
description:
WELCOME BACK for the 47th installment of this landmark running event for the mid-valley, an old-school 5K & 10K. Just like last year, the run will take place from the McNary field between 11th and 14th streets. Come for the run, stay for Fall Festival!

The run is presented by Heart of the Valley Runners. Proceeds from the event go back to the community in accordance with the mission of Heart of the Valley Runners -- to encourage and support local running at all levels.

This affordable, family-friendly event presents a welcoming and fun atmosphere for all who want to participate. HOTV Runners members receive a $5 discount on registration for the 5k and 10k through Saturday September 26, 2026. You can join the club as part of your registration and you will receive the discount. 

The 5k and 10k both begin at 9:00am.  The 1k Kids' Fun Run begins at 10:30am, or shortly after the last 5k/10k finishers. 
Day of race registration ($50 for 5k/10k, $20 for ages 18 and under, Free for 1k) begins at 7:00am.

name: Dave's Solstice Run at Blue Lake
description:
Join us on Saturday morning, June 20, 2026 to celebrate the summer solstice with Dave's Solstice Run 5K at Blue Lake.

This event is named after Dave Green, a long-time ORRC member and volunteer. Dave was an active board member, joining in 1981, and becoming president in 1992. Race director for multiple events, including the original Blue Lake Runs, Dave was also the “Treasurer Extraordinaire” and was instrumental in helping the club through some tough times financially in the past. This event epitomizes Dave Green, and his love for low-key, family friendly events.

name: Day of the Dead Race 12
description:
The streets of Talent, OR are calling and they want YOU.

Every year, the Day of the Dead Race brings our community alive with runners, walkers, families, and friends of all ages, all backgrounds, all paces. This isn't just a race. It's a celebration of Latin culture, of life, of the people we carry with us.

Expect the beat of music that moves you, food that feeds your soul, dance that spills into the streets, and art that stops you in your tracks. Come run. Come walk. Come belong. Because when we share our culture, we don't just build community we build understanding, joy, and something worth showing up for year after year.

Lace up. Show up. Celebrate.

name: Death by 5k Oregon
description:
Death by 5k is returning to Oregon!

Taking place at Elijah Bristow State Park, RunStrong Event's signature 24 hour challenge, Death by 5k requires participants to run ten 5ks starting every 2.5 hours, for 24 hours. The first 5k starts at 8 am, and subsequent 5ks start at 1030, 1, 330, 6, 830, 11, 130, 4, and 630 am. Participants need to be present at the start of each 5k, and have that 5k finished prior to the start of the subsequent 5k. This challenge is designed to test participants mentally and physically with physical fatigue, sleep deprivation, and running in the dark. (Headlamps, hand lights, or some other form of illumination will be required) all while having a great time in a beautiful location.

In between each 5k, participants will be able to car camp, or to put up tents in the group camping area which will also serve as the race HQ.

Hot food will be served at 830 am, 130 pm, 630 pm, 1130 pm and 430 am, along with plenty of snack food available throughout the event. Drinks provided will be water and mixed gatorade..

Participants will receive an event shirt and some great additional swag. Finishers will receive one of our coveted coffin awards and the pride that comes with surviving.

Registration will be limited to 150 participants. After that, a waitlist will be enabled and we will open spots if/when they become available only.

Death by 5k takes place at various locations including:
River West Festival Park, Tulsa, OK
Oak Mountain SP in Alabama
Runstrong HQ in Brandon, MS
Shelby Farms Park in Memphis
Adventures Unlimited in Milton, FL
George Wyth SP in Waterloo, IA
N Little Rock, and more sites coming soon!

name: Dragonslayer Fantasy Dash and Strut
description:
Step into your favorite character’s shoes—whether you’re a superhero, anti-hero, villain, knight, princess, or even Sasquatch—and join us for the inaugural Dragonslayer Fantasy Dash & Strut!

This 5K adventure invites you to walk or run through the magical trails of Gabriel Park (PDX). Along the way, you’ll encounter a thrilling Villain Zones for an extra dash of fun and excitement and be welcomed back to the Heroes Village!

Route includes mild inclines, a mixture of gravel and trail pathways, everyone is assured of a beautiful and accessible run, jog, or walk. The route is suitable for all ages and abilities. Leashed dogs and strollers welcome (strollers ensure you have wheels suitable for unpaved trails).

name: Eola Hills "No Hills" 5K/10K
description:
Proceeds from the Eola Hills "No Hills" run will be shared by the Track and field and cross-country programs at Dallas HS and Central HS.

This is a very fun and popular event that is capped at 350 racers.

New for 2026: Race is chip timed and you get a souvenir wine glass.

***IMPORTANT PARKING NOTE*** Parking at the event location fills fast, and parking is NOT be available at the Polk County Fairgrounds. Please carpool if possible. We have overflow parking about 1/4 mile south of Eola in a field.

There will be race day registration (exact cash amount is requested) and we can take credit/debit. Please arrive early to get your information on the roster.

Day of Race 10k=$60, 5k=$55

Check-in on race morning will open at 7:00am. The 10K run will set off from Eola Hills Wine Cellars at 9:00am.  At 9:15am the 5K run/walk will begin. This is a flat, fast, out-and-back course. It is chip-timed this year. Ensure your bib is on your front and visible, especially at the finish. We will pull bib tabs for place and timing verification. After your run enjoy the company of fellow runners and walkers in the wine cellar. You will get  pizza from Yeasty Beasty and a glass of wine, beer, or soda with thanks to Eola Hills.

Following the race end there will be ribbons handed out to the top finishers of each age group for both male and female racers.

 

**We ask that all participants finish their events within 90 minutes of the start time.

The top 3 male and female finishers of each race will receive prizes.  The top 3 in each 10-year age division, male/female, for each race will receive ribbons.

**No dogs are allowed on the course. Strollers are permitted but we ask you please not crowd the front of the start line.

description:
All levels of runners and walkers encouraged to participate!!
Registration fees includes a long sleeve tee shirt and personalized bib if registered by 11:59 pm on September 17th. 
Online day of event registration (no cash, no check, electronic payment only)

For more information, visit forestgrovelions.org, or contact Race Directors, Sydney, sdaniels@vgmhc.org Or Tom, tomr@johnlscott.com

name: GTD - Go The Distance 5K Fun Run/Walk and Kids Dash
description:
❤️🏃 Our mission: To build self-esteem, establish support systems, and empower recovery one run at a time. 

Go the Distance is a nonprofit organization that advocates for recovery through fitness, community, and compassion. Proceeds from this event will help empower more people in early recovery and support Go the Distance’s impact on our community members.

Join us for our 2nd annual GTD 5k Fun Run at Fernhill Park on Sept. 13th! Sign up to run with us for an even bigger and better event this year. 

Registration for this year’s race will also include the following: 

  • 2026 GTD 5k Medal
  • Race shirt featuring all our sponsors 
  • Specially customized GTD bib 
  • Timing- so you can improve on your time from last year!
  • Kids’ dash (free!)
  • Virtual 5k run/walk options if you can’t make it in person

As our valued community members that signed up to run with us last year, you are receiving a special $5 off race registration from now until Aug. 9, when the price will increase for general registration. 

Come one come all for a morning filled with PR’s (personal records) and PV’s (positive vibes) and spend it with your friends at GTD! 

 

📍 Race location: Fernhill Park

6010 NE 37th Ave, Portland, OR 97211

 

📝 T-shirt pick-up and race check-in:

T-shirt pick-up will be on race day, Sunday September 13th starting 9am at Fernhill Park

 

⏰ Race schedule:

All races will take place on Sunday, September 13th.

  • 9:00 am: Opening festivities
  • 9:30 am: Kids’ fun run
  • 10:00 am: Go the Distance 5k

 

📱 Follow Go The Distance on Instagram to receive updates and exciting news about the race! 

 

✉️ Questions: Reach out to info@gtdgothedistance.org

name: HAGG Lake Triathlon & Multi-Sports Festival
description:
RACE AT THIS HISTORICAL EVENT AND STUNNING VENUE!

Hagg Lake Triathlon – Rich in Beauty, Rich in Tradition!

Come race at the 45th Anniversary of the Annual Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival, one of the oldest and most gorgeous Triathlon courses in the nation! Now offering an Off-Road Triathlon, Half Marathon Trail Run, 5K Trail Run & Camping!

Olympic & Sprint Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike & NEW OFF-ROAD SPRINT TRIATHLON, DUATHLON & AQUABIKE, Half Marathon Trail Run, and 5K TRAIL RUN!

The modern sport of triathlon had its modest beginnings with an event held in Mission Bay in San Diego, CA on September 25, 1974. There were 46 athletes that day. Seven years later, Hagg Lake Triathlon became one of six stops on the Bud Light Triathlon Series Tour drawing about 500 athletes, with Dave Scott coming out on top. Today, as one of the nation’s oldest and longest-running triathlon events, Hagg Lake enters its 38th year and it continues to draw upwards of 700+ athletes. Its popularity is rooted in the rich tradition and the exceptional venue, which is one of the most scenic in the country. The Hagg Lake course offers a true test of this terrific sport with its rolling hills on both the bike and run leg portions of the event. Make the Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival one of your summer stops and compete on the course that has seen many of the greats in the sport of triathlon.

RACE AT THIS HISTORICAL EVENT AND STUNNING VENUE!

Hagg Lake Triathlon – Rich in Beauty, Rich in Tradition!

Come race at the 45th Anniversary of the Annual Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival, one of the oldest and most gorgeous Triathlon courses in the nation! Now offering an Off-Road Triathlon, Half Marathon Trail Run, 5K Trail Run & Camping!

Olympic & Sprint Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike & NEW OFF-ROAD SPRINT TRIATHLON, DUATHLON & AQUABIKE, Half Marathon Trail Run, and 5K TRAIL RUN!

The modern sport of triathlon had its modest beginnings with an event held in Mission Bay in San Diego, CA on September 25, 1974. There were 46 athletes that day. Seven years later, Hagg Lake Triathlon became one of six stops on the Bud Light Triathlon Series Tour drawing about 500 athletes, with Dave Scott coming out on top. Today, as one of the nation’s oldest and longest-running triathlon events, Hagg Lake enters its 38th year and it continues to draw upwards of 700+ athletes. Its popularity is rooted in the rich tradition and the exceptional venue, which is one of the most scenic in the country. The Hagg Lake course offers a true test of this terrific sport with its rolling hills on both the bike and run leg portions of the event. Make the Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival one of your summer stops and compete on the course that has seen many of the greats in the sport of triathlon.

name: Helvetia Wine Run 5k
description:
This race is currently Sold Out!  Please join the waitlist using the tile above and we will notify you ASAP if any spots become available. 

Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Saturday, June 20, 2026 at 8:30am and 10:30am for an exciting annual event that features the amazing scenery and landscape of Helvetia Vineyards & Winery!  Helvetia Vineyards and Winery is located in the foothills of the Tualatin Mountains, the northernmost grape growing area in the Willamette Valley and just 25 minutes from downtown Portland. So, whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wine, this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience!  This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing.  Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt included! 
  • Wine Glass: Shatterproof, Collapsible, and Portable!
  • Finisher Medal: Doubles as a Wine Stopper!
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!

name: Hillsboro Rotary Run 5K and Kids Dash
description:
Kick off your Fourth of July celebration with the Hillsboro Fourth of July 5K and Kids Dash! Join us on Saturday, July 4, 2026, for a festive run or walk along the official Hillsboro Fourth of July Parade route before the parade begins.

Hosted by the Hillsboro Rotary Club, this fun, family-friendly event welcomes runners, walkers, and kids of all ages. Whether you're chasing a personal record, enjoying a morning walk with friends, or cheering on your little ones in the free Kids Dash, there's something for everyone.

After crossing the finish line, stick around and enjoy one of Hillsboro's favorite Independence Day traditions as the community gathers for the annual Fourth of July Parade.

Best of all, your participation supports scholarships for local high school students pursuing higher education, helping invest in the next generation of community leaders. Celebrate Independence Day, support local students, and be part of a Hillsboro tradition!

name: Hood to Coast Semper Fi & America's Fund Team
description:
Join our Semper Fi & America's Fund Team for the Hood to Coast Relay and help us raise $20,000 for The Fund.

Our team will be comprised of Team Semper Fi (service members who participate in The Fund's Recovery through Sport program) and Community Athletes (Fundraisers). This partnership will be a unique experience for everyone involved!

The Providence Hood To Coast Relay, located in Oregon, is the most popular and largest running and walking relay race in the world, annually drawing participants from over 40 countries. Known as the Mother of All Relays, the event takes 12-member relay teams 199 miles from the iconic top of Mount Hood to the beaches of the Pacific Ocean. The event has sold-out for 30 straight years and on lottery opening day for 23 consecutive years. 

Fundraising minimum $3,000. Your $3,000 fundraising will cover the costs for a member of Team Semper Fi to participate in the Relay.

Registration cost $225.00 per person

  • As you register for the team a personal fundraising page will be created for you. This page can be customized with pictures and your personal message. 
  • Each team member will receive a Semper Fi & America's Fund running shirt.
  • Each team member is responsible for their own travel to and from the event.
  • The Fund will provide vans that will transport the team during the event.
  • The Hood to Coast Relay takes place on Friday, Aug 27nd through Saturday, August 30. Participants need to arrive in Portland no later than Thursday, Aug 27 and stay until Sunday, Aug 30.

name: Kiteboard 4 Cancer Derby Race
description:
** Please Read** Riders & Teams seeking each other : Fill out this form to connect and we will make the connection!

This year is Kiteboard 4 Cancer's 20th Anniversary so we wanted to design a race that embodies teamwork, connection, and community while celebrating the evolution of 20 years of windsports (it's gone far beyond just kiteboarding!)

All funds raised from the 20th KB4C Derby Race will benefit The Next Door and their Columbia Gorge Youth Connection - a Mental Health program in our local schools + Columbia Gorge Health Council, which funds multiple mental health initiatives in the Gorge, specifically when insurance is tapped out for individuals and families.

The new 20th Derby format will require participants to form teams of 3, with each individual selecting a discipline to race in, each with their own start: 

  1. Kiteboarding - the discipline that started it all
  2. Wingfoiling - A cross between windsurfing and kiteboarding... everybody's doing it these days
  3. Foil of Choice - Kitefoiling, Wingfoiling, Parawing, Windsurf foil, tin foil? Your choice!

The event will kickoff with the kiteboarding portion of the race, returning to the same rabbit start format from 2007 where kiteboarders idle on the Washington side of the Columbia River, and at the start-mark race toward Oregon, make the buoy turn in front of the event site, continue back up to the 2nd buoy upwind and continue this course for 1:45 (hour + 45 minutes). 

At 1:45 time, all timers will stop, kiters will land at the event site and there will be a 15 minute transition before the wingfoilers start their leg of the race from the event site beach next.

Wingfoilers will then race for 1:45 around the same course, then land at the event site after the 1:45 time ends. Again, there will be a 15 minute transition before the 3rd and final leg of the Derby -- the Foil of Choice -- will launch from the event site and race for 1:45 for the final leg of the race!

Watch Race Director Grom's video that explains how the race will work here.

The winners of the Derby will be the top combined laps of all three disciplines.

name: Ladybug Run for CDH Awareness 5K/10K
description:
2025 Results are here: https://www.hubertiming.com/results/2025Ladybug 
2024 Results are here: https://www.hubertiming.com/results/2024Ladybug 
2023 Results are here: https://www.hubertiming.com/results/2023Ladybug
2022 Results are here: https://www.hubertiming.com/results/2022LadyBug

Join us for the 15th annual running of this unique and popular 5K/10K race on July 11, 2026! This stroller-friendly event takes runners on a scenic course through the open green spaces and forested paths along the Tualatin River in Tigard's Cook Park and neighboring areas, offering a fun and memorable experience for all participants.

Perks for Participants:
All 5K and 10K finishers will receive a shirt, medal and a race packet filled with goodies to celebrate their accomplishment.

Can’t join us in person?
No problem! Sign up for the virtual race and run your own 5K or 10K course—anywhere, anytime. As a virtual participant, you’ll receive a race bib, a shirt, and a medal to commemorate your achievement. Want to run with friends? Organize a group virtual run, and we’ll promote it on our website so others can join you!

Race Day Details:
To ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone, the start line will remain open for 15 minutes, allowing for a staggered start and plenty of space.

Why We Run:
The best part? Proceeds from this event benefit the Ladybug CDH Foundation, whose mission is to: Raise public awareness about Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia (CDH), a potentially life-threatening birth defect affecting 1 in 2,500 children annually.
Fund critical medical research.
Provide direct support to families in the Pacific Northwest facing the challenges of CDH.

Survivor/Angel Signs:
We line the sidewalks at Cook Family Park with signs remembering and honoring Angels and Survivors. If you have a CDH Angel or Survivor you would like represented with a sign, please contact us at ladybugcdh@gmail.com. Send us a few sentences about their story and 2-3 photos. We'd love to be able to honor your CDH warrior. 

Don’t wait—register today to lace up your shoes, make a difference, and help us support families impacted by CDH. Together, we can bring hope and make strides for this important cause.

name: Longest Day Mile
description:
WHERE:  Phoenix High School Track

WHEN: Sunday, June 21st, 2026

  • 7:30pm- Heat 1  5:45min pace & Under 
  • 7:40pm- Heat 2  5:46 -7min Pace 
  • 7:50pm- Heat 3  7-9min Pace 
  • 8:05pm- Heat 4  9-11min Pace 
  • 8:20pm- Heat 5  11min Pace & Up

COURSE DETAILS:  Four times around the Phoenix High School Track

RACE FEES: $13 online or $15 day of

RACE DAY INFO: Registration 6:30-7:30pm

AWARDS:  Ribbons for the top 3 places in all age groups. $100 prize for any male who runs sub 4:00 minutes and any female who runs sub 4:40 minutes.

FOOD DRIVE: Like Longest Night Mile this race will be supporting the SOU Food Pantry.  Please bring an item to help us stock their pantry!  Main needs are: canned meats (tuna, spam, chicken, etc.), microwaveable sides, breakfast items, and snack foods.  

RESTRICTIONS: Absolutely no roller skaters, bicycles, skateboards, baby joggers, dogs, headphones, or unregistered participants

RACE DIRECTOR: Seamus Cowan

name: Longest Night Mile
description:
WHERE:  Phoenix High School Track

WHEN: Monday, December 21st, 2025

  • 6:15pm- Heat 1  5:45min pace & Under 
  • 6:25pm- Heat 2  5:46 -7min Pace 
  • 6:35pm- Heat 3  7-9min Pace 
  • 6:50pm- Heat 4  9-11min Pace 
  • 7:05pm- Heat 5  11min Pace & Up

COURSE DETAILS:  Four times around the Phoenix High School Track

RACE FEES: Option 1: Bring 2-3+ boxes of dry cereal. YES you read that right! The SOU food bank coordinator expressed to us in 2019 that the students are excited when there is cereal in the food bank because there rarely is and when it is there it doesn't last long. So, we thought it would be a fun treat before Christmas to stuff their pantry full of cereal goodness! We also hosted a can food drive at our Turkey Trot for the SOU food bank and a portion of the proceeds went to them as well so don't worry, we made sure they had other food items. 

Option 2: $13 online or $15 day of (cash or check only) which will also be donated to the SOU Student Food Pantry.

RACE DAY INFO: Registration 5-6pm - Bring $15 or 2-3+ boxes of dry cereal and sign waiver to participate.  

AWARDS:  Ribbons for the top 3 places in all age groups. $100 prize for any male who runs sub 4:00 minutes and any female who runs sub 4:40 minutes.

RESTRICTIONS: Absolutely no roller skaters, bicycles, skateboards, baby joggers, dogs, headphones, or unregistered participants

RACE DIRECTORS: Nathan & Shayla Watt

name: Mac's Run
description:
Hilly and challenging course with breathtaking ocean views. The race is entirely on paved roads.  

For both courses, runners loop through Shore Acres heading out (south), and run straight back on the return (north).

5K Course Map

10K Course Map

Note that students are $5.00.  Please use the coupon code Student2022 to register.  To avoid credit-card fees, you will not be charged at check-out.  Please bring $5.00 (exact change appreciated) to registration!

Starting Oct 1, 2025, all vehicles require a parking pass (cost is per vehicle, not per runner).  Cost of a day pass is $10 for in-state or $12 for out-of-state.  Daily passes are available at a kiosk near registration with a QR code using your phone.  We are working with the parks to see if we can sell them as part of registration, but details have not been worked out yet.  Annual state park passes are $30 for one year and $50 for two years.  They can be purchased at the gift shop at Shore Acres or on-line.  FYI, the price will double to $60 for an annual pass January 1 and they will no longer issue two-year passes, so if you visit our beautiful state parks, it is cheaper to buy now.

name: McCubbins Gulch Trail Race
description: Start your race with camping the night before under the stars.  Traditional potluck dinner the night before with music, games and other shenanigans will take place before turning in.  A leisurely wake up time before starting the stellar trail race in the beautiful Mt Hood forest where you must FOLLOW THE ORANGE RIBBONS NOT THE PERSON IN FRONT OF YOU.  Be prepared to cross through streams, over streams, up steep terrain and down steep terrain while keeping an eye out where to go.  There is a lot of fun to be had and plenty to talk about when you return through the finish line.  Food will follow along with the beer garden.  This is one of the favorite XDog races that we are glad to welcome back.

name: Milwaukie Mile
description:
Welcome to the third annual Milwaukie Mile! Our goal is to provide a safe and fast course for all members of the community to race their pace and set a new personal best in the mile! The course runs gently downhill along the Trolley Trail, starting at the Park Avenue Max Station and finishing in Milwaukie Bay Park. The race will be held the morning of Saturday July 11th, 2026.

The race is open to runners, walkers, and families with strollers. Dogs are not allowed to accompany runners, walkers, or volunteers. You can spectate with your dog on a leash, but please stand back from the course when doing so for the safety of the participants. 

***Please note - T-shirt size and availability are not guaranteed for registrations after July 1st.***

 

Awards

All registered participants will receive a Milwaukie Mile T-shirt. The top-3 finishers in the following categories will receive a special award:

  • Non-binary
  • Open Women
  • Open Men
  • 18 and under Girls
  • 18 and under Boys

 

Transportation

The race starts only a few steps from the Park Ave Orange Line Max Station. Participants and spectators are encouraged to use public transportation to travel to the race!  If you must drive to the race, auto users are encouraged to park in Downtown Milwaukie or at the Park Ave park and ride garage.

 

Donations

All net proceeds will be donated to the Milwaukie High School Cross Country team. If you want to make a dedicated donation to the team to support their 2027 season, we will gladly pass 100% of your donation on to the team! Any amount given would be greatly appreciated and thank you for your generosity! Please click the Donate tab above to donate directly. 

 

Sponsorship

The Milwaukie Mile is a small community event which would not be possible without the support of generous sponsors. If you would like to support or sponsor the event in any way, please email Milwaukiemile@gmail.com.

 

Volunteers

Milwaukie Mile is supported 100% by some amazing volunteers! They help us with event coordination, athlete safety, and logistics. If you would like to volunteer, please email Milwaukiemile@gmail.com.

 

Photos:

Mateo Flores was out on the course capturing all the fun in 2025. Photos can be found on a shared google drive linked HERE. These are free for you to download for personal use - we only ask that you honor Mateo’s hard work and give photo credit to Mateo Flores or tag @teotooktheflick when sharing on Instagram. Feel free to also tag @milwaukiemile so we can celebrate with you!

name: Mission Possible
description:
If you are looking for a reason to run other than the run itself, here is the Race for YOU! 

Run your traditional 5k or 10k chip timed trail run and then hang around for free pancakes and cheer on the All Abilities walk/runners.

 Cheer, Celebrate – Everyone’s Invited!

Lace up for a morning full of movement, encouragement, and community fun!

Whether you're hitting the trail for the 5K or 10K, or cheering on participants in the All Abilities Run/Walk (2.25-mile or 1.6-mile loop), there's something for everyone. The 5K and 10K are traditional trail runs, and part of your entry fee helps support the All Abilities event, making it possible for more people to join in the joy. 

The All Abilities 2.25-mile or 1.6-mile course is accessible and welcoming, following mostly flat, paved bike paths with a short section of hard-packed gravel at the start. Every participant is encouraged to bring a friend, family member, or support buddy to run alongside or cheer from the sidelines. Volunteers will be on the course to offer guidance and motivation.

After your run, stick around for FREE pancakes, snacks, drinks, and high-fives all around. Let’s lift each other up and celebrate what we can accomplish together!

name: Monsters & Mimosas 5K - Diamond Lake
description:
Get ready for a spooky-good time at the Monsters & Mimosas 5K, where Halloween fun meets festive celebration! This spirited run invites ghosts, goblins, and costumed creatures of all kinds to hit the course for a frightfully fantastic fall morning.

Join us at Diamond Lake Resort where all race participants will receive a custom finisher medal, a race-themed shirt, and a refreshing mimosa waiting for them at the finish line—because even monsters deserve a little sparkle after a solid run! We'll have juice and water for those under 21.

We’ll also be recognizing top finishers with awards in the usual five-year age groups starting at 10 & under, giving everyone a chance to show off their speed along with their costumes.

Join us for miles, mimosas, and a whole lot of Halloween magic!

name: Newport Celebration Run
description:
Join the Newport Celebration Run on July 4th!

Celebrate Our 12th Anniversary with a Unique and Scenic Running Experience!

Event Highlights:

🌊 Exclusive Run on NOAA Pier: A rare chance to run on the 1,300+ feet NOAA pier, thanks to NOAA's MOC-P.
🏅 Finisher's Medal: For all half marathon, 10k, and 5k finishers.
🍺 Free Beer: (21 and over) Courtesy of Rogue Brewery.
🎟️ Personalized Custom Bibs
⏱️ Professionally Chip-Timed Races

Course Information:

  • Half Marathon: Challenging course with ~1,500 ft elevation gain, featuring ~5.22 miles of pavement, ~5.28 miles of single-track trails, and ~2.6 miles of paved roads.
  • 10k & 5k: Flat, fast courses perfect for setting a personal record.
  • Kids Run: Fun and exciting race for the little ones!

What you'll get:

✔️ Finisher's Medal for all 1/2 Marathon, 10k & 5k finishers
✔️ Personalized custom bib
✔️ Professionally chip-timed
✔️ Beautiful scenic, flat courses
✔️ (1) Beer (21 and over) Courtesy of Rogue Brewery

name: Newport Celebration Run
description:
Join the Newport Celebration Run on July 4th!

Celebrate Our 12th Anniversary with a Unique and Scenic Running Experience!

Event Highlights:

🌊 Exclusive Run on NOAA Pier: A rare chance to run on the 1,300+ feet NOAA pier, thanks to NOAA's MOC-P.
🏅 Finisher's Medal: For all half marathon, 10k, and 5k finishers.
🍺 Free Beer: (21 and over) Courtesy of Rogue Brewery.
🎟️ Personalized Custom Bibs
⏱️ Professionally Chip-Timed Races

Course Information:

  • Half Marathon: Challenging course with ~1,500 ft elevation gain, featuring ~5.22 miles of pavement, ~5.28 miles of single-track trails, and ~2.6 miles of paved roads.
  • 10k & 5k: Flat, fast courses perfect for setting a personal record.
  • Kids Run: Fun and exciting race for the little ones!

What you'll get:

✔️ Finisher's Medal for all 1/2 Marathon, 10k & 5k finishers
✔️ Personalized custom bib
✔️ Professionally chip-timed
✔️ Beautiful scenic, flat courses
✔️ (1) Beer (21 and over) Courtesy of Rogue Brewery

name: Newport Harbor Triathlon and 5K
description: The Newport Harbor Triathlon and 5K is dedicated to promoting a healthy, active lifestyle for athletes of all ages while supporting the growth of youth athletics in our coastal community. Through an inclusive, family-friendly event set against the stunning backdrop of Newport, Oregon, we aim to inspire first-time participants and seasoned triathletes alike. Proceeds and partnerships help fund local youth sports programs, ensuring every child has the opportunity to move, grow, and thrive through access to positive, health-focused activities.

name: Northwest Electricfest
description:
Northwest Electric Fest (NWEF) is a five-day PEV festival nestled in the Pacific Northwest.

All Personal Electric Vehicles are welcome:

Onewheels / Electric Unicycles / E-Bikes / E-Scooters / E-Mountain Boards / TLT Boards

 
Racing
We offer chip-timed Onewheel and EUC races with multiple divisions for adults, teens, and kids — from beginner to advanced.

Our trail race is a dynamic mix of terrain including dirt, rock, roots, gravel, grass, uphill and downhill sections. Expect fast high-speed lines blended with slow, technical features, tight turns, and twists.

Top 3 riders from each division will podium.

 
Freestyle Trick Competition & Features
We build some of the coolest PEV freestyle courses you can session all weekend. We also host a judged freestyle competition for riders ready to throw down.

Jump Bags
We feature multiple massive launch ramps with inflatable landing airbags for EUC riders — and for the bravest Onewheel riders. This is your chance to level up your jumping skills, learn from other riders, and safely push your progression.

 
Night Rides & Community
Every night we host a group ride with music and lights that often ends in a community-wide game of Rumble.

Secret rides and pop-up parties happen throughout the event — so stay ready.

 
Games & Side Events
Horse / Chair / Box races for Onewheels
Sit-down EUC races to test your racing skills
Balance course challenges
Tire toss contest (think you can out-throw our long-distance legends?)
Multiple festival-style games with prizes
These events are just as fun to watch as they are to compete in.

 
Relax & Enjoy
We have multiple swimming spots for cooling off, plus canoe rides, canoe races, and even a pool.

There will be music and food throughout the event.

The venue is located just five minutes from town, so grocery runs are easy — but once you arrive, it feels completely tucked away in nature. The setting is truly something special.

 
Spectators
If you have family or friends who want to attend and spectate, please select the Friends/Family Add-On ticket after choosing your pass. This add-on ticket is valid for the entire event.

 
Racing, riding, contests, community, and pure STOKE.

We can’t wait to see you all!

name: Oktoberfest Races: 10k run and 5k run/walk
description:
Online registration ends on Saturday, Sept. 20 at noon.

Day of registration, 5k - $45; 10k - $50. Checks or via your phone with QR code.  

The Silverton Runners Club and Oktoberfest are again teaming up to host the Oktoberfest 5k and 10 races. The races have a little something for every type of runner. Track runner? The start and finish is on the Kennedy High School track. Road runner? The course meanders through the hamlet of Mt. Angel. Trail runner? Parts of the course are on gravel. Like it flat? It mostly is. Like hills? We have a couple. Like a good party after? Mt. Angel Oktoberfest! Every finisher will receive a pint glass and a ticket for a complimentary beer at the Oktoberfest. See, we got you all covered! See you there.

What you need to know:

The 10k course will be new this year.

We allow strollers, please line up in the back.

Though we like dogs, please do not bring them to run the races.

There will be day of registration.

If you register for the 10k, please maintain at least a 15:00/mile pace. The course will officially close at 10:30 so our volunteers can enjoy the Oktoberfest activities.

Proceeds from the races go to support the Kennedy, Silverton and Gervais middle & high school track and cross country programs.

Packet pick-up is Sunday (day of race) at the Kennedy High School track, starting at 7:00 AM. Day of registration will be from 7:00am to 8:45am. 

To guarantee a t-shirt, register and purchase your shirt before September 1.

Please note: We will have extra shirts on race day but availability will be limited to what we have on hand.

We can't wait to see you at the races!

1/1/25 to 4/30/25, 5k - $30; 10k - $35

5/1/25 to noon on 9/13/25, 5k - $35; 10k - $40

Day of race, 5k - $45; 10k - $50

Online registration ends on Saturday, Sept. 19 at noon.

There are no refunds.
