name: Oregon Cascades 100
description:
Oregon Cascades 100 

Welcome to Oregon Cascades! These point-to-point courses will take you from Bend to Sisters - two of Oregon's premier running towns - where the trails (and beer) are the best anywhere! 

​

The 100 mile race has roughly 10,700 ft of gain and 11,200ft of loss. Don't let the elevation gain fool you...it's packed into the first 100K of the course making this easy-on-paper race much harder than expected! The Bend side offers smooth, flowing single track in the shadow of Mount Bachelor before dropping onto some rugged terrain as you begin your descent into Sisters country. The course consists of 84% single-track trails and 13 full aid stations with awesome single track trails and views. You will have 32 hours, 1 minute and 18 seconds to finish. The 100 mile race is a Western States qualifier!

​

The 50 mile course has 4000ft of gain and 6500ft of loss with 5 aid stations and consisting of 85% single track trails and 15% gravel road, will make for fast times! The views will have you wanting to come back for more. You will have 16 hours to finish.

name: ORRC Best Dam Run - 10K
description:
Come run or walk the Best Dam Run! This point-to-point 10K course features views of pristine waters, shading forests, interesting geology and bald eagles, osprey and colorful waterfowl.

Participants are bused approximately 6 miles east of Estacada to the North Fork Lake start. The course meanders along the wild and scenic Clackamas River for most of your journey to the downtown Estacada finish line.  

Post-race food and awards will take place near the finish line at SE 4th Ave and Broadway.  After your event you can also stroll along the shops and venues of Estacada.

This event is limited to 750 entrants so don't wait and register now!

name: ORRC Free Member 5K Run/Walk
description:
♠  ♥  ♣  ♦

Free ORRC Member Poker Run/Walk!

This event is free for ORRC members who pre-register (and $25 for non-members). Everyone in the community is welcome!

Come one, come all! And don't stress about an accurate distance or time! This is just a fun way to spend Labor Day holiday morning. Don't be concerned about how fast or slow you are… the only thing that matters is your poker hand!

 

What is the Poker Run?

The Poker Run/Walk is a 5K course consisting of 3 out-and-back legs all within Greenway Park in Beaverton, starting and finishing at Tractor Park

The event is capped at 150 participants (due to limitations of the bike trail, and limited port-a-pottie!!! (there is only one in the park near the start area, and we are not allowed to bring in any more so... "GO BEFORE YOU GO!")

If you’re not an ORRC member, you can still join the fun for a small registration fee! To find out more about the benefits of ORRC membership – click here ORRC Membership

 

NOTE: There is no day of race registration!

 

Event Start Times:

-7:00 a.m. Registration opens

-7:45 a.m. Start of the 5K Walk

-8:00 a.m. Start of the 5K Run

-The course will close at 10 a.m.

 

Volunteering
We’d love to have you help us put on a great event on Labor Day. If you’re interested in volunteering, please go to the volunteer tab on this page (click here - Volunteer Free Member Run) or email race directors Julia & Tracy Reisinger at info@oregonroadrunnersclub.org.

name: ORRC Pumpkin Ridge Run 5K, 10K and Half Marathon
description:
Fun for the whole family. Multiple distances to choose from that include options for both runners and walkers. A looped course for the 10K and Half-Marathon, it's a hilly but fun course. There is a three-hour cutoff for the event. The course must close at 10am, so there is no walking option for the half-marathon. 

The event starts and finishes at North Plains Elementary School. The 10K and Half-Marathon courses will be run counterclockwise on a loop course on Pumpkin Ridge Road. The 5K will be an out-and-back on the same course so everybody finishes in the same direction. 

THE PUMPKIN RIDGE HALF MARATHON IS A USA Track & Field (USATF) CERTIFIED COURSE:  OR25002JH

name: ORRC Turkey Trot at The Zoo
description:
The ORRC Turkey Trot at the Oregon Zoo is a multi-generational family event. Runners and walkers of all abilities love the 5K, untimed out-and-back course.  The event starts at The Oregon Zoo by the Forestry Center and the Max station, then goes out toward the International Rose Garden, and finishes inside The Oregon Zoo at the Elephant Plaza. The Tot Trot (children 0- 4 years old) and the Gobble Gallop (for children between 5 and 10 years old) events follow the 5K at the Elephant plaza inside the zoo.

Every entrant in the 5K and kids events receive an awesome beanie hat and chocolate turkey. Event shirts are an optional purchase, but the deadline to request a shirt is November 1st.

PLEASE NOTE: The event is capped for non-ORRC members at 2,200 participants! The deadline to register is Thursday, November 19, 2026, and there is no day of race registration. Register early to ensure your entry!

 

Start Line Note: The last start is at 7:39 (for slower walkers, and families with strollers).

THERE IS NO LATE START! Plan to be at the Zoo NO LATER than 7:00am to have time to park, pick up your bibs, go to the bathroom, etc. before the start. If you arrive late, you might not be able to complete the entire course before it closes.

Approximately $25,000 of registration fees benefit The Oregon Zoo.

name: OUTLAST EUGENE
description:
What Is OUTLAST?

OUTLAST is a 6-hour trail endurance challenge where runners complete a 5K every hour, on the hour. Each lap must be finished within the hour to stay in the event. If you finish early, you rest until the next round. Miss a lap, and you’re out.

Complete all six rounds, and you OUTLAST.

This isn't just about speed — it's about pacing, discipline, and mental grit. Whether you're trying to survive all six or win your division, the challenge is the same: show up each hour, push your limits, and stay in it.

Each course is trail-based, with natural terrain, elevation, and unpredictable conditions. You’ll have time between rounds to recover, refuel, and refocus — but not much.

 

What You Earn:

​4 laps = “Grit Earned” patch
5 laps = “Survivor” patch
6 laps = Premium “OUTLAST” medal

​​All participants receive a premium OUTLAST Tee.

Top male and female with the fastest combined 5K times at each event win the 1st Place OUTLAST award. 

Finishers are ranked on the national leaderboard—and the fastest runner across all OUTLAST 6-hour events will be crowned National Champion and take home $1,000.

The 1st Place Male and Female 6-hour champions from each city will earn a spot in the Outlast Championship, where they’ll compete against the best of the best at the end of the Tour, and the 1st place male and female winners take home $1000 each. (This is separate from the national leaderboard prize money.)

By the end of the tour, the top 100 best times nationally will be invited to also compete in the Outlast Championship.

 

Frequently Asked Questions:

Do I have to run all 6 laps?
Nope. Run as many as you can. If you complete 4 or 5, you'll still earn a patch. Only those who finish all 6 get the OUTLAST medal and leaderboard ranking.

What happens if I don’t finish a lap in time?
You're out. The next lap starts at the top of the next hour, and only those who completed the last lap on time can continue.

How is the race timed?
Each 5K is timed individually. If you complete all 6, your combined time counts toward the local win and national leaderboard.

Are these trail races or road?
Every OUTLAST race is on trail terrain — dirt, rocks, roots, and elevation. Sometimes some pavement and gravel.

Can I walk?
Yes, as long as you finish the 5K within the hour. But some courses are rugged, and time can sneak up on you.

Are there aid stations?
Yes. There will be water, basic hydration, and snacks at the basecamp/loop start. This is a cupless event — bring your own bottle or hydration system.

What should I bring?
Trail shoes, hydration system, layers (weather dependent), fuel between laps, and grit.

Can I setup a tent?
Absolutely, bring your own aid station/tent setup.

Is OUTLAST for beginners?
Yes — if you're mentally tough. You don’t need to be fast, just consistent and ready to suffer a little.

How do I win?
If you finish all 6 laps and have the fastest combined time, you win your division (male/female). Winners are also added to the national leaderboard for a shot at the $1,000 national prize & title.

name: OXFORD Classic Community 5k
description:
Welcome to the 34th Annual Oxford Classic! This meet has become one of Central Oregon’s longest-running and most competitive cross country traditions. Each year it brings together teams from across the region for a high-level mid-season competition. For the first time, we are excited to add a Community 5k — open to everyone who wants to be part of the action!

The Oxford Classic will be held at Drake Park in Bend, Oregon. The course follows a loop through the park along the scenic Deschutes River, featuring a mix of grass and paved pathways. It is flat and fast, with wide stretches designed to accommodate pack racing and plenty of areas for spectators to cheer.

name: Paideia Back-To-School 5k
description:
Join us at the Paideia Back-to-School 5K for a fun, family-friendly event held by Paideia Classical Christian School!

This race is designed to kick off the school year with energy, connection, and community spirit. It will be held August 22nd, two weeks before classes begin and welcomes runners and walkers of all ages and abilities—from seasoned athletes to first-time participants.

Students, families, and friends are invited for a morning of movement and celebration marking the first of what we hope will become a cherished annual tradition for our school. Rooted in our school’s growing love for running and strong cross country culture, the race also reflects the excitement around the continued expansion of athletics at Paideia!

Each registered participant will receive a race bib equipped with a timing chip, allowing for accurate race results provided by Huber Timing Services, as well as a commemorative race shirt.

Register as a group for a discount! Groups of 4 or more will be refunded $4.00 per registrant.

Whether you're racing for a personal best or simply enjoying the course with friends, our goal is to provide a fun, well-organized experience that reflects the heart of our school.

All participants, families, and spectators are encouraged to pack a picnic and stay to enjoy time together at Mary S. Young Park as we prepare for the year ahead. Come be part of this meaningful start to the school year—we can’t wait to see you at the starting line!

name: Path to Freedom 5k Obstacle Run
description:
Path to Freedom 5K, a powerful obstacle course race to designed to challenge body and spirit. Tackle 22 mission-inspired obstacles across a 3.1-mile course.  Each obstacle symbolizes the journey from captivity to liberation.

All proceeds from the event go towards Path to Freedom Project's mission to raise awareness and fund organizations that fight human trafficking and support rehabilitating survivors. 

Perfect for runners, teams, and first-timers, this event blends Spartan-style intensity with heartfelt purpose. Join us to break barriers, build hope, and fund freedom for survivors. All fitness levels welcome—run, climb, and make a difference! 

Check-in Time:  9 AM

Race Start Time: 10 AM

Included with your registration:  Event T-Shirt

Food carts will be on site to purchase food

name: Portland Bridge Swim
description:
Portland Bridge Swim: Sellwood Bridge to St. Johns Bridge

Sunday July 12, 2026

Ultramarathon-Distance Open Water Event

Hosted by Portland Bridge Swim

 

LOCATION & COURSE:   The course is approximately 11 miles (17 km) on the east side of the Willamette River through downtown Portland, Oregon. The swim will start at Sellwood Riverfront Park (SE 7th Av. & Miller St.) south of the Sellwood Bridge, pass under all 12 of Portland’s bridges on the Willamette River, and finish at Cathedral Park (N. Edison & Pittsburg Av.) west of the St. Johns Bridge. Water temperature is expected to be 66–74 degrees Fahrenheit.


TIDES & START TIME:  High tide on July 12, 2026 is 3:13 am, and low tide is at 12:42 pm. The swim will start at 7:30 am and all swimmers must be out of the water by 3:30 pm.


ELIGIBILITY: This event is open to any swimmer over the age of 18 years old who has completed the eligibility requirements.


ENTRY WEBSITE & REGISTRATION:  To qualify, swimmers must show that they have completed a minimum 5000 m/5500 yd swim faster than 1:40, within 3 years of race day. Only pool swims will be accepted for qualification. Swimmers who cannot complete one mile in open water in 35 minutes should NOT enter. All entries MUST be received by 4:59 pm Pacific time on Sunday, July 5, 2026. Due to organization & safety needs, late or day-of-race entries will not be accepted.


ENTRY LIMITS:  The Portland Bridge Swim is limited to the first 100 entrants. We will maintain a waiting list in case early entrants drop out.


CANCELLATION POLICY:  Swimmers who do not compete, or who do not complete the swim, are not eligible for refunds. If the swim is canceled up to 60 days prior to race day, 50% of entry fees will be refunded. If the swim is canceled less than 60 days prior to race day, no fees will be refunded.


RULES:  

  • SAFETY TOW BUOYS (STBs): All swimmers MUST wear the STB, provided with their swim packets, during their entire portion of the swim. STBs, defined as inflatable buoys tethered to the waist of the swimmer, are permitted in Category I Swimwear events per USMS Rule 303.4.2.E. Swimmers may not use the STBs for flotation assistance.
  • Swimmers must wear the standard latex cap provided in their swim packet. Swimmers must notify race organizers by Friday, July 3, 2026 if the cap cannot be worn. You will need to wear a suitable cap of the color assigned to you for your wave.
  • All drafting is prohibited.  Swimmers must remain 3 meters or more from other swimmers, except when rounding buoys, when overtaking other swimmers when space is not readily available, when unescorted at the start and finish of the swim, and/or when the swimmer's escort craft becomes disabled.  Incidental or accidental incursion into the 3-meter zone of another swimmer shall not be the basis for disqualification.
  • Swimmers may not make deliberate contact with craft, craft operators, and/or physical features on or near the course during the swim.
  • Propulsive devices, such as fins & paddles, and flotation aids, such as pull-buoys, may be allowed at the discretion of the Race Director if an adaptive category is offered for the race. Please contact info@portlandbridgeswim.com before registering if you need to use an adaptive device.
  • Earphones and snorkels are also not allowed. 
  • Motorized watercraft are not permitted as escorts for swimmers. Under no circumstances may a swimmer come in contact with a motorized watercraft. Swimmers who are supported by motorized craft will be disqualified.

QUALIFYING SWIM:  

  • To qualify for individual entry, swimmers must show that they have completed a minimum 5000-meter (5500-yard) swim faster than 1:40, within 3 years of race day.
  • Only pool swims will be accepted for qualification. This qualifying swim does not have to take place in a competition, but registration requires the location of the swim and the signature of an observer. 
  • If you make a mistake in your entry, we will make a good-faith effort to get your correct qualifying swim information. However, swimmers who cannot provide appropriate qualifying time information WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO SWIM and their entry fee will not be refunded. 

CUT-OFF TIME:  For safety coverage, swimmers on the course who have cleared the Fremont Bridge (approximately 5.5 miles) within 4 hours of race start (note: later waves have less than 4 hours) will be stopped, transported to the race finish, and listed as DNF in the results. Swimmers who have not completed the race within 7 hours of race start will be stopped, transported to the race finish, and listed as DNF in the results.


SAFETY—OUR PRIMARY CONCERN:  Safety boats will monitor the entire course and medical personnel will be on site at the finish. Swimmers are required to have an escort in a non-motorized craft (kayak, stand up paddleboard) in a life vest and equipped with an additional life vest for the swimmer. Each escort will be provided additional mandatory race-specific safety materials. Swimmers MUST wear the brightly-colored swim cap and use the standard tow float provided in their race packet. Swimmers and escorts must follow all announced safety rules without exception.


ESCORTS:  Swimmers are required to have an escort in a non-motorized craft (ie. kayak or paddleboard). Swimmers must provide their own paddler escort and craft. For swimmer safety, motorized watercraft are not permitted to escort swimmers. 


KAYAK RENTALS: A limited number of kayaks, provided by Alder Creek Kayaks, are available for rental as an option at registration.  Kayak rental includes boat, paddle, two life jackets, delivery at the start, and pick-up at the finish. If the escort cannot fit in a standard-size rental kayak, please contact the race organizers to discuss options.


TRANSPORTATION:   A shuttle will be available at the finish to transport swimmers and escorts back to Sellwood Park. With the exception of the rental kayaks above, swimmers are responsible for transporting their kayaks and they may not be taken on the shuttle.


SCHEDULE:  Sunday, July 12, 2026

5:30-7:00 am Check-in at Sellwood Park
6:30 am Pre-race meeting
7:30 am Swim start
11:30 am Individual swimmers who have not reached mile 6 will be stopped & transported to the race finish.
2:00 pm Awards at finish in Cathedral Park
3:30 pm Individual swimmers who have not reached the finish will be stopped & transported to the race finish.

AWARDS:  All finishers will receive a 2026 Portland Bridge Swim medal.  Awards will be presented to overall race winners, and the top 3 finishers in each category. 


RESULTS:  Results will be available after the race, and will be posted at www.portlandbridgeswim.com.  


OREGON SERIES:  Involvement in the Oregon Series TBD.


EVENT WEBSITE:  www.portlandbridgeswim.com


EVENT DIRECTORS:  Daniela Klaz, info@portlandbridgeswim.com

name: Race for the Warriors
description:
This is a 5k fundraising race to help support Pink Sistas-a local organization dedicated to helping women find connections with other women as well as themselves again after a breast cancer diagnosis.

Women who have been diagnosed with breast cancer often times feel vulnerable. Although many women have the support of loved ones, many women go through the journey alone. No matter what support they have, it's a lonely journey that only those who have walked the same path can understand.

Pink Sistas offers that connection through no-cost day trips and no-cost 3-day retreats. 

At their day trips, women have the opportunity to share their story, have lunch on our 22-foot pink drifter party barge, kayak, paddle board, and network with other like-minded women who are also breast cancer survivors and warriors. The result is an amazing opportunity to create bonds and just relax and have fun. At our 3-day retreats, women share their story, relax, exercise together, enjoy meals together, doing crafts, and most importantly, create connections and get the love and support they need in a time when they need it most.

name: Race to Save the Harvest
description:
9th Annual Race to Save the Harvest!

Minto-Brown Island Park


It's hard to believe this family-friendly race has been going and growing for 9 years! Thank you for continuing to support our mission to feed hungry families and reduce food waste.


The 3k out-and-back course, and 5k loop course, will be within Minto-Brown Park along shaded, hard-surface paths. The start and finish lines will be at the south end of Parking Lot 3 near the covered picnic area. Please review the course maps located under the Race Info tab at the top of this webpage.


There will be No Official Timing at this event. Our focus is on providing a safe, fun, family event where you can run, walk, hop, skip, or jump your way through the course with friends and family to support the work and mission of Salem Harvest.


Two options for Packet Pick up (race bib, race shirt, swag, ...) 
Friday, June 26, from 4pm - 6pm at Gallagher Fitness Resources - 135 Commercial Street NE, Salem Oregon
Saturday, June 27, from 8am - 9:15am at Minto-Brown Island Park - 2200 Minto Island Rd SW SE, Salem Oregon - near parking lot 3.


What else to expect at the race?


All funds earned will be used to help Salem Harvest gather fresh produce from local farms that would go to waste and make it available for hungry families in the Willamette Valley. The harvested crops would be left in the fields to rot unless it is saved by quick working volunteers. These fruits and vegetables are perfectly delicious but not usable by growers. So... Salem Harvest volunteers Race to the fields to Save the Harvest and get this unused resource into the community!


Event t-shirts will be included with registrations being made before June 5th. Entry fees increase and shirts won't be available when registering on June 5th or later. Register early to get the best price and the swag you need!


Raffle prizes - Fabulous raffle prizes will be available to win! Each participant will receive one ticket and can choose which prize they would like to win. Simply fill in the information on the ticket, and at the race starting area, drop it in the jar for the prize you want to win. A winning ticket for each prize will be drawn shortly after the race - at about 10:35am. You don't have to be present to win.


Want to increase your odds of winning? At the race you will be able to purchase additional tickets! For just $1 per ticket or $5 for seven tickets, you could really increase your chances AND help feed more hungry families. Explore the list of prizes HERE.


Ima Blueberry will be in attendance! We can't have a Race to Save the Harvest without our favorite celebrity - Ima Oregon Blueberry - cheering everyone on and sharing the goodness of Oregon's favorite fruit. Come down to the park to visit Ima and cheer with her for participants along the course! Everyone is welcome!


Yard games, bicycle-blended smoothies, snacks, and community informational booths will be at the race too. Come join the FUN!

name: Raw Oregon Honey 5k
description:
The Honey Run benefits the Oregon City High School Cross Country Team and youth runners of the community. The event is open to runners and walkers of all ages and abilities. Join us for a Day of Cross Country, as we host over 50 schools on the same course following the Honey Run.

Course:

This 5k will be returning to the Oregon City High School Cross Country Course this year.  The terrain is stroller friendly with short grass, packed gravel and a short dirt trail though a wooded area.

All Entrants Receive: 

The 2026 Honey Run shirt. Plus, the SWAG BAGS are back again. Guaranteed to be loaded with more 'merch and local gifts' than ever before. The first 200 runners to register receive the custom SWAG BAGS.

Awards:

Because of the growing size of our event we are expanding with more Honey Awards!

          -at least 2 age groups per gender (TBA)

          -plus, a 13 and under Champion Award.

Check-In and Day of Registration: 

Opens at 7:30am on September 12, 2026. We will do our best, but cannot guarantee shirt/size for the day of registrants. Race starts at 9:30am.

Vendors: 

Kona Ice and other Food Vendors (TBA) will be onsite during the Honey Run, and throughout the high school invitational that follows.

 

*Since we are racing on campus we cannot allow pets or animals unless certified 'Service Animal'

Bring your friends, wear your red, white, and blue, and join us for fitness, fun and community.

PRIZES will be awarded for best dressed so pull out your stars and stripes and come join the fun!

Run. Celebrate. BBQ. Fireworks.

name: Rogue River Triathlon
description: The Rogue River Triathlon includes a Sprint Distance and a Mini Distance. Both distances begin with a down-river swim in the Rogue River. Next is the run, 3 miles for the Sprint Distance and 1.5 miles for the Mini. The run takes place on a paved Forest Service Road overlooking the beautiful Rogue River. The event ends with the bike ride, 12 miles for the Sprint and 6 miles for the Mini. The bike ride is also on a paved Forest Service Road and boasts views of the Rogue River. There is also an option for a 2-3 person relay.

name: Roseburg Optimist 5 K RUN/WALK
description:
What is a Zombie 5k Run?

Runners will endure a 5 K run/walk through a zombie-infested course. Test your speed, endurance, and strength while trying to avoid
ravenous zombies! Runners will wear a flag (provided) on one side of their waist (like flag football). These flags represent zombie health. Zombies will try to steal those flags throughout the course. 

5 K Zombie Run was founded to celebrate happiness, healthiness, and friendship! Our mission is not about mile markers, but about
memories made.

We hope our 5K run will be an inspiration for healthy living. Those wishing for a run time must submit their phone numbers. 
The runner’s time will be provided through this method.

What makes the 5 K the Zombie Run special?
This 5 K Zombie Run is a fundraising event for the Roseburg Optimist Club. 100% of the proceeds go to the Roseburg Optimist Club to support children’s events in Douglas County. Your participation in the 5 K Zombie Run makes a difference!

All participants will receive a FREE 5 K Zombie Run T-shirt.  A commemorative finisher medallion, a race bib, a flag, and snacks at the finish of the race will be provided by Thrive Umpqua. Commemorative medallions will be awarded to healthy racers and infected racers. Infected racers are those who lost their flag to a zombie during the race.

Race information:
The Zombie Run will take place on Saturday, October 17th, at Stewart Park. The check-in time is 8:00 am, with the race starting at 9:00 am.

name: Run For Mercy
description:
Old Town Forest Grove is excited to host the Run for Mercy, a family-friendly run/walk event designed to bring the Forest Grove community together to support local families in crisis. All proceeds go directly to our Mercy Program, which provides critical financial assistance to individuals and families in our community. Helping with urgent needs like rent, electricity, and other essential bills during times of hardship.

Whether you're a seasoned runner or someone who just wants to make a difference, this event is an opportunity to move your feet and show your heart.

name: Run for Salem Free Clinics
description:
2025 Race Results are here 

Thank you for supporting Salem Free Clinics, we exist to be an expression of Christ’s love to bridge the gap in healthcare access by providing quality compassionate care at no cost to those in need. Last year’s race was a huge success, raising more than $41,000! This year, we are excited to announce that we will have both an in-person and virtual race option again!

 

Register by July 23rd to be guaranteed a free t-shirt (only adult sizes available)!
•    $30 for Early Bird Pricing | $35 starting July 23rd as well
•    $15 registration fee for ages 6-12
•    Ages 5 and below register for free (no t-shirt included)

 

NOTE TO IN-PERSON PARTICIPANTS: At our event, we ask that you keep your furry friends at home. Thank you!

 

NOTE TO VIRTUAL PARTICIPANTS: Run or walk your distance between August 8th and August 15th and keep track of your time to send to Huber Timing if you want it posted. To post your time, follow the instructions in your Welcome Email sent at the race start time on August 8th.

name: Run for the Oaks
description:
Run for the Oaks

This is the 10th annual Run for the Oaks at Left Coast Cellars! The course will predominantly be on gravel roads or off-road with trail and paved road segments. The run will meander throughout the Left Coast Cellars estate and runners will pass oak forests, vineyards, and gardens with spectacular views of the Willamette Valley. This run has been created to raise funds for our Oak Savanna Restoration Project. The goal of the project is to model how ecological integrity can coincide with responsible industry.

Great Event

  • Complimentary wine tasting!
  • Participant T-Shirts
  • Finishers receive a custom wine glass
  • Event professionally chip timed
  • Free Parking
We hope to see you out there!

name: Run Whiskey Run
description:
For more information, visit our website at www.SouthCoastRunningClub.org

Located roughly 20 miles south of Coos Bay, the region’s first single-track trail system is open year-round to mountain bikers, but for the first time ever will be reserved for those of us who shred at running pace. 

We’ll start and finish at the main Whiskey Run Trailhead. 

Our chosen section of Whiskey Run is shaded and sheltered, which means these trails are rolling, smooth, and oh so loamy.

Course options include:

·      1.5 Mile (Shirley Temple)

·      5 Mile (Whiskey Ginger)

·      10 Mile (Double Shot) 

Please note that all courses are 100% trail, so not stroller friendly.

PRICES

Online

$15 Club member (your discount will appear at check-out), Non-member $25. 

Day of race

$20 Club member, Non-member $30

Students: $5.00.  Use the code Student2022 to register.  To avoid credit card charges, students will not be charged at on-line registration.  Please bring $5 (exact change appreciated) to registration!  

START TIMES

-      9am (10 Mile Double Shot)

-      9:30am (5 Mile Whiskey Ginger) 

-      9:45 (1.5 Mile Shirley Temple)

Course support ends at 12 PM.

Day of race registration and packet pick up begins at 8:00 at Whiskey Run Trailhead.

Runners should assemble at the starting line no later than 10 minutes before start time for instructions from the race director.  

Come dressed to run; no space is available for changing/showering.

INFORMATION ABOUT THE AREA

Whiskey Run is located on Oregon’s Adventure Coast. Our costal community offers endless opportunities for beach combing, fishing, crabbing, paddling, hiking, and golfing. And don’t forget about the mountain biking… bring your bike and explore the 30+ miles of premier single track at Whiskey Run.

Come see what attracts so many runners to Oregon’s Adventure Coast.

name: Running Scared 5K/13K - Eugene
description:
Get ready for a spine-tingling race experience at the Running Scared 5K & 13K—where thrills, chills, and fast times collide!
Whether you’re brave enough to tackle the 5K or daring enough to conquer the 13K, this Halloween-themed event delivers a fun and festive atmosphere perfect for runners of all levels. Costumes are encouraged, so come dressed to impress (or frighten) as you take on a course filled with seasonal spirit.
We will gather at Kiwanis Park in Eugene, OR.
All athletes will receive a long-sleeve race shirt—perfect for those crisp fall mornings—and a custom finisher medal to commemorate their accomplishment.
For those looking to push their limits, take on the Deadly Double by completing both the 5K and the 13K. It’s the ultimate test of endurance and Halloween courage!
Competitive runners will have plenty to race for. Awards will be presented to the Top Three Male and Female Overall finishers in both the 5K and 13K, as well as the Top Three in Masters, Grand Masters, and Senior Masters Overall categories. In addition, the top three athletes in each of the traditional five-year age groups will receive awards in both race distances. For those taking on the Deadly Double, special recognition will be given to the Top Three Male and Female finishers who complete both races.
Whether you’re running for fun, fitness, or a frightfully good challenge, the Running Scared 5K & 13K is sure to be a hauntingly good time you won’t want to miss!

name: Santiam Canyon River Run
description:
The Santiam Canyon River Run featuring three race distances: 10k Race, 5k Run/Walk, and 3k Run/Walk. It’s designed to cater to a variety of runners, from seasoned athletes to casual enthusiasts. The course is multi-surface, including sections of trail, pavement, and gravel, providing a diverse running experience. The event takes place in the picturesque setting of Stayton, with sections along the Santiam River. Participants will have a unique opportunity to enjoy the lush natural scenery as they push toward the finish line.  Runners can expect a well-organized event with clear markings and enthusiastic support from the community. Whether aiming for a personal best or simply looking to complete the course, the Santiam Canyon River Run is an excellent opportunity for runners to challenge themselves in a scenic environment. This will be a chipped and timed race provided by Athletic Timing. This race is hosted by Santiam Hospital & Clinics Foundation. 

All races will begin and end at Snow Peak Brewing Company. Each finisher will receive a commemorative pint glass along with a coupon for a soda or beer from Snow Peak Brewing Co. Check in will begin at 8:00am for a prompt 9:30am race start.

name: Southern Oregon Runners Turkey Trot Run
description:
Come to Talent, Oregon for our Thanksgiving run! We will be hosting a food drive for the SOU food bank and a portion of the proceeds will go to SOR Student Runners Programs which include Shoes for Kids (provides shoes to Jr. High and High School athletes who would like to participate in Cross Country and Track but cannot afford proper running shoes), KidsRunFree (provides free entry to all SOR races for kids 18 & under), and XC Project (provides timing support for schools during cross country season).

When - November 26, 2025

Free Turkey Dash Kids Run( 8 and Under)8:00AM| 8 Mile Run 8:15AM|5k Run/Walk 8:30AM|2 Mile Family Run/Walk 8:40AM $20 for members| $25 for non members| Youth 18 and Under are free. Family Pricing available for this event, this is for families and families with extended family in town for the holidays, only.  

Where - Cummins 300 W Valley View Rd, Talent, Oregon 97540

Packet Pick Up - November 25th from 3:30-8pm at Legend Cider Co. Talent Taphouse, 245 W Valley View, Talent, Oregon 97540. Packet pick up is also available from 7-8am on the day of the race. NO IN PERSON REGISTRATION will be offered. 

Participants will receive a custom race bib and finishers medal. No age group awards.

NO DOGS, BIKES, SKATEBOARDS OR SKATES PERMITTED.

*Races are on public roads and trails that ARE NOT closed to cars, pedestrian or cyclist.  Please use caution while on public roadways and paths.

name: Sprint Into Spring 5K
description:
USATF Certified, chip-timed 5K in Estacada! Experience a challenging yet rewarding course that takes you through the scenic city of Estacada. Starting with a short but steep climb that tests your early race strategy, the course then rewards you with rolling hills through beautiful neighborhoods and parks before culminating in an exhilarating downhill on Broadway that will have you flying to the finish line in downtown Estacada.

All proceeds go towards Estacada Parks & Recreation.

name: Stayton Fun Run
description:
Stayton Fun Run

Since 1983 Stayton has been celebrating fitness and this family tradition on the 4th of July. Both the runs and walk of this annual event will take place on asphalt and cross-country surfaces. The courses are excellent for the competitive runner, fun runner and walker.

The Runs and Walk is being held in conjunction with Stayton’s 4th of July festival. The festival features such activities as a Kid’s and Grand Parade, a community dinner, band concerts, variety show, kid’s games, food booths and a fantastic fireworks display. So, there is much to do after the race is over.

The MOST PATRIOTICALLY DRESSED RUNNER will win a patriotic denali blanket a $130. value 

WHEN: Every JULY 4th, starting at 9:00 a.m. (DAY OF REGISTRATION FOR TIMED RESULTS WILL END @ 8:45 AM) ***8:30am Race Day Scout Flag Ceremony (start your 4th of july off right)***

WHERE: Starts at the Stayton Community Center – 500 W Burnett St. (Off 1st St.). Stayton is 15 miles east of Salem on Highway 22.

FEE: $15.00 per person if you pre-register online (before July 4th). $20.00 per person day of the race (DAY OF REGISTRATION FOR TIMED RESULTS WILL END @ 8:45 AM). Registration begins at 7:30 a.m. at the Stayton Community Center.

INCLUDED: Ribbons to the top male and female finishers in five-year age-groups in the 5k and 10k races; Stay around after the race to see who won the most patriotically dressed!

WHAT’S NOT INCLUDED: High Entry Fees, Fancy Awards

Learn More About The Race: www.StaytonFunRun.com

description:
Participate in one or all of the STRIDE run/walk events! Taking place in some of Salem’s most loved parks and held once a month on a Saturday morning, May-September. Strollers and dogs on a leash are welcome!

Bibs are available for pick up at/on the day of the event. For this event, bibs are available near Phillips' Field. Parking off Cross and Yew Streets will put you closer to the start/finish area.

Maps are emailed to participants after 5 p.m. on Friday, the night before the event.

This event taking place in Bush's Pasture Park utilizes a mixture of both soft and hard trail surfaces.

name: Strut Your Kidney - a dash for NW Kidney Kids (Vamos a Caminar Con Orgullo Su Riñón - una carrera para “NW Kidney Kids” )
description:
Strut Your Kidney - Hybrid - 5K, 10K, Family Fun Run/Walk/Roll or Virtual

Strut Your Kidney to celebrate, honor, and raise awareness for children with chronic kidney disease. All proceeds raised will go to Northwest Kidney Kids, the only organization supporting children with kidney disease and their families in the Northwest. Let's come together as a community so celebrate and fundraise for our amazing kidney families!

Here is how it works...

Step 1. Register to run/walk/roll or our fun run and invite your friends to join!

Step 2. Help NW Kidney Kids raise more awareness and financial support for children with kidney disease and their families.

Step 3. Run/walk/roll with us in person on Sunday September 20th 2026 or on your own and on your own time! 
*If on your own, submit your time and a finishing photo to be added to the Strut Your Kidney results leader board. Post a picture of your run to Facebook or Instagram using #strutyourkidney.

*For registrations after September 1st we can not guarantee swag availability.

SPONSORS

If you would like to sponsor or make a donation, please contact Maggie@nwkidneykids.org!

Major thank you to Eclectic Edge Racing for being our 2026 Timing Company!

Check out their website!

Español:

Caminé con Orgullo Su Riñón - Carrera divertida familiar de 1 milla, 5k, 10k o virtual

Caminé Con Orgullo Su Riñón es para celebrar y crear conciencia para los niños que sufren de enfermedades crónicas de los riñones. Todas las ganancias serán para “Northwest Kidney Kids”, la única organización que apoya a niños con enfermedades de riñón y a sus familias en el Noroeste.  Vamos a juntarnos como comunidad, pero manteniendo la distancia, para apoyar esta gran causa.


Así es como funciona…


Paso # 1. Registrate para correr/caminar/hacer cualquier otra actividad en el maratón. Y/O participar en la carrera de diversión ¡Invita a tus amigos a participar!


Paso # 2. Ayude a NW Kidney Kids a crear más conciencia y apoyo financiero para los niños con enfermedad renal y sus familias.


Paso # 3. ¡Corre / camina / rueda con nosotros en persona el domingo 21 de septiembre de 2025 o por tu cuenta y en tu tiempo libre!
* Si está solo, envíe su tiempo y una foto final para que se agreguen a la tabla de clasificación de resultados de Strut Your Kidney. Publica una foto de tu carrera en Facebook o Instagram usando #strutyourkidney.

*Para aquellos que se registren después del primero de septiembre, no podemos garantizar la disponibilidad de las máscaras.

PATROCINADORES

Si desea patrocinar o hacer una donación por favor contactarse con Maggie@nwkidneykids.org!

name: SummerFest Fun Run & Walk 2026 Presented by Santiam Hospital & Clinics
description:
Santiam SummerFest Fun Run & Walk

Saturday, July 25 • Stayton, Oregon

Kick off Santiam SummerFest with one of Stayton's favorite summer traditions—the Santiam SummerFest Fun Run & Walk Presented by Santiam Hospital & Clinics!

Gather your family, friends, coworkers, and neighbors and join us on Saturday, July 25th 9am for a fun-filled morning of fitness, community, and celebration. Whether you're a seasoned runner, casual walker, or just looking for a great way to start your SummerFest experience, this event is for you. Title sponsors for the 30th Annual Santiam SummerFest include NW Preferred Federal Credit Union, Santiam Hospital & Clinics and SCTC 

Choose from two scenic courses:
🏃 5K Run/Walk
🚶 3K Run/Walk

Both routes showcase the beauty of Stayton, featuring picturesque waterways, peaceful trails, and stunning Willamette Valley scenery. Walk, jog, or run at your own pace while enjoying the fresh summer air and the energy of fellow participants.

After crossing the finish line, the fun is just beginning! Spend the day enjoying Santiam SummerFest, the Mid-Valley's premier free summer festival featuring:

🎵 Live music and entertainment
🍔 Delicious food trucks and local favorites
🛍️ Vendor marketplace and community booths
👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Family-friendly activities
🎉 And much more!

Make a day of it and help us celebrate everything that makes our community special.

Register today, invite your friends, and be part of the excitement as we kick off Santiam SummerFest 2026!

Early registration is encouraged. We can't wait to see you at the starting line!

name: Sunset Bay Trail Runs
description:
Hilly, scenic trail run along the scenic Oregon Coast.  Sunset Bay Trail Runs feature very challenging courses, especially for the longer distances and the views will take what breath you have left away.  Seriously, this race has it all, killer hills through the woods, and an amazing flat cliff section where you'll see sea lions, rocks, the deep blue sea, and if you're very lucky, a passing whale.  This is an amazing, not to be missed course.

Packet pickup and start/finish line is at the gazebo on far south end of Sunset Bay.  Packet pickup is race morning only.  Please come at least 1/2 hour before your race start time.  Sunset State Park is a very gracious host and we want to keep our welcome warm.  Please do not park on the grass!

Half-marathoners must have reached the aid station after the first loop at Cape Arago by 10:45. This is at approximately 6.5 miles. That is an 18:28 minute mile, which is almost a fast walking pace. If you arrive at the aid station after that, we will switch you to the 15K race, no worries, you will still have a great workout and a great time!

There will be water and Gatorade at the start/finish line and plenty of snacks at the finish. There is one aid station for the 15K and 1/2 marathon runners that will have water, gels, and other snacks. The 15K will pass the aid station twice and the 1/2 marathon will pass it 3 times.  While we will have cups available, we encourage runners to carry a bottle to reduce waste.  No littering on course!  Please leave all waste at the aid station or carry it to the finish.  Sunset Bay has been a gracious host for many years and we want to keep it beautiful. 

There are restrooms at 4 miles for the 15 K and 1/2 Marathon participants. The course isn't on the road very much, but it is open to traffic, so be alert.  This is a RRCA sanctioned event.  For safety, NO headphones, rollerblades, skateboards (hey, you're on trails, that's not even possible), bicycles, animals, or jogging strollers are allowed during the race.

Proceeds from the event will be donated to the Marshfield High School Cross Country Team who will be manning the aid stations.  Go Pirates!

Ribbons to top three winners overall and in each age-group.  Farr's Hardware will donate a $50 gift card to a lucky random winner from each race.  We will select a winner during awards.  Must be present to win.

name: Support the Girls 5K Run/Walk Fundraiser for Breast Friends
description:
REGISTRATION IS NOW OPEN!!!!

Join us for this exciting fundraising event at Stickmen Brewing in Tualatin! The course is paved and mostly flat - perfect for all abilities and ages! Gather your friends, co-workers, and family to enjoy this meaningful experience together. After crossing the finish line, relax and refuel with pizza and a beverage from Stickmen Brewing.

Each year, more than 4000 people in Oregon are diagnosed with breast cancer. Our mission at Breast Friends is to ensure no one goes through breast cancer alone. We strive to be relevant, accessible, and inclusive, empowering individuals to thrive beyond their diagnosis.

This fundraiser directly supports our programs for individuals in your community. Registrants will be signed up for an individual fundraiser and encouraged to fundraise. Every dollar raised provides education, resources, and support to those who need it. Together, we can make a lasting impact.

We are looking for photographers and a DJ with a sound system to donate their time and skills! If you or anyone you know are interested, please reach out to lizbrown@breastfriends.org. Thank you!

name: Terra Linda July 4th Race & Parade
description:
Terra Linda July 4th Race
Join us for a fun-filled and patriotic celebration at the Terra Linda July 4th Race! This exciting event is perfect for runners of all ages and abilities, with three different race options to choose from:

  • 1K Fun Run: Ideal for families and young children, this short and sweet race is a great way to get everyone moving.

  • 5K Run/Walk: Perfect for those looking for a moderate challenge, this race takes you through the beautiful Terra Linda neighborhood, offering a scenic and enjoyable route.

  • 7.4K Run: For the more experienced runners, this race provides a longer and more challenging course, perfect for testing your endurance and celebrating the holiday in style.

Proceeds from the race will benefit Terra Linda Elementary School PTC (GO TIGERS).

Event Details:

  • Date: July 4th
  • Location: 1998 NW 143rd Ave, Portland, OR 97229 (Terra Linda Elementary School)
  • Start Times:  The races will have a staggered start.  See event info tab for race start time!
  • Registration: Opens at 7:00 AM
  • Cost: $25 per runner (if you're unable to pay the entry fee, coupons are available to ensure everyone can participate)

Come out and celebrate Independence Day with us while supporting a great cause! Whether you're a seasoned runner or just looking for a fun way to spend the holiday, there's a race for everyone! 🎉🏃‍♂️🏃‍♀️

name: The 2026 Great Bark Bash
description:
The beloved Bark Bash is now part of Bend Oktoberfest—bigger, better, and borkier than ever! We’re bringing your favorite dog-friendly competitions to the main stage, and it’s all for a good cause.

2:00 PM – 4:00 PM | The 2026 Bark Bash Dog Races & Dog Show
Hosted in partnership with the Humane Society of Central Oregon

2:00 PM – Wiener Dog Races
2:30 PM – Running of the Bulldogs
3:00 PM – Corgi Crush
3:30 PM – Mutt Strut Dog Show

Day-of registration for all dog events opens at 1:30 PM

Race Requirements: All race competitors must be purebred Dachshunds, Bulldogs (English or French), or Corgis.

Dog Show: All breeds and mixes are welcome for the Mutt Strut! Categories may be split by size.

Note: All dogs must show proof of rabies vaccination to participate.

Support a Great Cause
All proceeds from Bark Bash registration fees benefit the Humane Society of Central Oregon, helping to support their vital rescue and wellness programs. At just $20 per registration, you’re not only having fun—you’re giving back.

 

LEARN MORE about the full event and Oktoberfest at oktoberfestbend.com

name: The Fanciest 5K. Ever.
description:
The Fanciest 5K Ever is a recreational, fun, community race were runners fight human trafficking by running in formal wear! Dresses, tuxedos, bow ties, top hats, tiaras, all the glitz and glam… but on the run for a great cause! Got an old prom dress or ridiculously frilly suit you'd love to strut around in again? Fancy yourself up! All of the money raised goes directly to Safety Compass, a local organization that provides free, confidential advocacy for sex-trafficking survivors in the mid-Willamette Valley region of OR. 

Runners have the opportunity to become fundraisers and set individual or team goals for donations raised! We've got great prizes for the top fundraisers! 

2025 will be a In-Person AND VIRTUAL event, so runners can join us in Salem at West Coast Strength (290 Moyer Ln NW, Salem, OR 97304)  for all the fancy festivities and run the course across the river into River Front Park OR they can register and have a two week window to complete their fancy run and submit their time and photos virtually from wherever they are in the world! Prizes for top finishers, top fundraisers and fanciest costumes will be awarded at the end of the one week window.

RACE DAY SCHEDULE:
9:00 AM - Participant Check In, Bib and T-shirt Pick-up and Day-Of Registration Open inside the West Coast Strength (290 Moyer Ln NW, Salem, OR 97304)

10:00 AM - RACE STARTS at Start/Finish Line in the West Coast Strength parking lot. Runners head out onto the 5K Route through Wallace Marine Park and River Front Park, ending where they started!

11:00 AM - AWARDS CEREMONY starts inside West Coast Strength, Prizes for top finishers, top fundraisers and fanciest outfits!

name: The Great Pumpkin Run
description:
Home Life is a 54 year old Oregon nonprofit that assists adults with intellectual and developmental
disabilities in Benton and Linn Counties. By signing up for the Great Pumpkin Run, you help make it
possible for over 150 of our community’s most vibrant and vulnerable citizens to receive the support
they need to live happy, healthy lives.


We are pleased to welcome local runners as well as their family and friends from all over to
participate in this Run/Walk event. We invite you to dress up for the Great Pumpkin Run. This will
automatically sign you up for our Costume Contest so have fun and get creative.


You can choose between a 5k run or walk, a 10k Run, and Fun Run (1k) plus inflatable obstacle course.


For more information about Home Life’s work and mission and how you can support our work,
please check out our website.

name: The Homer Races: The Homer Classic 5k and The Homer Parade Mile!
description:
NEW EVENT! The Homer Parade Mile.

Lead the Homer Davenport Community Festival parade! The Homer Parade Mile is Saturday morning, August 8. Runners will "lead" the parade by running the parade route through downtown Silverton, being cheered by the thousands of people lining the parade route.


The start will be on North Water St. near Silverton Middle School and finish just past Roth's Fresh Market on North First St.

Combine The Homer Parade Mile with the Homer's Classic 5k on Sunday to see who is the overall mile/5k winner.

 

Here are the Homer Davenport Community Festival Race options:

 

1 Mile run: Saturday, August 8, 9:45am start time.

Runners ages 0-12, $5

Runners over 13, $10

Day of registration ends at 9:15am.

 

5k run: Sunday, August 9, 9:00am start time.

      $25 until May 1: $30 May 1 - August 8 (online registration ends at 5:00pm) : $35 day of race.

Do the Duo, 1Mile/5k runs: Run the Mile on Saturday, the 5k on Sunday.

      Pre-register for both events and save $5 on registration.

 

T-shirts, $ 15 extra. Register before July 14 to be guaranteed a shirt.

Race packets are available day of race.

 

The Homer Parade Mile is Saturday morning, August 8. Runners will "lead" the parade by running the parade route through downtown Silverton, being cheered by the thousands of people lining the parade route.
The start will be on North Water St. near Silverton Middle School and finish just past Roth's Fresh Market on North First St.

 

Sunday, August 9,The Homer Classic 5k start and finish of is Silverton High School, 1456 Pine St., Silverton, OR. There is plenty of parking at the high school.

 

The 5k run features a scenic, flat and fast course running through the Historic Gallon House Bridge, the only covered bridge in Marion County.

 

The races are organized by the Silverton Runners' Club. Proceeds go to support the Silverton, Gervais and Mt. Angel schools' track and cross country programs, scholarships for youth runners to attend running camps, and other local fitness activities.

 

No dogs or motorized vehicles permitted.

name: The Portland Grindfest - August 14th @ 6pm at Benson High School!
description:
Grindfest is one long progression run originally developed in Milwaukee, Wisconsin in 2013. The race/workout has now been spread all over the world, arriving in Portland in 2019. 

The rules are simple - start at either 9 minute mile pace (wave 1) or 8 minute mile pace (wave 2) or 7 minute pace (wave 3) and progress 20 seconds every mile (3 laps to a mile at Benson!). You stay in as long as you can until you can no longer grind the pace down any further and you wave the white flag.

Benson's newly resurfaced track is a one-of-a-kind 4 lane 535 meter track where 3 laps is around 1 mile. It's a beautiful facility that is perfect for grinding out a long progression run. 

This year the Portland Grindfest will serve as a fundraiser for Benson Cross Country as we’re raising funds to help cover travel costs for end-of-season meets where runners have the chance to compete against top talent and create lasting memories. Your donation helps provide transportation, lodging, meals, and the opportunity for every athlete to finish the season strong—no matter their financial situation. Thank you for supporting Benson Cross Country!

name: USARA Adventure Race National Championships
description:
For more than 25 years, the annual USARA Adventure Race National Championships have seen some of the best teams from across the nation come together to compete in a non-stop, 30-hour adventure race. Many of these teams have to push the boundaries of human endurance and teamwork just to finish. Winning requires extreme willpower, mastery across disciplines, and sometime a little luck. 

When the race ends, teams come together for an evening meal. We announce the national champions, crown the winners of the national points series, and celebrate the amazing adventure racing community. 

The 2026 race is limited to teams of four in three divisions:  mixed gender, all-women, all-men.  There is not a separate masters division, though the top masters teams from across all divisions will be recognized.

Race check-in will be Thursday, October 22, 2026. The 30-hour race will start Friday morning, October 23, 2026, and end Saturday afternoon, October 24, 2026.

Priority registration opens January 1, 2026. Eligible teams will receive a link by email. Open registration begins February 1, 2026. You can find the most up-to-date information on the event at the USARA website.

REFUND POLICY:

The RunSignUp processing fee will be deducted from any and all refunds.  A racer who withdraws within one week of registering will receive a full refund, less processing fees.  A racer who withdraws more than one week after registering will receive a refund pursuant to the following scale: 


Before 6/1/26:  Entry fee less $50 and RSU processing fee
From 6/1/26 through 7/31/26:  Entry fee less $100 and RSU processing fee
From 8/1/26 through 8/31/25:  Entry fee less $200 and RSU processing fee 
From and after 9/1/26:  No refund


A racer can transfer their entry to another racer at no charge.  Contact nationals@usara.com to request a refund or transfer of entry.

name: Vineyard Stomp 5K - Wetzel Estate
description:
Get ready to lace up and let loose at the Vineyard Stomp 5K—a race experience that blends scenic beauty, great competition, and a well-earned celebration at the finish line!
This unique course winds its way through beautiful vineyard property at Wetzel Estate Vineyards & Winery, offering runners a one-of-a-kind setting with rolling views, fresh air, and the charm of the vines all around. Whether you’re racing for a personal best or simply enjoying the atmosphere, this is a course you won’t forget. 
All participants will be treated to a fantastic race shirt and a custom finisher medal to commemorate their run. After crossing the finish line, athletes 21 and over can enjoy a complimentary pour of wine, while those under 21 will receive juice—making it a fun and inclusive celebration for everyone.
For the competitive runners, there’s plenty to chase. Awards will be presented to the Top Three Male and Female Overall finishers, as well as the Top Three in Masters, Grand Masters, and Senior Masters Overall categories. In addition, awards will be given to the top three athletes in each of the traditional five-year age groups, ensuring runners of all ages have a chance to shine.
Come for the run, stay for the experience—because nothing pairs better than a great race and a great pour!

name: 10K On The Bay
description:
Lace up for a race with a view!

Presented by the Hayward Area Recreation and Park District, the 10K on the Bay returns on Saturday, September 27– and you won’t want to miss it.

Whether you're a seasoned runner or just out for some family fun, there's a course for everyone:

  • One-Mile Family Fun Run
  • 5K (3.1 miles)
  • 10K (6.2 miles)

All races start and finish at the scenic Hayward Shoreline Interpretive Center, with breathtaking bay views and cool coastal air to keep you going strong.

Every participant receives a finisher medal and commemorative t-shirt* – plus the satisfaction of supporting the Hayward Shoreline Interpretive Center’s vital education and conservation programs. *Limited to the first 300 runners to register.

Sign up today and run for a great cause – and an even better view!

Follow us on social for updates on Facebook and Instagram.

name: 12th Annual Native Breast Cancer Awareness Walk/Run
description:
**If you are a Breast Cancer Survivor, please contact Adiyama before registering: 
alecanadau@wiltonrancheria-nsn.gov

Come enjoy a 1.4 mile walk or 2.8 mile run and a day of fun activities in support of NBCAWR! 


Early Bird Registration: $45 (starts June 15th; ends Aug. 9th) 

Late Registration: $55 (starts Aug. 10th; closes Sep. 11th) 


Registration includes:  event t-shirt, swag bag, light breakfast, lunch, drinks, and raffle ticket. 


Fun Zone: carnival games, jump house, balloon artist and face painting. 


Extra Fun Stuff: Mammo van onsite for screenings, health booths, exercise, Garden of Hope, honoring of Breast 
Cancer survivors, traditional healing, live entertainment.  

Please call 916-683-6000 ext. 2011 to make an appointment for a Mammogram Screening on the day of!

Our Journey:
To increase breast cancer awareness and screening, especially for 
Native American women.  Breast cancer is the second leading cause of 
death for Native American women.  It's estimated that approximately 1 in 
8 women will get breast cancer in her lifetime.  Our goal is to raise 
awareness and encourage women to screen early. 


PACKET PICKUP 
When: Friday, October 9th (Office closed on Oct. 12th)  
Time: 2PM - 6PM

Location: Wilton Rancheria Tribal Warehouse (9728 Kent Street, Elk Grove)  

Parking is available in the parking lot in front of the warehouse or on the street. 
Friday, October 9th

Location: Race Site @ Elk Grove Regional Park (9950 Elk Grove Florin Rd.) Plot 9a/9b.

09:30 AM    Welcome + Prayer    
09:50 AM    Team Roll Call   
10:00 AM    Stretch    
10:15 AM    Wave 1 - Runners   
10:18 AM    Wave 2 - Walkers 
10:30 AM    Fun Zone + Booths open 
11:00 AM    Guest Speakers - TBD

11:20 AM    Honoring of Survivors 
12:15 PM    Lunch + Entertainment (Paul Steward)
1:15 PM      Raffle* (final items)   
2:00 PM      Closing Prayer 
**8AM - 11AM - Coffee available (until last drip)** 
**11AM - 2PM - Kona Ice available** 
** Raffle waves are announced throughout the event **

name: 13th Annual Turkey Trot OC 5K
description:
2026 ONLINE PRE-REGISTRATION IS OPEN!

Pre-registration is now open!

Now in its 13th year, we invite you to join us for the annual Turkey Trot OC 5K on Thanksgiving morning at 8:00 AM. Your participation helps continue the work of ending homelessness, one life at a time.

Lace up your shoes and help give OCRM families a hand-up as they leave homelessness behind.

REGISTRATION

Every participant must be registered to take part in the race.

Exception:  Children ages 5 and under, including those in strollers, are welcome to participate and do not need to register. However, T-shirts and medals are only for registered participants while supplies last.

PACKET PICK-UP

Save time and pick up your race packet before race day. Participants may also pick up packets on behalf of other registered runners.

Packet pick-up will take place on:

  • Monday, November 23 & Tuesday, November 24 
  • 3:30 PM – 6:00 PM 
  • 1 Hope Drive, Tustin 

Packets may also be picked up on race morning from 6:30 AM – 7:30 AM.

RACE-DAY SCHEDULE

  • Pre-race refreshments — 6:30 AM 
  • 5K Run/Walk begins — 8:00 AM 
  • Expo & awards — immediately following the race 

This event will take place rain or shine. 

AWARDS

Age division awards will be given to the first- and second-place finishers in of each of the following category:  

9 & under, 10-14, 15-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+.

Top Finisher prizes will also be awarded to the top three overall male and female finishers.

GIVEAWAYS

2026 T-shirts & medals will be distributed to registered participants while supplies last due to limited quantities.

name: 14th Annual Luc's Run
description:
Luc's Run is held annually each spring in historic Tuolumne, California and Virtually Anywhere in the World. Luc's Run is known as one of the premier races in the county.  We are looking at welcoming our local 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under) back to Tuolumne, CA in 2023! And of course welcoming our supporters around the globe through our virtual run where hundreds of enthusiasts from around the world walk and run in support of Luc’s legacy on their own turf with a virtual 1/2 marathon, 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under). Sign up for two events and save 5%, sign up for all three and save 15%! 

On January 28, 2013, Luc, a United States Air Force pilot was on a training mission over the Adriatic Sea off the coast of Italy. During the sortie, Luc was forced to eject from his F-16 and did not survive the ejection.  Luc is survived by family and friends who continue his Legacy through the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation.

Major Lucas Gruenther was an incredible human being.  He was an outstanding F-16 fighter pilot, community role model, and a true humanitarian.  He lived his life to the fullest and never took a single day for granted.  Luc is remembered for the way he treated people with wisdom and kindness and was a genuine human being who made a tremendous positive impact.

All proceeds from this race go to the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation, an IRS-approved 501(c)(3) non-profit organization.  The purpose of the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation is to bestow scholarships to Americans for the advancement of educational goals and self development.

description:

Luc's Run is known as one of the premier races in the county.  We are looking at welcoming our local 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under) back to Tuolumne, CA in 2023! And of course welcoming our supporters around the globe through our virtual run where hundreds of enthusiasts from around the world walk and run in support of Luc’s legacy on their own turf with a virtual 1/2 marathon, 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under). Sign up for two events and save 5%, sign up for all three and save 15%! 

On January 28, 2013, Luc, a United States Air Force pilot was on a training mission over the Adriatic Sea off the coast of Italy. During the sortie, Luc was forced to eject from his F-16 and did not survive the ejection.  Luc is survived by family and friends who continue his Legacy through the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation.

Major Lucas Gruenther was an incredible human being.  He was an outstanding F-16 fighter pilot, community role model, and a true humanitarian.  He lived his life to the fullest and never took a single day for granted.  Luc is remembered for the way he treated people with wisdom and kindness and was a genuine human being who made a tremendous positive impact.

All proceeds from this race go to the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation, an IRS-approved 501(c)(3) non-profit organization.  The purpose of the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation is to bestow scholarships to Americans for the advancement of educational goals and self development.

name: 16th Annual Reindeer Run/Walk
description:
The 16th Annual Reindeer Run will be here December 5th!

Come one, come all! There is something for everyone at the Reindeer Run. We welcome runners and walkers of every level to American Canyon on December 5th, beginning with pre-race festivities at 8am, and a staggered race start (10K at 9am, 5K at 9:05am for runners and 9:10am for walkers).  

This is a fun event for the whole family: kids 6-17 are $30 and youth 5 and under are just $5 and include a finisher's medal and souvenir antlers! Early bird registration begins June 1st, so be ready to register to join in the fun!

*This event is contingent upon the requirements of Napa County Health Guidelines. If deemed necessary by the county, all registrations will be switched to a virtual race.

*Registration fees are non-refundable. Unused race fees are considered a donation to ACParks.

Need a race before the Reindeer Run? Be sure to check out these fantastic races on Thanksgiving Morning, November 26th:

Solano Turkey Trot, by Fleet Feet Vacaville

Napa Valley Turkey Chase, by Athletic Feat

name: 17th Annual Mardi Gras Madness 5K/10K!
description:
About the Event

Join us on Sunday, February 28th, 2027, as the Junior Chamber International of Santa Clarita (JCI) and the Santa Clarita Track Club proudly present the 17th Annual Mardi Gras Madness 5K/10K and Mini Madness 1K — benefiting JCI Santa Clarita and Students Off And Running (SOAR).

SOAR provides local youth ages 14–18 with a fully supported Los Angeles Marathon training experience — completely free for participants and their families — and is an Official Featured Charity of the 2027 Los Angeles Marathon.

What to Expect

Mardi Gras Madness is Santa Clarita’s premier family-friendly run/walk event, offering fun and fitness for all ages! Participants will enjoy a scenic USATF-certified 5K/10K course, chip timing, custom finisher medals, marathon-quality tech shirts, and a vibrant Health & Fitness Expo.

The festivities continue with a beer garden, great food, costume contest, games and giveaways, silent auction, celebrity hosts, and live entertainment. Whether you’re a seasoned runner, a stroller-pusher, or bringing your furry friend, Mardi Gras Madness welcomes everyone!

 
🏃‍♀️ COURSE INFORMATION
The MGM course is a USATF-certified, rolling 5K/10K circuit featuring scenic paseos, bridge overpasses, and sections along the beautiful South Fork River Trail.

Note: The 10K route includes a dirt equestrian trail from Mile 3.25 to Mile 4.85.
 
🎟 EARLY PACKET PICKUP
Skip the lines and pick up your race materials early!

📍 Saturday, February 27th | 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM
Location: Canyon Club Courtyard (rear entrance near H&M), Valencia Town Center

Please bring a valid ID to receive your 2027 Beer Garden wristband. No exceptions.

Due to overwhelming demand, onsite registration cannot be guaranteed this year.
 
🕗 RACE DAY SCHEDULE

6:30 – 8:00 AM - Check-In and Pre-Registration
7:25 AM - 1K Warm-Up
7:30 AM - 1K Start
7:55 AM - 5K/10K Warm-Up
8:00 AM - 5K/10K Start
9:30 AM - Awards Ceremony & Prize Drawings
 
🏅 AWARDS
Top 3 Overall Men & Women (5K & 10K)
Top 3 per Age Group:

  • 10 & Under
  • 11–14
  • 15–18
  • 19–29
  • 30–39
  • 40–49
  • 50–59
  • 60+
  • Top 3 Team Finishes
  • All 5K/10K finishers receive a custom medal, t-shirt, and goodie bag!

 
📍 EVENT DETAILS
Date: Sunday, February 28, 2027
Time: 7:00 AM – 12:00 PM
Location: Valencia Town Center, Valencia, CA 91355

name: 18th Annual Sevathon 2026 - 5K, 10K, Tiny Trots, 1K, Virtual Runs & Yoga
description:
From the Sanskrit word ‘Seva’ meaning service, Sevathon was born as an India Community Center initiative. It is a platform designed to bring Non Profit Organizations and participants together. When participants register for an activity at Sevathon and select the NPO they want to support during their registration process, they help the NPO fundraise for their cause.
Walkers, runners yogis and community members come together each year to support and raise awareness for non profit causes across the community. 
Don’t miss out on the thrilling experience of participating in this race. Lace up your running shoes and be part of this incredible event. Come celebrate and fundraise with us!

 

Event: 18th Annual ICC Sevathon 2026
Date: Sunday, September 20, 2026
Time: 7:00 AM onward
Location: Baylands Park, Sunnyvale, California
In-Person Events: 10K, 5K, Tiny Trots, 1K, Yoga
Virtual Events:   Virtual 10K, Virtual 5K



Pre Event Pick Ups 
T-shirt and bib pick up will be available on Friday September 18th (3 pm - 7 pm) and Saturday September 19th (10 am -        3 pm).

Event Day Pick Ups
T-shirt and bib pick up is available on the race day. Please arrive early and head to the Registration Booth. Keep the QR code received in your confirmation email handy. To avoid delays in participating in your event, please plan for parking, check-in, t-shirt, and bib pick up accordingly. 

10K: https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6605736305
5K: https://https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6597503067
1K : https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6597507421
 
There are overall winner medals in each race for Men and Women. Additionally there are age group winner medals. Timing mats will be placed at the start/finish point . Make sure to cross them for your timing accuracy especially 10K who will be doing 2 loops and be counted for awards.
 

Sign Up Here to Volunteer for Sevathon 2026!
 

Unforgettable Challenge: Push your limits and conquer the course. Whether you’re a seasoned athlete or just starting your fitness journey, this race offers a challenge suitable for all levels.
Community Spirit: Join a community of like-minded individuals who share your passion for running. The camaraderie among participants will give you the energy and support throughout the entire race.
Prize medals: Compete and receive medals for your hard work and determination! 
 

• If you are unable to join us at ICC Sevathon 2026 on the race day but want to support a Non Profit Organization and its cause, you can sign up for the 10K, or 5K Virtual Run.

• Runners will have five (5) days to complete the Virtual Run. Pick a day between September 16th, 2026 - September 20th, 2026 to run anytime, anywhere.

• The Virtual Run (5K, 10K) has to be completed on the same day and not over a period of days.

• Participants will track their distance and time via a run-tracking app of their choice, and submit proof of their run time and distance via screenshot to receive the t-shirt.

• Email proof of submission to fiza@indiacc.org . Submissions accepted between September 16th, 2026 - September 21st, 2026.

• T-shirts can be picked up at ICC (525 Los Coches St, Milpitas, CA 95035) by October 20th, 2026. Please note, they will not be shipped. See the 'Pre-Event Pick Up' section for available pickup times before the race.

Register for the 18th Annual ICC Sevathon 2026 soon. See you at the starting line!
 
To learn more about India Community Center, visit IndiaCC.org To learn more about ICC Sevathon, visit ICCSevathon.org

name: 2.2 for 22 Challenge for Veterans Expo at LPC
description:
THE 2025 2.2 FOR 22 CHALLENGE FOR VETERANS

ONLINE REGISTRATION IS NOW CLOSED.

If you cannot attend, please consider making a donation to support the Veterans First Program.

This event is "in person" to be held at the Las Positas College Track and Field on Sunday, September 28, 2025 from 9 am to 12 pm.   Doors open at 8:30 am.  Opening Ceremony at 9 am with the National Anthem.  

If you did not register, but still in interested in participating, there is an on-site registration/donation fee of $22.  Please arrive between 8-8:30 to register in person at the LPC Track and Field.  Free Parking.  (Make your $22 donation here - show attendant your receipt.)

 

The primary objective of the 2.2 for 22 Challenge for Veterans Expo is to raise awareness about veteran suicide and to help prevent it—highlighting the tragic reality that an estimated 22 veterans take their own lives each day.


Participants will receive a 2.2 for 22 T-shirt and a commemorative finisher medal or challenge coin. Event organizers strongly encourage participants to complete as many challenges as they can or even attempt all of them. Participants are also welcome to join or create teams to enjoy the event together. 

Participants are encouraged to share pictures of themselves taking on the challenges using the hashtag #CHALLENGE22FORVETERANS

The entire event will be held "in person," featuring a new obstacle course challenge that will test participants’ physical, social, and emotional capabilities.  

Click here for 2023 Recap Video.

Check out our highlights from 2023.
