name: Bizz Johnson
description:
Set PRs and qualify for the Boston Marathon on this fast, downhill course! Total net downhill loss for the marathon is 929 feet making it the PERFECT course to qualify on! Per official B.A.A. confirmation, there will be no time penalties assessed for this course.

All races in 2026 will be Sunday, October 11. The marathon and 50K start at 8:00 AM at Mason Station Trailhead on McCoy Road with an out-and-back before jumping onto the Bizz Johnson Trail at Mason Station where the races travel through scenic Lassen National Forest. The first few miles of the course climb approximately 280 feet through the forest to Westwood Junction, then it’s downhill to the finish at Susanville, with a 1300-foot descent over the final 20 miles. The trail follows the route of the old Fernley and Lassen Branch Line of the Southern Pacific Railroad, built in 1914.

Roughly two-thirds of the way through the race, the trail enters the Susan River Canyon. Here, you’ll pass orange cliffs and cross the river ten times on picturesque wooden railroad bridges. About four miles from the finish, you’ll pass through two former railroad tunnels, 800 feet and 450 feet in length.

The Express Half Marathon starts at at 9:00 AM at Goumaz Campground which is Mile 14 of the full marathon route. After a short up-and-back, the Express Half Marathon flies down the Bizz Johnson to the finish.

Starting at Devil's Corral, the new Express 10K on Sunday does the last 6.2 miles of the full marathon. This course promises to be a fast, fun race. 

For all four events, you will be bused to a remote start.

PACKET PICKUP

  • Saturday Noon - 6 PM (50K, Marathon, Express Half Marathon, Express 10K): Susanville Historic Train Depot, 601 Richmond Road
  • Sunday Morning 6 AM - 7AM (Marathon and 50K), 7AM - 8 AM (Express Half Marathon and Express 10K): Susanville Historic Train Depot, 601 Richmond Road

PLEASE visit our website for maps, schedules, and all the important details!!

USAT&F certified full marathon course (CA18035RS)

name: Bizz Johnson's Southside Scramble
description:
Are you ready to SCRAMBLE? This amazing new trail race showcases the best of the Susan River Canyon! Runners will head up the Bizz Johnson Trail from Hobo Camp for the first half and return via the beautiful and flowy singletrack on the Southside trail across the river. The Southside Scramble has 3 different distances to choose from, a 22K, a 14K, and a 7K. All races start and end at the Hobo Camp Day Use Area. On ODD years, we will run a reversed course! For 2025, all races go out the Southside Trail and back on the Bizz Johnson Trail. 

For the Dirty Devil's 22K, runners start on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and take the "outbound" portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail approximately 6 miles all the way to Devil's Corral.  From Devil's Corral, runners turn and drop down to the Susan River, crossing over a seasonal foot bridge, and enter the stunningly beautiful Southside trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp.

The Tunnel's Blast 14K starts on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and takes the "outbound" portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail approximately 4 miles to the entrance to the first railroad tunnel. Before heading into the darkness of the tunnel, runners will veer off onto singletrack, where they climb over the top of the tunnel to reach the Southside Trail. From there, they will enjoy the stunningly beautiful Southside trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp

The "Hobo's Special" 7K starts on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and heads approximately 2 miles up to the Twin Bridges Access connector to the Southside Trail. You'll get just enough of the Bizz Johnson's steady climb to excite your senses for the fast, flowy Southside's single-track return.

Finishers:

At Hobo Camp Day Use Area, participants can enjoy a fun finish line party with food and beverages.  All finishers will receive a custom medal and a custom beach towel just in time for a cool dip in the Susan River! Overall awards will be given to 1st through 3rd finishers (M/F/NB). Age group awards will be given to 1st-3rd AG in 10-year age groups.  

Start Times:

7:30 Dirty Devil's 22K

7:45 Tunnel's Blast 14K

8:00 Hobo Special 7K

Aid Stations:

Aid stations will serve fruit and salty snacks, Heed electrolyte, and water.  This is a cup-less race so runners should have their own hydration systems. Hydrapak is our cupless racing partner and runners will be provided with a collapsible cup at packet pickup.

Aid Station #1 is located on the Bizz Johnson Trail at the lower end of the lower tunnel at Mile 3.8. This aid station serves both the 22K and the 14K. 

Aid Station #2 is located on the Bizz Johnson Trail at the Devil's Corral at the Southside trail turnoff at mile 5.94. 22K 

Aid Station #3 is located on the Southside Trail just above the Twin Bridges access trail. This is approximately 2 miles from the finish. This aid station serves all three race distances.

For ODD years, with the reversed course, the Aid Station distances are slightly different. Additionally, the Twin Bridges Aid Station reverts to just hydration.

This race is Trail-Sisters Approved. There will be equal space on the start line for women and women's hygiene products at all aid stations and the finish line.

Event Parking:

Carpooling is HIGHLY encouraged as parking at Hobo Camp is very limited.  

Here are your options:

1. Hobo Camp - Most parking is on the middle and upper levels. There will be volunteers helping you park very tightly. There is also some parallel parking along the entrance road to Hobo Camp after the gate. This parking must only be on the uphill side of the road and you must be pointed in the direction to LEAVE Hobo Camp. There is NO parking on the Fire Roads.

2. There is some parking at Miller Road at the Bizz Johnson Trail (You must not park blocking the Bizz Johnson Trail). This is a short walk of about .25 mile from the start line.

3. There is a LOT of parking at the Bizz Johnson Trailhead across from the Susanville Historic Train Depot at 601 Richmond Road. This is about .75 mi from the start line. This is a flat, easy walk. One option would be to bring your bicycle and ride to the start. It is a flat, easy, short ride. There will be a place at the finish line to lock your bike and leave your keys with the Race Director.

Packet Pickup:

Packet Pickup will be at the Susanville Historic Train Depot at 601 Richmond Road on Friday, June 21st from 3 PM until 6 PM.  Late Registration will be available on Friday at packet pickup.

Race Day morning packet pickup will be available at the Hobo Camp Day Use Area (Finish Line Area) beginning at 6 AM. There will be limited race day registration from 6 - 6:45 AM (22K), 6 - 7:15 AM (14K), and 6 - 7:30 AM (7K).

Post-Race Activities

The Finish Line is approximately .1 mile from the Start Line. Feel free to bring a picnic lunch and EZ-up and hang out on the grass watching the other finishers. We will have hotdogs, watermelon, water, sodas, and non-alcoholic brews from Athletic Brewing Company for runners. If your family wants to join you, there are several newer charcoal BBQs in the day use area. The river has excellent access at the Day Use area so cooling off is a MUST!

This race is capped at  150 runners total for all 3 events!

Before heading into the darkness of the tunnel, runners will veer off onto singletrack, where they climb over the top of the tunnel to reach the Southside Trail. From there, they will enjoy the stunningly beautiful Southside trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp

The "Hobo's Special" 7K starts on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and heads approximately 2 miles up to the Twin Bridges Access connector to the Southside Trail. You'll get just enough of the Bizz Johnson's steady climb to excite your senses for the fast, flowy Southside's single-track return.

Finishers:

At Hobo Camp Day Use Area, participants can enjoy a fun finish line party with food and beverages.  All finishers will receive a custom medal and a custom beach towel just in time for a cool dip in the Susan River! Overall awards will be given to 1st through 3rd finishers (M/F/NB). Age group awards will be given to 1st-3rd AG in 10-year age groups.  

Start Times:

7:30 Dirty Devil's 22K

7:45 Tunnel's Blast 14K

8:00 Hobo Special 7K

Aid Stations:

Aid stations will serve fruit and salty snacks, Heed electrolyte, and water.  This is a cup-less race so runners should have their own hydration systems. Hydrapak is our cupless racing partner and runners will be provided with a collapsible cup at packet pickup.

Aid Station #1 is located on the Bizz Johnson Trail at the lower end of the lower tunnel at Mile 3.8. This aid station serves both the 22K and the 14K. 

Aid Station #2 is located on the Bizz Johnson Trail at the Devil's Corral at the Southside trail turnoff at mile 5.94. 22K 

Aid Station #3 is located on the Southside Trail just above the Twin Bridges access trail. This is approximately 2 miles from the finish. This aid station serves all three race distances.

For ODD years, with the reversed course, the Aid Station distances are slightly different. Additionally, the Twin Bridges Aid Station reverts to just hydration.

This race is Trail-Sisters Approved. There will be equal space on the start line for women and women's hygiene products at all aid stations and the finish line.

Event Parking:

Carpooling is HIGHLY encouraged as parking at Hobo Camp is very limited.  

Here are your options:

1. Hobo Camp - Most parking is on the middle and upper levels. There will be volunteers helping you park very tightly. There is also some parallel parking along the entrance road to Hobo Camp after the gate. This parking must only be on the uphill side of the road and you must be pointed in the direction to LEAVE Hobo Camp. There is NO parking on the Fire Roads.

2. There is some parking at Miller Road at the Bizz Johnson Trail (You must not park blocking the Bizz Johnson Trail). This is a short walk of about .25 mile from the start line.

3. There is a LOT of parking at the Bizz Johnson Trailhead across from the Susanville Historic Train Depot at 601 Richmond Road. This is about .75 mi from the start line. This is a flat, easy walk. One option would be to bring your bicycle and ride to the start. It is a flat, easy, short ride. There will be a place at the finish line to lock your bike and leave your keys with the Race Director.

Packet Pickup:

Packet Pickup will be at the Susanville Historic Train Depot at 601 Richmond Road on Friday, June 21st from 3 PM until 6 PM.  Late Registration will be available on Friday at packet pickup.

Race Day morning packet pickup will be available at the Hobo Camp Day Use Area (Finish Line Area) beginning at 6 AM. There will be limited race day registration from 6 - 6:45 AM (22K), 6 - 7:15 AM (14K), and 6 - 7:30 AM (7K).

Post-Race Activities

The Finish Line is approximately .1 mile from the Start Line. Feel free to bring a picnic lunch and EZ-up and hang out on the grass watching the other finishers. We will have hotdogs, watermelon, water, sodas, and non-alcoholic brews from Athletic Brewing Company for runners. If your family wants to join you, there are several newer charcoal BBQs in the day use area. The river has excellent access at the Day Use area so cooling off is a MUST!

This race is capped at  150 runners total for all 3 events!

name: BOLD BREAKTHROUGHS 2026 CSNK2A1 Foundation Virtual Run, Walk & Roll
description:
JOIN US!  Join our worldwide Okur-Chung Neurodevelopmental Syndrome (OCNDS) community on OCTOBER 10TH and OCTOBER 11TH for our BOLD BREAKTHROUGHS Run, Walk & Roll for OCNDS! This event will help raise awareness and fund research for OCNDS, an ultra-rare genetic disease that affects individuals worldwide. IF YOU SIGN UP AFTER SEPTEMBER 18, WE CAN'T GUARANTEE YOUR RACE SHIRTS WILL ARRIVE ON TIME.

DO I NEED TO RUN TO PARTICIPATE?  Absolutely not! This is called a run, walk, or roll. Our goal is for you to safely come together with others to bring awareness to OCNDS. Invite some friends and family to join you to come together for OCNDS. You can meet at the park, your street corner, the beach, or anywhere - get out of the house and move! You can RUN. You can WALK. You can ROLL whether on a bike, wheelchair, walker, scooter, roller skates, or rollerblades.

What is our theme for the year? Our foundation theme for the year is BOLD BREAKTHROUGHS. The overarching goals of the foundation are to:

  1. Fund Research to Find Treatments/Cure
  2. Support Families
  3. Raise Awareness
  4. Advocate for Change
  5. Fundraise to support our efforts

We can’t do this alone, and we thank you for your commitment to come together to make the lives of those living with OCNDS brighter. Please send us photos of you with your family & friends moving toward BOLD BREAKTHROUGHS to bring awareness to OCNDS. 

WHY RUN, WALK or ROLL? WHY DONATE? OCNDS is a lifelong condition that significantly impacts the lives of those affected and their families. We’re raising $50,000 to support research focused on the top priorities identified at our recent conference—where families and researchers came together to chart the future of OCNDS. These include sleep, speech and language, anxiety, intellectual disability, GI health, and drug repurposing. Your support will help turn these priorities into progress.

HOW TO SIGN UP:

Step 1. Register to run/walk/roll the virtual 5k or 1 mile, and invite your family and friends to join! Give your t-shirt size and mailing address.  IF YOU SIGN UP AFTER SEPTEMBER 18, WE CAN'T GUARANTEE YOUR RACE SHIRTS WILL ARRIVE ON TIME.  

Step 2. Invite your friends and family to join you and register.  

Awards to be given for: *Loudest Family/Individual on Social Media, *Top Fundraiser, and *Most Creative Forward Together Photo on Facebook/Instagram

PRICING: $30 per adult registrant, $18 per child (2-18) registrant

name: BOO-gie Glow Run 5K 10K Half Marathon - SummerWeen Series  by Califlow Runs
description:
🎃 BOO-gie Glow Run
    Night Race SummerWeen Series

     July 26, 2026
🌙 5K • 10K • Half Marathon • 1 Miler • Doggie Glow Run
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803
🕓 Check-In & Registration: 4:00 PM
🏁 Start Times | Half: 5:30 PM | 5K & 10K: 7:30 PM | 1 Miler (Spooky Glow): 7:45 PM

 
💀 About the Event
Disco meets the dark side… and your dog’s invited. 🐾✨

Welcome to BOO-gie Night Run, part of our SummerWeen Series—where spooky season crashes into summer nights for one unforgettable beachside experience.

We’re talking glowing lights, eerie beats, costumed runners, and pups lighting up the course alongside their hoomans. Whether you’re chasing a PR, showing off your best spooky fit, or just vibing under the night sky, this is where fun, fitness, and a little chaos collide.

 
🌊 What to Expect
✔️ Flat, fast, paved beach path course
✔️ Professional chip timing ⏱️
✔️ Instant ChronoTrack results (within minutes)
✔️ Free race-day photos — no upsells, ever 📸
✔️ Finisher medals for all runners + their pups 🐾🏅
✔️ Overall & age group awards
✔️ Multiple on-course water stations 💧
✔️ DJ, lights & glowing SummerWeen vibes 🎶
✔️ Costume Contest — spooky, disco, or full chaos 👻🪩
✔️ Dog-friendly, stroller-friendly, all paces welcome

 
🌕 The Course
Starting at 5400 E Ocean Blvd, you’ll run along the Long Beach shoreline as the sun drops and the glow takes over.

Expect neon lights, eerie energy, and a course that comes alive after dark.

🐶 Doggie Glow Run: Because your pup deserves their main character moment too

 
🧿 The Vibe – SummerWeen Energy
This isn’t just a race… it’s a whole mood.

Where:
👻 Spooky meets summer
🪩 Disco meets darkness
🐾 Dogs + hoomans run together
🔥 And the finish line turns into a full-on glow party

No pressure. No judgment. Just wild energy, good people, and a night you won’t forget.

 
✨ BOO-gie into the night. Embrace the FUR-ight. Join the movement.

Roller skates. Gold chains. Big dreams. Inspired by the unforgettable energy of Boogie Nights (yes, that Boogie Nights), this race is a tribute to the over-the-top sparkle and grit of 70s/80s California cool — with just enough late-night chaos to make it magic.

name: Break the Chains: A Walk for Cult Recovery - 2026 International Cult Awareness Month
description:
This isn’t just a walk—it’s a movement.

Join us for Break the Chains: A Walk for Cult Recovery, a powerful virtual walk/run honoring the courage, resilience, and strength it takes to break free from coercive control and cultic abuse.

Whether you’re walking in honor of a survivor, raising awareness in your community, or celebrating your own journey of freedom—every step you take helps shed light on the realities of cultic abuse and the healing that follows.

Over the course of six weeks (one week before August, throughout International Cult Awareness Month (ICAM), and one week after), we’ll walk together—virtually but united. Each week, participants will receive empowering content including survivor stories, educational tools, inspiring challenges, and calls to action.

💥 Your registration includes:

  •  A digital race bib to print and wear proudly
  •  Weekly themed content to keep you motivated and learning
  •  A downloadable chain-breaking progress tracker
  •  Optional access to exclusive campaign merch
  •  A certificate of completion to honor your commitment

No matter where you are in the world, you can help raise awareness, honor survivors, and be part of breaking the cycle.

  • All paces and mobility devices welcome (walking, rolling, treadmill, etc.)
  • No GPS tracking or time submission required
  • Content and activities will be screen-reader accessible and inclusive in language and design

How far is the race? That's up to you and your capabilities. Take it as far as you'd like! Here are some suggestions:

  • 4 Miles for 4 Weeks of Awareness - A short but powerful tribute to each week of Cult Awareness Month.
  • 10 Miles to Represent the Average Years in a Cult - Or choose a number that reflects your story—or that of someone you walk for.
  • 26.2 Miles (Marathon of Liberation) - For those who want to take on a bold challenge in honor of long-term recovery.
  • Freedom Your Way – Custom Race - Set your own distance, pace, and purpose. Every step counts.

Walk with us. Learn with us. Break the chains.

Hosted by The Freedom Train Project, Incorporated, a nonprofit dedicated to helping survivors recover from coercive control and cultic abuse, this virtual walk/run is more than just an event—it’s a movement for awareness, healing, and hope.

name: Brian Waterbury Memorial Rock to Pier Run
description:
Run the Coast. Honor a Legacy. Experience the Central Coast at its Best!

Join us on Saturday, July 18, 2026, for the 56th annual Brian Waterbury Memorial Rock to Pier Fun Run and the 12th annual Rock’n Around the Pier Half Marathon, starting at 8:00 AM.

Set against the stunning backdrop of the Central Coast, both events begin at Morro Rock and take runners along the shoreline for an unforgettable beach-running experience.

Event Options
Rock to Pier Fun Run (6 miles)
Run from Morro Rock to the iconic Cayucos Pier, finishing right at the pier. This beach run is open to all ages and abilities—perfect for seasoned runners and first-timers alike.

Rock’n Around the Pier Half Marathon
A challenging and scenic out-and-back course starting at Morro Rock, heading to the Cayucos Pier, and returning south. At mile 10.5, runners will detour through Cloisters Park before finishing back at Morro Rock.
Course closes at 12:00 PM.

Race Day Details
Both events start at 8:00 AM

Water/Aid Stations throughout course!

Expect wet shoes—this is a true beach run!
Post-race breakfast and awards at Morro Rock
Bus transportation provided from Cayucos Pier back to Morro Rock for Rock to Pier participants
Parking is limited in Cayucos; ample parking available at Morro Rock (arrive early!)

Extras & Notes
Limited shirt sizes available (some sizes sold out)
Dogs are not allowed on the course due to Snowy Plover nesting season

Come celebrate tradition, community, and coastal beauty in one of California’s most unique running events. Whether you’re racing for a personal best or soaking in the scenery, this is a run you won’t forget!

name: CaliFlow Poker Run: High Stakes & Happy Tails 5K. 10K. 1 Miler
description:
♠️ High Stakes & Happy Tails Run 🐾
5K • 10K • 1 Miler Doggie Run • Poker Run Option
📍 5000 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803 (Granada Beach)
🕓 Check-In & Registration: 6:30 AM
🏁 Start Times |  5K & 10K: 8:00 AM | 1 Miler Doggie Run: 8:15 AM

 
💛 About the Event
Get ready for wagging tails, ocean breezes, and a little luck on your side… ♠️🐾

Welcome to the High Stakes & Happy Tails Run—where miles meet a little mischief and every runner has a shot at winning big.

Join us at beautiful Granada Beach for a feel-good morning filled with movement, community, and pure CaliFlow energy. Whether you're chasing a PR, walking with your pup, or testing your luck in the Poker Run, this event is all about connection, good vibes, and unforgettable finish line moments.

🐶 Leashed dogs are welcome and encouraged!

Even better—this run gives back. We’re proud to support Long Beach Animal Care Services, helping care for animals in our community.

 
♠️ The Poker Run Experience (Optional Add-On)
Feeling lucky? 👀

Turn your run into a game. Participants who choose the Poker Run will collect cards along the course:

🃏 Pick up 4 cards at designated stations
🃏 Grab your final card at the finish line
🃏 Build your best 5-card poker hand
🃏 Top hands win prizes 🎉

No speed required—this is anyone’s game.

 
🌊 What to Expect
✔️ Flat, fast, paved beach path course
✔️ Professional chip timing for 5K & 10K ⏱️
✔️ Instant results via ChronoTrack (within minutes)
✔️ FREE race-day photos — no upsells, ever 📸
✔️ Finisher medals for all (dogs + hoomans 🐾🏅)
✔️ Overall & age group awards
✔️ Poker Run prizes for top hands ♠️
✔️ On-course water stations (for humans + pups 💧)
✔️ Dog-friendly, stroller-friendly, beginner-friendly vibes
✔️ Music, vendors & a fun finish line festival 🎉

 
🐕 The Course
Starting at Granada Beach, you’ll head out along the scenic Long Beach shoreline—wide-open ocean views, fresh air, and plenty of room to run, walk, and vibe.

5K: One out-and-back
10K: Two loops of the 5K course
Poker Run: Card stops placed along the route for maximum fun
The 1 Miler Doggie/Kid/Family Run is all about joy—short, sweet, and perfect for pups and their humans to share the experience together.

 
🌟 The Vibe – CaliFlow Style
At CaliFlow Runs, we don’t just put on races—we create spaces where people (and pups) feel seen, supported, and celebrated.

This is where:
🐾 Dogs become running partners
🐾 Strangers become friends
🐾 And finish lines turn into full-on celebration zones

No pressure. No judgment. No one gets left behind.

 
✨ Final Word
Run fast. Walk slow. Bluff your way to a win.
Or just show up for the vibes.

Come for the run. Stay for the vibe. Bring your best friend. 🐾♠️

description:
🌞 CaliFlow Verano Run – Griffith Park Summer
📍 Griffith Park – Crystal Springs
📅 Sunday, July 19
🕓 Check-In & Registration: 7:00 AM
🏁 Start Times | 10K: 8:00 AM | 5K: 8:00 AM | 1 Miler: 8:45 AM

 
🔥 About the Event
Feel the rhythm. Catch the heat. Run the summer.

 

“El verano suena bonito en español… pero en Los Ángeles, cobra vida.”
(Summer sounds beautiful in Spanish… but in Los Angeles, it comes to life.)

Join us for the CaliFlow Verano Run, a vibrant summer experience set in the heart of Griffith Park. This isn’t just a race—it’s a celebration of culture, community, and that unmistakable LA summer energy.

From golden morning light to tree-lined paths, this course brings together nature, movement, and good vibes in one of Los Angeles’ most iconic spaces.

Corre con nosotros. Siente la energía. Vive el verano.
(Run with us. Feel the energy. Live the summer.)

Whether you’re chasing a PR or just soaking it all in—this is your moment to move, connect, and feel alive.

 
🌴 What to Expect
✔️ Flat, fast, scenic park course 🌿
✔️ Professional chip timing ⏱️
✔️ Instant results via ChronoTrack (within minutes)
✔️ FREE race-day photos — no upsells, ever 📸
✔️ Finisher medals for all participants 🏅
✔️ Overall & age group awards
✔️ Multiple on-course water stations 💧
✔️ Music, vendors & finish line festival vibes 🎉
✔️ Beginner-friendly, walker-friendly, all paces welcome

 
🌿 The Course

Set within the beautiful grounds of Griffith Park, the  course loops around the golf course, offering a smooth, scenic route surrounded by trees, open space, and fresh air.

This loop is easy to follow and perfect for all paces—whether you’re chasing a PR or cruising through a relaxed summer run with your crew. Expect a mix of sun and shade, wide paths, and that peaceful park energy that makes you forget you’re right in the middle of Los Angeles.

 
💃 The Vibe – Summer in LA
This is LA in the summer—alive, colorful, and full of energy.

At CaliFlow Runs, we bring people together. This is where:
🌞 Cultures connect
🌴 Community shows up
🔥 And every finish line feels like a celebration

Aquí no importa tu ritmo—todos pertenecen.
(Your pace doesn’t matter here—everyone belongs.)

No pressure. No judgment. Just movement, music, and that summer feeling you don’t want to end.

 
✨ CaliFlow Verano Run
Come feel the heat. Come run the city.
Ven por el verano. Corre con el flow.

name: CASA Superhero Run
description:
Get ready to unleash your inner superhero at the CASA Superhero Run on Saturday, October 25, 2025, at the Park at Riverwalk! Whether you're a seasoned runner or just looking for a fun, family-friendly event, this race is for you.

Join fellow heroes and villains as we run, walk, and fly in support of children in foster care. Choose from a 2K, 5K, or 10K. The 5K and 10K races are officially timed, perfect for runners aiming for a personal best, while the 2K is an untimed fun run for those who want to enjoy the excitement at their own pace.

🗓 Race Day Schedule – Saturday, October 25th
📍 Location: The Park at River Walk

7:00 AM – Registration Opens
8:00 AM – 10K Race Start
8:15 AM – 5K Race Start 
8:30 AM – 2K Kids & Family Fun Run Begins
10:30 AM – Raffle Prize Winners & Awards Ceremony (time subject to change)

🎭 Costume Contest – Show off your best superhero or villain look!
🎟 Raffle Prizes – Enter for a chance to win exciting prizes!
🛍 Local Vendors & Food – Explore delicious eats and fun activities for the whole family.

Every participant receives (while supplies last):
🏅 A one-of-a-kind CASA Superhero Medal
👕 An exclusive race t-shirt
🎒 A swag bag full of goodies

✨ Capes are available for purchase, so suit up and get ready to save the day!

Why run? Because every child deserves a hero, but children in foster care need a SUPERHERO. Your participation supports CASA’s mission to advocate for children who need a voice.

Register today and be a hero for kids in Kern County! 🚀💥

name: CASA Superhero Run 2026
description:
The CASA Superhero Fun Run is Here! 

Calling all superheroes!!! The Child Abuse Prevention Council and Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) are thrilled to invite you to participate in our Annual CASA Superhero 5K Fun Run on Saturday, September 26th.

 

Event Details: 

Join us at Lodi Lake on September 26th for the 5K fun run. The event will take place from 8:00 a.m.-11:00 a.m. The timer will start at 9 a.m. and you are free to time yourself.  The Kids Dash will begin at 10:15 a.m. Enjoy our Superhero Alley and Community Resource Fair after you run or walk the Superhero course. Medals for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place runners will be given out at the event. 

Registration Details: 

Registration opens on July 13th, 2026

Adults are $35 

Children ages 12 and under: $20 

Same-day registration opens at 8 a.m. 

Each registered runner 13 and up will receive a CASA Superhero t-shirt or cape while supplies last. All registered children aged 12 and under will receive a CASA Superhero cape while supplies last at our Registration Booth starting at 8:00 a.m.

Registration Includes:

- CASA Superhero T-shirt OR cape for ages 13 and up while supplies last
- CASA Superhero cape for children 12 and under while supplies last

So, grab your cape, don your mask, reveal your alter ego, and unleash the SUPERHERO inside of you!!!

name: Catalina Island Half-Marathon & 10K
description:
Experience the ultimate California trail half-marathon, an adventure that will test your limits while rewarding you with awe-inspiring beauty. Starting in the charming town of Avalon, the race kicks off with a scenic run past the historic Wrigley Mansion. From there, you’ll journey into Catalina Island’s rugged Interior, tackling challenging climbs that lead to breathtaking peaks.

At the summit, take in sweeping views of the Pacific Ocean, where, on a clear day, you might catch a glimpse of two other Channel Islands. The journey continues with a thrilling descent through the serene Wrigley Memorial, winding your way back into the heart of Avalon.

For runners looking for a shorter, yet equally stunning course, the 10K route offers a picturesque tour through Avalon’s scenic hillsides, capturing the island’s unique charm and natural beauty. Whether you’re taking on the half-marathon or the 10K, this race is a perfect blend of challenge, adventure, and unforgettable views.

name: Catalina Island Marathon, 10K, 5K
description: California's State Off-Road Marathon Championship is also the oldest trail marathon in the state and takes place on beautiful Catalina Island located off the coast of Los Angeles and surrounded by blue ocean, green hills and more beauty than you have ever run through.   Experience the Catalina Island Conservancy the way it was intended to be experienced, on foot, running, and noticing the history and beauty of the island.  This is a bucket list event that you will want to run year, after year, after year.

name: Cerro Gordo Silver Run 2027
description:
Saturday, May 29, 2027 | Start: 7:00 AM | Check-in by 6:00 AM
8 miles | 4,600 ft of vertical gain | Keeler, CA → Cerro Gordo

(Camping & lodging info at the bottom)

Watch the 2026 recap video for a feel of what you're signing up for.

----

OUR 5TH ANNUAL RUN — COME CELEBRATE WITH US

Are you tough enough to race up a mountain road built for mule trains and silver barons?

Join us for a legendary race in the Eastern Sierra — an 8-mile uphill battle climbing 4,600 vertical feet to the historic ghost town of Cerro Gordo, once the richest silver mine in California.

This is not your average run. This is a gut-check. A pilgrimage. A challenge against time, gravity, and yourself.

The infamous Cerro Gordo Road was carved out in 1865 to shuttle silver down from the mountains. Now, once a year, runners race back up — chasing glory, chasing ghosts, and chasing history.

What happens at the top

When you summit the town, the day's just beginning. Cross the finish line and celebrate with:

— A giant mountaintop BBQ with mains, sides, and drinks
— Live music and games
— Self-guided exploration of the abandoned town
— A well-earned sense of triumph

What's included with your entry

— Aid stations every mile, stocked with fuel and encouragement
— A limited-edition Silver Run 2027 shirt and finisher's medal
— Mountaintop BBQ (mains, sides, drinks)
— Shuttle vans for the ride back down
— Eternal bragging rights — the winner's name is engraved in silver and enshrined in Cerro Gordo's history

The bar to beat

2026 winning time: 1:18:26 by Garrett Patrick. Think you've got what it takes?

See the full 2026 results: https://my.raceresult.com/401628/

For everyone, not just the fastest

There's no time limit. Whether you finish in 1 hour or 5, this mountain has room for all. We've had teenagers run alongside their parents. We've had two 82-year-olds cross the finish line in the same year. All are welcome — as long as you're willing to dig deep and climb.

----

Camping & Lodging

Keeler camping (closest & cheapest): Our neighbor offers camping spots in Keeler, CA, less than a quarter mile from the starting line, for $20/spot. Restrooms available on site.

Lone Pine, CA (15 miles away): A wide range of hotels, motels, and RV parks.

BLM land (free): Plenty of BLM land in the area allows free camping for up to 14 days. Google "BLM camping Owens Valley" for options.

Parking: Multiple lots in Keeler will be available the morning of the race. Volunteers will direct you on arrival. After the race, shuttle buses will bring you back down to your car.

Spectators

Bring your family and friends. For 2027, spectators ride up the mountain in our shuttle vans before the race begins to cheer runners across the finish line. Spectator passes are $30 and include the shuttle ride up and the mountaintop BBQ.

name: Champion Mine Trail Race
description:
Challenge Yourself and Enjoy the Great Outdoors

Join the Sierra TrailBlazers Running Club and Bear Yuba Land Trust for the 2nd annual Champion Mine Trail Race! Money raised through the races, besides supporting a great race, will be used to support more trails in Nevada County and the Mines to Pines trail work.

NEW - Race map coming soon, route has been corrected with easier to follow directions. Stay tuned!

Get ready to travel to a must-see destination race in Northern California. Explore some of Nevada City’s most exciting trails with this challenging half-marathon (13.1 miles) event. The course winds through towering pines, crosses a historic swinging bridge, and challenges runners with a series of rewarding climbs. With multiple aid stations, historical landmarks, and a newly constructed trail section offering varied terrain, this course rivals some of the best trail races in Northern California.

Runners will enjoy breathtaking views along the Tribute Trail and Deer Creek, combined with a beautiful variety of landscapes throughout the race. Best of all, the adventure begins right on Nevada City’s historic Broad Street — a truly unforgettable starting line!

The Champion Mine Trail Run offers a dynamic mix of pavement, gravel, and single-track trails, making it a must-do event for any trail enthusiast.

There will also be a 5K and new this year, a 10K! A 5K too short for you and a 1/2 marathon just sounds painful, then please consider the 10K. You won't be disappointed.

name: Chester 4th of July Fun Run
description:
One mile route down historic Chester Main Street!

The Almanor Recreation and Park District’s 45th annual Chester 4th of July Fun Run will take place at 9 a.m. on Saturday, July 4, 2026. The one mile run/walk will start on the Collins Pine lawn located at 500 Main Street and proceed down Chester’s historic Main Street to the finish at the Bidwell House located at 1 Main Street.

Participants will receive a commemorative T-shirt (first 400 registrants) and enjoy refreshments at the finish line. After the event, there will be a 4th of July Craft Fair at Chester Park from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. and a 4th of July Parade starting at 11 a.m. on Main Street. The Craft Fair is sponsored by the Chester Elks and the Parade is sponsored by the Lake Almanor Area Chamber of Commerce.

The one mile route down Main Street is open to participants of all ages and abilities, and adds to the excitement of the 4th of July celebration in town. The Fun Run is ARPD's largest fundraising event and all proceeds benefit District programs and events, as well as capital improvement projects, with an emphasis on recreation, parks and trails.

Please join us this year for a great time and be sure to wear your favorite costume or sport your 4th of July colors and bling. Spectators are also welcome. Thanks for your support!

name: Chingona Fest
description:
This event is a fundraiser for Chingonas on the Run and an opportunity to bring our community together through running and camping.

 Chingonas on the Run: Camp & Loop 

Where miles, mountains, and mujeres meet.

Join us for a weekend that’s more than just miles — it’s a celebration of grit, comunidad, and the kind of campfire connections that linger long after the headlamps switch off.

On Sunday, June 28, 2026, you’ll take on a 6-hour challenge to complete as many loops as your legs (and ganas) can handle within the 6-hour timeframe. Each loop is 4.16 miles with 728 ft of gain, winding through sweet single track trails in the heart of the Angeles National Forest, summiting Mount Hillyer each time you circle. The loop starts and finishes at basecamp where our aid station will be ready to keep you fueled, hydrated, and cheered on — every lap, every time. Click here to view route.

Note the cut-off to start the last loop is 11:45 AM. Chingonas have the option to set out for one last loop by 11:45 AM or hang out at basecamp to ring their cowbell to welcome the remaining finishers. As a reminder you are encouraged to run at your own pace and ability. We are here to support you on any goal you set for yourself within the 6-hour time frame.

 

 The Flow

Saturday, June 27, 2026:
Camp check-in opens 1:00 PM – 4:00 PM (no late arrivals). Find your spot, pitch your tent, settle in under the pines. Your campground fee is included in your registration, so all you need is your gear and your ganas — and if you don’t have gear, no problem! Email us and we’ll connect you with resources to borrow what you need.

Sunday, June 28, 2026:
The loop begins at 7:00 AM, weaving through that sweet single track with your Chingona crew towards Mount Hillyer. Each loop starts and ends at our basecamp aid station, stocked with snacks, hydration, and all the encouragement you need to keep going, loop after loop. Run your heart out until the clock strikes 1:00 PM — see how many summits you can bag before the final bell rings.

When the loops are done, it’s time for a post-run celebration. Gather for a hearty lunch meal, swap stories, laugh under the pines, and soak up that Chingona magic. You’ll walk away with a finisher’s medal and a keepsake to remember every brave mile and every unstoppable smile.

Closing ceremony will end at 5:00 PM, runners will be able to clean-up and depart between 5:00 PM - 8:00 PM (Note: Sunset is at 8:07PM).

 

 What’s Included

Trail Aid: Aid station at the start/finish of each 4.16-mile loop fully stocked with food, snacks, hydration, and high-fives.

Food & Fuel: Grab-and-go breakfast Sunday morning, dinner Saturday night, a hearty post-run lunch Sunday evening and grab-and-go refreshments throughout the event.

Welcome Goodie Bag: Festival Swag

Finish Line Love: A finisher’s medal — because your miles deserve to be remembered.

Photos: FREE event photos by a professional photographer.

Post-Run Celebration: Stick around for post-run celebration activities — laughter, storytelling, and community under the pines.

Campground Fee: Included in your registration — one less thing to worry about.

Parking Pass: Included in your registration.

Need Gear? No gear, no problem — email us and we’ll connect you to resources to borrow camping gear. We’ve got you, amiga.

 

 This is for You

Bring your miles, your messy, your brave. Bring your tent, your trail shoes, your hunger for connection and your wild, resilient heart. No gear, no problem — email us and we’ll connect you to resources to borrow camping gear. We’ve got you, amiga. This is where Chingonas lift each other up — loop by loop, mile by mile, under the endless Angeles sky.

This event is for women and those whose identity aligns with womanhood — trans, non-binary, and gender-expansive folks are warmly welcome. To honor this safe space, this event is closed to cis men.

name: Christmas in July 5K
description:
It's that time of year to run down shaded Christmas Tree Lane… in JULY!
Experience one of Fresno’s most iconic routes in a whole new way. This festive 5K follows the same beloved course as the Jingle Bell Run, starting and finishing near Palm & Van Ness... only this time, we’re bringing the holiday magic to summer!
This is a fast, flat, and beautifully shaded course perfect for all paces. Whether you're chasing a PR or strolling with friends, this race brings the summer heat with a festive twist.
✨ Part of the California Classic Runner of the Year Series (10-point race!) 
👟 Special Rate: Children 9 and under automatically receive discounted entry during registration, making this a perfect family event!

description:

Prizes
Prizes will be distributed at the end of each race and for the overall series winners. There are three categories in which the prizes will be given out: Sport, Expert and Pro.  Prizes for each race are as follows:

Pro 
1st place - $2000 cash
2nd place - $250 cash

Registration
We are capping the race at 500 entries, we encourage to sign up right away.

Please help us preserve the beauty of our mountains and assist in maintaining an enjoyable, safe event for everyone involved.

name: Citrus Heritage Run
description:
The Citrus Heritage Run is a Half Marathon, 10K, 5K, and 1-mile kids race on Saturday, January 9, 2027. This unique and “sweet-smelling” course winds through the historic orange groves of the California Citrus State Historic Park in Riverside, CA. As one of the most scenic course routes in Southern California, you will experience breathtaking views of surrounding mountain ranges and skyline as you inhale the smell of sweet citrus and orange blossoms beginning to bloom. This race is truly one-of-a-kind and all race distances sold out in 2026!

This event is a great tune-up race for 2027.We offer high-quality tech-fabric long-sleeve tees, finisher medals and age group awards. Along the course, you will find entertainment (live bands) and several hydration stops. description:

name: City of Artesia 5K Run/Walk
description:
Come join us at the 3rd Annual City of Artesia 5K Run/Walk! The goal of our event is to promote health and fitness in the Artesia Community! We invite you to run or walk our event, meet new friends, and enjoy our Health & Wellness expo afterwards, featuring food truck, vendors, giveaways, and more! Event is rain or shine!

Race Bib Pickup: Participants will be able to pick up their race bibs early on Thursday, November 19 and Friday November 20 at the Albert O. Little Community Center at Artesia Park (18750 Clarkdale Ave.) during the hours of 5pm-8pm. Bibs can also be picked up the day of the race before 6:30am!

name: City of Placentia Centennial 5K & Fun Run!
description:
City of Placentia Centennial 5K & Fun Run

Pin on your bib, lace up your sneakers, and get ready to run!

The race begins promptly at 7:30 a.m., with the starting line at Tri-City Park and the finish at Kraemer Memorial Park. Following the 5K, kids ages 10 and under can join the fun in the 1K Kids Run.

After the race, enjoy the Expo, then head over to Old Town Placentia for discounted food, drinks, and more.

Registration is now open, and participants are encouraged to sign up early to take advantage of discounted pricing. Whether you’re racing, jogging, or cheering from the sidelines, come celebrate 100 years of community, history, and hometown pride with us!

name: Claremont Freedom 5K
description:
Join us for the Claremont Freedom 5K on July 4, 2026, starting and finishing at Memorial Park in Claremont, CA (840 N Indian Hill Blvd, Claremont, CA). This scenic course takes runners through Claremont’s charming neighborhoods on paved roads with some rolling hills—perfect for runners and walkers of all abilities.

There is a 1k kids run/walk which starts at 7:30am, followed by the 5k which starts at 8:00am. After the race stick around to enjoy the Claremont Village Parade and the city's lively July 4th Celebrations. Don’t miss out on this beloved community tradition!

All registered runners get a shirt (design coming soon) and there are awards for the top three in every gender category.

Climb to Kaiser Fondo & Tollhouse Century
Clovis Rodeo 5K
description: Rodeo week is here! Let’s get excited and celebrate The City of Clovis with The Clovis Rodeo 5K and 2M! Then join in for an exciting after party to celebrate your run and kick off Rodeo Week! Small town vibes meet big time fun! All of Clovis coming out to support each other and the amazing Rodeo we are known for! Any Age, any Ability, all Welcome! T-Shirt and exclusive Belt Buckle Finishers Medal for all participants!

name: Coalinga Turkey Trot
description:
The inaugural Coalinga Turkey Trot is happening on Thanksgiving morning!
Trot your way through the 5K course or walk the 2K (1.2 miles) before you head home to feast. 
The event is family-friendly, so make sure to sign up your all of your kids, cousins, aunts and uncles! 
The event takes place rain or shine at the Coalinga-Huron Sports Complex on Cambridge Avenue.
Please NO PETS, but strollers are welcome. 
Each participant will receive a Turkey Trot t-shirt. 
Proceeds from the race will benefit the Coalinga Lions Club.

name: Coffee Lover Run LOS ANGELES
description:
☕️ 🏃‍♂️ ☕️ 🏃‍♂️ ☕️ 🏃‍♂️ 
For all the Coffee Lovers, this run is for you! You’ll love the shirt we send you. Set a goal, bring a friend, and join this super fun 5K/10K/13.1 Half-Marathon! The first 5 runners, we'll send you some coffee.  😊 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

For all the Coffee Lovers, this run is for you! You’ll love the shirt we send you. Set a goal, bring a friend, and join this super fun 5K/10K/13.1 Half-Marathon! The first 5 runners, we'll send you some coffee.  😊 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

Join us for the Coffee Lovers Run, where every mile leads you closer to great coffee, good vibes, and even better company.  Set a goal, bring a friend, and join this super fun run.

 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com

name: Colby Mountain Trailfest
description:
Welcome to Colby Mountain Trailfest

A grassroots trail running celebration put together by Butte County Sheriff Search & Rescue, Chico Velo TrailWorks, and Bidwell Run Club. We are bringing together runners, trail advocates, and community members to experience and support the incredible Colby Mountain trail system.

This event was created with a simple mission: give back to the trails that bring our community together. Every mile run helps support the ongoing development, maintenance, and stewardship of the Colby Mountain trails. Net proceeds from the race will be split equally and directly benefit three local non-profits: Chico Velo Trailworks, Butte County Sheriff Search and Rescue, and Bidwell Run Club -helping ensure these trails remain safe, sustainable, and accessible for runners, hikers, and cyclists for years to come.

Colby Mountain Trailfest blends endurance sport with environmental stewardship, creating an event where participants are not only racing through beautiful terrain but also investing in the future of the trails themselves. By participating, you become part of a growing movement focused on community, sustainability, and responsible trail use.

Join us for the inaugural Colby Mountain Trailfest — a new trail running tradition in the making.

Saturday September 5th, 2026 at 8:00am, in Butte Meadows, California

Save by Signing up now early bird pricing until August 1st, 2026.

We have multiple distances ranging from 5k, 12k, and 24k.

Race Swag: Each registered runner gets a T-shirt, Medal, and a Hydrapak re-usable cup

Awards: Top 3 men & women, Top 3 for age group.

 

Lodging in the area is very limited, so make sure to make plans ahead of time. The cabins sleep multiple people, so consider bringing your friends and sharing a space! 

The nearest hotels are in Chico, about 45 mins away by car.

Lodging Options - Subject to Change

description:
Welcome to the second annual Concord 5000. Our first year was a huge success and we are looking forward to hosting this meet again. This race offers a unique opportunity to run a 5000 on a track and get your true 5000 time. Concord High School Cross Country and Track & Field teams are excited to host this unique opportunity for our community. Come join the fun with music and friends!

We plan on having a taco bar vendor for your post race meal!

name: Concord California Turkey Trot 5K
description:
Diablo Valley Federal Credit Union (DVFCU) is pleased to welcome you to our information page about the Concord Turkey Trot, a 5K run/walk benefiting Loaves and Fishes of Contra Costa.

The event will take place at Newhall Park on Thanksgiving, Thursday, November 26, 2026, at 8 AM.  For the safety and enjoyment of all participants, registration for this event is capped at a TBD number of participants.  Everyone participating in the 5K run/walk course must have a paid registration, with the exception of children 2 years old and under, who will be in a stroller for the duration of the event. 

The course includes varied terrain, including grass fields, park pathways, and city streets. Those participating with strollers or pets will be asked to enter at the back of the start area so as not to impede those wishing to race for time. All 5K Run/Walk Participants will receive a tech t-shirt and a medal!

The race will take place rain or shine.  Once your registration has been paid, there are no refunds. This includes inclement weather or any other reason, such as injuries, illness, or personal emergencies.

name: Coronado Rotary Low Tide Ride & Stride
description:
Celebrate the 29th Anniversary of the Low Tide Ride & Stride with a our 5K Course during the lowest tide of the month on the beach from North Beach down to the end of the Shores and back. Kick off summer with this fun, family-friendly, 5K chip-timed race. Run! Walk! Bike! Stroll! This Coronado signature event takes place along one of the top 10 beaches in the world and provides much needed funds with Local Military and First Responders being the primary beneficiaries. Drop your beach chair in Sunset Park along with your reusable water bottle. After the race, kick back and enjoy LIVE MUSIC, grab a snack, visit local vendors' booths, and more.                                                  

WHY THE 5K COURSE?

If you have participated in past Low Tide Ride & Stride events, you may have noticed military and civilian volunteers lining the beach along the State Park and Navy Base. They were protecting the Least Tern’s nesting grounds. You see, the Least Terns are an endangered species and their numbers continue to dwindle. Even the military must limit their training on the beach during nesting season March – September. According to the Audubon Society, since 1970 we have lost half of all bird populations globally. By keeping the course of the race off of the Amphibious Base, Rotary is protecting critical nesting grounds for the Least Tern and Snowy Plover. We are excited for race course -- less hassle, family friendly, and fun at Sunset Park!  We can’t think of a better way to bike, run, walk and celebrate the beginning of summer than the Low Tide Ride & Stride!. 

For any questions please contact the event organizer at info@lowtideride.com or call (734) 945-6443.

This Coronado signature event takes place along one of the top 10 beaches in the world and provides much needed funds with Local Military and First Responders being the primary beneficiaries. Drop your beach chair in Sunset Park along with your reusable water bottle. After the race, kick back and enjoy LIVE MUSIC, grab a snack, visit local vendors' booths, and more.                                                  

WHY THE 5K COURSE?

If you have participated in past Low Tide Ride & Stride events, you may have noticed military and civilian volunteers lining the beach along the State Park and Navy Base. They were protecting the Least Tern’s nesting grounds. You see, the Least Terns are an endangered species and their numbers continue to dwindle. Even the military must limit their training on the beach during nesting season March – September. According to the Audubon Society, since 1970 we have lost half of all bird populations globally. By keeping the course of the race off of the Amphibious Base, Rotary is protecting critical nesting grounds for the Least Tern and Snowy Plover. We are excited for race course -- less hassle, family friendly, and fun at Sunset Park!  We can’t think of a better way to bike, run, walk and celebrate the beginning of summer than the Low Tide Ride & Stride!. 

For any questions please contact the event organizer at info@lowtideride.com or call (734) 945-6443.

name: Corporal Javier Bejar Memorial Run     Reedley Police Department
description:
Join us as we honor the life and legacy of Corporal Javier Bejar, a Reedley Police Officer, Marine Corps veteran, and beloved member of our community who made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty.

This memorial run is more than a race—it’s a tribute to courage, service, and community. Every stride taken represents our gratitude for Corporal Bejar’s dedication and the enduring impact he left behind.

All participants will receive a commemorative race shirt and finisher’s medal, designed to celebrate his life and sacrifice. Whether you run, walk, or cheer from the sidelines, your presence helps keep his memory alive and supports the values he stood for: honor, commitment, and service.

Together, let’s run in remembrance and unity.

 

NOTE: Only the first 350 Runners are guaranteed a medal.

Any participant registered after 01/25/2027 is NOT guaranteed a shirt.

name: Courage Triathlon 2026
description:
12th Annual Courage Triathlon


Race to End Trafficking. Run With Purpose. Move With Courage.

Saturday, August 15, 2026 | Lake Almanor Country Club | 10:00 AM Start

 
For twelve years, the Courage Triathlon has united athletes, families, and advocates around a cause that demands our attention: the fight against child sex trafficking. What began as a local race has grown into a movement — and this year, we're taking it further than ever.

The 12th Annual Courage Triathlon returns to the stunning shores of Lake Almanor, and this year, we're opening registration to virtual participants nationwide. Whether you're standing at the start line or lacing up your sneakers a thousand miles away, you're part of this fight.

 
The Course
Run - 2.8 Miles - Scenic road run
Bike - 6.4 Miles - Road cycling course
Row - 3.1 Miles - Kayak or paddleboard


From the adrenaline of a our scenic run and ride through the pines to the rhythm of your paddle cutting across the glassy surface of Lake Almanor, every leg of this course is designed to challenge your body and renew your purpose.

You're not just racing — you're running toward a world where every child is safe.

 
How to Participate

Solo: Take on all three legs yourself — run, bike, and row the full course at Lake Almanor.

Team Relay:  Split the triathlon among two or three teammates. Each member completes one or more legs of the race. Grab your friends, your family, or your coworkers and race together.

Virtual: Can't make it to Lake Almanor? Now you don't have to. Register as a virtual participant and log your own activities, distances, and times — on your schedule, from wherever you are.

We want you to join us in person, however we know that distance should not discourage your heart for supporting Courage. The beauty of virtual participation is that it meets you where you are. Want to run five miles through your neighborhood to show your support? Log it. Planning to paddleboard for two hours around your local marina? We'd love to hear about it. Prefer a walk around the block with your kids and the dog? That counts, too. Every step, every stroke, every mile matters.

Post your photos on Instagram, tag @CourageWorldwide, and let's show the world what a nationwide community of courage looks like. This year, we want to see evidence of support for child survivors from coast to coast.

 
Why We Race
Every registration, every mile logged, and every dollar raised goes directly toward the mission of Courage Worldwide — an organization dedicated to providing residential housing and comprehensive therapeutic services for child survivors of sex trafficking. These are children who have endured unimaginable trauma, and Courage Worldwide exists to offer them safety, healing, and a future worth fighting for.

When you cross the finish line — whether that's at Lake Almanor or at the end of your driveway — you're telling a survivor that they are seen, they are valued, and they are not alone.

Event at a Glance
Date: Saturday, August 15, 2026
Location: Lake Almanor Country Club
Start Time: 10:00 AM
Format: Solo, Team Relay, or Virtual
Run: 2.8 Miles
Bike: 6.4 Miles
Row: 3.1 Miles (Kayak or Paddleboard)
 
Big or small. Near or far. Every act of courage counts.

Register today and join the movement.

Learn more about Courage Worldwide

name: Crown City Open Water Swim
description:
Coronado’s Crown City Open Water Swim (formerly the 4th of July Rough Water Swim) is a long-standing Independence Day weekend tradition bringing together swimmers, families, clubs, and the local community for an unforgettable open water experience at Glorietta Bay Park, alongside support from Coronado’s local swim community including Coronado Swim Team Elite. 

Set against the backdrop of the iconic Coronado Bridge, the protected bay course offers calm water conditions, creating an ideal environment for both first-time open water swimmers and experienced competitors alike. The updated event lineup features the 1-Mile Open Water Swim as the featured main event distance, alongside the ½ Mile Open Water Swim and the 250m Youth/Kids Sprint Swim, creating an approachable and exciting race day experience for swimmers of all ages and ability levels.

Registration fees include event insurance coverage.

All participants receive a finisher medal, commemorative swim cap, and race t-shirt.

name: Cupertino Splash and Dash #2
description:
Race is happening on a Thursday afternoon

The Splash and Dash Race is an aquathon consisting of a 1.5km (1-mile) swim and a 5km (3.2-mile) run for adults.

And 200m swim (out and back) with a 2km run for the youth category ( 11-15 ).

It is a fun, community focused, grassroots event. There are timing chips, transition is not fenced in with guards, and spectators, kids and dogs are encouraged. The swim is in Stevens Creek Reservoir right outside of Cupertino, CA. The run is on Stevens Creek Canyon park trails. It is a great way to get an intense effort with two disciplines, or a great way to get open water swimming practice.

name: Cycle Through the Vineyards
description:
CYCLE THROUGH THE VINEYARDS 2025

 

Temecula Sunrise Rotary (a 501c3 nonprofit) is again celebrating Spring in the beautiful Temecula Valley Wine Country on Sunday May 3rd with our annual CYCLE THROUGH THE VINEYARDS 2026! And for our past participants, 2026 brings exciting changes! For the first time LORIMAR Vineyards will be our host venue for the start/finish, post-ride celebration and raffle! And we are again excited to award a raffle grand prize drawing of an AVENTON E-BIKE from AVENTON BIKES! And our local AVENTON dealer Bicycle Warehouse of Temecula has upgraded the ebike and warranty coverage to bring the value of this ebike to over $2,500!  Secondly, we will again offer a shorter scenic guided tour route of 13 miles for our intermediate riders. While there is no way to totally avoid the challenges of the vineyards naturally hilly terrain, the shorter route is designed to better accomodate some of our intermediate level participants. 

Lorimar Winery is a popular local winery known for its daily live entertainment and is nestled amongst the gentle vine covered rolling hills in the heart of Temecula Wine Country. They will be offering discounts on their wines (both flights and bottles) and food for our ride participants! We are confident that our riders and guests will find LORIMAR Winery a great venue to hold our post ride “happy hour”! This year we will also be celebrating AMERICA 250 and have a fun filled experience planned for our participants! We are truly fortunate to have such a picturesque location for our Cycle Through the Vineyards this year.

name: Dalton Canyon Ultra
description:
Welcome to the Dalton Canyon Ultra Race. This event is right in the backyard of the Dalton Hotshots Camp on the Angeles National Forest in Glendora California. This is an extremely challenging course with over 9,000 total feet of elevation gain and loss mainly on dirt trails with sections of pavement. There is a 50K solo race, a 50k 4 person open relay race, and a 10K solo option.

The mission of our organization and this event is to bring the wildland fire community together, honor, share and preserve hotshot history, and this years money that is raised will be donated to the Wildland Firefighter Foundation.

The event is scheduled to take place February 6, 2027 rain or shine.

For general information, donation or volunteer inquiry please email daltoncanyonultra@gmail.com, or check out our instagram @DaltonCanyon50k

name: Davis Moonlight Run
description:
Event Day:

Saturday night, July 18, 2026

Four Timed Events:

  • 5K, 10K, 10 Mile, 2K (approx. 1.25 miles)

Two For-Fun Events:

  • Beer Dash, Kids Sprint
  • Both are 26.2 meters (approx. 86 ft)

 

Event Details:

The Davis Moonlight Run will take place at Schilling Robotics, 201 Cousteau Place in Davis.

The 2026 event will kick off at 7:35 pm with the Kids Mini Marathon, a 26.2 meter dash for 8 and under. (Approximately 86 feet). Following the Kids Sprint will be the Beer Dash. Participants in this event will walk away being able to say it was the fastest 26.2 they've ever done. The Beer Dash is open to those 21 and up who would like to get a taste of the Davis Moonlight Run experience by completing 26.2 (meters), but are really there for the post-race beer garden (entry includes both the beer sample all timed entrants receive plus one full size 12 oz pour). 

The timed races begin at 7:50 pm with the 10 Mile and 10K, followed by the 5K and 2K at 8:00 pm. These courses are flat and travel along city streets as well as Davis' well-loved greenbelts. 10K, 10 Mile and 5K participants with an estimated finish greater than 45:00 are strongly encouraged to wear a headlamp or bring a flashlight for visibility along the course(s) in the dark. At the finish line, participants will be greeted with a heavyweight finisher medal (yes, it's cow-themed) and live music. Post-race activities include refreshments (including pizza by the slice, available for purchase), complimentary sno-cones, beer samples (21+) and awards distribution (for age group and our unique special divisions; see below for more details).  There is a 2 hour, 30 minute cut-off time for the 10 Mile and a 2 hour 20 minute cut-off for the 10K. A dri-blend short sleeved race t-shirt is included with each entry; we also offer the ability to upgrade to a tank top (men's and women's sizing; 100% polyester fabric) or the race hat. Please note that dogs are not permitted in this race due to our race insurance, unless they are service animals. Wheelchairs and pushed wheelchairs for disabled athletes, as well as strollers, are permitted. 

Your entry to the Davis Moonlight Run 2K, 5K, 10K, or 10 Mile includes the following*:

  • T-shirt (option to opt-out and save $5)
  • Finisher's medal
  • Age Group awards 
  • Special Division eligibility
  • Post-race music, suds, and snacks
  • Free downloadable athlete photos (new for 2026!)
  • Finish under the stars! 

*One complimentary beer sample to those 21+. Sno-cones available for everyone including those who do not consume alcohol or who are designated driver. Additional beers available for purchase. 

The Beer Dash entry includes:

  • T-shirt (option to opt-out and save $5)
  • Race bib (crowd will judge winner!)
  • Post-race music, sno-cones, and snacks - including one beer sample plus a full size 12oz pour

Kids Sprint includes;

  • Race bib
  • Finisher medal
  • T-shirt (may opt out and save $5)

2026 Start Times


6:15 PM – Race Night Registration Opens
7:35 PM - Kids Sprint (8 and under; 26.2 meters (86ft))
7:40 PM - Beer Dash 26.2m
7:50 PM – 10 Mile and 10K Start
8:00 PM – 5K and 2K Start
10:00 PM – Cut Off For Course Support
10:15 PM – Finish Line Breakdown

Note: at this time of the year it gets dark at approximately 8:40 pm.
Start times are subject to change. Last updated 5/27/26.

Packet Pick Up

A Pre-Race Packer Pick Up will be held prior to race night; time and place TBA. Bib and T-shirt pick up is also held on race night starting at 6:15pm. Arrive an hour prior to your race start to have sufficient time to pick up, warm up, use restrooms, etc. Remember, hydrate all day so that you are well-hydrated for your run/walk.

Beneficiary: Cancer Champions

A Change of Pace is proud to announce our continued relationship with Cancer Champions as our ongoing charitable partner. Cancer Champions is a 501(c)(3) non-profit dedicated to supporting cancer survivors through custom fitness, nutrition, and mindset programming tailored to the unique needs of those battling or recovering from cancer treatment. Donations to Cancer Champions enable the organization to provide survivors with expert guidance to complement traditional cancer treatment. A Change of Pace and Cancer Champions both believe in the powerful and proven benefits of exercise, and we are very happy to be able to deepen our relationship in the name of health, fitness, and quality of life.

Location & Parking

All races start and finish at the same location, at Schilling Robotics, 201 Cousteau Place, Davis, CA 95618. Parking (free) is available in the adjacent business parks off Cousteau Place on the east side of Cousteau. 

Course Maps

Scroll to the bottom of this page to view course maps. Aid stations along the routes (denoted by a W on the map) will offer water and Gatorade. Please carry fluids with you if you are accustomed to drinking them more frequently during your training.

Please note: Our race insurance for this event does not permit dogs, except for service animals. If your dog is a service animal, they are welcome to join you. Otherwise, dogs unfortunately should not be brought on the race course. They are welcome to spectate with you if they are leashed, comfortable in crowds and non-reactive to other dogs. 

Post-Race
