  • Date & Time: Sunday, October 25, 2026
    Location: Wild Runners Fair Oaks, 10149 Fair Oaks Blvd, Fair Oaks, CA

Participant Packet Pick Up

  • Saturday, October 24, 2026, 10 am – 4 pm
  • Race Day, Sunday, October 25, 2026, 6:30am - 7:30 am
  • Location: Wild Runners Fair Oaks, 10149 Fair Oaks Blvd,  Fair Oaks Ca 95628

Race Day Schedule

  • 6:30 am - 7:30 am: Race day registration and packet pick up
  • 7:30 am: All final items dropped off for the La Ofrenda
  • 8:05 am - Kids Races begin
  • 8:20 am - Day of the Dead progression to starting line
  • 8:30 am - Day of the Dead 5k/10k race begins
  • 9:30 am - Awards ceremony and costume contest

Swag & Event

All participants receive:

  • Bib number, timing device and safety pins
  • Short-sleeved event shirt
  • Finisher medal
  • Coupon for one-free tamale for each participant*
  • Special offers from our sponsors

* Redeemable only at the post-event expo and festival on October 25, 2026. 

  • Family-Friendly Walk/Run Events: The Day of the Dead 5k has something for every generation to enjoy from a 5k for adults to our Kid Races. 
    Live Entertainment: Immerse yourself in Mexican tradition with live music and performances. With stilt walkers and live music, transport yourself to another time as we pay homage to the cultural heritage of our grandparents.
  • La Ofrenda: To honor loved ones who have passed, bring offerings, such as photographs, flowers, nostalgic items, and foods as we create a collective space of remembrance and gratitude.  All items should be placed on La Ofrenda by 7:30am in front of the Wild Runners store at 10149 Fair Oaks Blvd.
  • Antojitos Delights: Enjoy the flavors and culinary delights that our grandparents cherished. In addition to free home-made tamales for race participants, indulge in the food and delectable treats of Mexican heritage.
  • Post-Race Festival and Expo: Unwind and connect with fellow participants post race! Explore our Community Partner and vendor booths showcasing the latest in fitness, wellness, and recovery services.  

5k Course

The race kicks off with a 0.5-mile downhill through the charming Old Fair Oaks Village neighborhood and over the bridge. Following a 3.2-mile out-and-back path along the picturesque American River Trail towards Bannister Park, the course remains entirely on paved roads and trails, catering to participants of all abilities and those with strollers.  The race concludes with an approximate half-mile ascent back to the finish line.

Awards & Age Divisions

Awards ceremony to follow event at 9:30 a.m. for the 5k and costume contest. Prizes for overall male and female winners will be presented. Top three finishers in each age division will receive a special prize. Age-group winners pick up prizes at the Awards table.

Top boy and girl finishers in the 1/4 and 1/2 mile races will receive a special prize. All other kid finishers will receive medals.

Top 3 finishers in the male and female races will respectively receive: 

  • 1st Place: $100 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 2nd Place: $50 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 3rd Place: $25 gift card to Wild Runners

1st place finishers in each Age Group (5k Run) will receive a free pair of socks from our sponsor from OS1st:
12 & Under, 13-15, 16-18, 19-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80+

Costume Contest:

  • 1st Place: $100 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 2nd Place: $50 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 3rd Place: $25 gift card to Wild Runners

Rules & Guidelines for all entrants*

  • Bib numbers must not be altered, should be worn on the front of the runner, and be visible.
  • No unregistered runners, walkers or pacers.
  • Wearing headphones is discouraged.
  • No bicycles.
  • Your pup is welcome to participate in the 5k race (always on leash and after signing a waiver).
  • Strollers are welcome.
  • Walkers/runners of all abilities and capabilities welcome. 
  • Shirts are not guaranteed for the late registration ( you can ask for previos year shirt)

* No refunds

name: DB Beer Bus to Drakes!
description: Well, since last year was such a success, why not do it again?  This year we are heading back to the "five and dime" to visit our very favorite friends at Drake's Brewing.  That's right, 50 friends, one amazing bus and a free beer when you get there.  This is an easy way to support your favorite running club while enjoying a beer or two!

name: Death Valley Century
description: Join us below sea level in DEATH VALLEY National Park! Half century, metric century and full century options! First 50 is out and back to Badwater and beyond. Second half is a lolllipop loop up to Hells Gate via Beatty Rd and back via Daylight Pass Rd. 4500' of climbing for the century.

name: Define Your Glow 5K, 10K, Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
✨ Define Your Glow 5K, 10K & Half Marathon

Date: Saturday, January 16, 2027

📍 LongBeach – 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA
⏰ Race Start:

7:00 AM Half Marathon & 8:00 AM- 5K. 10K 
🏃‍♀️ Run • Walk • Stroller Friendly • Dog Friendly • Virtual Option Available

Some races are about finish times.
This one is about showing up — for yourself and for someone else.

Join us for the Define Your Glow Run + Healing Expo, a powerful morning on the Long Beach waterfront celebrating movement, resilience, and community.

Whether you run, jog, walk, or participate virtually from anywhere in the world, this event is about the simple truth that movement helps us heal, reset, and reconnect with our strength.

The course is a flat, scenic out-and-back along the beach path — perfect for beginners, walkers, experienced runners, families, and dogs.

Come for the miles.
Leave feeling stronger than when you arrived.

 
🌊 Why We Run

This event supports Define Your Glow, helping restore the home of founder Shannel, a certified run coach, 4 time IRONMAN finishers,  and wellness coach whose home suffered severe damage after 27,000 gallons of water flooded the property.

Shanell has spent years helping others rebuild their strength — physically and emotionally — through movement and personal growth.

Now our community is coming together to help rebuild her space so that healing work can continue.

Your registration, donation, or virtual miles help make that possible.

 
✨ Healing Expo After the Race

Stay after the run for the Healing Expo, featuring wellness vendors, recovery tools, and resources focused on physical, emotional, and spiritual well-being.

Because the finish line is just the beginning.

 
🔥 What You Get

✔️ Professional chip timing
✔️ Free race day photos
✔️ Finisher medals
✔️ Overall & age group awards
✔️ Beachfront race vibes
✔️ Access to the Healing Expo
✔️ The chance to run for something bigger than yourself

 
💛 Run anywhere. Run together.

Can’t make it to Long Beach?
Register as a virtual runner and complete your miles from anywhere in the world.

Every step counts.

 
✨ Come move.
Come connect.
Come define your glow.

🔗 Register at CaliFlowRuns.com

name: Día de  Muertos - Viva la Vida - 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
🌺 Viva La Vida 5K, 10K & Half Marathon
📅 Sunday, November 1 | Long Beach, CA
📍 Start/Finish: 5400 E Ocean Blvd

💀 Celebrate life, honor those who came before us, and run your heart out at our Day of the Dead-inspired race by the beach. Dress to impress—our costume contest is ON! Whether you're decked out in marigolds, skull face paint, or a full-on altar on your back (hey, we’ve seen it all), this run is about honoring traditions and having a blast.

 

🏁 Race Day Schedule:

Two Start Times for the different distances 

Half Marathon: 7:00 AM
5K & 10K: 8:00 AM

1 Miler: 8:45 AM
Bib Pick-Up (Runner Check in): 6:15–8:00 AM @ the Race Ready Athletics Tent
Course Cut-Off: 10:30 AM sharp


🎉 Event Highlights:

🏅 Viva la VidaFinisher Medals
📸 Free Race-Day Photos
⏱️ Chip-Timed with Awards
🚰 Water Stations & Restrooms on Course
👶 Stroller-Friendly, Beginner-Welcoming
🍩 Epic Photo Stops 
🎭 Costume Contest Prizes


🌞 Why CaliFlow Runs?
We're not just a race—we're a movement. Expect high vibes, community spirit, and themes that make you say "Wait, what?!" Whether you're chasing a PR or just vibing in your skeleton jumpsuit, you belong here.

 
#VivaLaVidaRun #DayOfTheDeadRun #LongBeachRaces #RunWithPurpose #CaliFlowRuns #RunTheLBC  #CelebrateLifeRun

name: Día De Los Muertos 5k Race
description:
Come celebrate Día De Los Muertos (Day Of The Dead) and run a 5k race. 

 

5k run/walk starts 9am on Saturday October 31st, 2026. All levels are welcome, it is a fully paved path, strollers are welcome.

Packet Pick up is Saturday October 31st 7am-8:45am at North Natomas Regional Park (Same location as the race).

All participants will receive a t-shirt and sticker with registration, top 3 in each age group and top 3 over all in male and female categories will receive ribbons.

 

The race will be held at North Natomas Regional Park, it is a flat course held on the sidewalk which is a loop around the entire park. All ages and running/walking abilities are welcome to participate. Participants are welcome to wear costumes.

Only dogs allowed are service dogs, this is a USATF rule because this is a sanctioned race by USA Track and field.

https://www.usatf.org/home/top-utility-nav-content/event-insurance-sanctions/sanctions-faqs#Can%20dogs%20or%20other%20animals%20participate%20in%20sanctioned%20events?

 

This is a fundraiser for the Azteca FC youth Cross Country and track program. Every season members from Azteca FC work hard to qualify for the Junior Olympics. This 5k is a fundraiser to assist the athletes who qualify to attend and compete in the Junior Olympics. In July 2025, Jackson Sevilla and Ethan Tang, represented Azteca FC at the Junior Olympics In Savannah, Georgia. Your generous support helps athletes compete at the highest level and gain national recognition to help them earn opportunities to compete at the college level.

www.Aztecafc.com

Sponsors of this race include Lisa Kaplan, District 1 City of Sacramento Councilmember and Azteca FC.

name: Diabetes Walk-Jog-Run-Move!!!
description:
We want to encourage all levels to get out and move for diabetes awareness!!!

The goal of this event is to get those impacted by diabetes to move together and see the benefits of movement.  We would like this event to allow for type 1's to connect with one another and move together.

We will have a few speakers share how they are overcoming the diagnosis and breakthrough will provide information on nutrition and management.

We will have literature/resources available- as well as special guest to kick of our event.

This walk will benefit Breakthrough in there research to better the lives of those impacted by diabetes.

description: The race is conducted by the Mira Costa Track and Cross Country teams. Proceeds from the run go back to the team. The race is named after former Director of the Department of Beaches Dick Fitzerald who helped start the International Surf Festival.

name: Dig Deep Dash 5K Run/Walk
description: The Dig Deep Dash 5K Run/Walk will be a 3.1 mile race to benefit the nonprofit 501(c)3 Dig Deep Theatre! Family friendly, all ages and experience levels welcome! The race will be held at 8am on Sunday, October 5, 2025 at West Creek Park (24247 Village Circle Dr.) in Valencia, CA. All proceeds from this 5K will go towards upcoming staged productions and readings of classic and contemporary dramas and comedies. As this event takes place in the month of Halloween - and we are a theatre company - participants are encouraged (but not required) to dress as a character from film, TV, or theatre! There will be prizes for Race and Best Costume winners, including passes to Top Out Climbing Gym and more. ALL PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE A MEDAL!

name: DINO DASH
description:
It's an Orange County tradition!

The Dinosaur Dash is a community run, walk, and bike event benefiting the Tustin Public Schools Foundation. There's something for everyone--a 2k fun run, chip-timed 5k and 10k runs, and Bike Tours for all riding levels (15k and a family-friendly 5k).

The finisher medal for the 10k, 5k, and Bike Tour features our unique, student-designed logo.

The 5k and 10k top finishers in each racing age division will receive the official Dino Dash trophy--hand-made by Tustin Unified students. Second- and third-place finishers will receive a medal. The 2k Fun Run and the Bike Tour are not timed and do not have age division awards.

The 15k bike tour passes through Tustin and Irvine before returning to The Market Place in Tustin.  This tour is recommended for riders age 13 and up since it is on open roads.  We also offer a family-friendly 5K tour on closed roads. The Bike Tours are not timed.

A free family Expo will offer activities, school fundraising booths, and exhibitors.

The Tustin Public Schools Foundation is a charitable organization that supports the students and teachers of Tustin Unified schools by funding grants, scholarships, and enrichment programs such as after-school sports, robotics, college readiness, Tustin Summer Academy, and more. 

PLEASE NOTE: Race day registrations (Sunday, November 1st) do not include a shirt.

6:30 AM - Bike Valet Opens

6:30 AM - Bike Tour - 15k begins on open roads

6:45 AM - Bike Tour - 5k begins on closed roads

7:00 AM - Dino Dash Expo Opens

7:00 AM - 10K Chip-timed Run Begins

8:00 AM - Food Court Opens

8:00 AM - 5K Chip-timed Run Begins

8:20 AM - TUSD Middle School Cross Country 5k Begins

8:45 AM - 2K Fun Run Begins (non-timed)

10:00 AM - Video Contest Awards - Expo Stage

10:30 AM - Event Ends

The 5k and 10k top finishers in each racing age division will receive the official Dino Dash trophy--hand-made by Tustin Unified students. Second- and third-place finishers will receive a medal. The 2k Fun Run and the Bike Tour are not timed and do not have age division awards.

The 15k bike tour passes through Tustin and Irvine before returning to The Market Place in Tustin.  This tour is recommended for riders age 13 and up since it is on open roads.  We also offer a family-friendly 5K tour on closed roads. The Bike Tours are not timed.

A free family Expo will offer activities, school fundraising booths, and exhibitors.

The Tustin Public Schools Foundation is a charitable organization that supports the students and teachers of Tustin Unified schools by funding grants, scholarships, and enrichment programs such as after-school sports, robotics, college readiness, Tustin Summer Academy, and more. 

PLEASE NOTE: Race day registrations (Sunday, November 1st) do not include a shirt.

name: Disco Miles: Beachfront Boogie 5K, 10K, Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
🪩 Disco Miles: Beachfront Boogie
Saturday, March 6, 2027 | Long Beach, CA
5K • 10K • Half Marathon

📍 Location: 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803

 

⏰ Race Day Schedule
🎽 Bib Pick-Up/Same Day Registration: 6:00AM – 8:00AM @ Race Ready Athletics Tent
🏁 Half Marathon Start: 7:00AM
🏁 5K & 10K Start: 8:00AM

🏅 Overall Finisher Awards | Costume Contest: 8:45AM, 9:00AM (Half Marathon Awards)
 
🚗 Parking Info
Street parking is available (please check posted signs for street sweeping).
Paid beach lot parking is available for $2.00 per hour via the Passport app or payment machine at the lot entrance. Arrive early for the best spots near the start line.


 
🏅 Awards & Medals:
All finishers receive a Disco Miles: Beachfront Boogie medal 🪩🌊
🏆 Age Group Awards available at Results Tent, just ask one of our staff members to verify for you.
🕺 Disco Costume Contest Awards for those who bring the sparkle, bell bottoms, and groove!
 

Get ready to lace up, turn up the groove, and run straight into a Sunday Funday celebration by the sea at Disco Miles: Beachfront Boogie 🕺🌊

This isn’t your average race — it’s a high-energy coastal run with disco flair, beach views, feel-good miles, and a finish line that feels like a party. Whether you’re chasing a PR, running with friends, or just here to boogie your way down the course, Disco Miles is all about movement, music, and fun — CaliFlow style.

Come run. Come dance. Come boogie on the beach.

 
🪩 Race Highlights
✨ Professionally chip-timed for accurate results
📸 FREE race-day photos & downloadable finish-line pics
🎖️ Finisher medals for all participants
🏆 Overall & Age Group Awards
🕺 Disco-themed costume contest — solo, duo, and group prizes!
🌊 Flat, fast, and scenic beachfront course
🥤 Water stations & restrooms along the course
🎶 Finish-line music, snacks, and epic photo ops

 
🌺 Why CaliFlow Runs?
At CaliFlow Runs, we believe running should be inclusive, affordable, and fun. With 60+ events each year, we create professionally produced race experiences that welcome every pace, every body, and every reason for showing up.

From the start line to the finish-line festival, our events are built around community, good vibes, and memorable moments — without the high price tag. Whether you’re running hard or just grooving through the miles, you belong here.

 
👟 Who Can Participate?
Everyone! Runners, walkers, strollers — all paces and abilities are welcome. Come as you are and leave with tired legs, a shiny medal, and a smile on your face 🪩

 


💫 A Quick Note
There are several races that take place in and around our Long Beach course locations — but there’s only one CaliFlow Runs 🌊
We are not affiliated with any other events in the area.

If you’re looking for a race experience with professional chip timing, free photos, organized staff, and that signature CaliFlow energy, always be sure you see the CaliFlow Runs name or logo before you register.

If it’s not CaliFlow, it’s just an average race. 🪩✨

name: Do It For Her 5K
description:
Run through Temecula’s Wine Country and enjoy the tranquil beauty of rolling vineyards and sun-drenched hills. As you run along the winding paths, the early morning light casts a golden hue over the landscape, highlighting the neat rows of grapevines and the rustic charm of the wineries scattered throughout the valley. Finish with a Vitagliano sangria made from some of the finest Super Tuscan-style wines produced in California.  Shop our local vendors carrying locally grown produce and handcrafted items, all under a beautiful covered patio.  Food Available for purchase.


All proceeds benefit the Heather Janikowski Foundation and the Make A Wish Foundation

Race day Information:

Please follow Parking signs/volunteer directions

7:00am Race Day Registration/Check In (also available Friday and Saturday - See below for times)

7:40am Warm Up 

8:00am Race begins

10:00am Awards

10:30am Raffle Drawing

7:00am-11:00am Enjoy, Coffee, Wine, Food, and our Vendor Market

*For the safety of our runners, please arrive no later than 7:40am

name: Dog Days of Summer – 5K, 10K, 10M, and Half Marathon
description:
🐾☀️ Join us at Alamitos Beach  for the Dog Days of Summer Run, a sun-soaked celebration of good vibes, wagging tails, and coastal miles. Whether you're chasing a new PR or just cruising the beach path, this feel-good race is your chance to run wild, stay cool, and soak up every last drop of summer.

Our nonprofit partners at K9 Kismet will be joining us for the Dog Days of Summer! Join us after the 5k for a doggie dash with your pup to get race photos together! There will be treats post-race!

Race Details

Start Location: Alamitos Beach, 780 E Shoreline Dr. Long Beach, CA
Parking: Parking in the local lots is usually $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free but limited.

Event Schedule

Friday

4-6:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email the week of the event)

Saturday

6:20am – Bib pick-up opens
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
9:00am – Doggie Dash photo opportunity (must have race bib for photos)
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10m)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Course

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More about the Course

The beach path is an open course, so you will encounter others using it. When we start the race, please stay on the right side of the beach path. The right side is for pedestrians and the left side is for cyclists.

On-Course Support: A fully stocked water station is located at the Belmont Pier. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, gatorade, gels, and fruit snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk, a runner turn sign, and a flag

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Awards: All finishers earn a race medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance.
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, the San Fernando Valley, and Orange County. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule

Have Another Question? Check our FAQ page, it's probably answered there!

Event Schedule

name: Donut Stop Running
description:
🍩Join us for the Donut Stop Running 5K, a fun-filled community race created to bring families, friends, schools, and local supporters together for an unforgettable morning of fitness and fun! Whether you’re running for a personal best, walking with friends, or just coming for the donuts and good vibes, this event is for everyone.

Participants will enjoy music, medals, giveaways, sweet treats, and an exciting race atmosphere while supporting a great cause. Proceeds from this event help provide back-to-school supplies, resources, and opportunities for local students through MEMC 1440 (Make Every Minute Count).

Walk. Run. Have Fun. Make Every Minute Count.

name: Double Dipsea
description:
Stinson Beach to Mill Valley and back to Stinson again, entirely on the world-famous Dipsea Trail both ways!


The Double Dipsea has been run 55 times since 1970 and 2026 will be #56.


This is a handicapped race, so everyone (except the male under 40 division) gets a head start.  In 2026 our winner was 66 (female) and our top 10 finishers included 3 females and 7 males with ages ranging from 15 to 67.  Waves are adjusted each year, so you never know who might cross the line first.

But it isn't really about the time, it's about the epic journey.  Young and old, fast and slow, all are welcome to start and as long as you can make the generous race cutoffs, you can get it done!

name: Downtown Visalia Kiwanis 0.5K Donut Run/Walk and Shoe Fling at Mooney Grove Park
description:
No matter how you measure a 0.5K (no typo here), it tallies up to one lap plus 180 feet on a standard running track, 5 1/2 football fields, half a kilometer, 546.8 yards, 1,640 feet, or 19,685 inches.

Because a marathon, a 10K or even a 5K may be too great a distance for some, members of the Downtown Visalia Kiwanis will offer a "Point 5K - The Race for The Rest of Us."

The race will begin at 10am on March 20, 2027, Saturday, at Mooney Grove Park (next to Tulare County Museum) in Visalia. Registration will begin at 9am.

An aid station (sponsored by Denny's restaurant) at the halfway mark is there to fill needs for a donut hole break, coffee, or juice.

When you make it to the finish line, you will get a donut and a 1st place medal. That's right, everyone gets a 1st place medal!

While the event is tongue in cheek, the Kiwanians' aim is sincere. Proceeds from the race will benefit Kiwanis projects that serve the children of our community.

Kids (10 years old and younger) can participate for FREE (No T-Shirt).  If you want a T-Shirt, sign up for Youth.  Strollers are welcome.

 

Come as a Donut!  

We will award a small trophy to the Best Dressed Donut costume.

 

Are you a Shoe-Kicking Master?  Prove it at our Brown's Shoe Fit Shoe Fling Competition right after the Donut Run/Walk.  Swing and kick your shoe as far as you can!  The competition will be divided into Adults (18 and over), Youth (Under 18), and Kids (10 and under).  Fly, shoe, fly!

 

We also have a special treat this year.  The 198 Express Barbershop Quartet will sing for us during registration (9am - 10am).

name: Dream Big 5k
description:
Join us for a day of fun and fitness at the third annual Dream Big 5k, proudly presented by the Kiwanis Club of Victorville. Whether you’re a seasoned runner or just looking for a fun walk with friends and family, this event promises an enjoyable experience for participants of all levels.

The race takes you through the scenic paths of Victor Valley College, located at 18422 Bear Valley Rd, Victorville, CA, starting bright and early at 8:00 am on Saturday, August 22. But the fun doesn't end at the finish line! Stick around for a variety of race day activities, including local vendors, lively music, and more. Every stride you take helps us support students in the Victor Valley, driving the change we wish to see in our community. Grab your running shoes, and let’s make dreams come true together at the Dream Big 5k!

After the main Dream Big 5K, stick around for even more fun—our Dream Big Mini K for children ages 12 and under! Held at Victor Valley College, this in-person event is all about encouraging kids to get active, dream big, and feel proud of their accomplishments. It’s a joyful, high-energy experience where little ones can cross the finish line to the cheers of friends and family.

The first 50 registered participants of the Mini K will receive a special finisher medal—so don’t wait to sign up! Let’s make it a day to remember filled with smiles, movement, and celebration. Come cheer them on and help create a lasting memory at the Dream Big Mini K!

name: Drumstick Dash
description:
Drumstick Dash LA is BACK and bigger than ever! Join us at LA County's LARGEST Thanksgiving day event.

Whether you’re chasing a PR or strolling with the whole family in costume, this is the ultimate way to kick off your holiday.

Expect high energy, epic vibes, tons of freebies, a costume contest that brings the heat, awards, and the unbeatable feeling of running for a powerful cause. Every runner scores a race T-shirt and the BIGGEST… boldest… most brag-worthy finisher medal yet!

Our course takes runners, joggers, and walkers straight through the vibrant NoHo Arts District, where cheering crowds line the streets and DJs keep the beats pumping from start to finish.

And the best part? Every step supports Hope the Mission in providing more than 2 MILLION hot meals to homeless men, women, and children.

Run. Celebrate. Give back. 🦃🔥

name: East Bay Front Runners Pride Run and Walk
description:
Hosted by East Bay Front Runners and Walkers 

Come join us at the East Bay's premier LGBTQ+ Pride Race, EBFRW's 22nd Annual Pride Run and Walk! We are offering both in-person and virtual options. NEW THIS YEAR: For simplicity, the 5K run and 5K walk have been combined into a single event. Participants may choose to run, walk, or a combination.

IN-PERSON PRIDE RUN AND WALK – At beautiful Lake Merritt in downtown Oakland

The race starts and finishes at the Adams Point picnic area adjacent to the Lake Merritt Sailboat House in Lakeside Park (on mapping apps: 568 Bellevue Ave., Oakland, CA) on Saturday, October 10, 2026 at 9am. Events include both 5K and 10K distances. Registration for each event is $43.75 (including $3.75 in fees). No refunds or exchanges. Proceeds benefit Running for a Better Oakland, Fishnets and Film, the Pacific Center for Human Growth, and East Bay Front Runners & Walkers. All participants receive discounted shopping at Sports Basement and Road ID, finisher ribbon, and a pair of famed rainbow-tipped Pride socks. Top finishers receive medals. Finisher times will be available on our website and social media. The race celebrates National Coming Out Day.

VIRTUAL PRIDE RUN OR WALK

You have from Saturday, October 10, 2026 through Sunday, October 18, 2026 to complete your distance. Events include both 5K and 10K distances. You can complete your race anywhere you like. Please do so safely. Registration fee is $38.75 (including $3.75 in fees). No refunds or exchanges. Please send us your result no later than Wednesday, October 21, 2026. Proceeds benefit Running for a Better Oakland, Fishnets and Film, the Pacific Center for Human Growth, and East Bay Front Runners & Walkers. All participants receive a PDF bib, discounted shopping at Sports Basement and Road ID, finisher certificate, and finisher ribbon. Print out your PDF bib and send us a photo of yourself wearing it. Finisher times will be available on our website and social media. The race celebrates National Coming Out Day.

name: Eden Rift Haunted Wine Run 5k
description:
Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Saturday, October 24, 2026 for an exciting event that features The Eden Rift Vineyards. Due to the popularity of this event, we are offering two start times at 9am and 11am. 

Located just 20 miles from the Monterey Bay, Eden Rift is the oldest continually producing vineyard in California. The Eden Rift Estate is one of those places that needs to been seen to be believed. So, whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wonderful wine and camaraderie this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience!  This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing.  Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt or Upgrade to a hoodie for only $10
  • Wine Glass: Shatterproof, Collapsible, and Portable!
  • Finisher Medal: Doubles as a Wine Stopper!
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!

Be sure to stick around after the event and enjoy the winery!   Race participants receive discounted wine glass specials ($12 for White Wines, and $15 for Red Wines) on race day!

name: Elevate 5k & 12 Hour Race at First Baptist Church
description:
Please visit www.ElevateRace.com for the most up to date and detailed information.
Thank you for your interest in participating in our 10th annual Elevate race!

  • What: 5k & 12 hour race
  • Purpose: To support our Elevate missions project
  • When: 5k starts Sat, Feb 13, 2027 @ 9:30am / 12 hour race starts Fri, Feb 12, 2027 @ 8:45pm
  • Where: First Baptist Church campus in Santa Maria, CA
  • Cost:
    • 5k = $22
    • 12 Hour = $45

All the proceeds from this event will go to support the Elevate missions project. Your participation as either a runner or volunteer will help make it possible!

5k: For only $22 you can challenge yourself to complete the 5k (3.1 miles) race. Awards will be given to the winners in both distances for the different age groups at the 10:30am awards ceremony. While this is a competition, everyone is invited to participate regardless of age or physical ability. It will be a lively and encouraging environment which will be fun for both first timers and experienced runners. Runners must arrive by 8:45 on race morning to receive their race bib and all final instructions before the race begins at 9:30am.  The 5k awards ceremony will take place at 10:30am.

12 Hour race: I know we have some adventurous people out there! How far do you think you could run and walk in 12 hours? The race runs from Friday night at 8:45pm until Saturday morning at 8:45am. It will finish 45 minutes before the start of the 5k. This is a great time to test yourself physically and mentally. Would you like to complete your first marathon? In 12 hours you could even walk a marathon if you could finish each mile in just under 28 minutes.

Here's some good news. We'll have some food and drinks to fuel you through the night, and you can take breaks as often as you'd like. Each lap is 1 mile, and near the start/finish line we'll have an area set up specifically for the 12 hour participants. You're encouraged to bring a comfortable chair, footrest, change of clothes, blankets and anything else that can help make your experience more comfortable. Napping is permitted but not encouraged. Friends and family members are invited to spend the evening there with us supporting and encouraging the participants. There is no minimum number of miles you have to complete. Yes, the person that completes the most loops is the winner, but runners and walkers of all levels are encouraged to set an individual goal and see what they're capable of doing. Races like this are typically very relaxed. Very few people would run the entire time in a race of this distance. Going through the night also provides a unique experience. There will be a variety of awards for the 12 hour race & the 12 hour race awards ceremony will take place at 8:45am right when the race finishes.

As a bonus (or maybe more like a penalty), all 12 Hour participants can also participate in the 5k for free if desired! 12 Hour runners must arrive by 8:00pm Friday evening to receive their race bib and all final instructions before the race begins at 8:45pm.

Course info: Each loop is 1.036 miles for the 5k. The 5k is three loops. For the 12 Hour race there is a minor adjustment to make each loop 1 mile. The loop is entirely on the First Baptist / VCA campus, and during the 5k there will be volunteers throughout the course in order to provide a safe environment for young runners. 12 Hour runners will need to have either a headlamp or flashlight to use on the back portion of the loop where there are no lights.

For the 5k we will have water, Gatorade and bananas during the race and celebratory ice cream sandwiches at the end for all finishers. The 12 Hour participants will have a variety of hot and cold drinks and solid foods to choose from. We hope you have a great time training for and participating in this race!

Please visit www.ElevateRace.com for the most up to date and detailed information.

name: Ely Mountain Trail Race
description:
Ely Mountain Trail Race – Shaver Lake, CA

14K (8.7mi) + 8K (4.9mi) | Balsam Forebay | Cooler temps. Hot trails.


We’re stoked to bring a brand new adventure to the San Joaquin Running Co lineup — and this one’s a beauty. Join us in the mountains above Shaver Lake for the first-ever Ely Mountain Trail Race, where crisp air, big climbs, and epic views are all on the menu.

 

The 14K course brings the heat with about 1,800 feet of climbing, including a 1,000’ ascent up Ely Mountain. You’ll earn sweeping views of the Sierra, Shaver Lake, and the valley below — then fly down some smooth and fast singletrack and dirt roads back to the finish.

 

The 8K hits a slightly easier route to the top but still climbs about 800 feet, with all the mountain vibes and finish line feels.

 

🏔️ Special Award for King & Queen of the Mountain – fastest segment times to the top of Ely!

🎽 Custom race shirts

🏅 Finisher medals + podium awards

🍕 Post-race food + refreshments

🌲 All the crisp mountain air you’ve been missing

We’re capping this one at 250 runners, so don’t sleep on it — grab your spot and come break in these trails with us.

name: Epilepsy Education Conference
description:
The Epilepsy Foundation of San Diego County’s Annual Epilepsy Education Conference will be held again at the beautiful Academy of Our Lady of Peace campus on Saturday, July 11, 2026. 

Exploring the theme Advances in Epilepsy—Innovations, Progress & Emerging Treatments, this year's educational conference highlights the latest breakthroughs transforming epilepsy care—from cutting-edge surgical approaches and emerging devices to new medications, rescue therapies, genetics, and clinical trials shaping the future. 

Through expert-led panels and powerful stories from individuals with lived experience, attendees will gain a comprehensive view of how science, technology, and patient-centered approaches are converging to improve outcomes and quality of life for those living with epilepsy. Whether you're a healthcare provider, researcher, caregiver, or person with epilepsy, this conference offers valuable insights and meaningful connection.

name: Father's Day Run for Rotary (Cancelled for 2026)
description:
This will be a fun 5K looping course beginning and ending at Newhall Park near the playground. There will also be a FREE kid's (7 and under) 400m fun run after the 5K run! Age group awards (medals) will be given to top three runners in each age group. T-Shirts guaranteed for pre-registered runners up to a 6/6/26 cutoff date, first come first served for race day registration if we have extras. The registration you pay will go to the Clayton Valley/Concord Sunrise Rotary Club, as well as the PFCs for both Mount Diablo Elementary and Diablo View Middle School. Please check out our Clayton Valley/Concord Sunrise Rotary Club at https://claytonvalleyrotary.org/

Packet Pickup:

Packet pickup will be on Saturday 6/20 at Sports Basement in Walnut Creek from 2pm to 5pm. Race registrants will be able to purchase goods at Sports Basement for a discount of 20% during this time! Please try to pick up your packet during this time to make the process more smooth the day of the race. If you can't make it on the 20th, you can get there early on the 21st to pick up. Thank you!

Sponsors:

Jeff Wilson, Broker Associate - Keller Williams Realty - Assisting real estate buyers and sellers since 2005! www.collmerwilson.com

Torsten Jacobsen

About our Rotary Club:

The Rotary Club of Clayton Valley/Concord Sunrise was chartered in May 1987 and locally serves the City of Clayton and the Clayton Valley area of Concord. The club is involved in many projects around the world but also has projects that are important in the local community as well.

The list below will give you an idea of some of the local projects that we are involved in. We also have some regional and several international projects as well. If you are interested in getting involved in a fun loving group that enjoys helping others Rotary might be for you. Our Club President, Secretary and the entire club invite you to come visit us...

Adopt-A-Family Program - Our club supports several needy families with gifts and food items for the Christmas holidays.

Camp Royal (youth leadership) - Camp Royal is located in the Trinity Alps near Hayfork, CA. It is a week long, summer camp, leadership training experience for juniors (to be seniors) high school students. It invites several motivational speakers and community leaders to speak and teach during the week. Speakers are flown in and out of the Hayfork airport by volunteer Rotarian pilots.

Camp Venture (business/entrepreneurship) - Camp Venture is a 4 day, summer camp, entrepreneur experience for juniors (to be seniors) high school students. It is designed to help teach the students how to run their own businesses after graduation. It is held at a Bay Area educational facility.

Clayton Library Foundation - Each week the regular speakers at our club sign and donate a book that is donated to the Clayton Library in lieu of a speaker’s gift. The club provides the books at the direction of the Clayton librarian then completes the process by giving the book to the library.

Junior Optimist Baseball League - We donate money to the league and they provide surplus or out dated equipment and uniforms that we in turn donate to our Twin Club project in San Felipe, Baja, Mexico.

Local Park Programs and Street Improvements - We are working with the City of Clayton to repair and update the Clayton Community Park and the work there should be done soon!                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Markham Park, Concord, is a 4 year old environmental project where we help restore the plants and the grounds in the gardens of Markham Park, Concord’s arboretum by the donation of labor and money.
Via Concord’s “Adopt-A-Block ” program, we do litter pick up on Clayton Road between Ayres and Ygnacio on a quarterly basis.
We have “adopted” the Cabin Trail in Mt Diablo State Park and provide routine maintenance on a regular basis.

Rotary International Polio Eradication Program - Since its beginning in 1987, our club has been donating to The Rotary Foundation for the world-wide eradication of Polio. Each member has pledged to donate as least $100 a year and so far has donated over $145,000. We are nearing our goal!

International Vision Volunteers - Support of a Rotarian run Eye Hospital in Zambia, Africa treating thousands of eye patients annually.

Adopt-A-Village Project - Since 2011, the Rotary Club of Clayton Valley/Concord Sunrise and three Ugandan clubs have adopted a village--the 2,500 residents of the Nsawo Village.  Through a series of Rotary global grants and district grants to establish and sustain health and education programs, as well as the construction of a pediatric clinic.

San Felipe, Baja Mexico - We've partnered with our twin club to establish and support a cancer screening clinic and hospice. Thousands of local men and women have used the screening facility over the years. In addition, we have provided scholarship support for high school students to help further their education

name: Father’s Day Classic – 5K, 10K, 10-Miler, and Half Marathon
description:
Celebrate Father's Day outside at the beach! Join us for our Father's Day Classic, where you can run, jog or walk with or in celebration of your dad, husband, grandpa, or any father figure in your life!

Race Details

Start Location: Alamitos Beach, 780 E Shoreline Dr. Long Beach, CA
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule

Saturday
1-3:00pm – Bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email the week of the event)

Sunday
6:20am – Race Day bib pick-up opens
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10m)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners and 10-milers only, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Course

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More about the Course

The beach path is an open course, so you will encounter others using it. When we start the race, please stay on the right side of the beach path. The right side is for pedestrians and the left side is for cyclists.

On-Course Support: A fully stocked water station is located along the course. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, electrolytes, gels, and fruit snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk, a runner turn sign, and a flag

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Awards: All finishers earn a medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance.
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, the San Fernando Valley, San Diego, and Orange County. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule

Have Another Question? Check our FAQ page, it's probably answered there!

RUN IT - WALK IT - CELEBRATE FREEDOM

 

Join us in San Diego for the 6th Annual FBE Juneteenth 5K Run/Walk.
 
Move with purpose. Celebrate freedom. Join us as we run, walk, or roll together in honor of Juneteenth and the generations who fought for liberation.

Together we move to improve our health, honor our ancestors, and strengthen the future of our community.

The FBE Juneteenth 5K is an annual community race hosted by Fit, Black, and Educated, Inc. (FBE).

Juneteenth commemorates June 19, 1865, when Union General Gordon Granger arrived in Galveston, Texas and announced that enslaved people were free—more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation.

Today, Juneteenth is recognized as a commemoration and celebration of family, liberation, heritage, unity, and resilience.

Through movement, the FBE Juneteenth 5K brings our community together to celebrate this important history while promoting health, wellness, and unity.

Participants of all fitness levels are welcome to run, walk, or roll.

name: Fiesta 5k
description:
Fiesta 5K
Hosted by the High Desert Hispanic Chamber of Commerce

Join us for the inaugural Fiesta 5K on September 19, a community run and walk celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month while bringing together families, friends, and neighbors for a morning of fitness, culture, and fun.

This event is designed for all ages and fitness levels. Whether you're an experienced runner chasing a personal best, a casual jogger, or simply looking to enjoy a walk with family and friends, the Fiesta 5K offers a welcoming and inclusive experience for everyone.

The Fiesta 5K is more than just a race—it's a celebration of community, wellness, and the vibrant culture that helps make the High Desert such a special place to live and work.

Registration is $35 per participant and includes an official race T-shirt and finisher medal.

Come celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month, stay active, and make lasting memories with your community. We look forward to seeing you at the starting line on September 19!

name: Filthy 50+ - MTB Ride with Benefits
description:
The 12th Annual Filthy 50+ will take you through various areas of San Dieguito River Park and Black Mountain Park. Fast and flowy for all skill levels. The 30 mile riders will head out and turn around at the 15 mile mark and the 50+ mile riders will continue on to the Black Mountain Park area where you will encounter a lollipop and new trails to go with it! The course will be fully marked with Pink Flags and Red Arrows. Fully stocked feed stations will be placed throughout the ride to keep you fueled up.

There will be a kid’s ride supported by Team Quick n’ Dirty at 8:45am. Awards will be given out immediately following the kids ride. Registration for the kid’s ride will be online and onsite. 

When riding the course please be aware that the trails will be open to the public so please pay attention to other riders, hikers, and horseback riders. Please pay special attention when riding the switchbacks portion of the course and use courtesy when passing. Thanks!

WHEN:

Saturday, October 31, 2026

  • Start times will be:
    • 8:00am for 50 mile
    • 8:30 for 30 mile
    • 8:45 for Kids Race

WHERE:

  • San Pasqual Staging Area near 18194 Bandy Canyon Rd., Escondido, CA 92025 GOOGLE MAPS LOCATION

REGISTRATION:

  • REGISTER EARLY - IT WILL SELL OUT!
  • Registration closes the day before the race -or- when registration is full. If registration is full, the waitlists will open.
    Check-in will be open from 6:00 to 7:30 on day of event

COURSES:

  • 50 Mile Course RideWithGPS
  • 30 Mile Course STRAVA

FEED STATIONS:

Please stop if you need to refuel. There will be plenty of Hammer Nutrition products available. The mile marker and addresses are below if your support crew want to do hand-ups.

#1– 11 Miles & #4– 42 Miles (12653 Sunset Dr Escondido, CA  92025)
#2– 21 Miles & #3– 32 Miles (San Dieguito River Park San Diego, CA 92127)

FILTHY 50+ REGISTERED RIDERS WILL RECEIVE:

  • Swag bag provided by Hammer Nutrition
  • Commemorative FILTHY 50+ event item
  • QnD Costume Party sponsor by 805 Beer!
  • Awards for the Top 3 Finishers in each class for the 50+ mile ride
  • Awards for the Top 3 Males and Top 3 Female finisher of the 30 mile ride
  • Electronic Timing and Results.
  • Fully stocked Feed Stations at strategic locations. Feed Stations will include: hydration by Hydro, fruit, food, and Hammer Nutrition Products. The station will also include a self-help mechanic area. (Each Feed Station can be accessed in both directions).

ENTERTAINMENT:

  • Live entertainment at the Filthy 50 Oasis
  • Kids area with a Kids ride!
  • Food will be available at an additional cost
  • Vendor Village
  • Prize raffle with a portion of the proceeds going to SDRP Bike Patrol.

The primary goal of the Filthy 50+ Fun Ride with Benefits is to bring the mountain biking community together and to celebrate what we all love to do, RIDE OUR BIKES! Additionally, we want to bring awareness concerning the trails we ride on, as well as give back to the organizations that keep us riding on those trails. As part of the Filthy 50+ we urge you to help us give back by donating to the SDRP Bike Patrol.

name: FINAL FANTESY ORCHESTRA EVENT – RADY SHELL
description:
Friday, July 17, 

We are thrilled to invite you to a magical evening at The Rady Shell at Jacobs Park in San Diego for the Final Fantasy Orchestra concert!

Immerse yourself in the iconic music of Final Fantasy, performed live by a full orchestra, set against the stunning backdrop of the bay. Whether you’re a long-time fan of the series or new to its music, this is a night you won’t want to miss! Secure your spot and be part of this unforgettable journey through the world of Final Fantasy!

name: Finish The Ride and Finish The Run Griffith Park
description:
Full event details can be found at www.streetsareforeveryone.org/finish-the-ride-griffith-park

Finish The Run Griffith Park
Saturday, March 20th, 2027 • 6:30 AM - 12:00 PM
The Autry Museum • 4700 Western Heritage Way, Los Angeles, CA 90027

Finish The Ride Griffith Park
Sunday, March 21st, 2027 • 7:00 AM - 5:00 PM
The Autry Museum • 4700 Western Heritage Way, Los Angeles, CA 90027

Join us for a memorable day of running, riding, walking, and rolling—all for a purpose. Finish The Ride & Finish The Run is more than an event; it’s a movement to make roads safer for cyclists, pedestrians, and drivers everywhere.

 
🌄 What to Expect


Multiple Ride Options (Routes are subject to change)

  • 12-Mile Family Fun Ride
  • 20-Mile Nice and Easy Ride
  • 35-Mile Leg Burn Ride
  • Andrew Jelmert Half Century
  • Bahati Foundation Metric Century
  • LA River Ride Century

Run/Walk Options (Routes are subject to change)

  • 5K Run/Walk
  • 10K Run/Walk
  • 15K Run -- This event is a split-time event. You will run the 10K, cross the finish line, and then begin the 5K at its starting time of 9:15 AM.
  • Half Marathon
  • 1K Kids and Puppy Run

 
🕒 Schedule for Finish The Run (Saturday, March 20th, 2027)


Time                                             Event


6:30 AM                                       Check‑in opens
7:30 AM                                       Half Marathon Starts
8:00 AM                                       10K/15K Start
8:45 AM                                       Expo area opens
9:15 AM                                       5K Start
10:15 AM                                     1K Kids & Puppy Runs begin
12:00 PM                                     Expo closes

 

🕒 Schedule for Finish The Ride (Sunday, March 21st, 2027)

Time                                             Event


6:00 AM                                       Check‑in opens
7:00 AM                                       LA River Ride Century & Bahati Foundation Metric Century Start
8:00 AM                                       Andrew Jelmert Half Century & 35 Mile Leg Burn Start
8:30 AM                                       20 Mile Nice and Easy & 12 Mile Fun Ride Start
8:45 AM - 2 PM                           Expo Hours

VIP Tent closes at 5 pm

 

 

 
✔ Important Details


Packet Pickup: Details on packet pickup location, dates, and times will be published as soon as they are finalized. 

 

Support & Aid: Rides are supported by marshals, sag wagons, and free repair/tune‑up stations. If you need assistance, we’re here to help. 


Water & Refreshments: Stations on route for rides & runs; snacks & food trucks at the expo. 


Age & Participation Rules:
• Children under 14 must be accompanied by parent/guardian. 
• Minimum ages vary by event: e.g. 12‑mile ride ≥ 5 yrs, 25‑mile ≥ 8 yrs, 62‑mile ≥ 15 yrs. Runs also have age minimum. 


 
🎯 Why This Matters
Finish The Ride & Finish The Run was founded by Damian Kevitt after a life‑changing hit‑and‑run. What began as one person’s effort to overcome tragedy has grown into a community movement advocating for safer streets in Southern California and beyond. By participating, you are helping raise awareness and support systemic changes—policies, education, infrastructure—that make roads safer for all through Streets Are For Everyone.

 
📍 Logistics & Registration


Location: The Autry Museum, Griffith Park – 4700 Western Heritage Way, Los Angeles

Transportation: You can access the Autry by biking (we’re right by the LA River bike path) or taking transit (the 96 bus line stops next to the Zoo, across from the Autry). If you plan to drive, there is plenty of parking at the Autry and the surrounding lots. 
Fees & Discounts: Registration options vary by event. Special rates may apply for veterans, first responders, groups, etc. Contact us directly at Events@StreetsAreForEveryone.org for more information.
What’s included: Event t‑shirt or athletic sleeves with registration, finishing medals for all events, awards, expo, etc. 
 
Come ride, run, walk, roll—or cheer—on this meaningful day. Let’s finish the ride, finish the run, and finish strong for safer streets for everyone. #NeverGiveUp

name: Firecracker 5k (Novablast Launch Party)
description:
Start your Fourth of July festivities with Fleet Feet Agoura Hills and ASICS as we celebrate the launch of the all-new Novablast 6!

Join us for a fun and festive 5K community run where you'll have the opportunity to demo the latest version of one of ASICS' most popular shoes before anyone else. Whether you're looking to run, jog, or walk, this event is open to all paces and experience levels.

name: Fleet Feet Fall Classic - Trail October 18th, 2026
description:
LOCATION

South Rim Trail Head/ Backside of Bidwell Golf Course
Chico, CA US 95928

 

DISCRIPTION 

Fleet Feet Chico is pleased to offer two trail races in our beautiful Upper Bidwell Park.  The two races will start on the south side of the park down Annies Trail for a fun adventure on the single-track trails. Toss in a creek crossing and a nice finish through Yahi and the golf course, you’re sure to enjoy your run! 

 

The two races include a half marathon and a 4-mile an hour backyard endurance challenge! 

 

The Half Marathon will start at 8:10am along the rock wall off Centennial/South Rim trail head. This race will be a challenging climb with 1600 ft of gain in the first half. Enjoy a party at the top of 10-mile house at Aid station #1 and enjoy an all downhill second half of the race!

 

4-mile endurance race will start at 8:00am. Runners will run a 4-mile loop. If you complete the loop in under 60 mins you will go back in the shoot for loop #2. At the top of each hour a new round will start. This will continue for 8 hours! Every other lap we will change the direction of the loop!  If there is more than one person going into the final hour the run will become a foot race to the finish! If you complete all 8 loops, you will have run approximately 32 Miles! Do you have what it takes? Do one loop, 3 loops or all 8! It’s sure to be a good time for the runners and the spectators!

 

After the race head up to Bidwell Golf Course Bar and grill for some delicious food and drinks! All runners get a breakfast burrito with your race registration plus and additional 15% off any other food or drink. 

 

By supporting this race, you are supporting two great causes! 

Chico Velo Trailworks. Launched in 2014, Chico Velo’s Trailworks supports and manages the creation and maintenance of sustainable and enjoyable trails in our region. They have established a strong partnership with the City of Chico to maintain the trails in Upper Bidwell Park. Trailworks have done additional work in the Oroville area and beyond. They are actively seeking new partnerships and opportunities within our community to promote sustainable trail design. Trailworks volunteers put in hundreds of hours every year improving trails for all users to enjoy. To see their latest project check out our Colby Mountain Recreation Project.  A portion of your race entry will go to this great local stewardship as they continue their work to help keep our local trails accessible for us all! If you would like more information on this program or would like to sign up for a park cleanup day, click the link below.

Chico Velo Trailworks - CHICO VELO

 

In addition to supporting Chico Velo Trailworks we are also donating a portion of the race proceeds to local fire academy cadets. Many of the current class are volunteer firefighters who have worked and volunteered in our community and are continuing their education to be able to make a lifelong career the Fire industry. With a fire prone environment that we live in throughout Butte County we rely on our local fire personnel, staff and volunteers to keep our community safe! Cadets will be volunteering on the racecourse to help ensure the safety of all our participants.  Cadets can be seen on our racecourse supporting our race as emergency EMTs and safety aids at the creek crossings. If you are interested in becoming a volunteer firefighter visit the links below for more information.

Become a Volunteer | Butte County, CA

 

RACE START TIMES


4-Mile Endurance Run            8:00am

Half Marathon                         8:10am

 

REGISTRATION

Registration for this race is available online.

  • Online registration closes October 16th at 9:00am.
  • In person registration on October 16th and 17th at Fleet Feet Chico from 10am-2pm.
  • Register by Friday September 25th to guarantee yourself race shirt.
  • If you register between September 28th – October 17th your shirt will NOT be guaranteed, they will be first come first serve at packet pickup.
  • All leftover shirts (if any) will be available for pickup or for sale (non-registered runners) AFTER the Half Marathon race on October 18th. The shirts will be available first come first serve starting at 10:00am.  

 

RACE FEE SCHEDULE

  • October 21st – December 31st - (online)        
    • Half Marathon   $80.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run     $80.00
  • January 1st – May  31st (online)         
    • Half Mar._______________$85.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$85.00
  • June 1st- September 30th (online)
    • Half Marathon__________$90.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$90.00
  • October 1st- October 16th (online, closes at 9:00am on 10.16)
    • Half Marathon__________$95.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$95.00

  • In person Registration at Packet Pickup (Oct. 16th and 17th) ONLY
    • Half Marathon__________$100.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$100.00

 

 

PRE-RACE SHAKE OUT RUN

Join us on Saturday October 17th at 7:30am at the Horseshoe Lake Parking Lot (Parking Lot E) in Upper Bidwell Park. We will head out on a beautiful 4 mile run before our race on Sunday! We will have coffee, muffins, and all the miles and smiles! All who attend will be entered in a drawing for a free race entry for 2026!

 

PACKET PICKUP

Packet pickup will be held at Fleet Feet Chico on the following days and times:

  • Friday and Saturday October 16th and 17th, 2026
  • 10:00am-2:00pm 

Race Day Packet Pick up (At Race Location)

  • Sunday October 18th
  • 6:45 - 7:45am

 

Fleet Feet - Chico
241 Main Street
Chico, CA 95928
(530) 345-1000

 

SWEAT CHECK

Sweat check will be available for all runners at this year’s race! If you have a jacket, extra shoes, a key or a phone that you don’t what to run with, you can check your bag at the sweat check tent. Clear poly bags will be provided for all runners who would like to use this service. At the tent we will tag your bag with your bib number and hold on to it while you run. Come back after the run to collect your items.

  • Sweat check will be available from 7:30am to 4:15pm on race day.

 

OFFICAL COURSE CERTIFICATION AND MAPS

Both the Half Marathon and the 4-Mile Endurance run will start on the south side of Upper Bidwell Park.

The 4-mile run will take Annies to J-Ford to cross over the creek to Yahi trail. On Yahi runners will continue up the trail to Day Bear Hole parking lot where there will be an Aid Station and restroom if needed before continuing down the Fire Road back to Lower Yahi to finish through the Golf Course. (Hopefully for your next loop) 

Click here for both course maps:

  • Half - Half Marathon Race Map
  • 4MPH Endurance Race Map

   

DIRECTIONS AND PARKING FOR OPTIONAL RACE LOCATION

To the course:

The race is located along the Centennial/South Rim rock wall, approximately a quarter mile past the gate at Centennial Ave and Chico Canyon Rd. 

 

Directions from HWY 99: 

Take exit at HWY 32 and head east on HWY 32/ Deer Creek HWY towards Bruce Rd. 

At the stoplight at Bruce Rd, you will turn left and continue to Chico Canyon Rd. 

Follow to the end where the road meets the gate. 

This is a drop off ONLY location! 

 

 

PARKING

Parking can be found at the following locations: 

  • 5 Mile Recreation - .5 mile from the start. The preferred parking area, gate will be open at 6am on race day.
  • Hooker Oak Park - .75 mile from the start
  • Observatory Parking Lot (limited) - .75 mile from the start
  • Horseshoe Lake Parking Lot – 1 mile from start
     

BIKE VALET

Bike valet will be available at the race this year! We encourage you to ride your bikes to the race and Chico Velo will have their bike valet services available to make sure your bike is safe while you run! This is a great way to warm up or cool down before and after your race. To encourage you to ride we are doing a raffle for everyone wo checks a bike in!

 

NO PARKING ALLOWED AT BIDWELL GOLF COURSE!
 

 
RACE RULES:

  • Be courteous when overtaking slower runners or walkers in your elected race location. We want you to race hard and fast, but with the safety of yourself and others in mind.
  • Use best trail educate. Calling out “runner back’ or ‘runner up” when on the trails
  • Follow all trail flagging and marking assigned to the race. Do not go off trails or cut the course. (Pink and Orange Flags)
  • Do NOT remove any course markings!
  • Where your race number on the front of your body so it is visible to the timers!
  • You must cross the timing mat for your chip to be read at the finish of the half marathon. If you are planning to race for top finisher, the race is based on gun time start and first to cross the finish line.
  • 4-Mile runners must complete the loop under the 60 min threshold to be able to start the next loop. If you choose not to start the next loop, you must drop by placing your race tag/bracelet in the drop box for your laps to be logged.
  • Please pack out all trash that you may have from your nutrition or hydration. Trash cans will be available at all aid stations. Leave no trace!
  • No crews or pacers will be allowed for either race on course. All crewing must happen at the start/finish area in the designated runner prep area.
  • All drop bags for the 4-mile race must be checked in by 7:45am on race day. They can be checked in and out between each lap as needed.
  • No pets will be allowed on the course during the race.
  • No strollers will be allowed on the course.
  • Run hard, run fast and have fun!
  • You must complete all 8 laps to be considered for top 3 male/female in the endurance race.

Thank you for understanding. 
 

AID STATIONS AND RESTROOMS
There will be 3 for the Half Marathon and 2 for the 4-Mile Challenge.

1.     10 Mile House (Green Gate) – Half Marathon
2.     End of Fire Road (U Ford/North side) – Half Marathon
3.     Bear Hole Parking Lot Mile 2/11.5 – Water, electrolytes, nutrition gels - 4-Mile and Half Marathon

4.      Start/Finish Area – Water, electrolytes, trail snacks, bars and gels, and more. This will also serve as a post-race fuel station for the Half Marathon and 4-Mile Endurance runners! 

 

Unnecessary waste and trash are something we are working to eliminate from our events. As an organization dedicated to maintaining a clean race and doing our part to keep our trails (roads) clean, starting this year, we will be making a push in our sustainability efforts. This means we are eliminating the use of disposable cups at our races. Runners will have the option of carrying their own hydration vessels or using a HydraPak reusable SpeedCup provided at packet pickup.

                                         

Visit HydraPak by clicking the link here

                                         

BATTLE OF THE AID STATIONS!                                                                                                                                    

This year we are having a battle of the aid stations!

This will be a fun competition for the aid stations to pump up of the spirit and have a good time on the course. Your job as a runner is to hit the aid stations and check out the energy, the refreshments and report back. We will have a voting box at the Fleet Feet tent for you to judge the aid stations! Winners of the Battle of the Aid Stations will be announced after each race.

Who has the "Best snacks, Best Energy, Best Overall aid station"

To sign up to be in the Battle of the Aid Stations or any other volunteer position please click the link below:

Link Available Soon!


Limited restrooms on the course will be located at the finish area of the race (South Rim Trail), Aid station one at the top of 10-Mile house road, and Bear Hole

 

POST RACE REFRESHMENTS

 


T-SHIRTS AND AWARDS

  • Guaranteed Tee-shirt cutoff is September 25th, 2026
  • Cotton blend shirts from Upper Park Clothing Co. will be provided to all participants who register for this event before the tee shirt cutoff. (9/25/26) Any participant who registers on or before September 25th will be guaranteed a race tee.
  • Any participant who registers after September 25th will be able to receive a race shirt based on limited size availability (very few extras will be ordered). Any shirts not picked up at packet pick up prior to the race will be available on a first come first serve basis to all paid runners for pick up, and available for sale to any unregistered spectators starting at 10:00am at the Fleet Feet booth.
  • All shirts come in adult male (unisex) sizes, so you may wish to choose a smaller size than normal for female and child runners.
  • No youth sizes will be available.

 

Awards will be presented to the top male and female finishers in the half marathon as well as the top 3 in each age group bracket. 

 Age group brackets will be as followed: 

  • 14 and under / 15-19 / 20-29 / 30-39 / 40-49 / 50-59 / 60-69 / 70 and over

 

The winner of the 4-Mile Endurance Challenge will be either the last person standing or the first to cross the finish line in the final hour foot race to the finish. 2nd and 3rd place will also receive an award for their efforts! (Male and Female)

 

SPECTATING

We would love to see everyone come out to support our local athletes in this new trail race! Because the trail is a single track there are limited locations that you can safely watch your favorite runners without interrupting the flow of the race. Here we have provided a few locations where you can safely watch your runners and help cheer them on to the finish.

 

  • Start/Finish area- in the meadow of the finish/ South Rim area. At this location you will not only see the runners start on the run, but this is also the location    of the finish. For the 4-Mile runners this will also serve as the location where they will hold until the start of the next loop.
  • Green Gate Parking Lot – This location will serve at Aid Station one for the half marathoners and will also be a great spot to cheer on your runners as they      will have just climbed the final hill of their run…. All downhill from here! Parking will be very limited. If you plan to cheer for your runners at this location, carpooling is highly recommended!
  • Bear Hole parking lot- This location is about one and a half miles past the Horseshoe Lake gate on Upper Park Rd. You will need to walk or bike to this location as the road will be closed to cars for the day. The Parking lot serves as aid station 3 for the half marathon as well as aid station 1 for the 4-mile runners. Runners will be coming in and out of this location from both directions, so this will be a fun and high energy place to spectate. 

 

VOLUNTEERING 

If you are interested in volunteering at the race, please check out all the available shifts! We cannot put on this event without great volunteers!

 

Link Available Soon!

 

For more information, please email shawna@feetfeetchico.com

 

            **No Refunds on race entries or merchandise purchased for this event**

name: Fleet Feet Fall Classic - Trail October 18th, 2026
description:
LOCATION

South Rim Trail Head/ Backside of Bidwell Golf Course
Chico, CA US 95928

 

DISCRIPTION 

Fleet Feet Chico is pleased to offer two trail races in our beautiful Upper Bidwell Park.  The two races will start on the south side of the park down Annies Trail for a fun adventure on the single-track trails. Toss in a creek crossing and a nice finish through Yahi and the golf course, you’re sure to enjoy your run! 

 

The two races include a half marathon and a 4-mile an hour backyard endurance challenge! 

 

The Half Marathon will start at 8:10am along the rock wall off Centennial/South Rim trail head. This race will be a challenging climb with 1600 ft of gain in the first half. Enjoy a party at the top of 10-mile house at Aid station #1 and enjoy an all downhill second half of the race!

 

4-mile endurance race will start at 8:00am. Runners will run a 4-mile loop. If you complete the loop in under 60 mins you will go back in the shoot for loop #2. At the top of each hour a new round will start. This will continue for 8 hours! Every other lap we will change the direction of the loop!  If there is more than one person going into the final hour the run will become a foot race to the finish! If you complete all 8 loops, you will have run approximately 32 Miles! Do you have what it takes? Do one loop, 3 loops or all 8! It’s sure to be a good time for the runners and the spectators!

 

After the race head up to Bidwell Golf Course Bar and grill for some delicious food and drinks! All runners get a breakfast burrito with your race registration plus and additional 15% off any other food or drink. 

 

By supporting this race, you are supporting two great causes! 

Chico Velo Trailworks. Launched in 2014, Chico Velo’s Trailworks supports and manages the creation and maintenance of sustainable and enjoyable trails in our region. They have established a strong partnership with the City of Chico to maintain the trails in Upper Bidwell Park. Trailworks have done additional work in the Oroville area and beyond. They are actively seeking new partnerships and opportunities within our community to promote sustainable trail design. Trailworks volunteers put in hundreds of hours every year improving trails for all users to enjoy. To see their latest project check out our Colby Mountain Recreation Project.  A portion of your race entry will go to this great local stewardship as they continue their work to help keep our local trails accessible for us all! If you would like more information on this program or would like to sign up for a park cleanup day, click the link below.

Chico Velo Trailworks - CHICO VELO

 

In addition to supporting Chico Velo Trailworks we are also donating a portion of the race proceeds to local fire academy cadets. Many of the current class are volunteer firefighters who have worked and volunteered in our community and are continuing their education to be able to make a lifelong career the Fire industry. With a fire prone environment that we live in throughout Butte County we rely on our local fire personnel, staff and volunteers to keep our community safe! Cadets will be volunteering on the racecourse to help ensure the safety of all our participants.  Cadets can be seen on our racecourse supporting our race as emergency EMTs and safety aids at the creek crossings. If you are interested in becoming a volunteer firefighter visit the links below for more information.

Become a Volunteer | Butte County, CA

 

RACE START TIMES


4-Mile Endurance Run            8:00am

Half Marathon                         8:10am

 

REGISTRATION

Registration for this race is available online.

  • Online registration closes October 16th at 9:00am.
  • In person registration on October 16th and 17th at Fleet Feet Chico from 10am-2pm.
  • Register by Friday September 25th to guarantee yourself race shirt.
  • If you register between September 28th – October 17th your shirt will NOT be guaranteed, they will be first come first serve at packet pickup.
  • All leftover shirts (if any) will be available for pickup or for sale (non-registered runners) AFTER the Half Marathon race on October 18th. The shirts will be available first come first serve starting at 10:00am.  

 

RACE FEE SCHEDULE

  • October 21st – December 31st - (online)        
    • Half Marathon   $80.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run     $80.00
  • January 1st – May  31st (online)         
    • Half Mar._______________$85.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$85.00
  • June 1st- September 30th (online)

    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$90.00
  • October 1st- October 16th (online, closes at 9:00am on 10.16)
    • Half Marathon__________$95.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$95.00

  • In person Registration at Packet Pickup (Oct. 16th and 17th) ONLY
    • Half Marathon__________$100.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$100.00

 

 

PRE-RACE SHAKE OUT RUN

Join us on Saturday October 17th at 7:30am at the Horseshoe Lake Parking Lot (Parking Lot E) in Upper Bidwell Park. We will head out on a beautiful 4 mile run before our race on Sunday! We will have coffee, muffins, and all the miles and smiles! All who attend will be entered in a drawing for a free race entry for 2026!

 

PACKET PICKUP

Packet pickup will be held at Fleet Feet Chico on the following days and times:

  • Friday and Saturday October 16th and 17th, 2026
  • 10:00am-2:00pm 

Race Day Packet Pick up (At Race Location)

Fleet Feet - Chico
241 Main Street
Chico, CA 95928

SWEAT CHECK

Sweat check will be available for all runners at this year’s race! If you have a jacket, extra shoes, a key or a phone that you don’t what to run with, you can check your bag at the sweat check tent. Clear poly bags will be provided for all runners who would like to use this service. At the tent we will tag your bag with your bib number and hold on to it while you run. Come back after the run to collect your items.

  • Sweat check will be available from 7:30am to 4:15pm on race day.

 

OFFICAL COURSE CERTIFICATION AND MAPS

Both the Half Marathon and the 4-Mile Endurance run will start on the south side of Upper Bidwell Park.

The 4-mile run will take Annies to J-Ford to cross over the creek to Yahi trail. On Yahi runners will continue up the trail to Day Bear Hole parking lot where there will be an Aid Station and restroom if needed before continuing down the Fire Road back to Lower Yahi to finish through the Golf Course. (Hopefully for your next loop)

DIRECTIONS AND PARKING FOR OPTIONAL RACE LOCATION

To the course:

The race is located along the Centennial/South Rim rock wall, approximately a quarter mile past the gate at Centennial Ave and Chico Canyon Rd. 

 

Directions from HWY 99: 

Take exit at HWY 32 and head east on HWY 32/ Deer Creek HWY towards Bruce Rd. 

At the stoplight at Bruce Rd, you will turn left and continue to Chico Canyon Rd. 

Follow to the end where the road meets the gate. 

This is a drop off ONLY location! 

 

 

PARKING

Parking can be found at the following locations: 

  • 5 Mile Recreation - .5 mile from the start. The preferred parking area, gate will be open at 6am on race day.
  • Hooker Oak Park - .75 mile from the start
  • Observatory Parking Lot (limited) - .75 mile from the start
  • Horseshoe Lake Parking Lot – 1 mile from start
     

BIKE VALET

Bike valet will be available at the race this year! We encourage you to ride your bikes to the race and Chico Velo will have their bike valet services available to make sure your bike is safe while you run! This is a great way to warm up or cool down before and after your race. To encourage you to ride we are doing a raffle for everyone wo checks a bike in!

 

NO PARKING ALLOWED AT BIDWELL GOLF COURSE!
 

 
RACE RULES:

  • Be courteous when overtaking slower runners or walkers in your elected race location. We want you to race hard and fast, but with the safety of yourself and others in mind.
  • Use best trail educate. Calling out “runner back’ or ‘runner up” when on the trails
  • Follow all trail flagging and marking assigned to the race. Do not go off trails or cut the course. (Pink and Orange Flags)
  • Do NOT remove any course markings!
  • Where your race number on the front of your body so it is visible to the timers!
  • You must cross the timing mat for your chip to be read at the finish of the half marathon. If you are planning to race for top finisher, the race is based on gun time start and first to cross the finish line.
  • 4-Mile runners must complete the loop under the 60 min threshold to be able to start the next loop. If you choose not to start the next loop, you must drop by placing your race tag/bracelet in the drop box for your laps to be logged.
  • Please pack out all trash that you may have from your nutrition or hydration. Trash cans will be available at all aid stations. Leave no trace!

  • Run hard, run fast and have fun!

Thank you for understanding.

This means we are eliminating the use of disposable cups at our races. Runners will have the option of carrying their own hydration vessels or using a HydraPak reusable SpeedCup provided at packet pickup.

                                         

Visit HydraPak by clicking the link here
