name: LA's Race Against Gun Violence
description:
The Race Against Gun Violence (RAGV) celebrates the life-changing work of community organizations and provides a dynamic platform for people who care about ending gun violence to not only raise direct unrestricted funds, but also connect and grow their network. Qualifying 501(c)(3) Charity Partners get 10 free entries to kickoff fundraising through the RAGV platform. 

The RAGV has raised over $1million in unrestricted funds since its founding in 2014, and over 1500 run/walk participants joined the 2025 Chicago event, alone. Strides for Peace has partnered with 300+ organizations in its lifetime. Join LA's inaugural Race Against Gun Violence and become part of the growing national network!

To participate as a Charity Partner, please submit your 501(c)(3) details using the form linked here and email rubye@stridesforpeace.org before completing any participant registrations. Thank you!

name: Lafayette Res Run for Education
description:
About the Lafayette Res Run for Education

The Lafayette Chamber and the City of Lafayette are co-sponsors of the Lafayette Res Run for Education which is traditionally held the third Sunday in October. 

 

The 2026 Lafayette Res Run for Education will be held Sunday, October 18. 5k: 8am, 10k: 8:15am, 2 mile: 8:45am in downtown Lafayette, CA.

 

Back by popular demand, from its introduction in 2020, you can register for the Reservoir Challenge – the virtual race which “runs” around the 2.7-mile paved trail of the Lafayette Reservoir October 10-17. Please note, the Reservoir Challenge is not an option on Sunday, October 18 as the Reservoir will be closed for the 10K runners. The Reservoir Challenge is great opportunity to safely walk or run the Reservoir on your own, perhaps beating your time from last year. 

 

Beneficiaries of the event are the local schools and the services and programs of the Chamber. See below for what we gave back to our schools last year! 

 

The Run is the city’s most popular “family affair”, involving kids, parents, grandparents, and hundreds of serious runners from throughout the Bay Area. Join us in 2025 for the 10k, 5k, the 2 mile run/walk for fun or the Reservoir Challenge! Sprinters, walkers, the “stroller brigade” and many of Lafayette’s top four legged residents are welcome to join in the fun. 

 

The first 100 students to register from each school will receive a voucher for a free 1/4 pound of bulk candy from Zoonie's during packet pickup! 

 

Packet Pickup
Race packets that include our traditional long sleeve t-shirt (while supplies last) and race bib will be available for pickup at the Lafayette Chamber Office, 251 Lafayette Circle, Lafayette, CA [map it] on the following dates/times (subject to change):

Tuesday, October 13, 9am-5pm
Wednesday, October 14,10am-6pm
Thursday, October 15, 9am-5pm
Friday, October 16, 9am-1pm

name: Lake Hodges Trail Duathlon
description:
THE LAKE HODGES TRAIL DUATHLON RUN | BIKE | RUN

TRAIL DUATHLON Run | Bike | Run is our one of a kind experience during our annual Lake Hodges Trail Fest. Challenge yourself and compete as and INDIVIDUAL or bring friends along for the challenge and compete as a TEAM.

We are a CUPLESS race series. Please make sure to bring some form of hydration vessel for your event. There will be no cups at aid stations.

name: Lake Hodges Trail Festival
description:
THE LAKE HODGES TRAIL RUNS & TRAIL DUATHLON- RUN | BIKE | RUN

is an annual trail running experience you don't want to miss. We offer something for the whole family to enjoy. Choose from the Lake Hodges 50K, 15K, 10k, 5k, and bring the kids for the the 1 Mile Kid's Fun Run!

 50K is a great introduction into ultra marathons, ideal for all running levels.

NEW! 25K is a great day on the trails, ideal for all running levels.

 15K is a beautiful courses for exploring new trails and accomplishing race goals.

 10K course challenges the runner with a 1,000ft gain but with a beautiful reward of the view from the summit of Bernardo Mountain Peak.

 5K is an old favorite with a new twist, exploring the lakes shore. Great for a quick run or walk.

 Stroller Trail 5K a new way to run on the trails with your little one.

The Kid’s 1 Mile Fun Run is open to children 10 and younger. This is a non-timed run. All kids receive a finisher’s medal and other treats.

 Trail Duathlon- Run | Bike | Run is our one of a kind experience to a weekend of racing. Challenge yourself and compete as and INDIVIDUAL or bring friends along for the challenge and compete as a TEAM.

We are a CUPLESS race series. Please make sure to bring some form of hydration vessel to carry hydration for your event. There will not be cups provided at aid stations.

description:
Choose you own path and walk, hike, or run a full 26.2 cumulative miles on recommended Livermore trails and park paths between September 7th - October 5th, and earn bragging rights plus a commemorative t-shirt. The Challenge is open to all ages.

name: LASAA Mug Run - Altadena Forever Run
description:
LASAA’s mission is to organize athletic events for our members, which include Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department employees and law enforcement officers. We aim to promote health, fitness, and camaraderie among our members.

The Mug Run series began in 1993. At that time, it was a small event with an average of just 10 runners per race, primarily attended by law enforcement personnel. Over the years, participation has grown significantly, expanding to welcome members of the public. Today, more than 300 runners join us, and the Mug Run continues to foster friendly competition and positive engagement between law enforcement and the community.

Each year, LASAA partners with Sheriff’s stations across the county to host a series of Mug Runs. Each station brings its own spirit, culture, and traditions to the event. This year, Altadena Station is dedicating their Mug Run to commemorating the two-year anniversary of the Altadena Eaton Fire.

One year after the fire blackened the ridges above our town, the inaugural Altadena Forever Run stands as a symbol of resilience and recovery. It honors those who were affected, those who responded, and those who continue working to rebuild and strengthen our community.

The Altadena Forever Run welcomes everyone. Your participation, sponsorship, and presence demonstrate solidarity, remembrance, and hope. Proceeds from this event will be directed to the Altadena Station Unit Fund to support community-benefit initiatives connected to the Eaton Fire Survivors organization, as well as programs supported by the Altadena Sheriff’s Support Group. LASAA’s part in the Mug Run series is to create meaningful, community-focused fitness events and transfer the proceeds to the station hosting the run. Altadena Station manages how this support is directed locally.

Packet Pickup Location: Grocery Outlet Parking Lot Altadena

2270 Lake Ave, Altadena, CA 91001

Days: TBD

Hours: TBD

Race start time is 8AM, January 10th.

name: LASD PINK PATCH 5K RUN/WALK
description:
Pink Patch 5K Run/Walk

Join us for the annual Pink Patch 5K Run/Walk, a powerful community event dedicated to breast cancer awareness and support. On September 12, 2026, participants will gather at Frank G. Bonelli Regional Park to make a meaningful difference in the fight against breast cancer.

Whether you're a runner, walker, or virtual participant, this event brings together individuals, teams, and law enforcement agencies united by a common goal. Every step you take helps raise awareness, support survivors, and honor those affected by breast cancer.

Event Highlights:

  • In-person and virtual participation options
  • Team categories including Law Enforcement, Survivor Teams, and Friends & Family
  • Breast Cancer Awareness Month commemoration
  • Community solidarity and hope

Register today and be part of this inspiring movement. Together, we can make a difference, one step at a time.

name: LBC Summer Breeze – 5K, 10K, 10M, and Half Marathon
description:
Let's celebrate summer in the city together!

Race Details

Start Location: Granada Beach, 5100 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach

Parking: Parking in the local lots is usually $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free but limited.

Event Schedule

Saturday
1-3:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email race week)

Sunday
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10m)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners and 10-milers only, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Course

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More about the Course

The beach path is an open course, so you will encounter others using it. When we start the race, please stay on the right side of the beach path. The right side is for pedestrians and the left side is for cyclists.

On-Course Support: A fully stocked water station is along the course. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, electrolytes, gels, and fruit snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk, a runner turn sign, and a flag

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Medals: All finishers earn a race medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, the San Fernando Valley, San Diego, and Orange County. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule

Have Another Question? Check our FAQ page, it's probably answered there!

name: LEARN: HOW TO OUTRIGGER CANOE
description:
Saturday, August 22, 10AM, FREE

Ready to try something unique on the water? Learn how to Paddle an outrigger canoe with Veteran Sailors! Learn the basics and experience a different style of teamwork in point loma. Instructions will cover water safety, team coordination and getting comfortable in the open water. This is a high energy sport so come prepared!

name: Legends of the Redwoods 5k
description: 5k race on the well-maintained gravel roads of Beckstoffer Vineyards near Ukiah, California. This event is in celebration of the 480 mile Native American Ultramarathon Races on the Redwood Highway from San Francisco to Grants Pass, Oregon, in 1927 and 1928.

name: Lemon Run presented by the Goleta Education Foundation
description:
Our Annual Lemon Run is back at Goleta Beach Park! Join us on September 20 at beautiful Goleta Beach for a day of fun, fitness, and community spirit. Let's run together to support education in our community! 🏃‍♂️🍋

With competitive 5K (Jr. Grand Prix) and 10K (Grand Prix) races, and 1K Family Fun Run, we’ve got something for everyone. It's a perfect event for competitive runners and first-timers alike. 

We'll have great prizes and goodies from local businesses, fabulous food, and fun family-friendly activities! Come join the Goleta Education Foundation and support our schools, families, and community in the Good Land.

Early bib pick-up will be on Saturday, 9/19 from 11 am-2 pm at Deckers Brand Showcase located at 6601 Hollister Ave. Late registration and packet pick-up will be at Goleta Beach Park Area D on Sunday 9/19, beginning at 7 am. Registration closes promptly 15 minutes before each race. 

Route Maps: 

  • 10K map (begins at 8:00AM)

    • 10K Winner Prizes announced at 9AM

  • 5K map (begins at 9:30AM)

    • 5K Winner Prizes announced at 10AM

  • 1K map (begins at 10:30AM)

Participants will begin as a rolling start for each event. Strollers are allowed and families are welcome to run together. See registration information for differences in pricing for Adults and Kids.

Parking & Transportation: Parking will be at Goleta Beach, and additional parking is available at UCSB Parking Lot 10. Parking at Goleta Beach is limited, so please plan accordingly. The beach lot closes at 9:00 am. Green transportation options are strongly encouraged.

  1. Ride your bike - Bike Valet available with Move SB.

  2. Carpool with family and friends from your neighborhood - additional carpool parking is available at Deckers Brand Showcase located at 6601 Hollister Avenue.

  3. Drop-off area is accessible in front of the Ellwood Restaurant parking lot.

Don’t forget your Lemon Run swag! Pre-order your Race T-shirts by 8/31 to ensure you get your size. We have Adult and Youth sizes S/M/L/XL. 

Lemon Run 2026 is presented by Goleta Education Foundation.

name: Liberty Bell 5k Fun Run
description:
Welcome to the 3rd annual Liberty High School Band 5k.  The Liberty High School Band is excited to host this event as it will directly benefit the marching band, jazz band, concert programs, winter percussion and winter guard programs.

IN PERSON 
The race will begin at Veterans Park and participants will run on the Marsh Creek Trail through Creekside Park and beyond for an out and back.  The 5k race will commence at 7:30am and the Kids Fun Run will begin at 8am.  Medals will be handed out at the finish line.  All participants will receive a 2026 t-shirt and medal for participating!

Packet pick up is scheduled for Thursday, July 3rd from 3:00-7:00pm at Fleet Feet, located at 6061 Lone Tree Way in Brentwood. 

The event will take place rain or shine. Once registered, there are no refunds for inclement weather, personal emergencies, injuries, illnesses, change of plans, etc. Those participating with strollers or pets will be asked to enter the start area at the back.

This race is open to any and all who want to participate, as long as they are human.  For the safety of all participants, NO ANIMALS are allowed on the course.  Strollers are welcome when pushed by an adult.  Bring the family, young and old and run or walk with us! We can't wait to see you out there.

Race Fees:
Children ages 3 and under are welcome to participate, no registration necessary.

Family 4-Pack Registration SPECIAL

Open to ages 2-99

$129

IMPORTANT: ALL FOUR INDIVIDUALS MUST BE REGISTERED AT THE TIME OF CHECKOUT. YOU CANNOT GO BACK AND ADD OR CHANGE PARTICIPANTS LATER. Limited number of entries available for the 4-pack special. Event will take place rain or shine. Once registered, there are no refunds for inclement weather, personal emergencies, injuries, illnesses, change of plans, etc. Those participating with strollers or pets will be asked to enter the start area at the back.

Charity 5k Run/Walk Entry

This "admit one" entry includes a $50 donation to Liberty High School Band. It also includes a special long-sleeve tech t-shirt with Band and race branding. 

5k - $45

Kids One Mile - $20


If you register on or after June 1st, you WILL NOT be asked for a t-shirt size.  You will be able to select a t-shirt from a variety of sizes at packet pick-up or on race day.  
Course Information: For the safety of our runners DOGS ARE NOT ALLOWED ON THE COURSE. Strollers are allowed on the course if they are pushed by an adult.

name: Liberty Station Adventure Race Training Event
description:
Registration closes 8/20/26 at noon!

Trekking/Biking/Kayaking

The next San Diego Adventure Racing Club (SDARC) training event will be based out of a new race location, Liberty Station, and offer UP TO 15 hours of fun.  As always, if you are scared, you can shorten it to your abilities.  This event's course designer and event director, Michael Dubois, has a fun course brewing with lots of paddling, biking and trekking.  Starting in boats, you'll get paddling, then biking and hiking (mountain bikes or gravel bikes OK).  As always, navigation will be with the maps provided at the start line, and no GPS allowed.  Compasses mandatory.

Start/Finish will be at 2335 Cushing Road.  This is a parking lot at Liberty Station.  This allows for you to purchase food from the Liberty Station vendors, if you so choose, during transitions and at the finish line.

Please register EACH person coming so that we have enough maps!

Donations always welcome as we will have the maps and truck as expenses but please do not feel obligated to give more than you think fair.

Can’t wait to see you out there.

TIMELINE

Club staff will be there at 4am with a box truck for your bike and one bin/paddle bag if necessary.

Kayak staging will start at 4am at Kellogg’s Beach (directions here url (https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=/maps/place/Kellogg%2BBeach,%2BPoint%2BLoma%2BWay,%2BSan%2BDiego,%2BCA%2B92106/data%3D!4m2!3m1!1s0x80deab917554d87d:0xa4247e8b6f5ce37b%3Fsa%3DX%26ved%3D1t:242%26ictx%3D111&ved=2ahUKEwiApvfd1ueUAxU5JkQIHaMDOusQ8gF6BAghEAI&usg=AOvVaw0F3xvuFD8toGW8kNiJhZS_)).  There will be a volunteer at the staging site to stay with your boats.

Race start will be on foot at 5am from the parking lot at Liberty Station.

GEAR

Kayak (~15 miles and under) - you will need your own boat.  San Diego has many rental options but due to the timing of the race you will need to rent a boat from Friday night to Sunday morning (sorry!).  Boats should be capable of being paddled in the busy San Diego Bay.
    -personal floatation device (PFD)
    -paddle
    -2 glow sticks per boat (Front & back)

Bike (25-30 miles and under) - the bike will consist of urban roads/bike trails/some fire-roads/some single-track.  Gravel bike would likely be fastest but mountain bike would be a safe bet.
    -helmet
    -repair kit
    -front white and rear red light just to be safe

Trek (15-20 miles and under)
    -pack to hold 2-3 liters of water and food for all the bike & trek
    -compass
    -clothing to protect from sun
    -first aid kit

COURSE SCHEMATIC

Stage 1 - Trek ~ 2.5 miles

Stage 2 - Kayak ~ 11 miles for all controls but will be set up to have shorter course.  

Stage 3 - Bike ~ 3-5 miles.  You will need to pack all of your food for the race at this transition.

Stage 4 - Trek ~ 6 miles or less.  There will be water and restrooms at the TA

Stage 5 - Bike ~ 10 miles.  Lots of road and bike path.  Be safe.  Water and restrooms at the TA

Stage 6 - Trek ~ 12 miles or less.  There will be water only at this TA

Stage 7 - Bike ~ 10 miles.  Lots of road and bike path.  Water only at this TA.

Stage 8 - Kayak ~ (you will leave your bikes at the box truck) 4 miles to get a couple controls, or not, and to the finish at Liberty Station

SPONSORS

Women of AR seeks to grow the sport by encouraging all types of people to join! Join the Facebook group to find teammates and learn about the Women of AR team, etc.

Pasokin is a delicious all-natural peanut butter snack made without preservatives or chemical additives, and is protein-rich - a great addition to any adventure racers repertoire!

name: Lights for Life 5K
description:
The team at Project 99 invites you to join us for the Lights for Life 5K, our signature mental health and suicide awareness campaign. This year’s event continues our mission to shine a light on suicide prevention and bring the conversation "out of the dark." Your participation helps us spread hope, raise awareness, and ensure that no one feels alone in their struggles.
By running, walking, or supporting this 5K, you are directly contributing to our efforts to educate local students and the broader community about mental health and suicide prevention. Project 99 Play for Life, Inc., is so grateful for the generous support that allows us to make an impact today and grow our mission for the future. All additional donations are tax-deductible and will help us expand our educational outreach, keeping students engaged and encouraging them to "stay in the game" and play for life.
In addition to participating in the race, we encourage youth to get involved behind the scenes, with opportunities to volunteer in event planning, preparation, and execution. Together, we can continue to build a community where mental health is prioritized, and no one is left in the dark.
Let's bring hope, awareness, and prevention into the light.

name: Logout and Lace up
description:
Logout & Lace Up is more than a 5k

its a community centered event designed to bring attention to three critical public health challenges: opioid misuse, mental health, and violence prevention. By combining education, physical activity, and community engagement, this event creates a space where participants can learn, reflect, and take meaningful action. Events like this help break stigma, encourage open conversations, and connect individuals with resources that can support healthier lives.

Opioid awareness is a key focus of this 5k, highlighting the impact of opioid misuse on individuals, families, and communities. Educational materials and outreach efforts aim to inform participants about the risks of opioid dependency, the importance of safe medication practices, and the availability of treatment and recovery services. By raising awareness, the event helps reduce misconceptions and promotes compassion for those affected by substance use disorders.

Mental health is another central theme, emphasizing that emotional well-being is just as important as physical health. The race promotes understanding of common mental health challenges such as anxiety, depression, and trauma, while encouraging people to seek support when needed. Community events like this can foster a sense of connection and belonging, which are essential protective factors for mental wellness.

Violence prevention is also highlighted, focusing on strategies to build safer, more supportive environments. This includes promoting conflict resolution, strengthening community relationships, and increasing awareness of resources for those impacted by violence. By addressing root causes and encouraging proactive solutions, the race helps empower individuals and communities to create lasting change.

Overall, this 5k for Awareness serves as a powerful reminder that collective action can drive progress. Through participation and education, individuals can contribute to a culture of care, understanding, and prevention, helping to build healthier, safer communities for everyone.

name: Long Beach Labor Day Run - Merging Forces 5K, 10K, Half Marathon,  1 Miler, Kids Dash
description:
Shoreline Aquatic Park, 200 Aquarium Way, Long Beach, CA 90802
📍 Shoreline Village, Long Beach, CA
📅 Labor Day - Monday, September 7, 2026


Start your Labor Day with purpose, movement, and community at the inaugural Labor of Love – Merging Forces Run.
Set against the stunning backdrop of Long Beach’s waterfront, this race begins near the iconic lighthouse at Shoreline Village and takes you on a scenic route through the village and out onto the beautiful beach path. It’s one of the most vibrant and picturesque courses the city has to offer—perfect for runners, walkers, and everyone in between.
This special event is proudly hosted in partnership with Merge Opportunities, a nonprofit dedicated to creating pathways for underserved youth, system-impacted individuals, and transitioning foster youth. Through job training, mentorship, and essential support services, Merge empowers individuals to rebuild, reconnect, and move forward with purpose.


💛 Run with meaning. Move with purpose. Be part of something bigger.
Come out and celebrate the launch of this brand-new Labor Day tradition—where community, impact, and good energy come together.


✨ What You Can Expect:
✔️ Professional Chip Timing
✔️ Instant Results – powered by ChronoTrack, available within minutes of finishing
✔️ Free Race Day Photos – no upsells, ever
✔️ Multiple On-Course Water Stations
✔️ Flat, Fast, Scenic Beach Path Course
✔️ Vendors, Music & Finish Line Festival Vibes
✔️ All the CaliFlow energy you know and love
 
Whether you’re chasing a PR, walking with friends, or just showing up for something meaningful—this is your moment.
Come for the run. Stay for the vibe. Run for a reason.

name: Long Beach Race for Rare 5K Run & Walk Event
description:
Join the National MPS Society at the 5th Annual Long Beach Race for Rare 5K Run & Walk Event hosted by Long Beach locals, Lynn and Scott Hopkins!

This event is to raise money and awareness to help change the lives of those living with a rare disease.  10% of Americans suffer from a rare disease and less than 5% have an FDA-approved treatment.  3 out of 10 children with a rare condition do not live to see their 5th birthday, and we work to change this.  Proceeds benefit the National MPS Society.

Race Details

7:30 AM: Onsite registration, packet pick-up, and pre-race entertainment
9:00 AM: 5K Run/Walk
10:00 AM: Awards/Raffle
10:30 AM: Beachside Picnic

Lunch is included in registration costs. Come out and enjoy a fun day to help raise awareness and funds for our MPS and ML families!

Start your Team Fundraiser!

At the top, hover over "Donate"
Select "become a fundraiser"
Create your team page - Choose your photo, team name, bio and fundraising goal!
Share the link for people to donate directly to your fundraiser!
You can do this before or after you register

Not able to join in person? Participate virtually!

It is just like any other 5K, except there is no official race location.  You get to choose where, with whom, and even how you want to complete the 5K.  by participating virtually, you can run the 5K at any time leading up to October 10th.  It can even be done in increments, keep track of your distance until you hit the 5K!

Contact Bethany Greene at bethany@mpssociety.org for sponsorship details.

In-person and virtual runners: Shirts guaranteed if you register by September 10th!

All proceeds go to furthering the mission of the National MPS Society.  FEIN: 11-2734849

name: Lookin' for a Cure Palo Alto
description:
Description

Join Us in the Pursuit of a Cure at the Lookin' For A Cure Palo Alto 5K!


Every year, Lookin' For A Cure 5k events light up cities across the United States. These events are not just about running, they are about igniting awareness, and unity in the fight against Ocular Melanoma. By participating, you're not only support groundbreaking research but also bringing together individuals affected by Ocular Melanoma.We are Lookin' For a Cure" in Palo Alto. Join A Cure in Sight on Saturday July 11th, 7AM-11AM at: 2452 Watson Ct. Palo Alto, CA US 94020. Help raise awareness and support the fight against Ocular Melanoma, the most common eye cancer in adults in the United States.  

A Partnership for Progress


A Cure In Sight collaborates with leading research facilities and dedicated physicians that specialize in Ocular Melanoma treatment. Together, we channel the net proceeds from these events into ongoing research projects and patient support programs. Your involvement directly contributes to advancing the quest for a cure. Walk shoulder-to-shoulder with Ocular Melanoma survivors, their families, and the medical professionals who care for them at the Byers Eye Institute at Stanford University School of Medicine. 

All ages are welcome to attend. Come run, walk, or stay in one place and play games at the Fourth Annual Lookin' for a Cure 5K at Stanford, hosted by A Cure in Sight and the Byers Eye Institute at Stanford.  Set up your team, invite your friends and family, start your fundraiser and you are off to the finish line. Proceeds from this event will support the Stanford Ocular Oncology Program. Stanford is a national leader in providing state-of-the-art care for ocular melanoma patients of all ages and has pioneered groundbreaking research advances. Prithvi Mruthyunjaya, MD, MHS, professor of ophthalmology who anchors the ocular tumor service at Stanford is also working hard at Stanford to bring this event to fruition.

The race also aims to spread the word about the importance of early detection by getting regular dilated eye exams. Ocular melanoma makes up approximately 5 percent of melanomas in the United States. It is estimated that between 6-8 people per million will be diagnosed annually in the Western world. 

Read more about the work Stanford is doing around ocular melanoma here.

Event Details

Packet pick up will be held at Road Runner Sports San Carlos located at: 1125 Industrial Rd, San Carlos, CA 94070. Details will be available soon. 

Race Swag

  • Guaranteed T-shirt, If Registered by June 27th.
  • Finisher Medal
  • Food & Drink
  • Course Aid Station
  • Commemorative Race Bib
  • Free Downloadable Photos
  • Official Finishers Time With Age Group Placements

Race day schedule

  • Registration 7 AM
  • Race start 8 AM
  • Announcements Awards 9:30 am

Free parking is available in the Byers Eye Institute parking lot on the corner of Embarcadero Rd. and Bayshore Rd.

name: Los Angeles Frontrunners Pride Run 2026
description:
ONLINE REGISTRATION HAS CLOSED - RACE IS SOLD OUT.  THERE IS NO RACEDAY REGISTRATION!

Pride Run turns 43!  Pride Run 2026 marks the 43rd running of the Los Angeles Frontrunners Pride Run. Come join us in celebrating 43 years of running, friendship, and community.  Each year LAFR makes a contribution to local charities with the proceeds from the Pride Run.  Pride Run 2026 features our traditional 5K and 10K race, free Kids Race and the Ultra Pride Run, where you race both the 5K and 10K!

There is no registration on race morning, so please register in advance until race sellout.

Race Details

  • Location: Crystal Springs Picnic Area, Griffith Park (same as 2025)
  • Course: Flat trail/packed dirt around the golf course (5K = 1 loop, 10K = 2 loops)

Start Times

  • 10K: 7:30 AM
  • Free Kids Race: 8:45 AM
  • 5K: 9:00 AM

Ultra Pride Run

Ultra Pride runners race BOTH races and do not race continuously.  After the 10K, Ultra Pride runners will race their 5K starting at 9:00 AM with the regular 5K.

Virtual Race

Can’t join us in person? Sign up for the virtual race and we’ll ship your race shirt and medal.

Beneficiaries/Sponsorship

Our 2026 beneficiaries are Friends of Griffith Park and Brave Trails!  If you would like to become a Pride Run sponsor, please click HERE.

Free Kids Race

The Kids Race will start at approximately 8:45 a.m. (after the 10K) and is free. Every child receives a race number and medal. You can register children during the registration process. To register children without adult participation, email your kid(s) name/age to lafrontrunners@gmail.com.

Awards

Awards will be given to the top 3 overall in the 5K, 10K and Ultra Pride. Age group awards for the 5K & 10K are top 3 in the following categories: 10 & Under, 11-14, 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80+.  Age group awards for the Ultra Pride Run are top 3 in the following categories: 19 & under, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60+

More Info/Past Results

For more race info including past results and course records, please click HERE.

About LAFR

Los Angeles Frontrunners (501c3) is a running and walking club for members and friends of the LGBTQ+ community.  In addition to running, walking, more running (and lots of eating), LAFR raises funds and collects goods to donate to local charities. Past beneficiaries include; The Rescue Train, Westside Food Bank, SRLA, PAWS/LA, Life Worth Saving, Friends of Griffith Park, InsideOut Community Arts, Friends of Project 10, Angel City Pit Bulls, The Breakfast Club at St. Thomas the Apostle, and the Don Thompson Scholarship at the USC Film School.

For more race info including past results and course records, please click HERE.

name: Los Angeles Sunset Relays | 5K & Kid Run
description:
For more Information go to: https://lasunsetrelay.com/

 

Get ready for an unforgettable evening of trail running at the Los Angeles Sunset Trail Relays & 5K! This race brings together adventure, teamwork, and breathtaking views in one epic event. As the sun sets over the city, you'll traverse scenic trails, soak in stunning skyline views, and take on a thrilling course through the heart of Griffith Park.

🏃 10 Mile Relay – Teams of 4! Gather your crew, with each runner completing the same scenic loop before passing the baton. It's the perfect mix of teamwork, strategy, and fun!

 

🏃 10 Mile Relay – Teams of 2! Grab a partner and take on a fast, scenic loop, with each runner completing 2 loops. It’s the perfect mix of teamwork, strategy, and fun!

 

🏃 5K Solo Race! A thoughtfully designed route that balances challenge and enjoyment — perfect for experienced trail runners and those new to the sport.

 

Whether you're racing with a team or taking on the 5K solo, this event is the perfect way to push your limits, connect with fellow runners, and embrace the magic of trail running under the evening sky. With well-stocked aid stations, an enthusiastic volunteer crew, and an electrifying atmosphere, you'll have everything you need to make this race one to remember.

So grab your teammates, lace up your trail shoes, and join us for an incredible night of running, camaraderie, and unforgettable moments! Register now and experience the Los Angeles Sunset Trail Relays & 5K like never before!

 

Each Participant receives:

  • Scenic, and well marked courses

  • Panoramic views of Griffith Park, the LA River, and Glendale.

  • Ultra-soft, ultra-comfy premium gender-specific short sleeve T-shirt featuring the names of every team at the event!* 

  • Unique Finisher’s medal for all participants

  • Live Music

  • Prizes from our sponsors awarded to the top 3 teams (Relays Only).

  • Exclusive Captain, and Anchor Badge for Last Leg Runners (Relays only)

  • Special Award for Overall and Age Grade Division Winners (5K only)

  • Special Trophy for the team with the Most Spirited Name (Relays Only)

  • Free Downloadable Race Photos from our professional photography team

  • Chip time results

  • Course Aid Stations with medical staff

  • Food Truck

  • Custom Bibs

  • Enthusiastic Volunteer Support

  • Finish Line Fruit, Snacks, Refreshments, and Full Body Wipes

  • Flexible deferral and transfer options

  • Access to the exclusive Los Angeles Sunset Trail Run sale at Fleet Feet Burbank

  • Lifelong memories with friends!

 
*Must register by August 31, 2026 to have your team name printed on the back.

name: LSA's Run Home 2026
description:
This is a fundraiser for Life Services Alternatives which provides homes and services for the I/DD community in the Bay Area.

 

Please register to race and donate, or just donate!

 

Life Services Alternatives Run Home

Life Services Alternatives celebrates 22 years after opening their first home with a Live Race Event

  • Race Distances -- 5K, 10K

  • Virtual Run Distances - 5k, 10k - for those who are unable to join on race day.

 

Register early before price goes up and to secure your T-shirt (Shirt sizes subject to availability).  Take advantage of $5 early bird special discount until June 3rd. 

 

Register for LSA's Run Home Here!

Life Services Alternatives, Inc sponsors this race and is the beneficiary. All participants are encouraged to donate and or raise funds for the Life Services Alternatives cause. If you are not a runner or are unable to run you are still available to donate to Life Services Alternatives!

 

About Life Services Alternatives

Life Services Alternatives provides exceptional community living and programs for adults with developmental disabilities. 
 
In our county, there is a housing shortage for adults with development disabilities. In the past 4 years, over 40 programs have closed due staffing issues, low government rates and the high cost of living in the Silicon Valley. A high percentage of adults with developmental disabilities live at home with their parents. Unfortunately, parents age, have health issues, or they can no longer care for their adult child. Parents worry about who will take care of their adult child when they no longer can.
 
Life Services Alternatives helps to alleviate those worries. We opened our first three homes in 2004 in Santa Clara. It was a goal of Life Services Alternatives to establish homes where residents could grow and thrive in a non-institutional setting.  We currently have 15 licensed homes throughout Santa Clara County (San Jose, Campbell, Santa Clara and Morgan Hill) that are home to men and women who are developmentally disabled. Our residents’ range in age from 20 to 80 years old with a wide range of disabilities. 16th home is in the process of renovation and retrofitting to meet the community home standards. Five of our fifteen homes are for individuals who have special health care needs and intensive support needs. Our remaining nine homes, are home to residents who need 24-hour a day, non-medical care and supervision. It is Life Services Alternatives goal to continue to open new homes in our county where residents can live their best possible lives. Your support is needed to reach our goal. Your donation is greatly appreciated and will help change the lives of a developmentally disabled adult.

description:

name: LUCHA RUN
description:
Get ready for the 3RD Annual Lucha Run—a lively, family-friendly event to finish the year with a bang! Bring your best "luchador/a" costume and join us for either a 6K run or a 3K (2-mile) walk. It’s a celebration of fitness, fun, and flavor for all ages! NEW FOR 2025: OUR EVENT WILL TAKE PLACE AT FRESNO CITY COLLEGE AS WE'LL HAVE A REAL "LUCHA LIBRE" WRESTLING MATCH AT THE END OF THE EVENT! 

  • Fun and Festive Atmosphere: Show off your best lucha-inspired costumes, and bring your friends and family to cheer you on.
  • Post-Race Fiesta: Celebrate at the finish line with delicious tacos, hot chocolate, and "pan dulce" waiting to refuel you.
  • Support Local Fitness: As with all Reyes Racing events, this run brings the community together to stay active and celebrate the joy of movement.

WE HAVE ADDED A 2 MILE SPEED WALK! TOP 5 MALE/FEMALE GET AWARDS! 

A FEW REASONS TO JOIN OUR EVENT!

  • DRI FIT LONG SLEEVE SHIRTS!
  • Unique MEDAL
  • TACOS
  • HOT CHOCOLATE
  •  "PAN DULCE"
  • REAL LUCHA EVENT AFTER THE EVENT!! NEW FOR 2025!
  • $100 CASH to top male/female!
  • $200 CASH to team with most participants!
  • $200 CASH to the fastest team (top 5 runners in your team count for scoring)
  • UNIQUE COFFEE MUGS FOR TOP 10 MALE/FEMALE OVERALL!
  • Unique AGE GROUP AWARDS
  • ATHENA/CLYDESDALE age group divisions
  • BEST COSTUME competition
  • GREAT RUNNING COURSE, FLAT AT FRESNO CITY COLLEGE CAMPUS!
  • KIDS RACES
  • FUN, MUSIC!

BIB PICK UP/LATE REGISTRATION:

SAT, DEC 5TH, 3:00-5:00PM @ FLEET FEET STORE

SUN, DEC 6TH, 7:45-8:45AM @ FRESNO CITY COLLEGE (Veterans Peace Memorial Area)

RACE DAY SCHEDULE:

8:45AM- KIDS RACES

9:00AM- 6K/2 MILE

10:30AM- AWARDS

11:00AM- LIVE LUCHA LIBRE!!! (FREE EVENT FOR ALL PARTICIPANTS. NON PARTICIPANTS/PUBLIC CAN BUY A TICKET FOR THE LUCHA LIBRE EVENT. $20 ADULTS, $10 KIDS. TICKEST CAN BE BOUGHT ONLINE OR AT THE DOOR AT THE EVENT)

Lucha Libre "mascaras" available for sale for $10-$15 for anyone who would like to buy one during bib pick up on Saturday and Sunday (race day).

This event welcomes participants of all ages, abilities, and fitness levels, celebrating movement, community, and the beauty of Malibu.

name: Mammoth Bar Trail Runs
description:
"Standard distance. Mammoth vert."

Mammoth Bar Trail Runs take place on the single-track and double-track trails of Mammoth Bar OHV Area in Auburn State Recreation Area, in the Endurance Capital of Auburn, California.

Mammoth Bar is known for its steep climbs and descents, as well as it's beautiful American River Canyon views.

These are not your average courses. You get more vert per dollar! Yay!

name: Mammoth BUFF - Beer Mile Run
description:
In honor of what once was Oktoberfest’s Bier Run, we now host our own beer run to keep the party going. Participate in the run AND the ride to be entered into the BUFF Category for Mammoth TUFF. Scored as an Omnium on time.

Date
Friday, September 18, 2026

Time
3pm-4:15pm: Pick up bib and swag in The Village at Mammoth
4:30PM: Race begins

Race Entry Fee
$30

All participants will receive three beers/water for the run.

Distance
3 laps of Lincoln House building in the Village
Distance: 3 x 0.3 mile

Layout
Race brief @ 4:30pm
All runners start together @ 4:35 

Format
Back by popular demand are 12-oz beers and traditional format of:
Drink 12oz beer, Run 0.3mi, Drink 12oz beer, Run 0.3mi, Drink 12oz beer, Run 0.3mi, Finish!
You must run all three laps and drink 3x12oz beers to get a finishing time within 25minutes of the timing start. 
Sober? No problem! We will have 12-oz sparkling water cans available for you.

Awards
1st place, BUFFEST WOMAN & MAN, will each receive a special gift.
Finishing times will be calculated into the BUFF Category omnium for awards on Sunday, Sept 20th.

name: MAMMOTH LAKES Intro to outdoor ROCK-CLIMBING TRIP
description:
PUT YOUR LEAVE IN!
MAMMOTH LAKES ROCK CLIMBING TRIP

Friday-Monday, September 4-7 Labor Day weekend 

Adventure Awaits in Mammoth Lakes! 
Join us for an unforgettable introduction to outdoor rock-climbing experience in the breathtaking mountains of Mammoth Lakes, California! Whether you’re a beginner or looking to sharpen your skills, our expert Alpine guides will help you conquer the cliffs safely and confidently.

Itinerary:

Friday, September 4

--Depart Coronado/San Diego en route to International Alpine Guides Mammoth Lakes, CA (campground about 8 hours)

-- set up camp, make dinner, brief for the weekend 

 

Saturday, September 5

--Depart campground, arrive at rock climbing instruction location

--Full day of instruction and climbing

 

Sunday, September 6

--Breakfast

--Pack up for local hike & town exploration

 

Monday, September 7

--Pack up camp and vehicles

--Depart Mammoth Lakes en route back to Coronado/San Diego 

A full list of what to bring will be provided to you via email. Camping, climbing and hiking gear is provided.

name: Manhattan Mile
description: Celebrate the Manhattan Grand Prix with us on July 12th as we host the coveted “Manhattan Mile” running event! The Manhattan Mile is a net-downhill race that will start and finish at Live Oak Park in Manhattan Beach, California.  All participants will receive a commemorative run t-shirt, plus there will be chip timing, $4,500 in potential cash awards to the top three overall male and female finishers, and awards to the top three male and female finishers in each age division.

description:
Runnin’ for Rhett hosts the MaraFUNrun in Land Park this year!

3,000 youth athletes from the Sacramento area take part in a 5K race celebrating the completion of six weeks of participation in our after-school Youth Fitness Program. You can support our local youth by joining us! Register to run, walk, or jog with the kids in our community 5K, volunteer your time, come out to cheer, or make a donation to help keep our Youth Fitness Program free for these youth athletes. It’s also the perfect shake-out before the big Marathon on Sunday.

name: Margaritaville Run San Diego Gaslamp 10K & 5K
description:
🌴 Lace up, Parrotheads! 🌴

Get ready to run straight into paradise at the Margaritaville Run San Diego Gaslamp, where tropical vibes meet city streets and every mile feels like a mini vacation. 🏃‍♀️🍹 Whether you’re here for the run, the party, or the post-race margaritas, this is your chance to turn race day into a full-on racecation.

Run through the heart of downtown San Diego, soak up the Gaslamp energy, and leave your worries back at the starting line. From start to finish, it’s all about good vibes, good company, and a well-earned celebration at the finish.

Sign up today and join the party! 🎉


 
The miles are easy when you're in the Margaritaville state of mind!

Set in the iconic Gaslamp Quarter, this run brings island vibes to one of San Diego’s most electric neighborhoods. Known for its historic streets, lively nightlife, and walkable downtown energy, the Gaslamp offers the perfect backdrop for a fun-forward run that doesn’t take itself too seriously.

With sunny skies, coastal air, and palm trees never far from view, San Diego is the ultimate place to escape the everyday.


The Perks of Participating

Run, walk or stroll in the Margaritaville State of Mind
Official Margaritaville Run Participant Tech Tee
Margaritaville Run Finisher Medal


Transfer Policy

Participants may transfer from one race distance to another at any time, provided the desired event is not sold out.

All transfers are subject to a $15 transfer fee (plus a small processing fee), regardless of whether you are upgrading or downgrading.
Upgrading to a longer or higher-priced distance: You will be responsible for the $15 transfer fee plus the difference between what you originally paid and the current registration price.
Downgrading to a shorter or lower-priced distance: The $15 transfer fee still applies, but no refunds will be issued for the price difference.

For assistance or additional questions, please email us at info@margaritavillerun.com.

 

Charity

Give Kids The World Village is an 89-acre, whimsical nonprofit in Central Florida that provides critically ill children and their families with magical weeklong wish vacations at no cost.  Since 1986, the Village has welcomed more than 174,000 families from all 50 states and 76 countries. For more information, visit www.gktw.org. 
 
For more information about the run visit www.MargaritavilleRun.com

name: Martha's Village & Kitchen 20th Annual Thanksgiving Day 5K
description:
The Martha’s Village & Kitchen Thanksgiving Day 5K is an annual, family friendly run and walk held in Palm Desert, California and this year we are celebrating 20 years of giving back!

This beloved Thanksgiving tradition brings more than 5,000 participants, spectators, and volunteers together to raise awareness and critical funds in support of Martha’s Village & Kitchen and our mission to end hunger and homelessness in the Coachella Valley.

Race day is a full celebration featuring a live DJ and stage, trophy presentations, and a high energy finish line experience. Register as an individual, start a team, or join an existing team and get ready to run or walk for a cause!

Do not forget to capture the moment! Share your race day photos and videos and tag @MarthasVillage or use #MVK5K on Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok!

name: May the 4th be with You- The Empire Strides Back  5K, 10K, & Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
May the 4th Be With You – 5K, 10K, Half Marathon | Long Beach

The Empire Strides Back – Medals, Chip Timing, Photos, Costume Fun!

 

🏅 Everyone Gets a Medal – No Force Powers Required!
Empire Strides Back – May the 4th Be With You 5K, 10K, & Half Marathon
📍 5000 E Ocean Blvd Long Beach, CA 90803
🗓 Sunday- May 2nd, 2027

 

Same Day Registration Opens at 6:00 AM @ the Race Ready Athletics Tents 

Runner Check In/Bib Pick Up Opens at 6:00 AM

 
👟 Start Times Based on Distance :

Half Marathon: 7:00 AM
5K & 10K : 8:00 AM

1 Miler: 9:00 AM

Kids Dash: 9:30 AM


 
🚗 Parking:
Street parking is free. Lot parking is $2.00 per hour. Pay at machine in parking lot 
 
🌌 Why You Should Join:
Ready to race through the galaxy? Whether you’re a Jedi, Sith, or Rebel runner, come show off your Force in this high-vibe, costumed run along the scenic Long Beach waterfront.

🎭 Costumes encouraged! Come dressed as your favorite hero, villain, or creature.
📸 Epic photo ops with galaxy props and backdrops.
🎶 Out-of-this-world vibes with music, cheering, and space-age fun.
 
 
🎉 Event Perks:
🏅 Everyone gets a finisher medal
📸 Free race-day photos
🔄 Chip-timed results posted on-site
🚰 Water stations & restrooms on course
👶 Stroller-friendly and beginner-welcoming

🏅 Age Group & Overall Awards
 
🎟 Sign up now and let the Force (and your feet) guide you!

name: Mean Girls 5K, 10K & Half Marathon
description:
On Mean Girls Day, October 3rd, 2026 he asked you what day it was. You said it’s October 3rd.

Now lace up and run.

Welcome to The Mean Girls 5K, 10K and Half Marathon, a pink powered comedy fueled tribute to the most quotable high school ever. This event transforms the LA River Path into North Shore High where every runner is either trying to make fetch happen or survive gym class without being personally victimized by Regina George.

Presented by Jed and Ted’s Excellent Races.

Wear pink if it’s Wednesday. Wear sweatpants only if it’s Saturday. Do not wear army pants and flip flops unless you want everyone else to buy army pants and flip flops.

This is your chance to run like you’re late for Calc, dodge Regina’s bus, and earn a medal pretty enough for the Spring Fling Court.

Choose your challenge:

  • The Burn Book 5K - A fast and funny out and back perfect for anyone who wants to run, walk, gossip, or talk about how butter is a carb.
  • The Glen Coco 10K - Six point two miles of pure candy cane energy. You go Glen Coco. Treat yourself and your friends. None for Gretchen Wieners.
  • The Full Plastics Half Marathon - Thirteen point one miles of pure drama control. Stay hydrated. Stay cute. Try not to start a three way call attack. Cross the finish feeling like the new Spring Fling Queen.
  • The Multiverse Lunch Table Dash (Virtual) - Run from anywhere. Work. School. Your bedroom. Africa.

Costumes Welcome

  • Pink everything
  • Plastics energy
  • Mathletes jackets
  • Mrs. Norbury teacher vibes
  • Kevin G rap battle looks
  • Mouse ears because duh you’re a mouse

Community Vibe

This race is all about fun, connection, silliness, and giving runners a day they’ll talk about in group chats all year. No cliques here. Everyone can sit with us.

 

Parody Note
This event is a fan made parody inspired by early 2000s teen pop culture and is not affiliated with or endorsed by any official rights holders.

name: Meet at: Fantasy Realm in Concert
description:
This one’s for all the Final Fantasy fans. Experience a special 25th‑anniversary celebration of Final Fantasy X in concert, performed by the San Diego Symphony. Your seats are located in Bridgeview Right, Row BB, offering a great view of this unforgettable musical tribute. 

 

Tickets will be transferred via phone number/email.

name: Meet at: Princess and the Beast Show
description:
Calling all princess fans—step into the magic with a live performance of Disney’s Beauty and the Beast. Enjoy an enchanting show filled with beloved characters, unforgettable music, and timeless fairytale charm. 

Tickets are located in Section BALCR 3 , Row Z.

name: Meet at: Safari Behind the Scenes Tour
description:
Get an up‑close look at wildlife on an exclusive Behind‑the‑Scenes tour. Enjoy an electric‑cart safari that brings you closer to some of your favorite animals as they roam and interact.

Open to ages 3 and up. 

The tour is 90 minutes long.

name: Meet at: San Diego Baseball All-Inclusive Game
description:
Spend a sunny day at the ballpark with all‑inclusive access to drinks and tacos. Enjoy sodas, adult beverages, fresh salad, a street‑taco station, rice and beans, and churros. Seating in the Beach section is first‑come, first‑served, and children 3 and under enter free. 

 

Baja Menu:

Individual Bags of Tortilla Chips

Mexican Caesar Salad

name: Merced Paws on Patrol Fun Run
description:
Complete the Paws on Patrol K-9 Heroes Series!  Love running for a great cause?  Take on the Paws on Patrol K-9 Heroes Series by participating in both Paws on Patrol events!

  Paws on Patrol 5K
  Castle Air Museum - Atwater, CA
  October 3, 2026 

  Merced Paws on Patrol Fun Run
  at Lake Yosemite - Merced, CA
  October 17, 2026 (Register your dog today!)

By registering for both events, you'll help provide support for local law enforcement K-9 teams while enjoying two unique race experiences dedicated to honoring these four-legged heroes.

Series participants will receive:

  • Two unforgettable race experiences
  • Exclusive K-9 themed finisher medals that are designed to become part of a larger collection
  • The satisfaction of helping support programs that benefit working police dogs and their handlers

Make it your mission to complete the entire series and celebrate the Honor • Courage • Service demonstrated by our K-9 heroes every day.  Register for both events today and join the pack!  Make it a true K-9 Heroes challenge!  Join runners from across the Central Valley by completing both Paws on Patrol events.

name: Merry Miles-  5K, 10K,  and Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
🎅 Merry Miles 5K. 10K. Half Marathon
📅 Saturday, December 6, 2026
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd Long Beach, CA 90803

 

This festive coastal run is all about holiday spirit, good vibes, and giving back — plus, we’re collecting donations for the Long Beach Animal Shelter to help local pets in need. 🐾
Bring a toy, treat, blanket, or bag of food from their wish list (posted at check-in) and help spread pawsitive cheer to our four-legged friends waiting for their forever homes.

 
🏃‍♀️ Event Highlights
✨ Professional chip timing on a flat, fast course
📸 Elfie Stations & finish-line photo ops galore
🏅  Finsher Medals for All - Overall and Age Group Awards
🎅 Costumes encouraged! Dress festive, funny, or fabulously extra 

🎅 Costume Contest with Prizes
🍪 Holiday treats & hot cocoa at the finish-line festival
🎶 DJ Claus spinning holiday remixes all morning

 
🕒 Schedule of Events
Bib Pick-Up: 6:00 AM – 8:00 AM at the Race Ready Athletics Tent
Half Marathon Start: 7:00 AM
5K & 10K Start: 8:00 AM
🏆 Awards: 9:30 AM

All finishers receive a medal, free race-day photos, and yummy holiday snacks — whether you’ve been naughty, nice, or somewhere in between.

 
💝 Why We Run
Because giving back feels even better than crossing the finish line.
Your donations to the Long Beach Animal Shelter help keep rescue pets warm, fed, and full of holiday hope. Every mile = a tail wag of gratitude. 🐾

 
💬 Why CaliFlow Runs
CaliFlow Runs creates inclusive, affordable, and high-vibe races that bring runners and walkers of all paces together. We keep it low-key, coastal, and full of good energy — because fitness and fun should always go hand in hand.

 
🚗 Parking
$2.00 per hour in the beach lot or Street Parking is FREE

name: Midway Shelter Winter Run / Walk ~ 5k, 10k and Kids Run
description:
General Info - December 5th, 2026


Join us for the annual Midway Shelter winter run. Event takes place at the Harbor Bay Ferry Terminal in Alameda on Bay Farm Island and supports a great cause. 


The run will take you along the beautiful shoreline of Bay Farm Island and is a flat out and back with views of San Francisco and the Alameda Main Island. the first half is on the Harbor Bay Road with closed lanes for runners and the return is on the trails


The Kids run for 12 and under will be a 1/2 mile course. Kids run will start at 9:45am and will follow a circular loop out and back on the shoreline trail. There is plenty of parking at the Ferry terminal and we will have snacks and drinks when the race is over. 


Packet Pick up and Race Schedule:

  • December 4th and 5th, 2026: 10:00am - 5:00pm Lauren's Closet 1420 Park St / Alameda, Ca. 94501
  • December 6th: 
    • 7:30am ~ raceday registration opens
      8:30am ~ 10k starts
      8:45am ~ 5k starts
      9:45am ~ kids 1/2 mile run starts
      10:00am ~ 5k and 10k awards
       

Midway Shelter provides emergency shelter to homeless women and children and is operated through a partnership with Alameda Homeless Network and Building Futures – learn more about our work by checking out our two websites, below!

Founded in 1989, Midway Shelter of Alameda provides a safe and supportive environment for women and children experiencing  homelessness. By pledging any dollar amount, in addition to your registration, you can support the Midway Shelter provide a safe place for women and their children. Your donation is tax deductible as the Alameda Homeless Network operates as a 501(c)3 Tax ID number 94-3078153)

 

http://midwayshelter.org/donate.htm
www.bfwc.org

name: MIGUEL REYES ELITE/FUN 5K Run/Walk
description:
11TH YEAR ANNIVERSARY FOR OUR MIGUEL REYES ELITE/OPEN 5K!! COME AND JOIN US AT THIS FUN, COMPETITIVE race in memory of a great person, runner and friend Miguel Reyes from Fresno, who passed away in 2015. Join his family, co-workers and friends participate in this 5K Run/Walk! This local race is considered "THE FASTEST, MOST COMPETITIVE RACE IN THE CENTRAL VALLEY".  We've had several Olympians who have joined us in the past and this year we are again expecting it to be a great running event. 

RACE AMENITIES:

  • OVER $18,000 TO BE GIVEN CASH AWARDS!
  • CIF HS CROSS COUNTRY CERTIFIED COURSE!
  • DRI FIT SINGLET SHIRT
  • UNIQUE MEDALS
  • FREE TACOS
  • "AGUAS FRESCAS"
  • ICE CREAM!
  • ATHENA CATEGORY ( Women>185lbs) 
  • CLYDESDALE CATEGORY ( Men>225 lbs)
  • TROPHY AWARDS FOR AGE GROUP CATEGORIES
  • CENTRAL VALLEY RUNNER OF THE YEAR EVENT
  • CHIP TIMING EVENT
  • KIDS RACES
  • FREE COMPLIMENTARY ENTRIES TO ELITE RUNNES

14:06 Evert Silva (2024)

TOP 3 KIDS ON EACH RACE (BOYS/GIRLS) GET TROPHIES!

name: Mile Madness Endurance Run
description:
Join the Ultimate Loop Adventure in the Heart of Trail Country!

Mile Madness is more than a race—it's a vibrant celebration of endurance, community, and personal triumph. Set against the stunning backdrop of Auburn, California, this looped trail event invites runners of all paces to push their limits (or simply enjoy the journey) on a meticulously designed 0.75-mile course and paved bike path, featuring a beautiful pond, shaded paths, and much more for an unforgettable experience.

Event Details:

Dates: September 18-21, 2026

Friday:

9:00 am 72 Hour Run

6:00 pm: 48 Hour Run

Saturday:

9:00 am 100 Mile Race and NEW 3-Hour Run

Noon: 12 Hour and 24 Hour

6:00 pm: 6 Hour Glow Run

Location: Auburn Recreation District Regional Park, 3770 Richardson Dr, Auburn, CA 95602

Race Options: Choose your challenge from 8 timed events, ranging from a beginner-friendly 3-hour run to the epic 72-hour ultra. With exceptionally long cutoffs and no strict time pressures, whether you're walking, running, or crawling, there's space for everyone to shine and even earn one of the coveted Mile Madness Buckles.

Course Highlights: A compact 0.75-mile loop means continuous laps with easy access to aid stations, festive decorations, and upbeat music to keep your spirits high. Aim for that first ultra milestone or chase elite goals—many of our runners discover untapped potential here. The course will be professionally measured prior to the race.

Why Mile Madness?

Inclusivity for All: We had runners from ages 10 to 82, with a balanced mix of 52.8% male and 47.2% female participants. In 2024, we welcomed 115 runners with a remarkable 72% buckle completion rate (applies to 48- and 72-hour runners); in 2025, we were 140 strong, and we're projecting 200-250 for 2026. Beginners who've never run an ultramarathon often surprise themselves with distances they never imagined.

Top-Notch Support: Fully stocked aid station featuring a rotating menu of hearty meals, electrolytes, all the typical aid station food, and endless encouragement from what might be the best volunteers in trail running. Other amenities include on-site massage therapists, family cheer zones, glow run, food trucks, and more...

Bling & Bragging Rights: Earn the coveted Silver 100-Mile Buckle (35 awarded in 2024, many to first timers!) or challenge yourself for the stunning Gold 150-Mile Buckle or the brand new 200-Mile buckle. Plus, a 100% rollover policy up to 24 hours before race start means zero risk if life throws a curveball.

SWAG: Every registered runner will receive MudGear/Mile Madness co-branded socks, a long-sleeve hooded tech shirt, and possibly more... We cannot guarantee sizes for registrations after 9/1/26, but we will do our best to accommodate requests. 

Bib Raffle: We will hold a bib raffle at regular intervals during the race. Registered runners will be entered into the raffle. It's a bonus: you might walk away with fantastic prizes, including shoes, handheld bottles, an antichafe stick, and more. Why should podium winners get all the bling?

Family & Community Focus: Bring your crew! Our expansive UltraLounge, which offers shaded comfort, music, free snacks and water, games, festive decorations, S’mores, and a DIY sign-making station to fuel the fun. Come solo or with friends—you'll leave with new bonds, shared stories, and memories that last a lifetime. Runners rave: "The highlight of my year!" (Summer W.) and "My favorite race ever!" (Shawnee).

Worry-Free Guarantee: We will roll over your race entry to the next year if you can't run due to injury, training challenges, or any other reason. We want you to enjoy the race you pay for, and we understand that life happens.

Extra Perks: Plenty of clean restrooms, and a commitment to giving back through the Run Free Foundation, whose mission is to empower at-risk youth and runners facing financial barriers by providing access to quality running gear and race registration scholarships, enabling them to pursue their athletic dreams and enhance their well-being. 

Mile Madness isn't just about the miles—it's about the madness of joy, grit, and connection that turns strangers into trail family. Whether you're chasing a PR, your first buckle, or just the thrill of the loop, we're here to support you through every step. We may have the best volunteers in the business.

New 3-Hour Race: We have wanted to offer a 3-hour race as a shorter option than the 6-hour race.  This is the perfect opportunity to experience looped-course racing, or for family and crew who may want to do fewer laps but still participate in the race. The 3-Hour race is priced lower and includes Co-Branded Mudgear/Mile Madness Socks and a shirt, food, and all amenities. The 3-Hour will not receive the larger SWAG item that the longer races keep, and the registration cost will be lower.  

Ultra Lounge: The family cheer zone is getting a more fitting name. We are borrowing the Ultra Lounge name and will have our 13x26 wedding tent with fun activities that will keep your crew going so they can keep cheering you on.  We will have food and water, a poster-making station, a glow party, cornhole, and more...

Referral Rewards: We want to reward you for referring other runners to Mile Madness.  When you register, you will get a referral code to share.  Have your family, friends, or social circle use that code, and you will receive a refund for every referral.

Earn $10 for any 6-Hour or 12-Hour referral.  Earn $20 for each referral to the 24-Hour or longer races.  The refund will happen automatically, and the referral code must be used by the person registering. 

Questions? Email Race Director Brian Goldman at brian@everydayenduranceraces.com. Let's make 2026 your most memorable madness yet!

name: Miles for Inclusion 5K (Walk, Jog or Run)
description: Our 5K is more than just a race it’s an opportunity to bring people together in support of a powerful organization. The Hrashq 5K is dedicated to raising awareness for our community of talented athletes with special needs, while promoting the importance of inclusion in everyday life. We aim to create a space where individuals of all abilities are celebrated, supported, and empowered. Through this event, we hope to unite not only the Armenian community, but diverse communities across Los Angeles fostering connection, understanding, and a shared commitment to inclusion. Together, we run, job or walk to inspire change, build acceptance, and strengthen a community where everyone belongs.

name: Miles for Mayo 5K
description:
Welcome to the Miles For Mayo 5K walk/run, a family-friendly event supporting local schools and running programs, representing the passion and values of Matías “Mayo” Rogers. In a short time, Matías ingrained himself in the local community as one of the best runners in Liberty High School history. He was also an honors AP student who lived the values of being kind, generous and helpful.

The race begins at Veteran's Park on Saturday, June 20 at 9 a.m. A virtual option is available for those who can not attend in person, but still want to be part of this special event.

Early Packet Pick-Up
Saturday, June 13, 2026
10a.m.-12p.m.
Mary Casey Black Elementary School – Multipurpose Room
480 Farmington Dr, Brentwood, CA 94513

Race fees before June 1, are as follows (children age 3 and under are welcome, no registration necessary):
Ages 4-9 $15
Ages 10-18 $20
Ages 19 and up $35

June 1 and after they are as follows:

Ages 4-9 $15
Ages 10-18 $25
Ages 19 and up $40

Additionally, starting June 1 shirt sizes are not guaranteed.

name: Millerton Madness Triathlon
description:
USAT Sanctioned Super Sprint Triathlon.  

Perfect for beginners, or a tune-up before your next big race.

400 yd swim | 5.4 mile bike | 2.2 mile run

Swim: Starting in the water at Millerton, athletes will utilize Millerton Lake Boat Launch. Athletes will swim 400 yards around buoys, back to the boat ramp, exit the water and proceed to the Transition Area.

Bike: Starting at the Transition Area, athletes will make their way north towards the Millerton park entrance, to the turnaround at the top Millerton Lake SRA sign. The bike is out and back with rolling hills. Returning to the transition area.

Run: Run is all asphalt road. Starting at the Transition Area, athletes head north from the parking lot along the street for approximately 1.1 miles towards the Millerton park entrance to the turn around, (at the crosswalk), and back to the finish line.

400 yd swim | 5.4 mile bike | 2.2 mile run

Swim: Starting in the water at Millerton, athletes will utilize Millerton Lake Boat Launch. Athletes will swim 400 yards around buoys, back to the boat ramp, exit the water and proceed to the Transition Area.

Bike: Starting at the Transition Area, athletes will make their way north towards the Millerton park entrance, to the turnaround at the top Millerton Lake SRA sign. The bike is out and back with rolling hills. Returning to the transition area.

Run: Run is all asphalt road. Starting at the Transition Area, athletes head north from the parking lot along the street for approximately 1.1 miles towards the Millerton park entrance to the turn around, (at the crosswalk), and back to the finish line.

name: MISSION INN RUN
description:
The 49th Annual Mission Inn Run returns to downtown Riverside on October 18, 2026! 

The Mission Inn Run, a signature Riverside event and key fundraiser for the Mission Inn Foundation, has been a Southern California Tradition for nearly 50 years. This historic race has traditionally launched in downtown Riverside, winding through the parks, landmarks and historic neighborhoods of our town. Proceeds support the nonprofit Mission Inn Foundation and Museum.

Races include the 5K, 10K and ½ Marathon with dedicated 5K Walk (perfect for the kids and pups!) Everyone from competitors to casual strollers are invited to join us!

•      All participants will receive the 2026 limited edition dry-tech T-shirt 
•      All participants will receive 2026 finisher medal 
•      All participants will receive limited edition non-woven reusable tote bag
·      Walk & Wag partnership with Mary S. Roberts Pet Adoption Center w/ pet bandana, pop-up dog park and more
•      All teams of 5 or more receive a $5/discount per member
•      Earn up to $20 off your registration by referring 5 or more friends (codes available after registration)

The Mission Inn Run, a Riverside tradition since 1977, is the primary fundraiser for the Mission Inn Foundation, a 501c3 non-profit museum organization. The Mission Inn Run is the trademarked intellectual property of the Mission Inn Foundation.  There is no affiliation with the Historic Mission Inn Corporation, nor does the Historic Mission Inn Corporation benefit from or support this event.  All funds raised go to the Mission Inn Foundation, a 501c3 non-profit organization.  For more information about the Mission Inn Foundation, please visit www.missioninnmuseum.org

name: MLK Jr. Freedom Run 5K/10K/13.1 LOS ANGELES
description:
Join in our annual Martin Luther King Jr. Day Run! Today, we gather to honor the legacy of Dr. King and his enduring commitment to justice, equality, and peace. As we lace up our shoes and hit the pavement, let’s reflect on his powerful message of love and resilience.
This event is not just about fitness; it’s a celebration of community, a call to action for social change, and a reminder of the work still to be done. Together, we can honor Dr. King’s dream and inspire one another to continue striving for a better world. Let’s run with purpose and passion! 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

description:
2026 here we come!

The Grafitti Classic Car theme will be back again with more cars and more entertainment. 

Visit our website for event details.

Our Cause

Proceeds benefit the Teens Run Modesto program, which challenges area youth, especially those at-risk, to experience the benefits of goal-setting, character development, adult mentoring, and improved physical fitness through a structured training program culminating in the running and completion of the Modesto Marathon.

name: Mojave Half Marathon
description:
2026 Results link:

Athletes can check their 2026 Mojave Half Marathon results here:

https://www.geminiraceresults.com/results/mojave-half-marathon/2026

 

This is a "Closed Gate" event and Military Installation access is a requirement.

Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is proud to announce the Mojave Half Marathon, taking place on Saturday, 13 March 2027 aboard Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center.  Military Installation access is required.  

This half marathon will challenge runners to test their stamina, determination, and grit. Whether you are a seasoned distance runner or preparing for your next major fitness goal, now is the time to start training!

Registration opens:  Thursday, October 1, 2026

Registration closes:  Thursday, February 12, 2027

Registration fee:  TBD

ATTENTION:  Please be aware.  There is a cut off time for this event.  Runners must accomplish the 7-mile mark within 2 hours, or they will be removed from participating.  The overall limit for the half marathon is 4 hours.  Runners who do not meet these cut off times will be pulled from the event.  This is standard and due to the requirement to reopen closed roads to the MCAGCC community.

REMINDER:  This is a "Closed Gate" event and Military Installation access is a requirement.

For questions or additional information, please contact MCCS Athletics at 760.830.6857 or email 29athletics@usmc-mccs.org.

name: Morgan Hill AAUW Wildflower Run
description:
The AAUW Wildflower Run raises money for scholarships and leadership programs for women & girls and community grants. (For information about our organization, go to www.aauwmh.org.) 10K Run, 5K Run, 5K Walk, and 5K stroller/baby jogger category are all on country roads with chip timing. The Kids' 2K  Run (ages 5-11) and our "all inclusive, non-competitive" 2K Fun Run/Walk (for ages 2-102) are both on a school track.  
Our new 5K and 10K routes are in a country setting surrounding Morgan Hill with flat terrain on paved roads. Flat and fast for runners wanting to improve their personal record times. Water available at start and finish of race, with multiple water stops along the routes. Strollers are welcome everywhere except on the school's track. No pets permitted on school grounds.
NOTE: The event is an "open course", so you will need to stay to the side of the road as some vehicular traffic is expected.
Register early to be guaranteed a unique, 2026 T-shirt in your size.  In addition to your limited edition T-shirt, we offer bonus baby-T's for the stroller event (while supplies last) and themed medals for youth. See wildflowerrun.org for details.
We offer discount pricing for groups, as follows:
  • groups of 10 or more (request a $5 off per person “coupon code” for your group in advance of registering; enter the code at checkout).
  • school teams (within boundaries of MHUSD) – if your principal has agreed to sign up your school for the "school competition", your school will have a unique school "coupon code" for $5 off any race for student/family/staff; enter the code at checkout.

name: Morgan Hill Freedom Run
description:
The Freedom Run is a premiere event at Morgan Hill’s annual Freedom Fest, one of the few all-day Independence Day celebrations in the Bay Area. Start your 4th of July celebration with a morning race that will take you through Morgan Hill’s historic, tree-lined downtown. Then stay for the award-winning parade, the largest privately organized parade in Northern California and the official 4th of July Parade of Santa Clara County. 

 

The Freedom Fest’s annual events also include the Patriotic Sing, Family Street Dance, Freedom Car Cruise and Show, and the spectacular fireworks and entertainment show, Fireworks on the Green. Celebrated in our historic downtown core, the Community and Cultural Center as well as the Outdoor Sports Center, our six events deliver a spectacular, fun-filled, family-friendly celebration every July 4th holiday!

 

Bib pickup will be Saturday June 27, 2026 from 10am to 2pm in the parking lot of the LDS church at 1790 E. Dunne Ave in Morgan Hill. There will be a second bib pickup day on July 2 or July 3 with time TBA. Bibs can also be picked up the morning of the race from 6:45am-7:30am at 17575 Peak Ave, near the finish line. Visit the race website for more information.

name: Morgan Hill Veterans Day  Run
description: The Morgan Hill Freedom Fest is proud to host the Veterans Day 5k & 10k and 1 mile children's Run to honor the men and women who have served or are currently serving in the armed forces of the United States.  You will have the opportunity to walk and run with these honorable men and women during the race and express your appreciation for their service as you finish the course with them. We encourage participants to take a moment and say, “Thank you for what you’ve done!” Small gestures mean a lot to those who have sacrificed so much. All proceeds from the  race will go to the Veteran organizations listed on our Partners page.  We hope to see you there!

name: Morning Paddle
description:
Kick off your summer morning with a refreshing paddle in the San Diego Bay. All kayaks and life jackets are provided, along with stunning waterfront views.

Participants must be at least 10 years old and able to swim.

name: Mountains 2 Beach Marathon and Half
description: Uniquely situated and completely surrounded by beautiful mountains, the city of Ojai holds the start of the Mountains 2 Beach Marathon while the half starts closer to the beach. This point to point race winds through the Ventura River Valley as it makes its way to the pristine beaches of the last great surf town in California, Ventura. Runners will love the gradual downhill nature of the race, which is prime to make you faster but not hurt the knees, and the amazing weather of the area. After a final tour of beach front Ventura, runners and their families are treated to a finish line party only steps away from the surf and the shops and restaurants of Historic Downtown Ventura. As a certified Boston Qualifier, the courses, the race and the surrounding communities make for the perfect destination marathon and half.
